description.zh: 一位会给动物看病的乡村医生，带着鹦鹉、猴子和猪远航非洲，为猴子们治病。
description.en: A country doctor who can talk to animals sails to Africa with his parrot, monkey and pig to cure the monkeys.

source.publisher: Frederick A. Stokes Company, New York
source.note: Project Gutenberg eBook #501 的转录，取 1920 年版正文。

title.en: The Doctor in the High Hat

paragraphs.text: Once upon a time, many years ago—when our grandfathers were little children—there was a doctor; and his name was Dolittle—John Dolittle, M.D. “M.D.” means that he was a proper doctor and knew a whole lot.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, many years ago—when our grandfathers were little children—there was a doctor; and his name was Dolittle—John Dolittle, M.D.
sentences.zh: 从前，很多很多年以前——那时我们的祖父还是小孩子——有一位医生，名叫杜立德，约翰·杜立德，医学博士。

sentences.text: “M.D.” means that he was a proper doctor and knew a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 「M.D.」的意思是，他是一位正统的医生，懂得非常多。

hints.zh: 医学博士（Doctor of Medicine）的缩写，说明他是正经挂牌的医生。
hints.en: Short for Doctor of Medicine: he was a properly qualified doctor.

paragraphs.text: He lived in a little town called, Puddleby-on-the-Marsh. All the folks, young and old, knew him well by sight. And whenever he walked down the street in his high hat everyone would say, “There goes the Doctor!—He’s a clever man.” And the dogs and the children would all run up and follow behind him; and even the crows that lived in the church-tower would caw and nod their heads.

sentences.text: He lived in a little town called, Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.
sentences.zh: 他住在一个叫「沼泽边的帕德尔比」的小镇上。

sentences.text: All the folks, young and old, knew him well by sight.
sentences.zh: 镇上的人，无论老少，都一眼就能认出他。

sentences.text: And whenever he walked down the street in his high hat everyone would say, “There goes the Doctor!—He’s a clever man.”
sentences.zh: 每当他戴着高礼帽走上街头，大家都会说：「医生来了！他可是个聪明人。」

sentences.text: And the dogs and the children would all run up and follow behind him; and even the crows that lived in the church-tower would caw and nod their heads.
sentences.zh: 狗和孩子都会跑上来跟在他身后；就连住在教堂钟楼里的乌鸦也会叫几声，点点头。

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」，故事发生的小镇。
hints.en: Puddleby-on-the-Marsh: the little town by the marsh where the story is set.

hints.zh: 凭长相、一眼认出；knew him well by sight 就是「一见就认得他」。
hints.en: From his appearance: they knew his face at once.

hints.zh: 高礼帽，旧时绅士出门戴的正式帽子。
hints.en: A tall formal hat worn out of doors by gentlemen of the time.

hints.zh: 人们（folks = people）。
hints.en: People; folks is a colloquial word for people.

paragraphs.text: The house he lived in, on the edge of the town, was quite small; but his garden was very large and had a wide lawn and stone seats and weeping-willows hanging over. His sister, Sarah Dolittle, was housekeeper for him; but the Doctor looked after the garden himself.

sentences.text: The house he lived in, on the edge of the town, was quite small; but his garden was very large and had a wide lawn and stone seats and weeping-willows hanging over.
sentences.zh: 他住在镇子边上，房子很小；花园却很大，有宽阔的草坪、石凳，还有垂柳低低地垂下来。

sentences.text: His sister, Sarah Dolittle, was housekeeper for him; but the Doctor looked after the garden himself.
sentences.zh: 他的姐姐萨拉·杜立德替他管家；不过花园是医生自己打理的。

paragraphs.text: He was very fond of animals and kept many kinds of pets. Besides the gold-fish in the pond at the bottom of his garden, he had rabbits in the pantry, white mice in his piano, a squirrel in the linen closet and a hedgehog in the cellar. He had a cow with a calf too, and an old lame horse—twenty-five years of age—and chickens, and pigeons, and two lambs, and many other animals. But his favorite pets were Dab-Dab the duck, Jip the dog, Gub-Gub the baby pig, Polynesia the parrot, and the owl Too-Too.

sentences.text: He was very fond of animals and kept many kinds of pets.
sentences.zh: 他非常喜欢动物，养了许多种宠物。

sentences.text: Besides the gold-fish in the pond at the bottom of his garden, he had rabbits in the pantry, white mice in his piano, a squirrel in the linen closet and a hedgehog in the cellar.
sentences.zh: 除了花园尽头池塘里的金鱼，他还在食品间养兔子，在钢琴里养白鼠，在放床单的柜子里养松鼠，在地窖里养刺猬。

sentences.text: He had a cow with a calf too, and an old lame horse—twenty-five years of age—and chickens, and pigeons, and two lambs, and many other animals.
sentences.zh: 他还养了一头母牛和它的小牛，一匹二十五岁的瘸腿老马，还有鸡、鸽子、两只小羊，以及许多别的动物。

sentences.text: But his favorite pets were Dab-Dab the duck, Jip the dog, Gub-Gub the baby pig, Polynesia the parrot, and the owl Too-Too.
sentences.zh: 但他最喜欢的宠物是鸭子达布达布、狗吉普、小猪咕咕、鹦鹉波利尼西亚和猫头鹰图图。

hints.zh: 放床单、毛巾和亚麻织物的柜子。
hints.en: The cupboard where bed linen and towels are kept.

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor's duck.

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor's dog.

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的宠物小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor's baby pig.

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor's parrot.

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor's owl.

introduction.zh: 帕德尔比的人都认识那位戴高礼帽的杜立德医生，见面总会说「他是个聪明人」。可这位人人敬重的医生，家里的食品间住着兔子，钢琴里住着白鼠。一个正经医生，家里怎么住满了动物？
introduction.en: Everyone in Puddleby knows the Doctor in his high hat. “He’s a clever man,” they say. But his small house is full of animals: rabbits in the food cupboard, white mice in the piano. Why would a proper doctor live like that?

quiz.question: What do people say when the Doctor walks down the street?
options: “The Doctor needs a new hat.”
“There goes the Doctor! He’s a clever man.”
“There goes a stranger.”

feedback.zh: 原文说他一上街，大家就说「医生来了！他是个聪明人」，狗和孩子都跟在后面。
feedback.en: The text says everyone would say “There goes the Doctor! He’s a clever man,” and the dogs and children followed him.

quiz.question: Where does the Doctor keep his rabbits?
options: In the pantry
In the piano
In the cellar

feedback.zh: 兔子在食品间；白鼠在钢琴里，松鼠在放床单的柜子里，刺猬在地窖里。
feedback.en: The rabbits live in the pantry; the mice are in the piano, the squirrel in the linen closet and the hedgehog in the cellar.

grammar.excerpt: whenever he walked down the street in his high hat everyone would say

focus.zh: would say 讲过去反复发生的事：每次他上街，大家都会这么说，不是「将会说」。
focus.en: Would say does not mean the future here: it describes what people said again and again in the past.

paragraphs.text: His sister used to grumble about all these animals and said they made the house untidy. And one day when an old lady with rheumatism came to see the Doctor, she sat on the hedgehog who was sleeping on the sofa and never came to see him any more, but drove every Saturday all the way to Oxenthorpe, another town ten miles off, to see a different doctor.

sentences.text: His sister used to grumble about all these animals and said they made the house untidy.
sentences.zh: 姐姐过去常常为这些动物发牢骚，说它们把屋子弄得乱七八糟。

sentences.text: And one day when an old lady with rheumatism came to see the Doctor, she sat on the hedgehog who was sleeping on the sofa and never came to see him any more, but drove every Saturday all the way to Oxenthorpe, another town ten miles off, to see a different doctor.
sentences.zh: 有一天，一位患风湿病的老太太来看病，一屁股坐在沙发上睡觉的刺猬身上；从那以后她再也没来找过他，而是每个星期六坐车跑十英里，去另一个镇奥克森索普看别的医生。

analysis.core: she sat on the hedgehog and never came to see him any more, but drove every Saturday all the way to Oxenthorpe

parts.text: when an old lady with rheumatism came to see the Doctor
parts.zh: when 从句交代时间：一位患风湿的老太太来看病时。
parts.en: The when-clause sets the time: an old lady with rheumatism came to see the Doctor.

parts.text: who was sleeping on the sofa
parts.zh: who 从句修饰 the hedgehog：刺猬正睡在沙发上。
parts.en: The who-clause describes the hedgehog: it was asleep on the sofa.

parts.zh: 同位语补充 Oxenthorpe：十英里外的另一个镇子。
parts.en: An appositive explains Oxenthorpe: another town ten miles off.

parts.zh: 不定式说明她跑那么远的目的：去看别的医生。
parts.en: The to-infinitive gives her purpose: to see a different doctor.

order.zh: 先把时间从句「有一天……来看病」放在前面，再说她坐到刺猬身上，最后用 but 引出她此后的做法：再也不来，改去十英里外的奥克森索普。
order.en: The time clause comes first, then what she sat on, then but introduces what she did afterwards: never return, and go to Oxenthorpe instead.

note.zh: 先找到主句的 sat、never came 和 drove；who 从句不是谓语，drove 与 sat、came 并列。
note.en: Find the main verbs sat, never came and drove; the who-clause is not a verb.

hints.zh: 奥克森索普，十英里外的另一个镇子。
hints.en: Oxenthorpe, another town ten miles away.

paragraphs.text: Then his sister, Sarah Dolittle, came to him and said,

sentences.text: Then his sister, Sarah Dolittle, came to him and said,
sentences.zh: 后来，他的姐姐萨拉·杜立德走到他面前，说：

paragraphs.text: “John, how can you expect sick people to come and see you when you keep all these animals in the house? It’s a fine doctor would have his parlor full of hedgehogs and mice! That’s the fourth personage these animals have driven away. Squire Jenkins and the Parson say they wouldn’t come near your house again—no matter how sick they are. We are getting poorer every day. If you go on like this, none of the best people will have you for a doctor.”

sentences.text: “John, how can you expect sick people to come and see you when you keep all these animals in the house?
sentences.zh: 「约翰，你屋里养着这么些动物，还指望病人上门来看病吗？

sentences.text: It’s a fine doctor would have his parlor full of hedgehogs and mice!
sentences.zh: 好医生才会让诊室里塞满刺猬和老鼠呢！

sentences.text: That’s the fourth personage these animals have driven away.
sentences.zh: 这已经是这些动物赶走的第四位客人了。

sentences.text: Squire Jenkins and the Parson say they wouldn’t come near your house again—no matter how sick they are.
sentences.zh: 詹金斯乡绅和教区牧师都说，不管病得多重，他们再也不会靠近你的房子。

sentences.text: We are getting poorer every day.
sentences.zh: 我们一天比一天穷。

sentences.text: If you go on like this, none of the best people will have you for a doctor.”
sentences.zh: 你再这样下去，体面人家谁也不会找你当医生了。」

hints.target: It’s a fine doctor would have his parlor full of hedgehogs and mice!
hints.zh: 萨拉的挖苦话：好医生才会让诊室里塞满刺猬和老鼠呢——意思是「哪有这样的医生」。
hints.en: Sarah is being sarcastic: a fine doctor indeed, who fills his parlour with hedgehogs and mice.

hints.zh: 人物、客人；这里带点夸张，指来看病的体面人。
hints.en: A person — here used a little pompously for a well-off patient.

hints.zh: 詹金斯乡绅，当地有地位的乡绅。
hints.en: Squire Jenkins: the local squire, a man of standing in the district.

hints.zh: 教区牧师。
hints.en: The parson: the priest of the parish.

hints.zh: 体面人、上流人家；萨拉指的是有钱有地位的主顾。
hints.en: The “best people”: the well-off families Sarah wants as patients.

paragraphs.text: “But I like the animals better than the ‘best people’,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “But I like the animals better than the ‘best people’,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可我喜欢动物，胜过喜欢那些『体面人』。」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “You are ridiculous,” said his sister, and walked out of the room.

sentences.text: “You are ridiculous,” said his sister, and walked out of the room.
sentences.zh: 「你真是荒唐。」姐姐说完，走出了房间。

introduction.zh: 姐姐萨拉替他管家，受够了满屋的动物。一位来看风湿的老太太坐到了沙发上睡觉的刺猬身上，从此再不上门。萨拉终于忍不住，把话挑明：再这样下去，谁还肯来找你看病？
introduction.en: His sister Sarah keeps house and has had enough of the animals. An old lady with rheumatism sits on the sleeping hedgehog and never comes back. At last Sarah speaks her mind: who will still come to the Doctor if things go on like this?

quiz.question: Why does the old lady never come back to the Doctor?
options: The Doctor was too busy to see her.
She moved to another country.
She sat on the sleeping hedgehog.

feedback.zh: 原文说她一屁股坐在沙发上睡觉的刺猬身上，从此再没上门，宁可每个星期六坐车去十英里外的奥克森索普。
feedback.en: The text says she sat on the hedgehog asleep on the sofa, and after that drove all the way to Oxenthorpe every Saturday instead.

quiz.question: What does Sarah say will happen if the Doctor keeps the animals?
options: He will become a farmer.
No fine people will come to him as patients.
The animals will eat his garden.

feedback.zh: 萨拉最后撂下话：再这样下去，体面人家谁也不会找他当医生了。
feedback.en: Sarah ends by telling him that if he goes on like this, none of the best people will have him for a doctor.

grammar.excerpt: His sister used to grumble about all these animals

focus.zh: used to grumble 表示过去常常抱怨，现在不一定如此；used to 后面跟动词原形。
focus.en: Used to grumble describes a habit in the past, not necessarily now; used to takes the base verb.

paragraphs.text: So, as time went on, the Doctor got more and more animals; and the people who came to see him got less and less. Till at last he had no one left—except the Cat’s-meat-Man, who didn’t mind any kind of animals. But the Cat’s-meat-Man wasn’t very rich and he only got sick once a year—at Christmas-time, when he used to give the Doctor sixpence for a bottle of medicine.

sentences.text: So, as time went on, the Doctor got more and more animals; and the people who came to see him got less and less.
sentences.zh: 日子一天天过去，医生的动物越来越多，上门看病的人却越来越少。

sentences.text: Till at last he had no one left—except the Cat’s-meat-Man, who didn’t mind any kind of animals.
sentences.zh: 到最后，他一个病人也没有了——只剩下那个卖猫食的人，他倒不在乎屋里有什么动物。

sentences.text: But the Cat’s-meat-Man wasn’t very rich and he only got sick once a year—at Christmas-time, when he used to give the Doctor sixpence for a bottle of medicine.
sentences.zh: 可卖猫食的人不太有钱，一年只病一次——就在圣诞节前后。那时他会给医生六便士，买一瓶药。

hints.zh: 卖猫食的人，走街串巷卖马肉、猫食的小贩。
hints.en: The cat's-meat man: a street seller who sold meat for cats and dogs.

hints.zh: 六便士，英国旧币制的小银币，当时是很少的一点钱。
hints.en: Sixpence: a small silver coin in the old British money, very little even then.

paragraphs.text: Sixpence a year wasn’t enough to live on—even in those days, long ago; and if the Doctor hadn’t had some money saved up in his money-box, no one knows what would have happened.

sentences.text: Sixpence a year wasn’t enough to live on—even in those days, long ago; and if the Doctor hadn’t had some money saved up in his money-box, no one knows what would have happened.
sentences.zh: 一年六便士，在那些久远的年月也不够过日子；要不是医生在存钱盒里攒了点钱，后来会怎样，谁也说不准。

hints.zh: 存钱盒、储蓄罐。
hints.en: A money-box where he kept his savings.

paragraphs.text: And he kept on getting still more pets; and of course it cost a lot to feed them. And the money he had saved up grew littler and littler.

sentences.text: And he kept on getting still more pets; and of course it cost a lot to feed them.
sentences.zh: 他还不断添置新的宠物；养它们当然要花不少钱。

sentences.text: And the money he had saved up grew littler and littler.
sentences.zh: 他攒下的钱越来越少。

paragraphs.text: Then he sold his piano, and let the mice live in a bureau-drawer. But the money he got for that too began to go, so he sold the brown suit he wore on Sundays and went on becoming poorer and poorer.

sentences.text: Then he sold his piano, and let the mice live in a bureau-drawer.
sentences.zh: 后来他卖掉了钢琴，让白鼠住进五斗柜的抽屉。

sentences.text: But the money he got for that too began to go, so he sold the brown suit he wore on Sundays and went on becoming poorer and poorer.
sentences.zh: 可卖钢琴的钱也渐渐花光了，于是他又卖掉礼拜天穿的棕色西装，日子越过越穷。

hints.zh: 五斗柜、带抽屉的柜子；不是「办公室」。
hints.en: A chest of drawers, not an office.

paragraphs.text: And now, when he walked down the street in his high hat, people would say to one another, “There goes John Dolittle, M.D.! There was a time when he was the best known doctor in the West Country—Look at him now—He hasn’t any money and his stockings are full of holes!”

sentences.text: And now, when he walked down the street in his high hat, people would say to one another, “There goes John Dolittle, M.D.!
sentences.zh: 如今他戴着高礼帽上街，人们会互相说：「约翰·杜立德医学博士来了！

sentences.text: There was a time when he was the best known doctor in the West Country—Look at him now—He hasn’t any money and his stockings are full of holes!”
sentences.zh: 想当年，他是整个英格兰西南部最有名的医生——你看看他现在——一个钱也没有，袜子上全是窟窿！」

hints.zh: 英格兰西南部地区。
hints.en: The West Country: the south-west of England.

paragraphs.text: But the dogs and the cats and the children still ran up and followed him through the town—the same as they had done when he was rich.

sentences.text: But the dogs and the cats and the children still ran up and followed him through the town—the same as they had done when he was rich.
sentences.zh: 可狗、猫和孩子们仍旧跑过来，跟着他穿过镇子——跟他有钱的时候一模一样。

introduction.zh: 病人一个接一个不来了，只剩那个一年只在圣诞节病一次的卖猫食的人。动物却越养越多，钱越花越快。医生开始卖东西：钢琴，还有礼拜天穿的棕色西装。下一件要卖的会是什么？
introduction.en: One patient after another stops coming, until only the cat’s-meat man is left, and he falls ill just once a year at Christmas. The animals multiply and the money runs out. The Doctor starts selling things: his piano, then his brown Sunday suit. What will he have to sell next?

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor sell his piano?
options: He needs money for food and for his animals.
He wants to buy a better one.
The mice have broken it.

feedback.zh: 一年六便士不够生活，他只能靠积蓄；动物越养越多，钱越花越快，只好卖东西换钱。
feedback.en: Sixpence a year was not enough to live on, so he lived on his savings; feeding more animals cost more, and he began to sell things.

quiz.question: What do the animals and children do now that the Doctor is poor?
options: They stay away from him.
They bring him money.
They still follow him through the town.

feedback.zh: 狗、猫和孩子仍旧跟着他走，跟他有钱的时候一样；变的只是大人们对他的议论。
feedback.en: The dogs, cats and children still run after him, just as they did when he was rich; only the grown-ups’ talk has changed.

grammar.excerpt: went on becoming poorer and poorer

focus.zh: poorer and poorer 用两个比较级表示程度不断加深：越来越穷；本段的 more and more、less and less 同理。
focus.en: Poorer and poorer joins two comparatives with and to show a change that keeps growing; more and more and less and less work the same way.

paragraphs.text: It happened one day that the Doctor was sitting in his kitchen talking with the Cat’s-meat-Man who had come to see him with a stomach-ache.

sentences.text: It happened one day that the Doctor was sitting in his kitchen talking with the Cat’s-meat-Man who had come to see him with a stomach-ache.
sentences.zh: 有一天，医生正坐在厨房里，跟卖猫食的人说话；那人是肚子疼，来找他看病的。

hints.zh: 卖猫食的人，走街串巷卖马肉给猫狗吃的小贩。
hints.en: The Cat’s-meat-Man: the man who sells meat for cats and dogs from door to door.

paragraphs.text: “Why don’t you give up being a people’s doctor, and be an animal-doctor?” asked the Cat’s-meat-Man.

sentences.text: “Why don’t you give up being a people’s doctor, and be an animal-doctor?” asked the Cat’s-meat-Man.
sentences.zh: 「你干吗不干脆别当给人看病的医生，改行给动物看病呢？」卖猫食的人问。

hints.zh: 给人看病的医生；跟后面 animal-doctor（给动物看病的医生）相对。
hints.en: A doctor for people, as opposed to an animal-doctor.

paragraphs.text: The parrot, Polynesia, was sitting in the window looking out at the rain and singing a sailor-song to herself. She stopped singing and started to listen.

sentences.text: The parrot, Polynesia, was sitting in the window looking out at the rain and singing a sailor-song to herself.
sentences.zh: 那只鹦鹉波利尼西亚正蹲在窗台上，望着外面的雨，自己哼着一支水手的歌。

sentences.text: She stopped singing and started to listen.
sentences.zh: 她停下歌声，开始听起来。

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor’s parrot.

paragraphs.text: “You see, Doctor,” the Cat’s-meat-Man went on, “you know all about animals—much more than what these here vets do. That book you wrote—about cats, why, it’s wonderful! I can’t read or write myself—or maybe I’d write some books. But my wife, Theodosia, she’s a scholar, she is. And she read your book to me. Well, it’s wonderful—that’s all can be said—wonderful. You might have been a cat yourself. You know the way they think. And listen: you can make a lot of money doctoring animals. Do you know that? You see, I’d send all the old women who had sick cats or dogs to you. And if they didn’t get sick fast enough, I could put something in the meat I sell ’em to make ’em sick, see?”

sentences.text: “You see, Doctor,” the Cat’s-meat-Man went on, “you know all about animals—much more than what these here vets do.
sentences.zh: 「你瞧，医生，」卖猫食的人接着说，「动物的门道你全懂——比这些个兽医懂得多得多。

sentences.text: That book you wrote—about cats, why, it’s wonderful!
sentences.zh: 你写的那本书——写猫的那本，哎哟，写得太好了！

sentences.text: I can’t read or write myself—or maybe I’d write some books.
sentences.zh: 我自己不识字，也不会写——要不然，说不定我也能写几本书。

sentences.text: But my wife, Theodosia, she’s a scholar, she is.
sentences.zh: 可我老婆西奥多西娅，她可是个有学问的人，真的。

sentences.text: And she read your book to me.
sentences.zh: 她把你的书念给我听过。

sentences.text: Well, it’s wonderful—that’s all can be said—wonderful.
sentences.zh: 哎，真是好极了——除了好极了，没别的话说——好极了。

sentences.text: You might have been a cat yourself.
sentences.zh: 你简直就像自己当过猫一样。

sentences.text: You know the way they think.
sentences.zh: 猫心里怎么想，你都知道。

sentences.text: And listen: you can make a lot of money doctoring animals.
sentences.zh: 还有，你听着：给动物看病能挣大钱。

sentences.text: Do you know that?
sentences.zh: 你知道不知道？

sentences.text: You see, I’d send all the old women who had sick cats or dogs to you.
sentences.zh: 你想啊，那些老太太的猫啊狗啊病了，我就把她们都打发到你这儿来。

sentences.text: And if they didn’t get sick fast enough, I could put something in the meat I sell ’em to make ’em sick, see?”
sentences.zh: 要是它们病得不够快，我就在卖给她们的马肉里搁点东西，让它们病起来，明白吧？」

hints.zh: 这些个兽医；these here 是口语里加重语气的说法，vet 就是兽医。
hints.en: These vets: these here adds rough spoken emphasis, and vet means animal doctor.

hints.zh: 西奥多西娅，卖猫食人的妻子。
hints.en: Theodosia, the Cat’s-meat-Man’s wife.

hints.zh: 这里指识字、读过书的人，不是「学者」。
hints.en: Here it just means someone who can read and write.

hints.zh: them 的口语说法，读作 /əm/。
hints.en: ’em is a spoken form of them.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, no,” said the Doctor quickly. “You mustn’t do that. That wouldn’t be right.”

sentences.text: “Oh, no,” said the Doctor quickly.
sentences.zh: 「不行，」医生连忙说。

sentences.text: “You mustn’t do that.
sentences.zh: 「你千万不能那么做。

sentences.text: That wouldn’t be right.”
sentences.zh: 那是不对的。」

introduction.zh: 卖猫食的人捂着肚子来找杜立德医生看病，顺口给他出了个赚钱的主意：专门给动物看病。他还热情地说，自己有办法让老太太们的猫狗病得快些——只要医生点头。医生会怎么接这个话头？
introduction.en: The Cat’s-meat-Man comes with a stomach-ache and a plan. He says the Doctor knows animals better than any vet, and that plenty of old ladies would pay him well. Then he explains how he would make sure the animals get sick. What will the Doctor say to that?

quiz.question: Why does the Cat’s-meat-Man think the Doctor should treat animals?
options: Because the Doctor is tired of people.
Because animals pay better than people do.
Because the Doctor knows more about animals than the vets do.

feedback.zh: 他夸医生懂动物，「比这些个兽医懂得多得多」，还说他写猫的那本书好极了。
feedback.en: He says the Doctor knows all about animals, much more than the vets do.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor say about making the animals sick?
options: It is all right if only cats are made sick.
It must not be done, and it would not be right.
It is a clever way to find patients.

feedback.zh: 医生连忙说「你千万不能那么做」，还说那是不对的。
feedback.en: The Doctor answers quickly, “You mustn’t do that. That wouldn’t be right.”

grammar.excerpt: Why don’t you give up being a people’s doctor, and be an animal-doctor?

focus.zh: Why don’t you + 动词原形是在提建议，不是真问原因；give up 后面接动名词 being。
focus.en: Why don’t you …? offers advice rather than asking about a reason; give up is followed by the -ing form.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, I didn’t mean real sick,” answered the Cat’s-meat-Man. “Just a little something to make them droopy-like was what I had reference to. But as you say, maybe it ain’t quite fair on the animals. But they’ll get sick anyway, because the old women always give ’em too much to eat. And look, all the farmers round about who had lame horses and weak lambs—they’d come. Be an animal-doctor.”

sentences.text: “Oh, I didn’t mean real sick,” answered the Cat’s-meat-Man.
sentences.zh: 「哦，我不是说真让它们病，」卖猫食的人回答。

sentences.text: “Just a little something to make them droopy-like was what I had reference to.
sentences.zh: 「我指的是稍微搁一点东西，让它们蔫头蔫脑的。

sentences.text: But as you say, maybe it ain’t quite fair on the animals.
sentences.zh: 不过照你说的，这么干对动物也许有点不公道。

sentences.text: But they’ll get sick anyway, because the old women always give ’em too much to eat.
sentences.zh: 可它们反正也会病，因为老太太们总给它们吃太多。

sentences.text: And look, all the farmers round about who had lame horses and weak lambs—they’d come.
sentences.zh: 再说，你看，附近所有养着瘸马、弱羊羔的农场主——他们都会来找你。

sentences.text: Be an animal-doctor.”
sentences.zh: 就当个动物医生吧。」

hints.zh: 蔫头蔫脑的、没精神的；-like 表示「像……的样子」。
hints.en: Droopy-like: looking limp and low; -like means “in the manner of”.

hints.zh: 口语里的 isn’t／is not，很土的说话方式。
hints.en: Ain’t is a rough spoken form of isn’t here.

paragraphs.text: When the Cat’s-meat-Man had gone the parrot flew off the window on to the Doctor’s table and said,

sentences.text: When the Cat’s-meat-Man had gone the parrot flew off the window on to the Doctor’s table and said,
sentences.zh: 卖猫食的人走了以后，鹦鹉从窗口飞到医生的桌子上，说：

paragraphs.text: “That man’s got sense. That’s what you ought to do. Be an animal-doctor. Give the silly people up—if they haven’t brains enough to see you’re the best doctor in the world. Take care of animals instead—they’ll soon find it out. Be an animal-doctor.”

sentences.text: “That man’s got sense.
sentences.zh: 「那个人有脑子。

sentences.text: That’s what you ought to do.
sentences.zh: 你就该这么干。

sentences.text: Be an animal-doctor.
sentences.zh: 当个动物医生吧。

sentences.text: Give the silly people up—if they haven’t brains enough to see you’re the best doctor in the world.
sentences.zh: 别管那些蠢人了——他们连你是世上最好的医生都看不出来。

sentences.text: Take care of animals instead—they’ll soon find it out.
sentences.zh: 你不如去照顾动物——它们很快就会明白你的本事。

sentences.text: Be an animal-doctor.”
sentences.zh: 当个动物医生吧。」

hints.zh: 有头脑、明白事理。
hints.en: Has got sense: is sensible.

hints.zh: 发现、弄明白（这件事）；find out 是「查明」。
hints.en: Find it out: discover it for themselves.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, there are plenty of animal-doctors,” said John Dolittle, putting the flower-pots outside on the window-sill to get the rain.

sentences.text: “Oh, there are plenty of animal-doctors,” said John Dolittle, putting the flower-pots outside on the window-sill to get the rain.
sentences.zh: 「哦，动物医生已经够多了，」约翰·杜立德说着，把花盆搬到窗台外面去淋雨。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，医生的全名。
hints.en: John Dolittle, the Doctor’s full name.

paragraphs.text: “Yes, there are plenty,” said Polynesia. “But none of them are any good at all. Now listen, Doctor, and I’ll tell you something. Did you know that animals can talk?”

sentences.text: “Yes, there are plenty,” said Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「是够多的，」波利尼西亚说。

sentences.text: “But none of them are any good at all.
sentences.zh: 「可他们一个顶用的也没有。

sentences.text: Now listen, Doctor, and I’ll tell you something.
sentences.zh: 听我说，医生，我有件事告诉你。

sentences.text: Did you know that animals can talk?”
sentences.zh: 你知道动物会说话吗？」

paragraphs.text: “I knew that parrots can talk,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “I knew that parrots can talk,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我知道鹦鹉会说话，」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “Oh, we parrots can talk in two languages—people’s language and bird-language,” said Polynesia proudly. “If I say, ‘Polly wants a cracker,’ you understand me. But hear this: Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee?”

sentences.text: “Oh, we parrots can talk in two languages—people’s language and bird-language,” said Polynesia proudly.
sentences.zh: 「哦，我们鹦鹉会说两种话——人话和鸟语，」波利尼西亚得意地说。

sentences.text: “If I say, ‘Polly wants a cracker,’ you understand me.
sentences.zh: 「我要是说『波莉想要一块饼干』，你就听得懂。

sentences.text: But hear this: Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee?”
sentences.zh: 可你听听这个：卡—卡 奥伊—伊，菲—菲？」

hints.zh: 鸟语，鸟之间用的语言；后面马说的是 horse-language。
hints.en: Bird-language: the language birds use among themselves.

hints.zh: 一种薄脆饼干；「波莉想要一块饼干」是人教鹦鹉说的老句子。
hints.en: A thin dry biscuit; “Polly wants a cracker” is the classic phrase taught to parrots.

introduction.zh: 卖猫食的人走了，鹦鹉波利尼西亚从窗口飞到桌上，替医生抱不平：那些人既然不识货，不如不要再给他们看病。医生却叹口气说，兽医本来就够多了。鹦鹉歪着头，只问了他一句话。
introduction.en: The Cat’s-meat-Man has gone, and Polynesia flies from the window to the Doctor’s table. She has sharp words about people and about what he should do with them. The Doctor only sighs: there are plenty of animal-doctors already. Then the parrot asks him one question.

quiz.question: Why does Polynesia tell the Doctor to give up his people’s patients?
options: Because they cannot see that he is the best doctor in the world.
Because they are too poor to pay him.
Because they keep animals at home.

feedback.zh: 她说那些蠢人「连你是世上最好的医生都看不出来」，那就不值得再管他们。
feedback.en: She says they have not got brains enough to see that he is the best doctor in the world.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor answer to her advice?
options: He has never thought about it before.
He would rather go on treating people.
There are plenty of animal-doctors already.

feedback.zh: 他一边把花盆搬到窗外淋雨，一边说「动物医生已经够多了」。
feedback.en: He says there are plenty of animal-doctors already as he puts the flower-pots out in the rain.

grammar.excerpt: Give the silly people up—if they haven’t brains enough to see you’re the best doctor in the world.

focus.zh: if 从句放在祈使句后补充条件：他们要是看不出你是最好的医生，就不必管他们；从句用现在时 haven’t。
focus.en: The if-clause comes after the imperative and gives the condition; it uses the present tense, not will.

paragraphs.text: “Good Gracious!” cried the Doctor. “What does that mean?”

sentences.text: “Good Gracious!” cried the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「老天爷！」医生叫了起来。

sentences.text: “What does that mean?”
sentences.zh: 「那是什么意思？」

hints.zh: 感叹语，「老天爷」「天哪」，表示吃惊。
hints.en: Good Gracious!: an old exclamation of surprise.

paragraphs.text: “That means, ‘Is the porridge hot yet?’—in bird-language.”

sentences.text: “That means, ‘Is the porridge hot yet?’—in bird-language.”
sentences.zh: 「那是说：『粥热了吗？』——用鸟语说的。」

hints.zh: 燕麦粥，英国人常吃的热早餐。
hints.en: Porridge: hot oatmeal, a common British breakfast.

paragraphs.text: “My! You don’t say so!” said the Doctor. “You never talked that way to me before.”

sentences.text: “My!
sentences.zh: 「哎呀！

sentences.text: You don’t say so!” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 真有这种事！」医生说。

sentences.text: “You never talked that way to me before.”
sentences.zh: 「你以前从来没这么跟我说过话。」

hints.zh: 「真有这种事」，表示惊讶，不是叫对方别说。
hints.en: You don’t say so! means “Really!” — surprise, not an order to be silent.

paragraphs.text: “What would have been the good?” said Polynesia, dusting some cracker-crumbs off her left wing. “You wouldn’t have understood me if I had.”

sentences.text: “What would have been the good?” said Polynesia, dusting some cracker-crumbs off her left wing.
sentences.zh: 「那有什么用呢？」波利尼西亚说，一边掸掉左翅膀上的饼干渣。

sentences.text: “You wouldn’t have understood me if I had.”
sentences.zh: 「就算我说了，你也听不懂。」

paragraphs.text: “Tell me some more,” said the Doctor, all excited; and he rushed over to the dresser-drawer and came back with the butcher’s book and a pencil. “Now don’t go too fast—and I’ll write it down. This is interesting—very interesting—something quite new. Give me the Birds’ A.B.C. first—slowly now.”

sentences.text: “Tell me some more,” said the Doctor, all excited; and he rushed over to the dresser-drawer and came back with the butcher’s book and a pencil.
sentences.zh: 「再给我说一些，」医生兴奋极了，冲到碗柜抽屉那儿，拿了一本屠夫的账本和一支铅笔回来。

sentences.text: “Now don’t go too fast—and I’ll write it down.
sentences.zh: 「别说得太快——我记下来。

sentences.text: This is interesting—very interesting—something quite new.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思——太有意思了——是全新的东西。

sentences.text: Give me the Birds’ A.B.C. first—slowly now.”
sentences.zh: 先给我讲鸟语的字母表——慢慢来。」

hints.zh: 屠夫记订单用的本子；医生随手拿它当纸写。
hints.en: The butcher’s order book, used here as rough paper.

hints.zh: 鸟语的字母表，指鸟语最基本的音。
hints.en: The Birds’ A.B.C.: the basic sounds of bird-language, like an alphabet.

paragraphs.text: So that was the way the Doctor came to know that animals had a language of their own and could talk to one another. And all that afternoon, while it was raining, Polynesia sat on the kitchen table giving him bird words to put down in the book.

sentences.text: So that was the way the Doctor came to know that animals had a language of their own and could talk to one another.
sentences.zh: 就这样，医生知道了动物有它们自己的语言，能互相说话。

sentences.text: And all that afternoon, while it was raining, Polynesia sat on the kitchen table giving him bird words to put down in the book.
sentences.zh: 那天下午一直下着雨，波利尼西亚就坐在厨房桌上，把一个个鸟语的词说给他记在本子上。

hints.zh: 互相、彼此。
hints.en: One another: each other.

paragraphs.text: At tea-time, when the dog, Jip, came in, the parrot said to the Doctor, “See, he’s talking to you.”

sentences.text: At tea-time, when the dog, Jip, came in, the parrot said to the Doctor, “See, he’s talking to you.”
sentences.zh: 喝茶的时候，狗吉普走进来，鹦鹉对医生说：「你看，他在跟你说话呢。」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

paragraphs.text: “Looks to me as though he were scratching his ear,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Looks to me as though he were scratching his ear,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我看他像是在挠耳朵，」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “But animals don’t always speak with their mouths,” said the parrot in a high voice, raising her eyebrows. “They talk with their ears, with their feet, with their tails—with everything. Sometimes they don’t want to make a noise. Do you see now the way he’s twitching up one side of his nose?”

sentences.text: “But animals don’t always speak with their mouths,” said the parrot in a high voice, raising her eyebrows.
sentences.zh: 「可动物并不总是用嘴说话，」鹦鹉提高声音说，还扬起了眉毛。

sentences.text: “They talk with their ears, with their feet, with their tails—with everything.
sentences.zh: 「它们用耳朵说话，用脚说话，用尾巴说话——用全身说话。

sentences.text: Sometimes they don’t want to make a noise.
sentences.zh: 有时候它们不想出声。

sentences.text: Do you see now the way he’s twitching up one side of his nose?”
sentences.zh: 你现在看见没有，他一边鼻子在抽动？」

introduction.zh: 一句鸟语，杜立德医生听得目瞪口呆，急忙翻出本子和铅笔，要波利尼西亚把鸟语从头教给他——从字母表开始。到了喝茶的时候，鹦鹉却让他先看看那只刚走进来的狗。
introduction.en: One sentence of bird-language leaves the Doctor speechless. He runs for a notebook and a pencil and begs Polynesia to teach him everything, starting with the Birds’ A.B.C. By tea-time she has something else for him: a dog has just walked in, and it is talking.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor do when he first hears bird-language?
options: He asks her to say it again in people’s language.
He fetches a book and a pencil and asks her to teach him slowly.
He runs out into the rain to tell the neighbours.

feedback.zh: 他兴奋地冲去拿本子和铅笔，还要波利尼西亚先教他鸟语的字母表，慢慢说。
feedback.en: He rushes off for the butcher’s book and a pencil, and asks for the Birds’ A.B.C., slowly.

quiz.question: According to Polynesia, how do animals talk?
options: With their ears, feet and tails — with everything.
Only with their mouths, like people.
Only when they are alone together.

feedback.zh: 她说动物用耳朵、脚、尾巴说话——用全身；有时它们只是不想出声。
feedback.en: She says they talk with their ears, feet and tails — with everything — and sometimes keep quiet.

grammar.excerpt: So that was the way the Doctor came to know that animals had a language of their own

focus.zh: know 后面接 that 从句说明知道的内容；that 只起连接作用，从句里主语 animals、谓语 had 都在。
focus.en: Know is followed by a that-clause telling us what he knew; that only joins the two clauses.

paragraphs.text: “What’s that mean?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “What’s that mean?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「那是什么意思？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “That means, ‘Can’t you see that it has stopped raining?’” Polynesia answered. “He is asking you a question. Dogs nearly always use their noses for asking questions.”

sentences.text: “That means, ‘Can’t you see that it has stopped raining?’” Polynesia answered.
sentences.zh: 「那是说：『你看不见雨已经停了吗？』」波利尼西亚回答。

sentences.text: “He is asking you a question.
sentences.zh: 「他是在问你一个问题。

sentences.text: Dogs nearly always use their noses for asking questions.”
sentences.zh: 狗想问问题的时候，几乎总是用鼻子。」

paragraphs.text: After a while, with the parrot’s help, the Doctor got to learn the language of the animals so well that he could talk to them himself and understand everything they said. Then he gave up being a people’s doctor altogether.

sentences.text: After a while, with the parrot’s help, the Doctor got to learn the language of the animals so well that he could talk to them himself and understand everything they said.
sentences.zh: 过了一阵，在鹦鹉的帮助下，医生把动物的语言学得非常好，自己能跟它们交谈，它们说什么他都听得懂。

sentences.text: Then he gave up being a people’s doctor altogether.
sentences.zh: 于是他干脆不当给人看病的医生了。

hints.zh: get to do 表示「渐渐做到、终于做到」；got to learn 就是「学会了」。
hints.en: Got to learn: gradually came to learn.

hints.zh: 完全地、彻底地；gave up … altogether 就是「彻底不干了」。
hints.en: Altogether: completely.

paragraphs.text: As soon as the Cat’s-meat-Man had told every one that John Dolittle was going to become an animal-doctor, old ladies began to bring him their pet pugs and poodles who had eaten too much cake; and farmers came many miles to show him sick cows and sheep.

sentences.text: As soon as the Cat’s-meat-Man had told every one that John Dolittle was going to become an animal-doctor, old ladies began to bring him their pet pugs and poodles who had eaten too much cake; and farmers came many miles to show him sick cows and sheep.
sentences.zh: 卖猫食的人一到处说约翰·杜立德要改行当动物医生，老太太们就开始把吃多了蛋糕的哈巴狗和卷毛狗抱来给他看；农场主也跑上好多英里，把病牛病羊带来给他瞧。

hints.zh: 哈巴狗和卷毛狗，两种常见的宠物狗。
hints.en: Pugs and poodles: two kinds of small pet dogs.

paragraphs.text: One day a plow-horse was brought to him; and the poor thing was terribly glad to find a man who could talk in horse-language.

sentences.text: One day a plow-horse was brought to him; and the poor thing was terribly glad to find a man who could talk in horse-language.
sentences.zh: 有一天，有人给他牵来一匹耕马；这可怜的家伙发现有人会说马话，高兴极了。

hints.zh: 耕马，拉犁干农活的马。
hints.en: A plow-horse: a horse used for pulling a plow.

paragraphs.text: “You know, Doctor,” said the horse, “that vet over the hill knows nothing at all. He has been treating me six weeks now—for spavins. What I need is spectacles. I am going blind in one eye. There’s no reason why horses shouldn’t wear glasses, the same as people. But that stupid man over the hill never even looked at my eyes. He kept on giving me big pills. I tried to tell him; but he couldn’t understand a word of horse-language. What I need is spectacles.”

sentences.text: “You know, Doctor,” said the horse, “that vet over the hill knows nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 「你知道，医生，」马说，「山那边那个兽医什么也不懂。

sentences.text: He has been treating me six weeks now—for spavins.
sentences.zh: 他给我治了六个星期——治的是飞节肿。

sentences.text: What I need is spectacles.
sentences.zh: 我需要的是一副眼镜。

sentences.text: I am going blind in one eye.
sentences.zh: 我有一只眼睛快瞎了。

sentences.text: There’s no reason why horses shouldn’t wear glasses, the same as people.
sentences.zh: 马没理由不能像人一样戴眼镜。

sentences.text: But that stupid man over the hill never even looked at my eyes.
sentences.zh: 可山那边那个蠢货，连我的眼睛都没瞧过一眼。

sentences.text: He kept on giving me big pills.
sentences.zh: 他老给我吃大药丸。

sentences.text: I tried to tell him; but he couldn’t understand a word of horse-language.
sentences.zh: 我想告诉他；可他对马话一个字也听不懂。

sentences.text: What I need is spectacles.”
sentences.zh: 我需要的是一副眼镜。」

hints.zh: 山那边的兽医；over the hill 就是「山那头」。
hints.en: The vet over the hill: the animal doctor on the other side of the hill.

hints.zh: 飞节肿，马腿关节的一种肿胀病。
hints.en: Spavins: a swelling of a horse’s leg joint.

hints.zh: 眼镜，比 glasses 老式的说法。
hints.en: Spectacles: an old-fashioned word for glasses.

introduction.zh: 学会动物的语言以后，杜立德医生干脆不再给人看病；上门来的换成了哈巴狗、病牛和病羊。一天，有人牵来一匹耕马，它有一肚子委屈：山那边的兽医治了它六个星期，药越吃越多，眼睛却越来越坏。
introduction.en: The Doctor gives up his people’s practice. Pugs, poodles, cows and sheep now come to his door. Then a plow-horse is led in, glad to find someone who speaks horse-language. The vet over the hill has treated it for six weeks, but what it wants is not medicine.

quiz.question: What is wrong with the plow-horse?
options: It has eaten too much cake.
Its legs are lame from pulling the plow.
It is going blind in one eye and wants glasses.

feedback.zh: 马说「我有一只眼睛快瞎了」，它要的不是药，而是一副眼镜。
feedback.en: The horse says it is going blind in one eye; what it needs is spectacles.

quiz.question: What did the vet over the hill do for the horse?
options: He told the farmer the horse was too old to work.
He treated it six weeks for spavins and kept giving it big pills.
He looked at its eyes and sent it to a spectacle-maker.

feedback.zh: 兽医给它治了六个星期飞节肿，一直给它大药丸，连眼睛都没看过。
feedback.en: He treated it for six weeks for spavins and kept giving big pills, but never looked at its eyes.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as the Cat’s-meat-Man had told every one that John Dolittle was going to become an animal-doctor

focus.zh: as soon as 引出先发生的事：卖猫食的人一放出话，老太太们就上门；主句动作紧随其后。
focus.en: As soon as marks the first event; the action in the main clause follows at once.

paragraphs.text: “Of course—of course,” said the Doctor. “I’ll get you some at once.”

sentences.text: “Of course—of course,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「当然——当然，」医生说。

sentences.text: “I’ll get you some at once.”
sentences.zh: 「我马上给你弄一副。」

paragraphs.text: “I would like a pair like yours,” said the horse—“only green. They’ll keep the sun out of my eyes while I’m plowing the Fifty-Acre Field.”

sentences.text: “I would like a pair like yours,” said the horse—“only green.
sentences.zh: 「我想要一副跟你一样的，」马说，「不过要绿的。

sentences.text: They’ll keep the sun out of my eyes while I’m plowing the Fifty-Acre Field.”
sentences.zh: 我在五十英亩地里耕地的时候，它们能替我挡太阳。」

hints.zh: 五十英亩地，农场里一块田的名字。
hints.en: The Fifty-Acre Field: the name of a field on the farm.

paragraphs.text: “Certainly,” said the Doctor. “Green ones you shall have.”

sentences.text: “Certainly,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「当然可以，」医生说。

sentences.text: “Green ones you shall have.”
sentences.zh: 「一定给你绿的。」

paragraphs.text: “You know, the trouble is, Sir,” said the plow-horse as the Doctor opened the front door to let him out—“the trouble is that anybody thinks he can doctor animals—just because the animals don’t complain. As a matter of fact it takes a much cleverer man to be a really good animal-doctor than it does to be a good people’s doctor. My farmer’s boy thinks he knows all about horses. I wish you could see him—his face is so fat he looks as though he had no eyes—and he has got as much brain as a potato-bug. He tried to put a mustard-plaster on me last week.”

sentences.text: “You know, the trouble is, Sir,” said the plow-horse as the Doctor opened the front door to let him out—“the trouble is that anybody thinks he can doctor animals—just because the animals don’t complain.
sentences.zh: 「你知道，麻烦就在这儿，先生，」医生打开前门送耕马出去时，耕马说，「麻烦就在于，谁都以为自己能给动物治病——就因为动物不会抱怨。

sentences.text: As a matter of fact it takes a much cleverer man to be a really good animal-doctor than it does to be a good people’s doctor.
sentences.zh: 其实，要做一个真正高明的动物医生，得比做一个高明的给人看病的医生聪明得多。

sentences.text: My farmer’s boy thinks he knows all about horses.
sentences.zh: 我那个农场主家的孩子自以为对马无所不知。

sentences.text: I wish you could see him—his face is so fat he looks as though he had no eyes—and he has got as much brain as a potato-bug.
sentences.zh: 真希望你见见他——他的脸胖得好像没长眼睛——脑子跟马铃薯甲虫差不多。

sentences.text: He tried to put a mustard-plaster on me last week.”
sentences.zh: 上星期他还想给我贴芥末膏。」

hints.zh: 事实上、其实；用来补充或纠正前面的话。
hints.en: As a matter of fact: in fact, used to add or correct something.

hints.zh: 马铃薯甲虫，一种小害虫；说他「脑子跟它一样多」就是骂人笨。
hints.en: A potato-bug: a small beetle; “as much brain as a potato-bug” means very stupid.

hints.zh: 芥末膏，旧时敷在皮肤上发热治病的膏药。
hints.en: A mustard-plaster: an old remedy, mustard paste spread on the skin to make it hot.

paragraphs.text: “Where did he put it?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Where did he put it?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「他贴哪儿了？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “Oh, he didn’t put it anywhere—on me,” said the horse. “He only tried to. I kicked him into the duck-pond.”

sentences.text: “Oh, he didn’t put it anywhere—on me,” said the horse.
sentences.zh: 「哦，他哪儿也没贴成——没贴到我身上，」马说。

sentences.text: “He only tried to.
sentences.zh: 「他只是想贴。

sentences.text: I kicked him into the duck-pond.”
sentences.zh: 我一脚把他踢进了鸭池。」

hints.zh: 鸭池，农场上给鸭子游水的小池塘。
hints.en: The duck-pond: the small pond where the ducks swim.

paragraphs.text: “Well, well!” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Well, well!” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「哎呀，哎呀！」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “I’m a pretty quiet creature as a rule,” said the horse—“very patient with people—don’t make much fuss. But it was bad enough to have that vet giving me the wrong medicine. And when that red-faced booby started to monkey with me, I just couldn’t bear it any more.”

sentences.text: “I’m a pretty quiet creature as a rule,” said the horse—“very patient with people—don’t make much fuss.
sentences.zh: 「我一向是个挺安静的动物，」马说，「对人很耐心——不怎么闹。

sentences.text: But it was bad enough to have that vet giving me the wrong medicine.
sentences.zh: 可那个兽医给我吃错药，已经够糟了。

sentences.text: And when that red-faced booby started to monkey with me, I just couldn’t bear it any more.”
sentences.zh: 等那个红脸笨蛋开始摆弄我，我就再也受不了了。」

hints.zh: 大惊小怪、吵闹；don’t make much fuss 就是「不怎么闹」。
hints.en: Fuss: needless noise and complaint.

hints.zh: 笨蛋、傻瓜，骂人的话。
hints.en: Booby: a stupid person — an insult.

hints.zh: 乱动、瞎摆弄别人的东西。
hints.en: Monkey with: to fiddle with something carelessly.

introduction.zh: 马要一副眼镜，还指定要绿的，好在五十英亩地里耕地时挡太阳。到了门口，它又停下来，说还有件事不吐不快：谁都觉得能给动物治病，只因为动物不会抱怨。上星期就有个人试过。
introduction.en: The horse wants spectacles — green ones — to keep the sun out of his eyes while he ploughs the Fifty-Acre Field. At the door he stops with one more thing on his mind: anyone thinks he can doctor animals, just because animals do not complain. Someone tried only last week.

quiz.question: What kind of glasses does the horse ask for?
options: Green ones, like the Doctor’s.
Small round black ones.
Gold ones for Sundays.

feedback.zh: 它说要一副跟医生一样的，只不过要绿的，好在田里挡太阳。
feedback.en: It asks for a pair like the Doctor’s — only green, to keep the sun out of its eyes.

quiz.question: What did the farmer’s boy try to do to the horse?
options: Give it the vet’s big pills.
Sell it to the vet over the hill.
Put a mustard-plaster on it.

feedback.zh: 马说上星期那孩子还想给它贴芥末膏，它一脚把他踢进了鸭池。
feedback.en: The horse says the boy tried to put a mustard-plaster on it, so it kicked him into the duck-pond.

grammar.excerpt: it takes a much cleverer man to be a really good animal-doctor than it does to be a good people’s doctor.

focus.zh: much 放在比较级 cleverer 前加强语气；than 后面的 it does 代替 it takes，避免重复。
focus.en: Much strengthens the comparative cleverer; than it does stands in for than it takes.

paragraphs.text: “Did you hurt the boy much?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Did you hurt the boy much?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「你把那孩子伤得重吗？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “Oh, no,” said the horse. “I kicked him in the right place. The vet’s looking after him now. When will my glasses be ready?”

sentences.text: “Oh, no,” said the horse.
sentences.zh: 「哦，不重，」马说。

sentences.text: “I kicked him in the right place.
sentences.zh: 「我踢的地方正合适。

sentences.text: The vet’s looking after him now.
sentences.zh: 现在兽医正在照看他。

sentences.text: When will my glasses be ready?”
sentences.zh: 我的眼镜什么时候能好？」

hints.zh: 正合适的地方；马是说它踢在该踢的地方。
hints.en: The right place: the spot that deserved the kick.

paragraphs.text: “I’ll have them for you next week,” said the Doctor. “Come in again Tuesday—Good morning!”

sentences.text: “I’ll have them for you next week,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「下星期我就给你弄好，」医生说。

sentences.text: “Come in again Tuesday—Good morning!”
sentences.zh: 「星期二再来一趟——早上好！」

paragraphs.text: Then John Dolittle got a fine, big pair of green spectacles; and the plow-horse stopped going blind in one eye and could see as well as ever.

sentences.text: Then John Dolittle got a fine, big pair of green spectacles; and the plow-horse stopped going blind in one eye and could see as well as ever.
sentences.zh: 后来约翰·杜立德弄到一副又大又好的绿眼镜；耕马的一只眼不再瞎下去，视力跟从前一样好。

paragraphs.text: And soon it became a common sight to see farm-animals wearing glasses in the country round Puddleby; and a blind horse was a thing unknown.

sentences.text: And soon it became a common sight to see farm-animals wearing glasses in the country round Puddleby; and a blind horse was a thing unknown.
sentences.zh: 不久，帕德尔比一带的乡下就常能见到戴眼镜的农家牲口；瞎马成了闻所未闻的事。

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡小镇，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor’s home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

hints.zh: 闻所未闻的事，直译是「不为人知的东西」。
hints.en: A thing unknown: something nobody had ever heard of.

paragraphs.text: And so it was with all the other animals that were brought to him. As soon as they found that he could talk their language, they told him where the pain was and how they felt, and of course it was easy for him to cure them.

sentences.text: And so it was with all the other animals that were brought to him.
sentences.zh: 别的动物被带来找他看病，情形也都是这样。

sentences.text: As soon as they found that he could talk their language, they told him where the pain was and how they felt, and of course it was easy for him to cure them.
sentences.zh: 它们一发现他会说它们的语言，就告诉他哪儿疼、自己感觉怎样，他治起来自然就容易了。

hints.zh: 治好、治愈；不是「照顾」。
hints.en: Cure: to make a sick animal well again, not just to look after it.

paragraphs.text: Now all these animals went back and told their brothers and friends that there was a doctor in the little house with the big garden who really was a doctor. And whenever any creatures got sick—not only horses and cows and dogs—but all the little things of the fields, like harvest-mice and water-voles, badgers and bats, they came at once to his house on the edge of the town, so that his big garden was nearly always crowded with animals trying to get in to see him.

sentences.text: Now all these animals went back and told their brothers and friends that there was a doctor in the little house with the big garden who really was a doctor.
sentences.zh: 这些动物回去以后，都跟自己的兄弟姐妹和朋友说：那座大花园小房子里有一位医生，是真正的医生。

sentences.text: And whenever any creatures got sick—not only horses and cows and dogs—but all the little things of the fields, like harvest-mice and water-voles, badgers and bats, they came at once to his house on the edge of the town, so that his big garden was nearly always crowded with animals trying to get in to see him.
sentences.zh: 后来，只要有动物生病——不只是马、牛、狗，还有田野里所有的小东西，像禾鼠、水田鼠、獾和蝙蝠——它们马上就到他镇边的家来，于是他的大花园里几乎总挤满了想进去看病的动物。

hints.target: the little things of the fields
hints.zh: 田野里的小生灵，指各种小动物。
hints.en: The little things of the fields: all the small creatures living out in the fields.

hints.zh: 禾鼠，住在庄稼地里的小鼠。
hints.en: Harvest-mice: small mice that live in the corn.

hints.zh: 水田鼠，住在水边的小型鼠类。
hints.en: Water-voles: small rat-like animals that live by the water.

introduction.zh: 耕马踢人的事，医生只问了一句「伤得重吗」。绿眼镜做好以后，帕德尔比一带的牲口纷纷戴上了眼镜。消息越传越远，医生家的大花园渐渐挤满了从各处赶来的动物。
introduction.en: The plow-horse gets its green spectacles, and soon farm animals all round Puddleby are wearing glasses too. The news travels from stable to field and from field to forest. The Doctor’s big garden begins to fill with animals that have walked a long way. What brings them all there?

quiz.question: What does the Doctor ask about the farmer’s boy?
options: Whether the boy would come for treatment.
Whether the horse hurt him much.
Whether the boy had said sorry.

feedback.zh: 他问「你把那孩子伤得重吗」，马说踢的地方正合适，兽医正在照看他。
feedback.en: He asks, “Did you hurt the boy much?” The horse says it kicked him in the right place.

quiz.question: What happens soon after the horse gets its glasses?
options: Farm animals round Puddleby start wearing glasses.
The horse goes back to the vet over the hill.
The Doctor stops treating animals.

feedback.zh: 不久帕德尔比一带常能见到戴眼镜的农家牲口，瞎马成了闻所未闻的事。
feedback.en: Soon farm animals round Puddleby are seen wearing glasses, and a blind horse is unknown.

grammar.excerpt: they told him where the pain was and how they felt

focus.zh: tell + 人 + 疑问词从句：where the pain was 和 how they felt 都用陈述语序，不用疑问语序。
focus.en: Tell + person + wh-clause: both clauses keep statement order, not question order.

paragraphs.text: There were so many that came that he had to have special doors made for the different kinds. He wrote “HORSES” over the front door, “COWS” over the side door, and “SHEEP” on the kitchen door. Each kind of animal had a separate door—even the mice had a tiny tunnel made for them into the cellar, where they waited patiently in rows for the Doctor to come round to them.

sentences.text: There were so many that came that he had to have special doors made for the different kinds.
sentences.zh: 来的动物太多了，他只好请人给不同的动物做专门的门。

sentences.text: He wrote “HORSES” over the front door, “COWS” over the side door, and “SHEEP” on the kitchen door.
sentences.zh: 他在前门上方写了「马」，在侧门上方写了「牛」，在厨房门上写了「羊」。

sentences.text: Each kind of animal had a separate door—even the mice had a tiny tunnel made for them into the cellar, where they waited patiently in rows for the Doctor to come round to them.
sentences.zh: 每种动物都有各自的门——连老鼠也有了一条通到地窖的小地道，它们在那儿排着队耐心等医生过来看。

paragraphs.text: And so, in a few years’ time, every living thing for miles and miles got to know about John Dolittle, M.D. And the birds who flew to other countries in the winter told the animals in foreign lands of the wonderful doctor of Puddleby-on-the-Marsh, who could understand their talk and help them in their troubles. In this way he became famous among the animals—all over the world—better known even than he had been among the folks of the West Country. And he was happy and liked his life very much.

sentences.text: And so, in a few years’ time, every living thing for miles and miles got to know about John Dolittle, M.D.
sentences.zh: 就这样，没过几年，方圆好多英里内的每一种活物都知道了约翰·杜立德医学博士。

sentences.text: And the birds who flew to other countries in the winter told the animals in foreign lands of the wonderful doctor of Puddleby-on-the-Marsh, who could understand their talk and help them in their troubles.
sentences.zh: 冬天飞到别的国家去的鸟，又向异乡的动物讲起沼泽边的帕德尔比那位了不起的医生：他听得懂它们的话，能帮它们解除烦恼。

sentences.text: In this way he became famous among the animals—all over the world—better known even than he had been among the folks of the West Country.
sentences.zh: 就这样，他在动物中间出了名——全世界都知道他——甚至比他在英格兰西南部人中间还有名。

sentences.text: And he was happy and liked his life very much.
sentences.zh: 他很快乐，非常喜欢自己的生活。

hints.zh: 医学博士（Doctor of Medicine）的缩写，跟在名字后表示医生资格。
hints.en: M.D., short for Doctor of Medicine, put after his name.

hints.zh: 沼泽边的帕德尔比，医生家乡的全名。
hints.en: Puddleby-on-the-Marsh: the full name of the town by the marsh.

hints.zh: 英格兰西南部，帕德尔比所在的乡间。
hints.en: The West Country: the south-west of England.

hints.zh: 就这样、用这种方式，承接上文说过的做法。
hints.en: In this way: by this means; it points back to what came before.

paragraphs.text: One afternoon when the Doctor was busy writing in a book, Polynesia sat in the window—as she nearly always did—looking out at the leaves blowing about in the garden. Presently she laughed aloud.

sentences.text: One afternoon when the Doctor was busy writing in a book, Polynesia sat in the window—as she nearly always did—looking out at the leaves blowing about in the garden.
sentences.zh: 一天下午，医生正忙着往一个本子里写东西，波利尼西亚照例蹲在窗台上，望着花园里被风吹得乱飞的树叶。

sentences.text: Presently she laughed aloud.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，她笑出了声。

hints.zh: 被风吹得四处打转。
hints.en: Blowing about: moving around in the wind.

hints.zh: 过了一会儿、不久；不是「现在」。
hints.en: Presently: after a short while, not “at present”.

paragraphs.text: “What is it, Polynesia?” asked the Doctor, looking up from his book.

sentences.text: “What is it, Polynesia?” asked the Doctor, looking up from his book.
sentences.zh: 「怎么了，波利尼西亚？」医生从本子上抬起头问。

paragraphs.text: “I was just thinking,” said the parrot; and she went on looking at the leaves.

sentences.text: “I was just thinking,” said the parrot; and she went on looking at the leaves.
sentences.zh: 「我只是在想事情，」鹦鹉说，继续看着树叶。

paragraphs.text: “What were you thinking?”

sentences.text: “What were you thinking?”
sentences.zh: 「你在想什么？」

introduction.zh: 来看病的动物实在太多，医生只好请人做门：前门给马，侧门给牛，厨房门给羊，连老鼠都有了自己的小地道。几年之间，他的名字传遍各地。一天下午，窗台上的波利尼西亚忽然笑出了声。
introduction.en: So many animals come that the Doctor has special doors made: one for horses, one for sheep, and a tiny tunnel for the mice. In a few years his name is known everywhere. Then one afternoon Polynesia, sitting in the window, laughs out loud and will not say why.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor have special doors made?
options: He wants to sell the house to a farmer.
The cows have broken the old doors.
So many animals come that each kind needs its own door.

feedback.zh: 来的动物太多，他只好请人给不同的动物各做一扇门，连老鼠都有小地道。
feedback.en: So many animals come that each kind gets its own door — even the mice get a tiny tunnel.

quiz.question: How does the Doctor become known all over the world?
options: Travellers read about him in the newspapers.
Birds flying to other countries tell the animals there about him.
He writes letters to doctors in foreign lands.

feedback.zh: 冬天飞到别国的鸟，把他讲给异乡的动物听，他在动物中间就出了名。
feedback.en: The birds that fly to other countries in winter tell the animals there about him.

grammar.excerpt: he had to have special doors made for the different kinds

focus.zh: had to 是「不得不」，后面的 have special doors made 是「请人做门」：have + 宾语 + 过去分词，活儿由别人干。
focus.en: Have + object + past participle means getting something done by others: he had the doors made.

paragraphs.text: “I was thinking about people,” said Polynesia. “People make me sick. They think they’re so wonderful. The world has been going on now for thousands of years, hasn’t it? And the only thing in animal-language that people have learned to understand is that when a dog wags his tail he means ‘I’m glad!’—It’s funny, isn’t it? You are the very first man to talk like us. Oh, sometimes people annoy me dreadfully—such airs they put on—talking about ‘the dumb animals.’ Dumb!—Huh! Why I knew a macaw once who could say ‘Good morning!’ in seven different ways without once opening his mouth. He could talk every language—and Greek. An old professor with a gray beard bought him. But he didn’t stay. He said the old man didn’t talk Greek right, and he couldn’t stand listening to him teach the language wrong. I often wonder what’s become of him. That bird knew more geography than people will ever know.—People, Golly! I suppose if people ever learn to fly—like any common hedge-sparrow—we shall never hear the end of it!”

sentences.text: “I was thinking about people,” said Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「我在想人的事，」波利尼西亚说。

sentences.text: “People make me sick.
sentences.zh: 「人真让我受不了。

sentences.text: They think they’re so wonderful.
sentences.zh: 他们自以为多么了不起。

sentences.text: The world has been going on now for thousands of years, hasn’t it?
sentences.zh: 这世界已经运转了几千年了，是不是？

sentences.text: And the only thing in animal-language that people have learned to understand is that when a dog wags his tail he means ‘I’m glad!’—It’s funny, isn’t it?
sentences.zh: 而动物语言里，人唯一学会看懂的一件事，就是狗摇尾巴是表示『我很高兴』！——这挺好笑，不是吗？

sentences.text: You are the very first man to talk like us.
sentences.zh: 你是头一个能像我们这样说话的人。

sentences.text: Oh, sometimes people annoy me dreadfully—such airs they put on—talking about ‘the dumb animals.’
sentences.zh: 哦，有时候人真是把我气坏了——架子摆得那么大——还说什么是『不会说话的畜生』。

sentences.text: Dumb!—Huh!
sentences.zh: 不会说话！——哼！

sentences.text: Why I knew a macaw once who could say ‘Good morning!’ in seven different ways without once opening his mouth.
sentences.zh: 我认得一只金刚鹦鹉，他能用七种不同的腔调说『早上好！』，一次都不用张嘴。

sentences.text: He could talk every language—and Greek.
sentences.zh: 他会说各种语言——还会希腊语。

sentences.text: An old professor with a gray beard bought him.
sentences.zh: 一个花白胡子的老教授把他买去了。

sentences.text: But he didn’t stay.
sentences.zh: 可他没留下。

sentences.text: He said the old man didn’t talk Greek right, and he couldn’t stand listening to him teach the language wrong.
sentences.zh: 他说那老头希腊语说得不对，他受不了听他把这门语言教错。

sentences.text: I often wonder what’s become of him.
sentences.zh: 我常常想，他后来怎么样了。

sentences.text: That bird knew more geography than people will ever know.—People, Golly!
sentences.zh: 那只鸟懂的地理，比人将来能懂的还多。——人啊，天哪！

sentences.text: I suppose if people ever learn to fly—like any common hedge-sparrow—we shall never hear the end of it!”
sentences.zh: 我猜，要是人哪天学会飞了——像随便一只篱雀那样——那我们就别想再有清静日子了！」

hints.zh: 让我恶心、受不了；这里不是「让我生病」。
hints.en: Make me sick: here it means “annoy me”, not “make me ill”.

hints.zh: 摆架子、装样子；put on airs 就是「摆谱」。
hints.en: Put on airs: behave as if you are better than other people.

hints.zh: 哑的、不会说话的；「the dumb animals」是旧时轻视动物的说法。
hints.en: Dumb: unable to speak; “the dumb animals” was a look-down-on way of speaking.

hints.zh: 金刚鹦鹉，一种长尾的大鹦鹉。
hints.en: A macaw: a large parrot with a long tail.

hints.zh: 希腊语；英语里常拿它代表「难懂的学问」。
hints.en: Greek: the language of Greece, a byword for bookish learning.

hints.zh: 篱雀，一种极常见的小褐鸟。
hints.en: A hedge-sparrow: a very common little brown bird.

hints.target: we shall never hear the end of it
hints.zh: 我们就别想再听到别的了，意思是被他们念叨个没完。
hints.en: We shall never hear the end of it: they will talk about it forever.

paragraphs.text: “You’re a wise old bird,” said the Doctor. “How old are you really? I know that parrots and elephants sometimes live to be very, very old.”

sentences.text: “You’re a wise old bird,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「你是一只有智慧的老鸟，」医生说。

sentences.text: “How old are you really?
sentences.zh: 「你到底多大了？

sentences.text: I know that parrots and elephants sometimes live to be very, very old.”
sentences.zh: 我知道鹦鹉和大象有时候能活得很老很老。」

paragraphs.text: “I can never be quite sure of my age,” said Polynesia. “It’s either a hundred and eighty-three or a hundred and eighty-two. But I know that when I first came here from Africa, King Charles was still hiding in the oak-tree—because I saw him. He looked scared to death.”

sentences.text: “I can never be quite sure of my age,” said Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「我从来拿不准自己多大岁数，」波利尼西亚说。

sentences.text: “It’s either a hundred and eighty-three or a hundred and eighty-two.
sentences.zh: 「不是一百八十三，就是一百八十二。

sentences.text: But I know that when I first came here from Africa, King Charles was still hiding in the oak-tree—because I saw him.
sentences.zh: 可我知道，我刚从非洲到这里来的时候，查理国王还躲在橡树上——因为我看见他了。

sentences.text: He looked scared to death.”
sentences.zh: 他看上去吓得要命。」

hints.zh: 查理国王，指查理二世；传说他战败后躲在橡树上，波利尼西亚借这事说自己年纪极大。
hints.en: King Charles: Charles II, who hid in an oak tree after a battle — her way of saying she is very old.

introduction.zh: 波利尼西亚坐在窗台上看落叶，越想越气：人总以为自己了不起，几千年只学会了看懂狗摇尾巴。她还说起一只会用七种腔调说「早上好」的鹦鹉。医生听着，忍不住问她到底多大年纪。
introduction.en: Polynesia has been watching the leaves and thinking about people: how pleased they are with themselves, and how little animal-language they understand. She remembers a macaw, a professor and a very old king. Then the Doctor asks her a simple question: how old is she really?

quiz.question: What is the one thing in animal-language that people understand?
options: That a dog wagging his tail means “I’m glad!”
That a horse’s ears show where it hurts.
That birds sing to warn of rain.

feedback.zh: 波利尼西亚说，人只学会看懂一件事：狗摇尾巴是表示「我很高兴」。
feedback.en: Polynesia says the only thing people understand is that a wagging tail means “I’m glad!”

quiz.question: Why did the macaw leave the old professor?
options: The professor forgot to feed him.
The professor sold him to a sailor.
The professor did not speak Greek properly.

feedback.zh: 金刚鹦鹉说那老头希腊语说得不对，受不了听他教错这门语言，就走了。
feedback.en: The macaw said the old man did not talk Greek right and could not stand hearing him teach it wrongly.

grammar.excerpt: The world has been going on now for thousands of years, hasn’t it?

focus.zh: 前句是肯定，附加问句就用否定 hasn’t；助动词 has 与前句一致，主语换成 it。
focus.en: The statement is positive, so the tag is negative: hasn’t it? Has matches the statement, and it replaces the subject.

paragraphs.text: And soon now the Doctor began to make money again; and his sister, Sarah, bought a new dress and was happy.

sentences.text: And soon now the Doctor began to make money again; and his sister, Sarah, bought a new dress and was happy.
sentences.zh: 不久，医生又开始挣钱了；他的姐姐萨拉买了一条新裙子，很高兴。

paragraphs.text: Some of the animals who came to see him were so sick that they had to stay at the Doctor’s house for a week. And when they were getting better they used to sit in chairs on the lawn.

sentences.text: Some of the animals who came to see him were so sick that they had to stay at the Doctor’s house for a week.
sentences.zh: 来看病的动物里，有些病得太重，不得不在医生家里住上一个星期。

sentences.text: And when they were getting better they used to sit in chairs on the lawn.
sentences.zh: 等它们好些了，就常常坐在草坪上的椅子里。

paragraphs.text: And often even after they got well, they did not want to go away—they liked the Doctor and his house so much. And he never had the heart to refuse them when they asked if they could stay with him. So in this way he went on getting more and more pets.

sentences.text: And often even after they got well, they did not want to go away—they liked the Doctor and his house so much.
sentences.zh: 而且常常是病好了也不想走——它们太喜欢医生和他的家了。

sentences.text: And he never had the heart to refuse them when they asked if they could stay with him.
sentences.zh: 它们问能不能留下来跟他住，他从来不忍心拒绝。

sentences.text: So in this way he went on getting more and more pets.
sentences.zh: 就这样，他的宠物越来越多。

hints.zh: 忍心（做某事）；never had the heart to refuse 就是从不肯拒绝。
hints.en: To have the heart to do something is to be able to bear doing it; he never had the heart to refuse them.

paragraphs.text: Once when he was sitting on his garden wall, smoking a pipe in the evening, an Italian organ-grinder came round with a monkey on a string. The Doctor saw at once that the monkey’s collar was too tight and that he was dirty and unhappy. So he took the monkey away from the Italian, gave the man a shilling and told him to go. The organ-grinder got awfully angry and said that he wanted to keep the monkey. But the Doctor told him that if he didn’t go away he would punch him on the nose. John Dolittle was a strong man, though he wasn’t very tall. So the Italian went away saying rude things and the monkey stayed with Doctor Dolittle and had a good home. The other animals in the house called him “Chee-Chee”—which is a common word in monkey-language, meaning “ginger.”

sentences.text: Once when he was sitting on his garden wall, smoking a pipe in the evening, an Italian organ-grinder came round with a monkey on a string.
sentences.zh: 有一次傍晚，他正坐在花园的围墙上抽烟斗，一个意大利手摇风琴师牵着一只猴子转了过来。

sentences.text: The Doctor saw at once that the monkey’s collar was too tight and that he was dirty and unhappy.
sentences.zh: 医生一眼就看出，那猴子的项圈勒得太紧，它又脏又不快活。

sentences.text: So he took the monkey away from the Italian, gave the man a shilling and told him to go.
sentences.zh: 于是他把猴子从意大利人手里要了过来，给了那人一先令，叫他走。

sentences.text: The organ-grinder got awfully angry and said that he wanted to keep the monkey.
sentences.zh: 手摇风琴师气坏了，说他要留着这只猴子。

sentences.text: But the Doctor told him that if he didn’t go away he would punch him on the nose.
sentences.zh: 可医生告诉他，要是他不走开，就一拳打在他鼻子上。

sentences.text: John Dolittle was a strong man, though he wasn’t very tall.
sentences.zh: 约翰·杜立德是个结实的人，虽然个子不高。

sentences.text: So the Italian went away saying rude things and the monkey stayed with Doctor Dolittle and had a good home.
sentences.zh: 于是那意大利人骂骂咧咧地走了，猴子留在了杜立德医生家，有了一个好归宿。

sentences.text: The other animals in the house called him “Chee-Chee”—which is a common word in monkey-language, meaning “ginger.”
sentences.zh: 家里的其他动物都叫它「奇奇」——这是猴语里一个常见的词，意思是「姜」。

hints.zh: 手摇风琴师，走街串巷拉风琴卖艺的人。
hints.en: A street musician who plays a barrel organ for money.

hints.zh: 先令，英国旧币制里的银币，一先令合十二便士，当时是笔小钱。
hints.en: A shilling: an old British silver coin worth twelve pence, a small sum of money.

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，医生的全名。
hints.en: John Dolittle, the Doctor’s full name.

hints.zh: 奇奇，本书里那只猴子；这个名字在猴语里是「姜」的意思。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey; in monkey-language the word means “ginger.”

introduction.zh: 钱又回来了，姐姐萨拉买了新裙子，脸上也有了笑。可家里的动物只多不少，病好了也不肯走。一天傍晚，一个意大利手摇风琴师牵着猴子走过花园围墙，那猴子脖子上的项圈，勒得太紧了。
introduction.en: Money comes in again, and Sarah buys a new dress. But the house only fills with more animals; the ones that get well refuse to leave. One evening an organ-grinder comes past the garden wall with a monkey on a string. Its collar is far too tight.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor take the monkey away from the Italian?
options: The collar was too tight and the monkey looked dirty and unhappy.
The Italian asked him to look after it for a week.
He wanted a monkey to live in his garden.

feedback.zh: 原文说医生一眼看出猴子的项圈勒得太紧，它又脏又不快活，才把它从意大利人手里要了过来。
feedback.en: The Doctor saw at once that the collar was too tight and the monkey was dirty and unhappy, so he took it from the Italian.

quiz.question: Where does the name “Chee-Chee” come from?
options: The Doctor found it in a book about Africa.
It is a common monkey-language word meaning “ginger.”
It was the Italian’s own name for the monkey.

feedback.zh: 其他动物叫它「奇奇」，这是猴语里的常用词，意思是「姜」。
feedback.en: The other animals called him “Chee-Chee,” a common monkey-language word meaning “ginger.”

grammar.excerpt: when he was sitting on his garden wall, smoking a pipe in the evening

focus.zh: was sitting 和 smoking 是过去进行时：那时他正坐在围墙上抽烟斗，when 从句给出这个背景时间。
focus.en: Was sitting and smoking are past continuous: he was in the middle of it when the organ-grinder came round.

paragraphs.text: And another time, when the circus came to Puddleby, the crocodile who had a bad toothache escaped at night and came into the Doctor’s garden. The Doctor talked to him in crocodile-language and took him into the house and made his tooth better. But when the crocodile saw what a nice house it was—with all the different places for the different kinds of animals—he too wanted to live with the Doctor. He asked couldn’t he sleep in the fish-pond at the bottom of the garden, if he promised not to eat the fish. When the circus-men came to take him back he got so wild and savage that he frightened them away. But to every one in the house he was always as gentle as a kitten.

sentences.text: And another time, when the circus came to Puddleby, the crocodile who had a bad toothache escaped at night and came into the Doctor’s garden.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，马戏团来到帕德尔比，那条牙疼得厉害的鳄鱼夜里逃了出来，爬进了医生的花园。

sentences.text: The Doctor talked to him in crocodile-language and took him into the house and made his tooth better.
sentences.zh: 医生用鳄鱼话跟它说话，把它带进屋，治好了它的牙。

sentences.text: But when the crocodile saw what a nice house it was—with all the different places for the different kinds of animals—he too wanted to live with the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 可鳄鱼一看这房子多好——每种动物都有自己的地方——它也想跟医生住在一起。

sentences.text: He asked couldn’t he sleep in the fish-pond at the bottom of the garden, if he promised not to eat the fish.
sentences.zh: 它问，要是它答应不吃鱼，能不能睡在花园尽头的鱼池里。

sentences.text: When the circus-men came to take him back he got so wild and savage that he frightened them away.
sentences.zh: 马戏团的人来接它回去时，它又凶又野，把他们吓跑了。

sentences.text: But to every one in the house he was always as gentle as a kitten.
sentences.zh: 可对屋里的每一个，它总是像小猫一样温顺。

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡小镇，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby: the Doctor’s home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

paragraphs.text: But now the old ladies grew afraid to send their lap-dogs to Doctor Dolittle because of the crocodile; and the farmers wouldn’t believe that he would not eat the lambs and sick calves they brought to be cured. So the Doctor went to the crocodile and told him he must go back to his circus. But he wept such big tears, and begged so hard to be allowed to stay, that the Doctor hadn’t the heart to turn him out.

sentences.text: But now the old ladies grew afraid to send their lap-dogs to Doctor Dolittle because of the crocodile; and the farmers wouldn’t believe that he would not eat the lambs and sick calves they brought to be cured.
sentences.zh: 可是现在，老太太们因为这条鳄鱼，不敢把哈巴狗送到杜立德医生这儿来了；农夫们也不肯相信他不会吃掉他们送来治病的羊羔和病牛犊。

sentences.text: So the Doctor went to the crocodile and told him he must go back to his circus.
sentences.zh: 于是医生去找鳄鱼，告诉它必须回马戏团去。

sentences.text: But he wept such big tears, and begged so hard to be allowed to stay, that the Doctor hadn’t the heart to turn him out.
sentences.zh: 可它哭出那么大的泪珠，又苦苦哀求让它留下，医生实在不忍心把它赶出去。

hints.zh: 哈巴狗、抱在膝上的小宠物狗。
hints.en: Lap-dogs: small pet dogs kept on the lap.

hints.zh: 把他赶出去、撵走。
hints.en: To turn somebody out is to drive him out of the house.

paragraphs.text: So then the Doctor’s sister came to him and said,

sentences.text: So then the Doctor’s sister came to him and said,
sentences.zh: 于是医生的姐姐走过来，对他说：

paragraphs.text: “John, you must send that creature away. Now the farmers and the old ladies are afraid to send their animals to you—just as we were beginning to be well off again. Now we shall be ruined entirely. This is the last straw. I will no longer be housekeeper for you if you don’t send away that alligator.”

sentences.text: “John, you must send that creature away.
sentences.zh: 「约翰，你必须把那个东西送走。

sentences.text: Now the farmers and the old ladies are afraid to send their animals to you—just as we were beginning to be well off again.
sentences.zh: 现在农夫和老太太们都不敢把动物送到你这儿来了——我们才刚刚要好过一点。

sentences.text: Now we shall be ruined entirely.
sentences.zh: 这下我们要彻底完蛋了。

sentences.text: This is the last straw.
sentences.zh: 这是最后一根稻草。

sentences.text: I will no longer be housekeeper for you if you don’t send away that alligator.”
sentences.zh: 你要是不把那条短吻鳄送走，我就不再给你当管家了。」

hints.zh: 最后一根稻草；忍到极限时压下来的最后一件小事。
hints.en: The last straw: the final small trouble that makes you give up.

hints.zh: 管家，替家里料理家务的人。
hints.en: A housekeeper: the person who runs the household.

introduction.zh: 马戏团来到帕德尔比，一条牙疼得厉害的鳄鱼夜里逃了出来，爬进医生的花园。医生用鳄鱼话一问，就治好了它的牙。可它很喜欢这个家，还打听花园尽头的鱼池能不能住——那些把猫狗送来的人，还敢上门吗？
introduction.en: A circus comes to Puddleby, and a crocodile with a bad toothache escapes at night into the Doctor’s garden. The Doctor speaks crocodile-language and cures the tooth. Then the crocodile asks whether it may live in the fish-pond. What will the old ladies and the farmers say?

quiz.question: What does the crocodile ask the Doctor?
options: Whether it can go back to Africa with him.
For a warm place by the kitchen fire.
Whether it can sleep in the fish-pond if it leaves the fish alone.

feedback.zh: 它请求：只要答应不吃鱼，能不能睡在花园尽头的鱼池里。
feedback.en: It asks whether it can sleep in the fish-pond at the bottom of the garden if it promises not to eat the fish.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor tell the crocodile it must go back to the circus?
options: The circus-men have paid him for the crocodile.
The crocodile has eaten the fish in the pond.
The old ladies and the farmers are afraid to send him their animals.

feedback.zh: 老太太们不敢送哈巴狗来，农夫也不信它不吃羊羔和病牛犊，医生只好让它回马戏团。
feedback.en: The old ladies were afraid to send their lap-dogs, and the farmers did not trust it with their lambs, so the Doctor told it to go back.

grammar.excerpt: he was always as gentle as a kitten

focus.zh: as gentle as a kitten 是 as + 形容词原形 + as，跟小猫一样温顺；两个 as 中间不用比较级。
focus.en: As gentle as a kitten uses as + adjective + as; no comparative goes between the two as.

paragraphs.text: “It isn’t an alligator,” said the Doctor—“it’s a crocodile.”

sentences.text: “It isn’t an alligator,” said the Doctor—“it’s a crocodile.”
sentences.zh: 「那不是短吻鳄，」医生说，「是鳄鱼。」

hints.zh: 短吻鳄（美洲鳄）；姐姐一直把这个词用错，医生在纠正她。
hints.en: An alligator: the American crocodile. Sarah uses the wrong word and the Doctor corrects her.

paragraphs.text: “I don’t care what you call it,” said his sister. “It’s a nasty thing to find under the bed. I won’t have it in the house.”

sentences.text: “I don’t care what you call it,” said his sister.
sentences.zh: 「我不管你怎么叫它，」他姐姐说。

sentences.text: “It’s a nasty thing to find under the bed.
sentences.zh: 「在床底下发现这么个东西，真恶心。

sentences.text: I won’t have it in the house.”
sentences.zh: 我不许它待在这屋里。」

hints.zh: 不许它待在这儿；这里的 have 是「容忍、容许」。
hints.en: Will not have it means will not allow it in the house.

paragraphs.text: “But he has promised me,” the Doctor answered, “that he will not bite any one. He doesn’t like the circus; and I haven’t the money to send him back to Africa where he comes from. He minds his own business and on the whole is very well behaved. Don’t be so fussy.”

sentences.text: “But he has promised me,” the Doctor answered, “that he will not bite any one.
sentences.zh: 「可它答应过我，」医生回答，「它不咬任何人。

sentences.text: He doesn’t like the circus; and I haven’t the money to send him back to Africa where he comes from.
sentences.zh: 它不喜欢马戏团；我也没有钱把它送回它来的非洲。

sentences.text: He minds his own business and on the whole is very well behaved.
sentences.zh: 它管自己的事，总的来说非常规矩。

sentences.text: Don’t be so fussy.”
sentences.zh: 别这么小题大做。」

hints.zh: 只管自己的事，不招惹别人；这里说它安分守己。
hints.en: Minds his own business: keeps to itself and troubles nobody.

paragraphs.text: “I tell you I will not have him around,” said Sarah. “He eats the linoleum. If you don’t send him away this minute I’ll—I’ll go and get married!”

sentences.text: “I tell you I will not have him around,” said Sarah.
sentences.zh: 「我跟你说，我不能让它待在这儿，」萨拉说。

sentences.text: “He eats the linoleum.
sentences.zh: 「它啃地板革。

sentences.text: If you don’t send him away this minute I’ll—I’ll go and get married!”
sentences.zh: 你要是现在不把它送走，我就——我就去结婚！」

hints.zh: 亚麻油地毡，铺在厨房地上的那层硬面材料。
hints.en: Linoleum: the hard floor covering used in kitchens.

paragraphs.text: “All right,” said the Doctor, “go and get married. It can’t be helped.” And he took down his hat and went out into the garden.

sentences.text: “All right,” said the Doctor, “go and get married.
sentences.zh: 「好吧，」医生说，「去结婚吧。

sentences.text: It can’t be helped.”
sentences.zh: 这也是没办法的事。」

sentences.text: And he took down his hat and went out into the garden.
sentences.zh: 他取下帽子，走到花园里去了。

hints.zh: 没办法的事，只能这样。
hints.en: It can’t be helped: there is nothing to be done about it.

paragraphs.text: So Sarah Dolittle packed up her things and went off; and the Doctor was left all alone with his animal family.

sentences.text: So Sarah Dolittle packed up her things and went off; and the Doctor was left all alone with his animal family.
sentences.zh: 于是萨拉·杜立德收拾好自己的东西走了；医生独自留下，陪着他的动物一家。

paragraphs.text: And very soon he was poorer than he had ever been before. With all these mouths to fill, and the house to look after, and no one to do the mending, and no money coming in to pay the butcher’s bill, things began to look very difficult. But the Doctor didn’t worry at all.

sentences.text: And very soon he was poorer than he had ever been before.
sentences.zh: 很快，他比以前任何时候都穷。

sentences.text: With all these mouths to fill, and the house to look after, and no one to do the mending, and no money coming in to pay the butcher’s bill, things began to look very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这么多张嘴要喂，房子要照看，没人缝缝补补，也没有钱付肉铺的账，日子开始显得很难。

sentences.text: But the Doctor didn’t worry at all.
sentences.zh: 可医生一点也不发愁。

hints.zh: 肉铺的账单，也就是欠肉铺的钱。
hints.en: The butcher’s bill: the money owed to the butcher for meat.

paragraphs.text: “Money is a nuisance,” he used to say. “We’d all be much better off if it had never been invented. What does money matter, so long as we are happy?”

sentences.text: “Money is a nuisance,” he used to say.
sentences.zh: 「钱是个麻烦东西，」他过去常说。

sentences.text: “We’d all be much better off if it had never been invented.
sentences.zh: 「要是钱从来没被发明出来，我们大家都会过得好得多。

sentences.text: What does money matter, so long as we are happy?”
sentences.zh: 只要快活，钱又算什么呢？」

introduction.zh: 姐姐萨拉把这条爬行动物叫作「短吻鳄」，说它啃厨房的地板，在床底下撞见它实在恶心。医生一边纠正她的用词，一边替它说情：它答应过不咬人。萨拉的条件越来越硬，还拿自己的婚事来说事。
introduction.en: Sarah calls the creature an alligator and says it eats the kitchen floor. The Doctor corrects her word and speaks up for his guest: it has promised not to bite. Sarah’s terms get harder and harder — and then she makes a strange threat.

quiz.question: What does Sarah threaten to do if the Doctor keeps the creature?
options: Tell the farmers about the crocodile.
Sell the house and the garden.
Go and get married.

feedback.zh: 萨拉说，他要是不立刻把它送走，她就「去结婚」——这是她逼医生的最后一句狠话。
feedback.en: Sarah says that if he does not send it away this minute, she will go and get married.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor say about money?
options: He says money is the only thing worth having.
He says he will borrow some from Sarah.
He says they would all be better off if money had never been invented.

feedback.zh: 他说钱是个麻烦东西，要是钱从没被发明出来，大家都会过得好得多。
feedback.en: He calls money a nuisance and says they would all be much better off if it had never been invented.

grammar.excerpt: I haven’t the money to send him back to Africa where he comes from

focus.zh: Africa where he comes from 里 where 等于 from which：它来自非洲；where 从句紧跟在表示地点的名词后。
focus.en: In Africa where he comes from, where means from which; the where-clause follows a place noun.

paragraphs.text: But soon the animals themselves began to get worried.
