And one evening when the Doctor was asleep in his chair before the kitchen-fire they began talking it over among themselves in whispers. And the owl, Too-Too, who was good at arithmetic, figured it out that there was only money enough left to last another week—if they each had one meal a day and no more.

sentences.text: But soon the animals themselves began to get worried.
sentences.zh: 可不久，动物们自己也发起愁来。

sentences.text: And one evening when the Doctor was asleep in his chair before the kitchen-fire they began talking it over among themselves in whispers.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，医生在厨房炉火前的椅子上睡着了，它们就开始小声地商量这件事。

sentences.text: And the owl, Too-Too, who was good at arithmetic, figured it out that there was only money enough left to last another week—if they each had one meal a day and no more.
sentences.zh: 猫头鹰图图擅长算术，它算出来，剩下的钱只够再维持一个星期——前提是大家每天只吃一顿，不能多。

hints.zh: 图图，那只猫头鹰，会算账。
hints.en: Too-Too, the owl, who is good with figures.

paragraphs.text: Then the parrot said, “I think we all ought to do the housework ourselves. At least we can do that much. After all, it is for our sakes that the old man finds himself so lonely and so poor.”

sentences.text: Then the parrot said, “I think we all ought to do the housework ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这时鹦鹉说：「我看我们该自己动手做家务。

sentences.text: At least we can do that much.
sentences.zh: 至少这点事我们还做得来。

sentences.text: After all, it is for our sakes that the old man finds himself so lonely and so poor.”
sentences.zh: 说到底，老人家弄得这么孤单、这么穷，都是为了我们。」

hints.zh: 为了我们，全是为了我们好。
hints.en: For our sakes: for our good, because of us.

paragraphs.text: So it was agreed that the monkey, Chee-Chee, was to do the cooking and mending; the dog was to sweep the floors; the duck was to dust and make the beds; the owl, Too-Too, was to keep the accounts, and the pig was to do the gardening. They made Polynesia, the parrot, housekeeper and laundress, because she was the oldest.

sentences.text: So it was agreed that the monkey, Chee-Chee, was to do the cooking and mending; the dog was to sweep the floors; the duck was to dust and make the beds; the owl, Too-Too, was to keep the accounts, and the pig was to do the gardening.
sentences.zh: 于是大家说定：猴子奇奇负责做饭和缝补；狗扫地；鸭子掸灰、铺床；猫头鹰图图管账；猪管菜园。

sentences.text: They made Polynesia, the parrot, housekeeper and laundress, because she was the oldest.
sentences.zh: 他们让鹦鹉波利尼西亚当管家兼洗衣妇，因为她年纪最大。

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉，现在当了管家兼洗衣妇。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor’s parrot, now housekeeper and laundress.

hints.zh: 记账、管账。
hints.en: Keep the accounts: look after the money and write it all down.

hints.zh: 洗衣妇，旧时替人家洗衣裳的女人。
hints.en: A laundress: a woman paid to wash clothes.

paragraphs.text: Of course at first they all found their new jobs very hard to do—all except Chee-Chee, who had hands, and could do things like a man. But they soon got used to it; and they used to think it great fun to watch Jip, the dog, sweeping his tail over the floor with a rag tied onto it for a broom. After a little they got to do the work so well that the Doctor said that he had never had his house kept so tidy or so clean before.

sentences.text: Of course at first they all found their new jobs very hard to do—all except Chee-Chee, who had hands, and could do things like a man.
sentences.zh: 当然，一开始大家都觉得这些新活儿很难干——只有奇奇除外，它有手，能像人一样做事。

sentences.text: But they soon got used to it; and they used to think it great fun to watch Jip, the dog, sweeping his tail over the floor with a rag tied onto it for a broom.
sentences.zh: 可它们很快就习惯了；看着狗吉普把一块抹布绑在尾巴上当作扫帚，让尾巴在地板上扫来扫去，它们总觉得好玩极了。

sentences.text: After a little they got to do the work so well that the Doctor said that he had never had his house kept so tidy or so clean before.
sentences.zh: 过了一阵，它们的活儿干得那么好，医生说他的房子从来没这么整齐、这么干净过。

hints.zh: 吉普，那只狗。
hints.en: Jip, the dog.

introduction.zh: 钱快用完了，这回是动物们先慌了。一天晚上，医生在厨房炉火前睡着了，它们凑在一起小声商量。会算账的猫头鹰图图报出一个数字，谁听了都不作声——一只猴子、一只鸭子、一头猪，撑得起这个家吗？
introduction.en: This time it is the animals who begin to worry. One evening, while the Doctor sleeps in his chair by the kitchen fire, they talk the matter over in whispers. Too-Too is good at arithmetic, and the figures are not cheerful. So who will do the housework now?

quiz.question: How much money does Too-Too work out they have left?
options: Enough for another week, with one meal a day each.
Enough for another month.
Nothing at all.

feedback.zh: 图图算出来，剩下的钱只够再撑一个星期，还得大家每天只吃一顿。
feedback.en: Too-Too works out that there is only enough money for another week, if they each have one meal a day.

quiz.question: According to the parrot, why is the old man so poor and lonely?
options: Because the circus took all his money.
Because of the animals — it is for their sakes.
Because he spends his money on himself.

feedback.zh: 鹦鹉说，老人家这么孤单、这么穷，全是为了它们这些动物。
feedback.en: The parrot says the old man is lonely and poor for their sakes.

grammar.excerpt: the monkey, Chee-Chee, was to do the cooking and mending

focus.zh: was to do 表示按商量好的安排「该由谁来做」；be 随主语和时态变，后面跟动词原形。
focus.en: Was to do shows what had been arranged: this was the job given to him. Be changes, the verb stays in the base form.

paragraphs.text: In this way things went along all right for a while; but without money they found it very hard.

sentences.text: In this way things went along all right for a while; but without money they found it very hard.
sentences.zh: 就这样，日子还算过得去了一阵；可没有钱，他们觉得很难。

paragraphs.text: Then the animals made a vegetable and flower stall outside the garden-gate and sold radishes and roses to the people that passed by along the road.

sentences.text: Then the animals made a vegetable and flower stall outside the garden-gate and sold radishes and roses to the people that passed by along the road.
sentences.zh: 后来动物们在花园门外摆了个菜摊和花摊，把萝卜和玫瑰卖给从路旁经过的人。

paragraphs.text: But still they didn’t seem to make enough money to pay all the bills—and still the Doctor wouldn’t worry. When the parrot came to him and told him that the fishmonger wouldn’t give them any more fish, he said,

sentences.text: But still they didn’t seem to make enough money to pay all the bills—and still the Doctor wouldn’t worry.
sentences.zh: 可他们好像还是挣不到足够的钱来付清所有账单——医生仍旧不着急。

sentences.text: When the parrot came to him and told him that the fishmonger wouldn’t give them any more fish, he said,
sentences.zh: 鹦鹉来告诉他，鱼贩子不肯再给他们鱼了，他说：

hints.zh: 鱼贩子，卖鱼的人。
hints.en: A fishmonger: a man who sells fish.

paragraphs.text: “Never mind. So long as the hens lay eggs and the cow gives milk we can have omelettes and junket. And there are plenty of vegetables left in the garden. The Winter is still a long way off. Don’t fuss. That was the trouble with Sarah—she would fuss. I wonder how Sarah’s getting on—an excellent woman—in some ways—Well, well!”

sentences.text: “Never mind.
sentences.zh: 「没关系。

sentences.text: So long as the hens lay eggs and the cow gives milk we can have omelettes and junket.
sentences.zh: 只要母鸡下蛋、奶牛产奶，我们就能有煎蛋卷和凝乳甜点吃。

sentences.text: And there are plenty of vegetables left in the garden.
sentences.zh: 园子里还剩好多菜。

sentences.text: The Winter is still a long way off.
sentences.zh: 冬天还远着呢。

sentences.text: Don’t fuss.
sentences.zh: 别大惊小怪。

sentences.text: That was the trouble with Sarah—she would fuss.
sentences.zh: 萨拉的毛病就在这儿——她总爱大惊小怪。

sentences.text: I wonder how Sarah’s getting on—an excellent woman—in some ways—Well, well!”
sentences.zh: 不知道萨拉现在过得怎么样——一个极好的女人——在某些方面——唉，唉！」

hints.zh: 凝乳甜点，牛奶加凝乳做成的软甜食，旧时乡下常吃。
hints.en: Junket: a soft milk pudding set with rennet, a country dish.

hints.zh: 还远着呢，离现在还有很久。
hints.en: A long way off: still far away in time.

hints.zh: 别大惊小怪、别瞎操心。
hints.en: Don’t fuss: don’t make a needless bother about it.

hints.zh: 过得怎么样、日子过得如何。
hints.en: How she is getting on: how she is managing, how life is treating her.

paragraphs.text: But the snow came earlier than usual that year; and although the old lame horse hauled in plenty of wood from the forest outside the town, so they could have a big fire in the kitchen, most of the vegetables in the garden were gone, and the rest were covered with snow; and many of the animals were really hungry.

sentences.text: But the snow came earlier than usual that year; and although the old lame horse hauled in plenty of wood from the forest outside the town, so they could have a big fire in the kitchen, most of the vegetables in the garden were gone, and the rest were covered with snow; and many of the animals were really hungry.
sentences.zh: 可那年雪来得比往年早；虽然那匹瘸腿的老马从城外的树林里拉来许多柴火，好让厨房里能生起一大堆火，园子里的菜却大半没了，剩下的都盖在雪底下；许多动物真的饿了。

hints.zh: （用车子）拉来、运来；这里指拉柴火。
hints.en: Hauled in: dragged or carted in — here, the wood.

introduction.zh: 动物们在花园门外支起一个摊子，把萝卜和玫瑰卖给过路的人。可钱还是不够付账，连鱼贩子都不肯再赊鱼了。医生照样不着急，说母鸡下蛋、奶牛产奶就够了。可那一年的冬天，地里的菜还够吗？
introduction.en: The animals sell radishes and roses at a stall by the garden gate. The bills are still not paid, and the fishmonger sends no more fish. The Doctor is not worried: the hens lay eggs and the cow gives milk. But snow may come early this year.

quiz.question: What do the animals sell at the garden gate?
options: Fish from the pond.
Roses and radishes.
Eggs and milk.

feedback.zh: 它们在花园门外摆摊，卖的是萝卜和玫瑰。
feedback.en: They set up a stall outside the garden gate and sold radishes and roses.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor say when the fishmonger refuses to give them more fish?
options: He says they must sell the cow.
He says they can have omelettes and junket instead.
He says he will go and see the fishmonger himself.

feedback.zh: 他说没关系：只要母鸡下蛋、奶牛产奶，就有煎蛋卷和凝乳甜点吃。
feedback.en: He says never mind: so long as the hens lay eggs and the cow gives milk, they can have omelettes and junket.

grammar.excerpt: although the old lame horse hauled in plenty of wood from the forest outside the town

focus.zh: although 引导让步从句「虽然老瘸马拉来很多柴」；主句仍旧说菜被雪盖住、动物挨饿。
focus.en: Although starts a concession: plenty of wood was hauled in, yet the vegetables were gone and the animals were hungry.

paragraphs.text: That Winter was a very cold one. And one night in December, when they were all sitting round the warm fire in the kitchen, and the Doctor was reading aloud to them out of books he had written himself in animal-language, the owl, Too-Too, suddenly said,

sentences.text: That Winter was a very cold one.
sentences.zh: 那个冬天非常冷。

sentences.text: And one night in December, when they were all sitting round the warm fire in the kitchen, and the Doctor was reading aloud to them out of books he had written himself in animal-language, the owl, Too-Too, suddenly said,
sentences.zh: 十二月的一个晚上，大家都围坐在厨房暖烘烘的炉火旁，医生正大声念他自己用动物语写的书给他们听，这时猫头鹰图图忽然说：

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor's owl.

paragraphs.text: “Sh! What’s that noise outside?”

sentences.text: “Sh!
What’s that noise outside?”
sentences.zh: 外面那是什么声音？」

paragraphs.text: They all listened; and presently they heard the sound of some one running. Then the door flew open and the monkey, Chee-Chee, ran in, badly out of breath.

sentences.text: They all listened; and presently they heard the sound of some one running.
sentences.zh: 大家都侧耳去听；不一会儿，他们听见有人奔跑的声音。

sentences.text: Then the door flew open and the monkey, Chee-Chee, ran in, badly out of breath.
sentences.zh: 接着门猛地被推开，猴子奇奇跑了进来，喘得上气不接下气。

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey.

paragraphs.text: “Doctor!” he cried, “I’ve just had a message from a cousin of mine in Africa. There is a terrible sickness among the monkeys out there. They are all catching it—and they are dying in hundreds. They have heard of you, and beg you to come to Africa to stop the sickness.”

sentences.text: “Doctor!” he cried, “I’ve just had a message from a cousin of mine in Africa.
sentences.zh: 「医生！」他喊道，「我刚收到非洲一位表亲捎来的消息。

sentences.text: There is a terrible sickness among the monkeys out there.
sentences.zh: 那边的猴子中间正闹一种可怕的病。

sentences.text: They are all catching it—and they are dying in hundreds.
sentences.zh: 它们一个接一个染上——成百成百地死去。

sentences.text: They have heard of you, and beg you to come to Africa to stop the sickness.”
sentences.zh: 它们听说过你，求你到非洲去，把这场病止住。」

paragraphs.text: “Who brought the message?” asked the Doctor, taking off his spectacles and laying down his book.

sentences.text: “Who brought the message?” asked the Doctor, taking off his spectacles and laying down his book.
sentences.zh: 「消息是谁带来的？」医生问，一边摘下眼镜，放下了书。

paragraphs.text: “A swallow,” said Chee-Chee. “She is outside on the rain-butt.”

sentences.text: “A swallow,” said Chee-Chee.
sentences.zh: 「一只燕子。」奇奇说。

sentences.text: “She is outside on the rain-butt.”
sentences.zh: 「她就在外面，站在接雨水的桶上。」

hints.zh: 接雨水的大桶，放在屋外接屋檐流下来的雨水。
hints.en: A big barrel outside that catches rain-water from the roof.

paragraphs.text: “Bring her in by the fire,” said the Doctor. “She must be perished with the cold. The swallows flew South six weeks ago!”

sentences.text: “Bring her in by the fire,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「把她带到火边来。」医生说。

sentences.text: “She must be perished with the cold.
sentences.zh: 「她一定冻坏了。

sentences.text: The swallows flew South six weeks ago!”
sentences.zh: 燕子六个星期前就飞到南方去了！」

hints.zh: 这里不是「死了」，是「冻得受不了」，口语里夸张的说法。
hints.en: Here it means "half frozen", not "dead": a strong everyday exaggeration.

paragraphs.text: So the swallow was brought in, all huddled and shivering; and although she was a little afraid at first, she soon got warmed up and sat on the edge of the mantelpiece and began to talk.

sentences.text: So the swallow was brought in, all huddled and shivering; and although she was a little afraid at first, she soon got warmed up and sat on the edge of the mantelpiece and began to talk.
sentences.zh: 于是燕子被带了进来，缩成一团，瑟瑟发抖；她起初还有点害怕，但很快就暖和过来，落在壁炉架的边上，开始说话了。

introduction.zh: 十二月的一个寒夜，大家围着厨房的炉火，听医生念他自己写的动物语故事。猫头鹰图图忽然竖起耳朵：外面有动静。这样冷的夜里，谁会在外面奔跑？
introduction.en: A cold December night. Everyone sits round the kitchen fire while the Doctor reads aloud from books he wrote himself in animal-language. Suddenly the owl lifts its head: there is a noise outside. Who would be running about on such a night?

quiz.question: What news does Chee-Chee bring from Africa?
options: The Doctor's cousin is coming to England.
The monkeys there have found a new king.
The monkeys there are dying of a terrible sickness.

feedback.zh: 奇奇说非洲的猴子中间正闹一种可怕的病，它们成百成百地死去，所以才来求医生去止住它。
feedback.en: Chee-Chee reports a terrible sickness among the monkeys out there: they are catching it and dying in hundreds.

quiz.question: What is the Doctor doing as he asks who brought the message?
options: Packing a bag for the journey.
Lighting the kitchen fire.
Taking off his spectacles and laying down his book.

feedback.zh: 原文写他一边摘下眼镜、放下书，一边问「消息是谁带来的」。
feedback.en: He takes off his spectacles and lays down his book as he asks the question.

grammar.excerpt: when they were all sitting round the warm fire in the kitchen, and the Doctor was reading aloud to them

focus.zh: when 从句用过去进行时 were sitting、was reading 铺开背景：大家正坐着听书，事情就在这时发生。
focus.en: The when-clause uses the past continuous (were sitting, was reading) to set the scene before something else happens.

paragraphs.text: When she had finished the Doctor said,

sentences.text: When she had finished the Doctor said,
sentences.zh: 她说完，医生说：

paragraphs.text: “I would gladly go to Africa—especially in this bitter weather. But I’m afraid we haven’t money enough to buy the tickets. Get me the money-box, Chee-Chee.”

sentences.text: “I would gladly go to Africa—especially in this bitter weather.
sentences.zh: 「我很愿意去非洲——尤其是这样的冷天。

sentences.text: But I’m afraid we haven’t money enough to buy the tickets.
sentences.zh: 可我怕我们钱不够买船票。

sentences.text: Get me the money-box, Chee-Chee.”
sentences.zh: 把存钱盒给我拿来，奇奇。」

paragraphs.text: So the monkey climbed up and got it off the top shelf of the dresser.

sentences.text: So the monkey climbed up and got it off the top shelf of the dresser.
sentences.zh: 于是猴子爬上去，把它从餐具柜最上层取了下来。

hints.zh: 厨房里的餐具柜、碗柜；不是卧室里的梳妆台。
hints.en: A kitchen cupboard for dishes, not a bedroom dressing-table.

paragraphs.text: There was nothing in it—not one single penny!

sentences.text: There was nothing in it—not one single penny!
sentences.zh: 里面什么也没有——连一个便士都没有！

paragraphs.text: “I felt sure there was twopence left,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “I felt sure there was twopence left,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我原以为里头还剩两便士呢。」医生说。

hints.zh: 两便士，英国旧币制里的铜币，是很少的一点钱。
hints.en: Twopence: two old British pennies, a very small sum.

paragraphs.text: “There was” said the owl. “But you spent it on a rattle for that badger’s baby when he was teething.”

sentences.text: “There was” said the owl.
sentences.zh: 「本来是有的。」猫头鹰说。

sentences.text: “But you spent it on a rattle for that badger’s baby when he was teething.”
sentences.zh: 「可你拿它给那只獾的娃娃买了个摇铃，那会儿他正长牙。」

hints.zh: 婴儿玩的摇铃、拨浪鼓，一摇就响，长牙的孩子常拿着啃。
hints.en: A baby's rattle: a toy that makes a noise when it is shaken.

paragraphs.text: “Did I?” said the Doctor—“dear me, dear me! What a nuisance money is, to be sure! Well, never mind. Perhaps if I go down to the seaside I shall be able to borrow a boat that will take us to Africa. I knew a seaman once who brought his baby to me with measles. Maybe he’ll lend us his boat—the baby got well.”

sentences.text: “Did I?” said the Doctor—“dear me, dear me!
sentences.zh: 「是吗？」医生说，「天哪，天哪！

sentences.text: What a nuisance money is, to be sure!
sentences.zh: 钱这东西，真是麻烦！

sentences.text: Well, never mind.
sentences.zh: 好吧，算了。

sentences.text: Perhaps if I go down to the seaside I shall be able to borrow a boat that will take us to Africa.
sentences.zh: 也许我下到海边去，能借到一条送我们去非洲的船。

sentences.text: I knew a seaman once who brought his baby to me with measles.
sentences.zh: 我认识一个水手，他有一次抱了娃娃来找我看麻疹。

sentences.text: Maybe he’ll lend us his boat—the baby got well.”
sentences.zh: 也许他肯把船借给我们——那娃娃后来好了。」

paragraphs.text: So early the next morning the Doctor went down to the sea-shore. And when he came back he told the animals it was all right—the sailor was going to lend them the boat.

sentences.text: So early the next morning the Doctor went down to the sea-shore.
sentences.zh: 于是第二天一大早，医生就下到海边去了。

sentences.text: And when he came back he told the animals it was all right—the sailor was going to lend them the boat.
sentences.zh: 他回来的时候告诉动物们事情办成了——那个水手愿意把船借给他们。

paragraphs.text: Then the crocodile and the monkey and the parrot were very glad and began to sing, because they were going back to Africa, their real home. And the Doctor said,

sentences.text: Then the crocodile and the monkey and the parrot were very glad and began to sing, because they were going back to Africa, their real home.
sentences.zh: 于是鳄鱼、猴子和鹦鹉都高兴起来，唱起了歌，因为它们要回非洲去了，那是它们真正的家。

sentences.text: And the Doctor said,
sentences.zh: 医生却说：

introduction.zh: 非洲在等着，可医生的话很明白：他连船票都买不起。奇奇被派去取存钱盒，那里头究竟还剩多少？一个连两便士都留不住的人，要怎么渡海？
introduction.en: Africa is waiting, but the Doctor has a plain problem: he cannot even pay for the tickets. Chee-Chee is sent to fetch the money-box. How much is still inside it, and how does a man with no money reach the sea?

quiz.question: Why is there no money in the money-box?
options: Chee-Chee took it with him to Africa.
It was lost in the snow outside.
The Doctor spent it on a rattle for the badger's baby.

feedback.zh: 猫头鹰说，那点钱被医生拿去给獾的娃娃买摇铃了，因为那孩子正在长牙。
feedback.en: The owl explains that the money went on a rattle for the badger's baby, who was teething.

quiz.question: How does the Doctor hope to get a boat?
options: A sailor whose baby he once cured may lend him one.
He will buy one with his savings.
The Cat's-meat-Man will give him one.

feedback.zh: 医生提起一个抱着娃娃来看麻疹的水手，希望那人肯借船——那孩子后来好了。
feedback.en: He remembers a seaman whose baby he cured of measles, and hopes the man will lend him his boat.

grammar.excerpt: if I go down to the seaside I shall be able to borrow a boat

focus.zh: if 从句讲的是将来的事，动词却用一般现在时 go；主句才用 shall be able to。从句里不加 will。
focus.en: The if-clause talks about the future but keeps the present tense go; the main clause carries shall be able to.

title.en: What to Take on a Ship

paragraphs.text: “I shall only be able to take you three—with Jip the dog, Dab-Dab the duck, Gub-Gub the pig and the owl, Too-Too. The rest of the animals, like the dormice and the water-voles and the bats, they will have to go back and live in the fields where they were born till we come home again. But as most of them sleep through the Winter, they won’t mind that—and besides, it wouldn’t be good for them to go to Africa.”

sentences.text: “I shall only be able to take you three—with Jip the dog, Dab-Dab the duck, Gub-Gub the pig and the owl, Too-Too.
sentences.zh: 「我只能带你们三个——再加上狗吉普、鸭子达布达布、小猪咕咕和猫头鹰图图。

sentences.text: The rest of the animals, like the dormice and the water-voles and the bats, they will have to go back and live in the fields where they were born till we come home again.
sentences.zh: 其余的动物，像睡鼠、水田鼠和蝙蝠，只好回到它们出生的田野里去住，等我们回家。

sentences.text: But as most of them sleep through the Winter, they won’t mind that—and besides, it wouldn’t be good for them to go to Africa.”
sentences.zh: 不过它们大多数整个冬天都在睡觉，不会在意这件事——再说，去非洲对它们也不好。」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor's dog.

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor's duck.

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor's pig.

paragraphs.text: So then the parrot, who had been on long sea-voyages before, began telling the Doctor all the things he would have to take with him on the ship.

sentences.text: So then the parrot, who had been on long sea-voyages before, began telling the Doctor all the things he would have to take with him on the ship.
sentences.zh: 于是，那只出过许多次远洋的鹦鹉，开始告诉医生这趟上船他得带上哪些东西。

paragraphs.text: “You must have plenty of pilot-bread,” she said—“‘hard tack’ they call it. And you must have beef in cans—and an anchor.”

sentences.text: “You must have plenty of pilot-bread,” she said—“‘hard tack’ they call it.
sentences.zh: 「你得带足硬面包，」她说，「他们管它叫『硬饼干』。

sentences.text: And you must have beef in cans—and an anchor.”
sentences.zh: 还得有罐头牛肉——外加一只锚。」

hints.zh: 船员吃的硬面饼，烤得很干、放得久不坏，也叫 hard tack（硬饼干）。
hints.en: Pilot-bread, or hard tack: a hard dry biscuit that keeps for months at sea.

paragraphs.text: “I expect the ship will have its own anchor,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “I expect the ship will have its own anchor,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我想船自己会带锚吧。」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “Well, make sure,” said Polynesia. “Because it’s very important. You can’t stop if you haven’t got an anchor. And you’ll need a bell.”

sentences.text: “Well, make sure,” said Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「那就看清楚了。」波利尼西亚说。

sentences.text: “Because it’s very important.
sentences.zh: 「因为这很要紧。

sentences.text: You can’t stop if you haven’t got an anchor.
sentences.zh: 没有锚，船就停不下来。

sentences.text: And you’ll need a bell.”
sentences.zh: 你还需要一只铃铛。」

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉；她出过远门，懂航海。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor's parrot, who has been on long voyages before.

paragraphs.text: “What’s that for?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “What’s that for?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「那要它做什么？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “To tell the time by,” said the parrot. “You go and ring it every half-hour and then you know what time it is. And bring a whole lot of rope—it always comes in handy on voyages.”

sentences.text: “To tell the time by,” said the parrot.
sentences.zh: 「用来报时间呀。」鹦鹉说。

sentences.text: “You go and ring it every half-hour and then you know what time it is.
sentences.zh: 「你每隔半小时去敲一敲，就知道现在是什么时辰。

sentences.text: And bring a whole lot of rope—it always comes in handy on voyages.”
sentences.zh: 再多带些绳子——出海的时候，绳子总派得上用场。」

hints.zh: 派得上用场、迟早用得上；不是「拿在手里」。
hints.en: Comes in handy: turns out to be useful when you need it.

paragraphs.text: Then they began to wonder where they were going to get the money from to buy all the things they needed.

sentences.text: Then they began to wonder where they were going to get the money from to buy all the things they needed.
sentences.zh: 接着他们开始发愁：买这些东西的钱，该到哪里去弄。

introduction.zh: 能上船的只有几位，其余动物要在冬天回田野里去。鹦鹉波利尼西亚远航过多次，开始一样样清点船上必备的东西：硬饼干、罐头牛肉、锚，还有一只铃铛。船上的铃铛到底是做什么用的？
introduction.en: Only a few animals can go; the rest go back to the fields for the winter. The parrot Polynesia has made long voyages, so she lists what the ship must carry: hard biscuit, tins of beef, an anchor — and a bell. What could a ship want with a bell?

quiz.question: Why will most of the animals go back to the fields?
options: There is not enough room for them on the ship.
They are afraid of going on the water.
Most of them sleep through the winter, and Africa would not suit them.

feedback.zh: 医生说它们大多整个冬天都在睡觉，不会在意；再说，去非洲对它们也不好。
feedback.en: The Doctor says most of them sleep through the winter so they will not mind, and Africa would not be good for them.

quiz.question: Why does Polynesia say they need a bell?
options: To call the animals to their meals.
To warn other ships in the dark.
To tell the time by, ringing it every half-hour.

feedback.zh: 她说每隔半小时去敲一次铃，就知道现在是什么时辰了。
feedback.en: She says you ring it every half-hour, and then you know what time it is.

grammar.excerpt: it wouldn’t be good for them to go to Africa

focus.zh: for them 是不定式 to go 的逻辑主语：对他们来说，去非洲不好；for 后面用宾格 them。
focus.en: For them is the logical subject of to go: going to Africa would not be good for them.

title.en: The Key for the Old Horse

paragraphs.text: “Oh, bother it! Money again,” cried the Doctor. “Goodness! I shall be glad to get to Africa where we don’t have to have any! I’ll go and ask the grocer if he will wait for his money till I get back—No, I’ll send the sailor to ask him.”

sentences.text: “Oh, bother it!
sentences.zh: 「唉，真烦人！

sentences.text: Money again,” cried the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 又是钱。」医生叫起来。

sentences.text: “Goodness!
sentences.zh: 「天哪！

sentences.text: I shall be glad to get to Africa where we don’t have to have any!
sentences.zh: 到了非洲我就高兴了，在那儿我们根本不用花钱！

sentences.text: I’ll go and ask the grocer if he will wait for his money till I get back—No, I’ll send the sailor to ask him.”
sentences.zh: 我去问问杂货店老板，能不能等我回来再付钱——不，我让水手去问他。」

paragraphs.text: So the sailor went to see the grocer. And presently he came back with all the things they wanted.

sentences.text: So the sailor went to see the grocer.
sentences.zh: 于是水手去见杂货店老板。

sentences.text: And presently he came back with all the things they wanted.
sentences.zh: 不久，他就带着他们要的各样东西回来了。

paragraphs.text: Then the animals packed up; and after they had turned off the water so the pipes wouldn’t freeze, and put up the shutters, they closed the house and gave the key to the old horse who lived in the stable. And when they had seen that there was plenty of hay in the loft to last the horse through the Winter, they carried all their luggage down to the seashore and got on to the boat.

sentences.text: Then the animals packed up; and after they had turned off the water so the pipes wouldn’t freeze, and put up the shutters, they closed the house and gave the key to the old horse who lived in the stable.
sentences.zh: 接着动物们收拾行李；他们关掉水阀，免得管子冻裂，又装上护窗板，然后把房子锁好，把钥匙交给住在马厩里的那匹老马。

sentences.text: And when they had seen that there was plenty of hay in the loft to last the horse through the Winter, they carried all their luggage down to the seashore and got on to the boat.
sentences.zh: 等他们看清阁楼里的干草足够老马吃上一冬，就把全部行李搬到海边，上了船。

hints.zh: 护窗板，钉在窗外的木挡板，主人出远门时装上，防风防贼。
hints.en: Wooden boards fixed over the windows when a house is left empty.

hints.zh: 阁楼、草料棚，马厩上面堆放干草的地方。
hints.en: The loft: the space above the stable where hay is stored.

paragraphs.text: The Cat’s-meat-Man was there to see them off; and he brought a large suet-pudding as a present for the Doctor because, he said he had been told, you couldn’t get suet-puddings in foreign parts.

sentences.text: The Cat’s-meat-Man was there to see them off; and he brought a large suet-pudding as a present for the Doctor because, he said he had been told, you couldn’t get suet-puddings in foreign parts.
sentences.zh: 卖猫食的人也来送行；他给医生带来一个很大的板油布丁作礼物，因为他说，他听人讲外国买不到板油布丁。

hints.zh: 卖猫食的人，走街串巷卖马肉、猫食的小贩。
hints.en: The cat's-meat man: a street seller who sold meat for cats and dogs.

hints.zh: 板油布丁，用牛油和面做的英国传统点心，冬天常吃。
hints.en: Suet pudding: a heavy traditional British pudding made with beef fat.

paragraphs.text: As soon as they were on the ship, Gub-Gub, the pig, asked where the beds were, for it was four o’clock in the afternoon and he wanted his nap. So Polynesia took him downstairs into the inside of the ship and showed him the beds, set all on top of one another like book-shelves against a wall.

sentences.text: As soon as they were on the ship, Gub-Gub, the pig, asked where the beds were, for it was four o’clock in the afternoon and he wanted his nap.
sentences.zh: 他们一上船，小猪咕咕就问床在哪儿，因为当时是下午四点，他想睡午觉了。

sentences.text: So Polynesia took him downstairs into the inside of the ship and showed him the beds, set all on top of one another like book-shelves against a wall.
sentences.zh: 于是波利尼西亚带他下到船肚子里，指给他看那些床——它们一张摞一张，像靠墙的书架。

introduction.zh: 又是因为钱。医生气得直嚷嚷，非得派人去跟杂货店老板谈。房子要关起来，行李要搬下海边，家里还有一位老住户走不了——钥匙该交给谁？
introduction.en: Money again. The Doctor shouts in anger, and someone must go and talk to the grocer. The house is to be shut up, the luggage carried down to the sea, and one old resident cannot go with them. Who should have the key?

quiz.question: What do they do with the key of the house?
options: They hang it inside the front door.
They leave it with the Cat's-meat-Man.
They give it to the old horse in the stable.

feedback.zh: 他们把房子锁好，钥匙交给住在马厩里的那匹老马，还请它看家。
feedback.en: They lock the house and give the key to the old horse who lives in the stable.

quiz.question: Why does the Cat's-meat-Man bring a suet-pudding?
options: He has been told you cannot get them in foreign parts.
The Doctor asked him to buy one for the voyage.
It is a present for Gub-Gub, who likes puddings.

feedback.zh: 他说他听人讲，到了外国就买不到板油布丁了，所以带一个来送给医生。
feedback.en: He says he has been told that suet-puddings cannot be got in foreign parts.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as they were on the ship

focus.zh: as soon as 引导时间从句，意思是「一……就……」；主句 asked 用一般过去时，两件事紧接着发生。
focus.en: As soon as introduces the time clause: the moment they were on the ship, Gub-Gub asked.

paragraphs.text: “Why, that isn’t a bed!” cried Gub-Gub. “That’s a shelf!”

sentences.text: “Why, that isn’t a bed!” cried Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「哎呀，这哪是床！」咕咕叫起来。

sentences.text: “That’s a shelf!”
sentences.zh: 「这是个架子！」

paragraphs.text: “Beds are always like that on ships,” said the parrot. “It isn’t a shelf. Climb up into it and go to sleep. That’s what you call ‘a bunk.’”

sentences.text: “Beds are always like that on ships,” said the parrot.
sentences.zh: 「船上的床都是这样的。」鹦鹉说。

sentences.text: “It isn’t a shelf.
sentences.zh: 「这不是架子。

sentences.text: Climb up into it and go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 爬上去睡就是了。

sentences.text: That’s what you call ‘a bunk.’”
sentences.zh: 这个呀，就叫『铺位』。」

hints.zh: 铺位，船上或宿舍里固定在墙上的窄床，常常上下叠放。
hints.en: A bunk: a narrow fixed bed on a ship, often one of two stacked together.

paragraphs.text: “I don’t think I’ll go to bed yet,” said Gub-Gub. “I’m too excited. I want to go upstairs again and see them start.”

sentences.text: “I don’t think I’ll go to bed yet,” said Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「我看我还是先不睡了。」咕咕说。

sentences.text: “I’m too excited.
sentences.zh: 「我太兴奋了。

sentences.text: I want to go upstairs again and see them start.”
sentences.zh: 我想再上去，看他们开船。」

hints.zh: 看他们开船；start 在这里是「出发」，不是「开始做某事」。
hints.en: See them start: watch the ship set off; start here means "set out".

paragraphs.text: “Well, this is your first trip,” said Polynesia. “You will get used to the life after a while.” And she went back up the stairs of the ship, humming this song to herself,

sentences.text: “Well, this is your first trip,” said Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「也难怪，这是你头一回出海。」波利尼西亚说。

sentences.text: “You will get used to the life after a while.”
sentences.zh: 「过些日子，你就习惯这种日子了。」

sentences.text: And she went back up the stairs of the ship, humming this song to herself,
sentences.zh: 她一边沿着船梯往上走，一边自己哼着这首歌：

hints.zh: 慢慢习惯这种生活；get used to 是「变得习惯」，跟表示「过去常常」的 used to 不是一回事。
hints.en: Get used to the life means become accustomed to it — not the same as "used to do", which talks about past habits.

paragraphs.text: I’ve seen the Black Sea and the Red Sea; I rounded the Isle of Wight; I discovered the Yellow River, And the Orange too—by night. Now Greenland drops behind again, And I sail the ocean Blue. I’m tired of all these colors, Jane, So I’m coming back to you.

sentences.text: I’ve seen the Black Sea and the Red Sea; I rounded the Isle of Wight; I discovered the Yellow River, And the Orange too—by night.
sentences.zh: 我见过黑海，也见过红海；我绕过怀特岛；我发现了黄河，还有橙河——都是在夜里。

sentences.text: Now Greenland drops behind again, And I sail the ocean Blue.
sentences.zh: 如今格陵兰又退到身后，我航行在蓝色的大洋上。

sentences.text: I’m tired of all these colors, Jane, So I’m coming back to you.
sentences.zh: 简，这些颜色我都看厌了，所以我要回到你身边。

hints.zh: 怀特岛，英格兰南岸外的小岛，船出海时常从它旁边经过。
hints.en: The Isle of Wight: a small island off the south coast of England.

hints.zh: 简，歌里水手思念的姑娘，是泛指的，不是这本书里的人物。
hints.en: Jane is the sailor's sweetheart in the song — not a character in this book.

paragraphs.text: They were just going to start on their journey, when the Doctor said he would have to go back and ask the sailor the way to Africa.

sentences.text: They were just going to start on their journey, when the Doctor said he would have to go back and ask the sailor the way to Africa.
sentences.zh: 他们正要启程，医生却说，他得回去问问水手去非洲怎么走。

paragraphs.text: But the swallow said she had been to that country many times and would show them how to get there.

sentences.text: But the swallow said she had been to that country many times and would show them how to get there.
sentences.zh: 可燕子说，那个国家她去过很多次，愿意指给他们看怎么走。

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor told Chee-Chee to pull up the anchor and the voyage began.

sentences.text: So the Doctor told Chee-Chee to pull up the anchor and the voyage began.
sentences.zh: 于是医生让奇奇把锚拉上来，航行就这样开始了。

introduction.zh: 行李都搬上了船，咕咕被领到船肚子里看他的床。他站在那儿，怎么也不肯相信这东西是给人睡的。船就要开了，可这一船人和动物里，谁认得去非洲的路？
introduction.en: The luggage is on board, and Gub-Gub is taken down inside the ship to see his bed. He stands and stares: he will not believe that anyone could sleep in it. The ship is about to sail — but who on board knows the road to Africa?

quiz.question: What does Gub-Gub think of the bed on the ship?
options: He thinks it is a table for the animals.
He thinks it is a shelf.
He thinks it is too small for him.

feedback.zh: 咕咕一看就叫起来：这哪是床，这是个架子；鹦鹉只好告诉他，船上管这个叫「铺位」。
feedback.en: Gub-Gub cries that it is not a bed at all but a shelf; the parrot has to explain that it is called a bunk.

quiz.question: Who says she can show them the way to Africa?
options: Polynesia.
The sailor.
The swallow.

feedback.zh: 医生本来还想回去问水手，燕子说那个国家她去过很多次，愿意带路。
feedback.en: The Doctor was going back to ask the sailor, but the swallow says she has been there many times and will show them the way.

grammar.excerpt: They were just going to start on their journey

focus.zh: were going to start 是过去的打算：他们正要出发；just 强调「就差一点」，when 从句随即打断。
focus.en: Were going to start is a plan in the past: they were just about to leave when something interrupted them.

paragraphs.text: Now for six whole weeks they went sailing on and on, over the rolling sea, following the swallow who flew before the ship to show them the way. At night she carried a tiny lantern, so they should not miss her in the dark; and the people on the other ships that passed said that the light must be a shooting star.

sentences.text: Now for six whole weeks they went sailing on and on, over the rolling sea, following the swallow who flew before the ship to show them the way.
sentences.zh: 就这样，整整六个星期，他们在起伏的大海上一路向前，跟着那只燕子——她飞在船的前面，给他们指路。

sentences.text: At night she carried a tiny lantern, so they should not miss her in the dark; and the people on the other ships that passed said that the light must be a shooting star.
sentences.zh: 夜里她提着一盏小灯笼，好让他们在黑暗中不会跟丢她；过往船上的人都说，那道光一定是颗流星。

paragraphs.text: As they sailed further and further into the South, it got warmer and warmer. Polynesia, Chee-Chee and the crocodile enjoyed the hot sun no end. They ran about laughing and looking over the side of the ship to see if they could see Africa yet.

sentences.text: As they sailed further and further into the South, it got warmer and warmer.
sentences.zh: 他们越往南航行，天气就越来越热。

sentences.text: Polynesia, Chee-Chee and the crocodile enjoyed the hot sun no end.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚、奇奇和鳄鱼都喜欢这大太阳，喜欢得不得了。

sentences.text: They ran about laughing and looking over the side of the ship to see if they could see Africa yet.
sentences.zh: 他们跑来跑去，笑着往船舷外张望，看是不是已经能看见非洲了。

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉，见多识广，会说人话。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor's parrot, who has seen a great deal of the world and can talk.

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey.

hints.zh: 口语里表示「没完没了地、极其」，enjoyed it no end 就是喜欢得不得了。
hints.en: An informal phrase meaning “very much”: enjoyed the sun no end.

paragraphs.text: But the pig and the dog and the owl, Too-Too, could do nothing in such weather, but sat at the end of the ship in the shade of a big barrel, with their tongues hanging out, drinking lemonade.

sentences.text: But the pig and the dog and the owl, Too-Too, could do nothing in such weather, but sat at the end of the ship in the shade of a big barrel, with their tongues hanging out, drinking lemonade.
sentences.zh: 可是在这样的天气里，猪、狗和猫头鹰图图什么也做不了，只能坐在船尾一只大木桶的阴凉里，伸着舌头，喝柠檬水。

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor's owl.

paragraphs.text: Dab-Dab, the duck, used to keep herself cool by jumping into the sea and swimming behind the ship. And every once in a while, when the top of her head got too hot, she would dive under the ship and come up on the other side. In this way, too, she used to catch herrings on Tuesdays and Fridays—when everybody on the boat ate fish to make the beef last longer.

sentences.text: Dab-Dab, the duck, used to keep herself cool by jumping into the sea and swimming behind the ship.
sentences.zh: 鸭子达布达布常常跳进海里，游在船后面，好让自己凉快凉快。

sentences.text: And every once in a while, when the top of her head got too hot, she would dive under the ship and come up on the other side.
sentences.zh: 每隔一阵子，等她头顶晒得太烫了，她就潜到船底下，从另一边冒出来。

sentences.text: In this way, too, she used to catch herrings on Tuesdays and Fridays—when everybody on the boat ate fish to make the beef last longer.
sentences.zh: 她也用这个法子，在星期二和星期五抓鲱鱼——那两天船上的人都吃鱼，好让牛肉能多撑些日子。

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor's duck.

hints.zh: 让牛肉能多吃几天、撑得更久；last 在这里是「维持、用下去」。
hints.en: To make the beef last longer: to make the meat go further, so it is not eaten up too soon.

introduction.zh: 为了给非洲的猴子治病，杜立德医生带着一船动物出海，一只燕子提着灯笼在船前领路。船越往南开，天越热，动物们的日子也越来越难熬。非洲到底还有多远？
introduction.en: The Doctor's ship has been at sea for six weeks. A swallow with a tiny lantern flies ahead to show the way. The further south they sail, the hotter it gets, and not every animal enjoys the heat. How far is Africa?

quiz.question: Why does the swallow fly in front of the ship?
options: To find other ships in the dark.
To carry the lantern home.
To show them the way.

feedback.zh: 原文说燕子「飞在船前面给他们指路」，夜里还提着灯，好让他们不跟丢。
feedback.en: The text says the swallow flew before the ship to show them the way, and at night she carried a lantern so they would not lose her.

quiz.question: What do the pig, the dog and the owl do in the hot weather?
options: They climb the mast and look for land.
They sit in the shade of a big barrel and drink lemonade.
They swim behind the ship to keep cool.

feedback.zh: 他们热得什么也做不了，只能坐在大木桶的阴凉里伸着舌头喝柠檬水；游泳的是鸭子。
feedback.en: They can do nothing in the heat, so they sit in the shade of a big barrel with their tongues out, drinking lemonade; it is the duck who swims.

grammar.excerpt: following the swallow who flew before the ship to show them the way

focus.zh: who 指前面的 the swallow，是从句的主语：who flew before the ship 说明是哪只燕子。
focus.en: Who points back to the swallow and is the subject of its own clause: who flew before the ship tells us which swallow.

paragraphs.text: When they got near to the Equator they saw some flying-fishes coming towards them. And the fishes asked the parrot if this was Doctor Dolittle’s ship. When she told them it was, they said they were glad, because the monkeys in Africa were getting worried that he would never come. Polynesia asked them how many miles they had yet to go; and the flying-fishes said it was only fifty-five miles now to the coast of Africa.

sentences.text: When they got near to the Equator they saw some flying-fishes coming towards them.
sentences.zh: 当他们驶近赤道时，看见一些飞鱼朝他们游过来。

sentences.text: And the fishes asked the parrot if this was Doctor Dolittle’s ship.
sentences.zh: 那些鱼问鹦鹉，这是不是杜立德医生的船。

sentences.text: When she told them it was, they said they were glad, because the monkeys in Africa were getting worried that he would never come.
sentences.zh: 她回答说是，它们听了很高兴，因为非洲的猴子们一直担心他再也不会来了。

sentences.text: Polynesia asked them how many miles they had yet to go; and the flying-fishes said it was only fifty-five miles now to the coast of Africa.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚问它们还要走多少英里；飞鱼们说，现在离非洲海岸只有五十五英里了。

hints.zh: 赤道；船从北往南驶近这条线，越过去天就更热了。
hints.en: The Equator: the line round the middle of the earth. Sailing south towards it, the ship meets hotter weather.

hints.zh: 杜立德医生，这本书的主角，一位会给动物看病的医生。
hints.en: Doctor Dolittle, the hero of the book: a doctor who can speak with animals and treat them.

paragraphs.text: And another time a whole school of porpoises came dancing through the waves; and they too asked Polynesia if this was the ship of the famous doctor. And when they heard that it was, they asked the parrot if the Doctor wanted anything for his journey.

sentences.text: And another time a whole school of porpoises came dancing through the waves; and they too asked Polynesia if this was the ship of the famous doctor.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，一整群海豚在浪里跳着舞过来；它们也问波利尼西亚，这是不是那位名医的船。

sentences.text: And when they heard that it was, they asked the parrot if the Doctor wanted anything for his journey.
sentences.zh: 听说确实是他，它们就问鹦鹉，医生这趟路需不需要带点什么。

hints.zh: school 这里不是「学校」，而是「一群」鱼或海兽；porpoise 是鼠海豚，常成群游动。
hints.en: A school is a group of sea animals, not a place of learning; porpoises are small dolphins that swim together.

paragraphs.text: And Polynesia said, “Yes. We have run short of onions.”

sentences.text: And Polynesia said, “Yes.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚说：「有。

sentences.text: We have run short of onions.”
sentences.zh: 我们的洋葱吃完了。」

hints.zh: 快用完了、不够了；run short of onions 就是洋葱快没了。
hints.en: To run short of something is to have almost none left: they are running out of onions.

paragraphs.text: “There is an island not far from here,” said the porpoises, “where the wild onions grow tall and strong. Keep straight on—we will get some and catch up to you.”

sentences.text: “There is an island not far from here,” said the porpoises, “where the wild onions grow tall and strong.
sentences.zh: 「离这儿不远有一座岛，」海豚们说，「那里的野洋葱长得又高又壮。

sentences.text: Keep straight on—we will get some and catch up to you.”
sentences.zh: 你们一直往前开——我们去弄一些，再追上你们。」

hints.zh: 一直朝前开，别拐弯、别停下。
hints.en: Keep straight on: go on in the same direction without turning.

paragraphs.text: So the porpoises dashed away through the sea. And very soon the parrot saw them again, coming up behind, dragging the onions through the waves in big nets made of seaweed.

sentences.text: So the porpoises dashed away through the sea.
sentences.zh: 于是海豚们飞快地穿过大海游走了。

sentences.text: And very soon the parrot saw them again, coming up behind, dragging the onions through the waves in big nets made of seaweed.
sentences.zh: 很快，鹦鹉又看见了它们：它们从后面赶上来，用海草做成的大网拖着洋葱穿过浪头。

paragraphs.text: The next evening, as the sun was going down, the Doctor said,

sentences.text: The next evening, as the sun was going down, the Doctor said,
sentences.zh: 第二天傍晚，太阳正在落下去的时候，医生说：

paragraphs.text: “Get me the telescope, Chee-Chee. Our journey is nearly ended. Very soon we should be able to see the shores of Africa.”

sentences.text: “Get me the telescope, Chee-Chee.
sentences.zh: 「奇奇，把望远镜给我。

sentences.text: Our journey is nearly ended.
sentences.zh: 我们的旅程快结束了。

sentences.text: Very soon we should be able to see the shores of Africa.”
sentences.zh: 很快我们应该就能看见非洲的海岸了。」

introduction.zh: 船快到赤道时，海面上先来了会飞的鱼，接着又是一群海豚——它们好像都认得杜立德医生的名字。可船上偏偏缺了一样不起眼的东西。海里的朋友能帮上忙吗？
introduction.en: Near the Equator, flying-fish leap towards the ship, and a school of porpoises dances through the waves. They all seem to know the Doctor's name. But the ship has run short of something small and ordinary. Can the sea help them?

quiz.question: What do the flying-fishes say about the monkeys in Africa?
options: They are getting worried that the Doctor will never come.
They have already left Africa.
They have plenty of onions to give him.

feedback.zh: 飞鱼说非洲的猴子一直担心医生永远不会来，所以听说这正是他的船就很高兴。
feedback.en: The flying-fishes say the monkeys were getting worried that he would never come, so they were glad to hear it was his ship.

quiz.question: How do the porpoises bring the onions to the ship?
options: They carry them in their mouths one by one.
They leave them on the island for the ship to collect.
They drag them through the waves in big nets made of seaweed.

feedback.zh: 海豚游到长野洋葱的岛上，用海草编成大网，拖着洋葱从后面追上船来。
feedback.en: The porpoises swim to the island where the wild onions grow and come up behind the ship, dragging the onions in big nets made of seaweed.

grammar.excerpt: asked them how many miles they had yet to go

focus.zh: ask + 人 + 疑问词从句要用陈述语序：how many miles they had yet to go，不能说 had they。
focus.en: After ask + person, the wh-clause keeps statement order: how many miles they had yet to go, not had they.

paragraphs.text: And about half an hour later, sure enough, they thought they could see something in front that might be land. But it began to get darker and darker and they couldn’t be sure.

sentences.text: And about half an hour later, sure enough, they thought they could see something in front that might be land.
sentences.zh: 大约半小时后，果然，他们觉得前面好像能看见点什么，也许是陆地。

sentences.text: But it began to get darker and darker and they couldn’t be sure.
sentences.zh: 可是天越来越黑，他们没法确定。

paragraphs.text: Then a great storm came up, with thunder and lightning. The wind howled; the rain came down in torrents; and the waves got so high they splashed right over the boat.

sentences.text: Then a great storm came up, with thunder and lightning.
sentences.zh: 接着来了一场大风暴，伴着雷电。

sentences.text: The wind howled; the rain came down in torrents; and the waves got so high they splashed right over the boat.
sentences.zh: 狂风怒吼；大雨倾盆而下；浪头高得直接泼过了船身。

paragraphs.text: Presently there was a big BANG! The ship stopped and rolled over on its side.

sentences.text: Presently there was a big BANG!
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，只听轰的一声巨响！

sentences.text: The ship stopped and rolled over on its side.
sentences.zh: 船停住了，向一侧翻倒。

hints.zh: 旧式用法，意思是「不一会儿、很快」，不是「现在」。
hints.en: An old-fashioned word here meaning “soon” or “in a moment”, not “at present”.

paragraphs.text: “What’s happened?” asked the Doctor, coming up from downstairs.

sentences.text: “What’s happened?” asked the Doctor, coming up from downstairs.
sentences.zh: 「出什么事了？」医生从下面走上来，问道。

paragraphs.text: “I’m not sure,” said the parrot; “but I think we’re ship-wrecked. Tell the duck to get out and see.”

sentences.text: “I’m not sure,” said the parrot; “but I think we’re ship-wrecked.
sentences.zh: 「我说不准，」鹦鹉说，「不过我想我们是触礁失事了。

sentences.text: Tell the duck to get out and see.”
sentences.zh: 叫鸭子出去看看。」

hints.zh: 船只失事、触礁沉没；这里指船撞坏了，走不了了。
hints.en: Ship-wrecked: having lost or broken the ship, as in a wreck.

paragraphs.text: So Dab-Dab dived right down under the waves. And when she came up she said they had struck a rock; there was a big hole in the bottom of the ship; the water was coming in; and they were sinking fast.

sentences.text: So Dab-Dab dived right down under the waves.
sentences.zh: 于是达布达布一头扎进浪里。

sentences.text: And when she came up she said they had struck a rock; there was a big hole in the bottom of the ship; the water was coming in; and they were sinking fast.
sentences.zh: 等她浮上来，她说他们撞上了礁石；船底有个大洞；水正往里灌；船在下沉，而且沉得很快。

paragraphs.text: “We must have run into Africa,” said the Doctor. “Dear me, dear me!—Well—we must all swim to land.”

sentences.text: “We must have run into Africa,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我们一定是撞上非洲了，」医生说。

sentences.text: “Dear me, dear me!—Well—we must all swim to land.”
sentences.zh: 「天哪，天哪！——好吧——我们大家都得游到岸上去。」

hints.zh: 感叹语，「天哪、哎呀」，表示吃惊或着急，不是说「亲爱的我」。
hints.en: An old exclamation of surprise or worry, not a way of addressing anyone.

paragraphs.text: But Chee-Chee and Gub-Gub did not know how to swim.

sentences.text: But Chee-Chee and Gub-Gub did not know how to swim.
sentences.zh: 可是奇奇和咕咕不会游泳。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的宠物小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor's little pig.

paragraphs.text: “Get the rope!” said Polynesia. “I told you it would come in handy. Where’s that duck? Come here, Dab-Dab. Take this end of the rope, fly to the shore and tie it on to a palm-tree; and we’ll hold the other end on the ship here. Then those that can’t swim must climb along the rope till they reach the land. That’s what you call a ‘life-line.’”

sentences.text: “Get the rope!” said Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「把绳子拿来！」波利尼西亚说。

sentences.text: “I told you it would come in handy.
sentences.zh: 「我早说过它会有用的。

sentences.text: Where’s that duck?
sentences.zh: 那只鸭子呢？

sentences.text: Come here, Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 过来，达布达布。

sentences.text: Take this end of the rope, fly to the shore and tie it on to a palm-tree; and we’ll hold the other end on the ship here.
sentences.zh: 抓住绳子这一头，飞到岸上，把它系在一棵棕榈树上；我们把另一头拉在船上。

sentences.text: Then those that can’t swim must climb along the rope till they reach the land.
sentences.zh: 这样，那些不会游泳的就得顺着绳子爬，一直爬到岸上。

sentences.text: That’s what you call a ‘life-line.’”
sentences.zh: 这就叫『救生索』。」

hints.zh: 派得上用场、迟早有用。
hints.en: To come in handy: to turn out to be useful.

hints.zh: 救生索；这里指从岸上拉到船上的一根绳子，不会游泳的顺着它爬过去。
hints.en: A life-line: here, a rope stretched from the shore to the ship for the animals to climb along.

introduction.zh: 夜里他们以为看见了陆地，风暴却先扑了上来。一声巨响之后，船停住、歪向一边，水正往船底的大洞里灌。不会游泳的奇奇和咕咕，怎么才能上岸？
introduction.en: They think they can see land in the dark, and then the storm hits. After a great BANG the ship stops and rolls over, and water pours through a hole in the bottom. Chee-Chee and Gub-Gub cannot swim. How will they reach the shore?

quiz.question: What happens to the ship in the storm?
options: It turns round and goes back to Puddleby.
It strikes a rock, and water starts coming in through a hole.
It sails safely to the coast of Africa.

feedback.zh: 达布达布潜下去看，回来说他们撞上了礁石，船底破了个大洞，水正往里灌，船在下沉。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab dives down and reports that they have struck a rock: there is a big hole in the bottom, water is coming in and the ship is sinking.

quiz.question: Why does Polynesia want the rope?
options: So the animals that cannot swim can climb along it to the land.
To tie the ship to a palm-tree and stop it sinking.
To pull the Doctor's trunk out of the water.

feedback.zh: 她让鸭子把一头系在岸上的棕榈树上，另一头留在船上，不会游泳的就顺着绳子爬上岸。
feedback.en: She tells the duck to tie one end to a palm-tree on the shore and keep the other on the ship, so those who cannot swim can climb along the rope.

grammar.excerpt: the waves got so high they splashed right over the boat

focus.zh: so + 形容词 + 从句表示结果：浪高到直接泼过了船身；这里省略了 that。
focus.en: So + adjective + clause shows a result: the waves were so high that they splashed over the boat; that is left out.

paragraphs.text: So they all got safely to the shore—some swimming, some flying; and those that climbed along the rope brought the Doctor’s trunk and hand-bag with them.

sentences.text: So they all got safely to the shore—some swimming, some flying; and those that climbed along the rope brought the Doctor’s trunk and hand-bag with them.
sentences.zh: 于是他们都平安到了岸上——有的游水，有的飞；那些顺着绳子爬过来的，还把医生的箱子和手提包带了过来。

hints.zh: 这里指大行李箱，不是「树干」。
hints.en: Here a trunk is a large travelling case, not part of a tree.

paragraphs.text: But the ship was no good any more—with the big hole in the bottom; and presently the rough sea beat it to pieces on the rocks and the timbers floated away.

sentences.text: But the ship was no good any more—with the big hole in the bottom; and presently the rough sea beat it to pieces on the rocks and the timbers floated away.
sentences.zh: 可那条船已经不能再用了——船底有个大洞；不久，汹涌的海浪把它在礁石上撞得粉碎，船板四散漂走。

paragraphs.text: Then they all took shelter in a nice dry cave they found, high up in the cliffs, till the storm was over.

sentences.text: Then they all took shelter in a nice dry cave they found, high up in the cliffs, till the storm was over.
sentences.zh: 于是他们躲进高崖上找到的一个干爽的好山洞，一直待到风暴过去。

paragraphs.text: When the sun came out next morning they went down to the sandy beach to dry themselves.

sentences.text: When the sun came out next morning they went down to the sandy beach to dry themselves.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上太阳出来，他们下到沙滩上，把身上弄干。

paragraphs.text: “Dear old Africa!” sighed Polynesia. “It’s good to get back. Just think—it’ll be a hundred and sixty-nine years to-morrow since I was here! And it hasn’t changed a bit!—Same old palm-trees; same old red earth; same old black ants! There’s no place like home!”

sentences.text: “Dear old Africa!” sighed Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「亲爱的老非洲！」波利尼西亚叹了口气。

sentences.text: “It’s good to get back.
sentences.zh: 「回来真好。

sentences.text: Just think—it’ll be a hundred and sixty-nine years to-morrow since I was here!
sentences.zh: 你想想——到明天，我离开这儿就整整一百六十九年了！

sentences.text: And it hasn’t changed a bit!—Same old palm-trees; same old red earth; same old black ants!
sentences.zh: 而且它一点都没变！——还是那些老棕榈树；还是那片老红土；还是那些老黑蚂蚁！

sentences.text: There’s no place like home!”
sentences.zh: 没有哪个地方比得上家！」

hints.zh: 旧式拼法，即现代拼写的 tomorrow，意思是「明天」。
hints.en: An old spelling of “tomorrow”.

hints.zh: 谚语「没有哪个地方比得上家」；她回到故乡，最想说的就是这一句。
hints.en: A well-known saying: home is better than anywhere else.

paragraphs.text: And the others noticed she had tears in her eyes—she was so pleased to see her country once again.

sentences.text: And the others noticed she had tears in her eyes—she was so pleased to see her country once again.
sentences.zh: 其他人都注意到她眼里含着泪——能再见到自己的故乡，她太高兴了。

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor missed his high hat; for it had been blown into the sea during the storm. So Dab-Dab went out to look for it. And presently she saw it, a long way off, floating on the water like a toy-boat.

sentences.text: Then the Doctor missed his high hat; for it had been blown into the sea during the storm.
sentences.zh: 后来医生发现他的高礼帽不见了；原来它在风暴中被吹进了海里。

sentences.text: So Dab-Dab went out to look for it.
sentences.zh: 于是达布达布出去找。

sentences.text: And presently she saw it, a long way off, floating on the water like a toy-boat.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，她就看见了它，远远地漂在水上，像一只玩具小船。

hints.zh: 这里是「发现（东西）不见了」，不是「想念」：医生发现高礼帽丢了。
hints.en: Here missed means “noticed that something was gone”, not “felt sad about its absence”.

paragraphs.text: When she flew down to get it, she found one of the white mice, very frightened, sitting inside it.

sentences.text: When she flew down to get it, she found one of the white mice, very frightened, sitting inside it.
sentences.zh: 她飞下去拿的时候，发现里面坐着其中一只白鼠，吓得要命。

hints.zh: 白鼠；这些白鼠原本养在医生家的钢琴里，出发时被留在帕德尔比。
hints.en: The white mice that used to live in the Doctor's piano at home; they were meant to stay behind in Puddleby.

paragraphs.text: “What are you doing here?” asked the duck. “You were told to stay behind in Puddleby.”

sentences.text: “What are you doing here?” asked the duck.
sentences.zh: 「你在这儿干什么？」鸭子问。

sentences.text: “You were told to stay behind in Puddleby.”
sentences.zh: 「早就让你留在帕德尔比了。」

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡，全名是「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor's home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

introduction.zh: 大家都平安上了岸，可船在礁石上撞成了碎片，行李只剩一只箱子。他们在崖上找到一个山洞躲雨，第二天太阳出来才看清这片新土地。医生的高礼帽又漂到哪里去了？
introduction.en: Everyone gets safely ashore, but the ship breaks up on the rocks and the animals have only one trunk left. They shelter in a cave until the sun comes out. Then the Doctor finds that his high hat is gone. Where is it now?

quiz.question: What happens to the ship after everyone reaches the shore?
options: The animals pull it up the beach and mend it.
It floats away with the trunk still inside.
The rough sea beats it to pieces on the rocks.

feedback.zh: 船底破了大洞，已经不能用了；不久汹涌的海浪把它在礁石上撞得粉碎，木头都漂散了。
feedback.en: With the big hole in the bottom the ship is no good any more, and the rough sea soon beats it to pieces on the rocks.

quiz.question: What does Dab-Dab find inside the Doctor's hat?
options: A young monkey from the jungle.
One of the white mice, very frightened.
A small toy boat.

feedback.zh: 她飞下去拿帽子，发现里面坐着其中一只白鼠，吓得要命——这只白鼠本来该留在帕德尔比。
feedback.en: She flies down for the hat and finds one of the white mice sitting inside it, very frightened — a mouse that was supposed to stay in Puddleby.

grammar.excerpt: in a nice dry cave they found, high up in the cliffs

focus.zh: cave 后面省略了关系词：they found 的宾语就是 cave，作宾语时 that/which 可以省。
focus.en: The relative pronoun after cave is left out: cave is the object of they found, and an object pronoun can be dropped.

paragraphs.text: “I didn’t want to be left behind,” said the mouse. “I wanted to see what Africa was like—I have relatives there. So I hid in the baggage and was brought on to the ship with the hard-tack. When the ship sank I was terribly frightened—because I cannot swim far. I swam as long as I could, but I soon got all exhausted and thought I was going to sink. And then, just at that moment, the old man’s hat came floating by; and I got into it because I did not want to be drowned.”

sentences.text: “I didn’t want to be left behind,” said the mouse.
sentences.zh: 「我不想被留下，」老鼠说。

sentences.text: “I wanted to see what Africa was like—I have relatives there.
sentences.zh: 「我想看看非洲是什么样子——我在这儿有亲戚。

sentences.text: So I hid in the baggage and was brought on to the ship with the hard-tack.
sentences.zh: 所以我藏在行李里，跟着硬饼干一起被搬上了船。

sentences.text: When the ship sank I was terribly frightened—because I cannot swim far.
sentences.zh: 船沉的时候我吓坏了——因为我游不了多远。

sentences.text: I swam as long as I could, but I soon got all exhausted and thought I was going to sink.
sentences.zh: 我拼命游，能游多久就游多久，可很快就累得一点力气都没有，觉得自己要沉下去了。

sentences.text: And then, just at that moment, the old man’s hat came floating by; and I got into it because I did not want to be drowned.”
sentences.zh: 就在这时，老头子的帽子漂了过来；我就爬了进去，因为我不想被淹死。」

hints.zh: 硬饼干，船上给水手和乘客吃的干粮。
hints.en: Hard-tack: hard dry biscuit kept on ships as food.

paragraphs.text: So the duck took up the hat with the mouse in it and brought it to the Doctor on the shore. And they all gathered round to have a look.

sentences.text: So the duck took up the hat with the mouse in it and brought it to the Doctor on the shore.
sentences.zh: 于是鸭子叼起装着老鼠的帽子，把它带到岸上的医生那儿。

sentences.text: And they all gathered round to have a look.
sentences.zh: 大家都围过来看。

paragraphs.text: “That’s what you call a ‘stowaway,’” said the parrot.

sentences.text: “That’s what you call a ‘stowaway,’” said the parrot.
sentences.zh: 「这就叫『偷渡客』，」鹦鹉说。

hints.zh: 偷渡客，藏在船或行李里偷偷搭乘的人。
hints.en: A stowaway: someone who hides on a ship or in the luggage and travels without being seen.

paragraphs.text: Presently, when they were looking for a place in the trunk where the white mouse could travel comfortably, the monkey, Chee-Chee, suddenly said,

sentences.text: Presently, when they were looking for a place in the trunk where the white mouse could travel comfortably, the monkey, Chee-Chee, suddenly said,
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，他们正想给白鼠在箱子里找一个能舒舒服服待着的地方，猴子奇奇忽然说：

paragraphs.text: “Sh! I hear footsteps in the jungle!”

sentences.text: “Sh!
I hear footsteps in the jungle!”
sentences.zh: 我听见丛林里有脚步声！」

paragraphs.text: They all stopped talking and listened. And soon a black man came down out of the woods and asked them what they were doing there.

sentences.text: They all stopped talking and listened.
sentences.zh: 大家都停下来听。

sentences.text: And soon a black man came down out of the woods and asked them what they were doing there.
sentences.zh: 很快，一个黑人男子从树林里走出来，问他们在那里做什么。

paragraphs.text: “My name is John Dolittle—M.D.,” said the Doctor. “I have been asked to come to Africa to cure the monkeys who are sick.”

sentences.text: “My name is John Dolittle—M.D.,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我叫约翰·杜立德——医学博士，」医生说。

sentences.text: “I have been asked to come to Africa to cure the monkeys who are sick.”
sentences.zh: 「有人请我到非洲来，给生病的猴子治病。」

hints.zh: 医学博士（Doctor of Medicine）的缩写，报全名时一起说出，表示自己是有执照的医生。
hints.en: Short for Doctor of Medicine: he gives it with his name to show he is a properly qualified doctor.

paragraphs.text: “You must all come before the King,” said the black man.

sentences.text: “You must all come before the King,” said the black man.
sentences.zh: 「你们都得去见国王，」那个黑人说。

paragraphs.text: “What king?” asked the Doctor, who didn’t want to waste any time.

sentences.text: “What king?” asked the Doctor, who didn’t want to waste any time.
sentences.zh: 「什么国王？」医生问，他不想浪费一点时间。

hints.target: didn’t want to waste any time
hints.zh: 不想浪费一点时间，急着去给猴子治病。
hints.en: Didn't want to waste any time: he was in a hurry to get on with his work.

paragraphs.text: “The King of the Jolliginki,” the man answered. “All these lands belong to him; and all strangers must be brought before him. Follow me.”

sentences.text: “The King of the Jolliginki,” the man answered.
sentences.zh: 「乔利金基的国王，」那人回答。

sentences.text: “All these lands belong to him; and all strangers must be brought before him.
sentences.zh: 「这些土地都归他所有；所有外乡人都得带到他面前。

sentences.text: Follow me.”
sentences.zh: 跟我来。」

hints.zh: 乔利金基，非洲的这个王国；「乔利金基国王」统治这片土地，外乡人都得先去见他。
hints.en: Jolliginki, the African kingdom; its King rules these lands, and every stranger must be brought before him.

paragraphs.text: So they gathered up their baggage and went off, following the man through the jungle.

sentences.text: So they gathered up their baggage and went off, following the man through the jungle.
sentences.zh: 于是他们收拾好行李，跟着那个人穿过丛林走了。

introduction.zh: 帽子捞上来了，里面却坐着一位谁也没想到的乘客。大家还没来得及问清楚，奇奇忽然听见丛林里有脚步声。来的会是谁？
introduction.en: The hat is pulled out of the sea, and there is a passenger inside that nobody expected. Before anyone can ask questions, Chee-Chee hears footsteps in the jungle. Who is coming, and what does he want?

quiz.question: Why did the mouse hide in the baggage?
options: It wanted to see Africa, and it has relatives there.
The Doctor had asked it to come along.
It was looking for the ship's hard-tack.

feedback.zh: 老鼠说它不想被留下，想看看非洲是什么样子，还说自己在非洲有亲戚，所以才藏进行李上了船。
feedback.en: The mouse says it did not want to be left behind: it wanted to see what Africa was like, and it has relatives there.

quiz.question: What does the man from the jungle tell them to do?
options: Go back to their ship at once.
Wait in the cave until morning.
Come before the King of the Jolliginki.

feedback.zh: 那人说这一带的土地都归乔利金基国王，所有外乡人都必须带到他面前，于是叫他们跟着走。
feedback.en: The man says all these lands belong to the King of the Jolliginki and every stranger must be brought before him, so they must follow him.

grammar.excerpt: I swam as long as I could

focus.zh: as … as 是同级比较：as long as I could 就是「能游多久就游多久」，第二个 as 后面接从句。
focus.en: As … as compares two things as equal: as long as I could means “for as long as I was able”; the second as starts a clause.

paragraphs.text: When they had gone a little way through the thick forest, they came to a wide, clear space; and they saw the King’s palace which was made of mud.

sentences.text: When they had gone a little way through the thick forest, they came to a wide, clear space; and they saw the King’s palace which was made of mud.
sentences.zh: 他们在茂密的森林里走了一小段路，来到一片开阔的空地；只见国王的宫殿就在眼前，是用泥巴盖成的。

paragraphs.text: This was where the King lived with his Queen, Ermintrude, and their son, Prince Bumpo. The Prince was away fishing for salmon in the river. But the King and Queen were sitting under an umbrella before the palace door. And Queen Ermintrude was asleep.

sentences.text: This was where the King lived with his Queen, Ermintrude, and their son, Prince Bumpo.
sentences.zh: 这里就是国王和王后埃明特鲁德，还有他们的儿子邦波王子住的地方。

sentences.text: The Prince was away fishing for salmon in the river.
sentences.zh: 王子到河里捕鲑鱼去了。

sentences.text: But the King and Queen were sitting under an umbrella before the palace door.
sentences.zh: 但国王和王后正坐在宫门前的阳伞下。

sentences.text: And Queen Ermintrude was asleep.
sentences.zh: 埃明特鲁德王后睡着了。

hints.zh: 埃明特鲁德，乔利金基国王的王后。
hints.en: Ermintrude, the Queen of Jolliginki.

hints.zh: 邦波王子，国王与王后的儿子。
hints.en: Prince Bumpo, the son of the King and Queen.

paragraphs.text: When the Doctor had come up to the palace the King asked him his business; and the Doctor told him why he had come to Africa.

sentences.text: When the Doctor had come up to the palace the King asked him his business; and the Doctor told him why he had come to Africa.
sentences.zh: 医生走到宫殿前，国王问他是来做什么的；医生便告诉他，自己为什么来到非洲。

paragraphs.text: “You may not travel through my lands,” said the King. “Many years ago a white man came to these shores; and I was very kind to him. But after he had dug holes in the ground to get the gold, and killed all the elephants to get their ivory tusks, he went away secretly in his ship— without so much as saying ‘Thank you.’ Never again shall a white man travel through the lands of Jolliginki.”

sentences.text: “You may not travel through my lands,” said the King.
sentences.zh: 「你不准从我的国土上经过。」国王说。

sentences.text: “Many years ago a white man came to these shores; and I was very kind to him.
sentences.zh: 「许多年前，有一个白人来到这片海岸；我对他非常和气。

sentences.text: But after he had dug holes in the ground to get the gold, and killed all the elephants to get their ivory tusks, he went away secretly in his ship— without so much as saying ‘Thank you.’
sentences.zh: 可他在土里挖洞取走金子，又杀光了所有大象，只为取它们的象牙，然后坐上自己的船悄悄走了——连一句『谢谢』都没说。

sentences.text: Never again shall a white man travel through the lands of Jolliginki.”
sentences.zh: 白人再也休想从乔利金基的国土上经过。」

hints.zh: 乔利金基，非洲的一个王国，这位国王的领地。
hints.en: Jolliginki, the African kingdom ruled by this King.

hints.zh: 连……都没说；so much as 用在否定句里，强调连最小的事都没做。
hints.en: Without so much as saying: not even saying — the phrase stresses how little he did.

paragraphs.text: Then the King turned to some of the black men who were standing near and said, “Take away this medicine-man—with all his animals, and lock them up in my strongest prison.”

sentences.text: Then the King turned to some of the black men who were standing near and said, “Take away this medicine-man—with all his animals, and lock them up in my strongest prison.”
sentences.zh: 于是国王转向站在旁边的几个黑人，说：「把这个巫医——连同他所有的动物，一起带走，关进我最坚固的监狱。」

hints.zh: 巫医；这里国王轻蔑地用它称呼医生，觉得他靠巫术治病。
hints.en: A medicine-man: the King uses the word scornfully for a healer who works by magic.

paragraphs.text: So six of the black men led the Doctor and all his pets away and shut them up in a stone dungeon. The dungeon had only one little window, high up in the wall, with bars in it; and the door was strong and thick.

sentences.text: So six of the black men led the Doctor and all his pets away and shut them up in a stone dungeon.
sentences.zh: 于是六个黑人把医生和他所有的宠物带走，关进一间石头砌成的地牢。

sentences.text: The dungeon had only one little window, high up in the wall, with bars in it; and the door was strong and thick.
sentences.zh: 地牢里只有一扇小窗，高高地开在墙上，还装着铁栅栏；门又厚又结实。

introduction.zh: 杜立德医生带着动物们穿过密林，终于来到乔利金基国王的宫殿——一座用泥巴盖成的王宫。国王和王后正坐在门前的阳伞下，王后已经睡着了。医生走上前去，说明自己为什么来到非洲——这位国王会怎么回答他？
introduction.en: The Doctor and his animals come through the thick forest to the King of Jolliginki’s palace, which is made of mud. The King and Queen sit outside under an umbrella; the Queen is asleep. The Doctor explains why he has come to Africa — what will the King say?

quiz.question: Why will the King not let a white man travel through his lands?
options: A white man once took gold and ivory and left without a word of thanks.
The Doctor has no money to pay for the journey.
The King is afraid of the Doctor’s animals.

feedback.zh: 国王说，多年前一个白人挖走金子、杀象取牙，然后偷偷坐船走了，连句『谢谢』都没说，所以他再也不许白人过境。
feedback.en: The King remembers a white man who dug for gold, killed elephants for their tusks and slipped away without even saying thank you.

quiz.question: Where is Prince Bumpo when the Doctor arrives?
options: Asleep under the umbrella with the Queen.
Locked in the King’s strongest prison.
Away fishing for salmon in the river.

feedback.zh: 原文说王子到河里捕鲑鱼去了；在宫门前的是国王和王后，王后还睡着了。
feedback.en: The text says the Prince was away fishing for salmon in the river; only the King and Queen were at the palace door.

grammar.excerpt: Never again shall a white man travel through the lands of Jolliginki.

focus.zh: Never again 置于句首，助动词 shall 要提到主语 a white man 前面；这是强调「再也不会」，不是疑问句。
focus.en: Putting Never again at the front pulls the auxiliary shall before the subject a white man; this is emphasis, not a question.

paragraphs.text: Then they all grew very sad; and Gub-Gub, the pig, began to cry. But Chee-Chee said he would spank him if he didn’t stop that horrible noise; and he kept quiet.

sentences.text: Then they all grew very sad; and Gub-Gub, the pig, began to cry.
sentences.zh: 于是大家都非常难过；小猪咕咕哭了起来。

sentences.text: But Chee-Chee said he would spank him if he didn’t stop that horrible noise; and he kept quiet.
sentences.zh: 可奇奇说，他要是再不停下那难听的哭声，就揍他一顿；咕咕便安静了。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生养的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s little pig.

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey.

paragraphs.text: “Are we all here?” asked the Doctor, after he had got used to the dim light.

sentences.text: “Are we all here?” asked the Doctor, after he had got used to the dim light.
sentences.zh: 「我们都在这里吗？」医生适应了昏暗的光线后问道。

paragraphs.text: “Yes, I think so,” said the duck and started to count them.

sentences.text: “Yes, I think so,” said the duck and started to count them.
sentences.zh: 「是的，我想都在。」鸭子说着，开始数起来。

paragraphs.text: “Where’s Polynesia?” asked the crocodile. “She isn’t here.”

sentences.text: “Where’s Polynesia?” asked the crocodile.
sentences.zh: 「波利尼西亚在哪儿？」鳄鱼问。

sentences.text: “She isn’t here.”
sentences.zh: 「她不在这儿。」

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉，会说话，也能模仿人声。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor’s parrot, who can talk and mimic voices.

paragraphs.text: “Are you sure?” said the Doctor. “Look again. Polynesia! Polynesia! Where are you?”

sentences.text: “Are you sure?” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「你肯定吗？」医生说。

sentences.text: “Look again.
sentences.zh: 「再仔细看看。

sentences.text: Polynesia!
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚！

sentences.text: Polynesia!
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚！

sentences.text: Where are you?”
sentences.zh: 你在哪儿？」

paragraphs.text: “I suppose she escaped,” grumbled the crocodile. “Well, that’s just like her!—Sneaked off into the jungle as soon as her friends got into trouble.”

sentences.text: “I suppose she escaped,” grumbled the crocodile.
sentences.zh: 「我猜她是逃走了，」鳄鱼嘟囔道。

sentences.text: “Well, that’s just like her!—Sneaked off into the jungle as soon as her friends got into trouble.”
sentences.zh: 「哼，这太像她了！——朋友们一有麻烦，她就溜进丛林里去了。」

hints.zh: 偷偷溜走；鳄鱼用它埋怨鹦鹉不告而别。
hints.en: Sneaked off: slipped away secretly, as the crocodile complains she did.

paragraphs.text: “I’m not that kind of a bird,” said the parrot, climbing out of the pocket in the tail of the Doctor’s coat. “You see, I’m small enough to get through the bars of that window; and I was afraid they would put me in a cage instead. So while the King was busy talking, I hid in the Doctor’s pocket—and here I am! That’s what you call a ‘ruse,’” she said, smoothing down her feathers with her beak.

sentences.text: “I’m not that kind of a bird,” said the parrot, climbing out of the pocket in the tail of the Doctor’s coat.
sentences.zh: 「我可不是那种鸟，」鹦鹉说着，从医生外套后摆的口袋里爬了出来。

sentences.text: “You see, I’m small enough to get through the bars of that window; and I was afraid they would put me in a cage instead.
sentences.zh: 「你看，我个子小，能从那个窗口的铁栅栏之间钻出去；可我怕他们反倒把我关进笼子里。

sentences.text: So while the King was busy talking, I hid in the Doctor’s pocket—and here I am!
sentences.zh: 所以国王忙着说话的时候，我就躲进医生的口袋里——这不，我在这儿呢！

sentences.text: That’s what you call a ‘ruse,’” she said, smoothing down her feathers with her beak.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们说的『计策』，」她说着，用喙把羽毛捋平。

hints.zh: 计策、花招；波利尼西亚得意地说自己使了个小计谋。
hints.en: A ruse: a trick or piece of cunning, which she is proud of.

paragraphs.text: “Good Gracious!” cried the Doctor. “You’re lucky I didn’t sit on you.”

sentences.text: “Good Gracious!” cried the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「老天爷！」医生叫道。

sentences.text: “You’re lucky I didn’t sit on you.”
sentences.zh: 「算你走运，我没一屁股坐到你身上。」

paragraphs.text: “Now listen,” said Polynesia, “to-night, as soon as it gets dark, I am going to creep through the bars of that window and fly over to the palace. And then—you’ll see—I’ll soon find a way to make the King let us all out of prison.”

sentences.text: “Now listen,” said Polynesia, “to-night, as soon as it gets dark, I am going to creep through the bars of that window and fly over to the palace.
sentences.zh: 「听我说，」波利尼西亚说，「今晚天一黑，我就从那个窗口的铁栅栏间钻出去，飞到王宫去。

sentences.text: And then—you’ll see—I’ll soon find a way to make the King let us all out of prison.”
sentences.zh: 然后——你等着瞧——我很快就能想出办法，让国王把我们全都放出监狱。」

paragraphs.text: “Oh, what can you do?” said Gub-Gub, turning up his nose and beginning to cry again. “You’re only a bird!”

sentences.text: “Oh, what can you do?” said Gub-Gub, turning up his nose and beginning to cry again.
sentences.zh: 「唉，你能做什么呢？」咕咕说着，翘起鼻子，又要哭起来。

sentences.text: “You’re only a bird!”
sentences.zh: 「你不过是只鸟！」

introduction.zh: 六个黑人把医生和动物们关进石砌的地牢，只有墙高处一扇带铁栅栏的小窗，门又厚又结实。大家难过起来，小猪咕咕哭个不停。鸭子开始清点人数——她会数出什么来？
introduction.en: Six men shut the Doctor and his pets into a stone dungeon, where one little window sits high in the wall and the door is thick and strong. Everyone is sad, and Gub-Gub begins to cry. The duck starts to count them — what will she find?

quiz.question: Why did Polynesia hide in the Doctor’s pocket?
options: She was tired and wanted a warm place to sleep.
She was small enough to slip through the bars, but she was afraid of being put in a cage.
She wanted to listen to what the King would say.

feedback.zh: 她说自己个子小，本可以从铁栅栏间钻出去，但怕他们把她关进笼子，就躲进了医生的口袋。
feedback.en: She says she could have got through the bars, but she was afraid they would put her in a cage instead.

quiz.question: What does the crocodile think has happened to Polynesia?
options: She has sneaked off into the jungle because her friends are in trouble.
She has been taken away by the King’s men.
She is hiding somewhere in the dungeon.

feedback.zh: 鳄鱼嘟囔说她准是逃走了，还抱怨「这太像她了」——朋友一有麻烦就溜进丛林。
feedback.en: The crocodile grumbles that she has escaped: it is just like her to sneak off when her friends are in trouble.

grammar.excerpt: as soon as it gets dark, I am going to creep through the bars of that window

focus.zh: as soon as 从句讲将来的事，却用一般现在时 gets；主句用 be going to 表示已经打算好的行动。
focus.en: The clause after as soon as refers to the future but uses the present tense gets; the main clause uses be going to for a plan.

paragraphs.text: “Quite true,” said the parrot. “But do not forget that although I am only a bird, I can talk like a man—and I know these darkies.”

sentences.text: “Quite true,” said the parrot.
sentences.zh: 「说得一点不错，」鹦鹉说。

sentences.text: “But do not forget that although I am only a bird, I can talk like a man—and I know these darkies.”
sentences.zh: 「可别忘了，我虽然只是只鸟，却能像人一样说话——而且我了解这些黑人。」

hints.zh: 旧时对黑人的轻慢称呼；这里波利尼西亚随口说来，表示自己熟悉当地人。
hints.en: An old, belittling word for Black people; the parrot uses it casually to say she knows the locals.

paragraphs.text: So that night, when the moon was shining through the palm-trees and all the King’s men were asleep, the parrot slipped out through the bars of the prison and flew across to the palace. The pantry window had been broken by a tennis ball the week before; and Polynesia popped in through the hole in the glass.

sentences.text: So that night, when the moon was shining through the palm-trees and all the King’s men were asleep, the parrot slipped out through the bars of the prison and flew across to the palace.
sentences.zh: 于是那天夜里，月光透过棕榈树照下来，国王的部下都睡着了，鹦鹉从牢房的铁栅栏间溜了出去，飞向王宫。

sentences.text: The pantry window had been broken by a tennis ball the week before; and Polynesia popped in through the hole in the glass.
sentences.zh: 食品间的窗户上周被网球打破过；波利尼西亚就从玻璃上的破洞里钻了进去。

hints.zh: 国王的部下，这里指王宫里的卫兵和仆人。
hints.en: The King’s men: his soldiers and servants.

paragraphs.text: She heard Prince Bumpo snoring in his bedroom at the back of the palace. Then she tip-toed up the stairs till she came to the King’s bedroom. She opened the door gently and peeped in.

sentences.text: She heard Prince Bumpo snoring in his bedroom at the back of the palace.
sentences.zh: 她听见邦波王子在王宫后部的卧室里打呼噜。

sentences.text: Then she tip-toed up the stairs till she came to the King’s bedroom.
sentences.zh: 然后她踮着脚上楼，一直走到国王的卧室。

sentences.text: She opened the door gently and peeped in.
sentences.zh: 她轻轻推开门，往里偷看。

paragraphs.text: The Queen was away at a dance that night at her cousin’s; but the King was in bed fast asleep.

sentences.text: The Queen was away at a dance that night at her cousin’s; but the King was in bed fast asleep.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上王后到表亲家参加舞会去了；国王却躺在床上，睡得正熟。

hints.zh: 熟睡；fast 在这里不是「快」，而是「沉沉地」。
hints.en: Fast asleep means deeply asleep; fast here does not mean quickly.

paragraphs.text: Polynesia crept in, very softly, and got under the bed.

sentences.text: Polynesia crept in, very softly, and got under the bed.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚轻手轻脚地爬进去，钻到床底下。

paragraphs.text: Then she coughed—just the way Doctor Dolittle used to cough. Polynesia could mimic any one.

sentences.text: Then she coughed—just the way Doctor Dolittle used to cough.
sentences.zh: 接着她咳了一声——正是杜立德医生平时咳嗽的样子。

sentences.text: Polynesia could mimic any one.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚能模仿任何人。

hints.zh: 模仿别人的声音或样子。
hints.en: To mimic: to copy someone’s voice or way of speaking.

paragraphs.text: The King opened his eyes and said sleepily: “Is that you, Ermintrude?” (He thought it was the Queen come back from the dance.)

sentences.text: The King opened his eyes and said sleepily: “Is that you, Ermintrude?” (He thought it was the Queen come back from the dance.)
sentences.zh: 国王睁开眼睛，睡意朦胧地说：「是你吗，埃明特鲁德？」（他以为是王后跳完舞回来了。）

paragraphs.text: Then the parrot coughed again—loud, like a man. And the King sat up, wide awake, and said, “Who’s that?”

sentences.text: Then the parrot coughed again—loud, like a man.
sentences.zh: 接着鹦鹉又咳了一声——声音很响，像个男人。

sentences.text: And the King sat up, wide awake, and said, “Who’s that?”
sentences.zh: 国王坐起身，完全醒了，说：「是谁？」

paragraphs.text: “I am Doctor Dolittle,” said the parrot—just the way the Doctor would have said it.

sentences.text: “I am Doctor Dolittle,” said the parrot—just the way the Doctor would have said it.
sentences.zh: 「我是杜立德医生，」鹦鹉说——正是医生会有的那种口气。

paragraphs.text: “What are you doing in my bedroom?” cried the King. “How dare you get out of prison! Where are you?—I don’t see you.”

sentences.text: “What are you doing in my bedroom?” cried the King.
sentences.zh: 「你在我卧室里干什么？」国王叫道。

sentences.text: “How dare you get out of prison!
sentences.zh: 「你竟敢从监狱里逃出来！

sentences.text: Where are you?—I don’t see you.”
sentences.zh: 你在哪儿？——我看不见你。」

introduction.zh: 那天夜里，王宫的人都睡了，波利尼西亚从牢窗钻出去，飞过夜空。食品间的玻璃窗早被网球打破，她就从破洞钻进去，踮着脚上楼，来到国王的卧室。国王睡得正熟，她却在床底下咳了一声——正是杜立德医生的那种咳嗽。
introduction.en: That night the parrot slips out through the bars and flies to the palace. She pops in through a broken pantry window, tip-toes up to the King’s bedroom and finds him asleep. Then, under his bed, she coughs — just like Doctor Dolittle.

quiz.question: How does Polynesia get into the palace?
options: Through the King’s bedroom door, which was left open.
Through the bars of the King’s window.
Through the hole in the broken pantry window.

feedback.zh: 食品间的窗户上周被网球打破，波利尼西亚就从玻璃的破洞钻了进去。
feedback.en: The pantry window had been broken by a tennis ball, and she popped in through the hole in the glass.

quiz.question: Why does the King ask, “Is that you, Ermintrude?”
