options: He hears the Queen calling him from the stairs.
He thinks the Queen has come back from the dance.
He is still dreaming about the Queen.

feedback.zh: 他睡得迷迷糊糊，听见咳嗽声，以为是去表亲家跳舞的王后回来了。
feedback.en: He is sleepy and thinks the Queen has come back from the dance at her cousin’s.

grammar.excerpt: although I am only a bird, I can talk like a man

focus.zh: although 引出让步从句「虽然我只是只鸟」，主句 I can talk like a man 才是重点；中文不再加「但是」。
focus.en: Although introduces a concession — she is only a bird — and the main clause carries the point: she can talk like a man.

paragraphs.text: But the parrot just laughed—a long, deep, jolly laugh, like the Doctor’s.

sentences.text: But the parrot just laughed—a long, deep, jolly laugh, like the Doctor’s.
sentences.zh: 可鹦鹉只是笑——又长又低沉的开怀大笑，跟医生一模一样。

paragraphs.text: “Stop laughing and come here at once, so I can see you,” said the King.

sentences.text: “Stop laughing and come here at once, so I can see you,” said the King.
sentences.zh: 「别笑了，马上过来，让我看看你，」国王说。

paragraphs.text: “Foolish King!” answered Polynesia. “Have you forgotten that you are talking to John Dolittle, M.D.—the most wonderful man on earth? Of course you cannot see me. I have made myself invisible. There is nothing I cannot do. Now listen: I have come here to-night to warn you. If you don’t let me and my animals travel through your kingdom, I will make you and all your people sick like the monkeys. For I can make people well: and I can make people ill—just by raising my little finger. Send your soldiers at once to open the dungeon door, or you shall have mumps before the morning sun has risen on the hills of Jolliginki.”

sentences.text: “Foolish King!” answered Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「愚蠢的国王！」波利尼西亚答道。

sentences.text: “Have you forgotten that you are talking to John Dolittle, M.D.—the most wonderful man on earth?
sentences.zh: 「你难道忘了，你是在跟约翰·杜立德医学博士说话——天底下最了不起的人？

sentences.text: Of course you cannot see me.
sentences.zh: 你当然看不见我。

sentences.text: I have made myself invisible.
sentences.zh: 我已经让自己隐身了。

sentences.text: There is nothing I cannot do.
sentences.zh: 没有我做不到的事。

sentences.text: Now listen: I have come here to-night to warn you.
sentences.zh: 现在听着：我今晚来这儿，是要警告你。

sentences.text: If you don’t let me and my animals travel through your kingdom, I will make you and all your people sick like the monkeys.
sentences.zh: 你要是不让我和我的动物们从你的王国经过，我就让你和你所有的子民都像那些猴子一样病倒。

sentences.text: For I can make people well: and I can make people ill—just by raising my little finger.
sentences.zh: 因为我能让人痊愈，也能让人生病——只消抬一抬我的小指头。

sentences.text: Send your soldiers at once to open the dungeon door, or you shall have mumps before the morning sun has risen on the hills of Jolliginki.”
sentences.zh: 马上派士兵去打开地牢的门，否则，不等太阳升上乔利金基的山头，你就要得腮腺炎了。」

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德医学博士；M.D. 是医学博士（Doctor of Medicine）的缩写。
hints.en: John Dolittle, M.D.: M.D. stands for Doctor of Medicine.

hints.zh: 抬一抬小指头；她声称只动一下小指就能让人病倒。
hints.en: Raising my little finger: she claims this tiny gesture is enough to make people ill.

hints.zh: 腮腺炎，一种让脸颊和下巴肿起来的传染病。
hints.en: Mumps: a disease that makes the cheeks and jaw swell.

paragraphs.text: Then the King began to tremble and was very much afraid.

sentences.text: Then the King began to tremble and was very much afraid.
sentences.zh: 国王开始发抖，害怕极了。

paragraphs.text: “Doctor,” he cried, “it shall be as you say. Do not raise your little finger, please!” And he jumped out of bed and ran to tell the soldiers to open the prison door.

sentences.text: “Doctor,” he cried, “it shall be as you say.
sentences.zh: 「医生，」他叫道，「就照你说的办。

sentences.text: Do not raise your little finger, please!”
sentences.zh: 求你别抬起你的小指头！」

sentences.text: And he jumped out of bed and ran to tell the soldiers to open the prison door.
sentences.zh: 他跳下床，跑去吩咐士兵打开监狱的门。

hints.target: it shall be as you say
hints.zh: 就照你说的办；shall 在这里是旧式说法，表示许诺或顺从。
hints.en: It shall be as you say: an old-fashioned way of promising to do as he asks.

paragraphs.text: As soon as he was gone, Polynesia crept downstairs and left the palace by the pantry window.

sentences.text: As soon as he was gone, Polynesia crept downstairs and left the palace by the pantry window.
sentences.zh: 他刚一走，波利尼西亚就爬下楼，从食品间的窗户离开了王宫。

paragraphs.text: But the Queen, who was just letting herself in at the backdoor with a latch-key, saw the parrot getting out through the broken glass. And when the King came back to bed she told him what she had seen.

sentences.text: But the Queen, who was just letting herself in at the backdoor with a latch-key, saw the parrot getting out through the broken glass.
sentences.zh: 可王后正用随身钥匙从后门进屋，恰好看见鹦鹉从破玻璃窗里钻出去。

sentences.text: And when the King came back to bed she told him what she had seen.
sentences.zh: 国王回到床上时，她把自己看见的事告诉了他。

hints.zh: 弹簧锁钥匙，出门随身带的门钥匙。
hints.en: A latch-key: a door key carried by someone who lives there.

paragraphs.text: Then the King understood that he had been tricked, and he was dreadfully angry. He hurried back to the prison at once.

sentences.text: Then the King understood that he had been tricked, and he was dreadfully angry.
sentences.zh: 国王这才明白自己上了当，气得要命。

sentences.text: He hurried back to the prison at once.
sentences.zh: 他立刻赶回监狱。

paragraphs.text: But he was too late. The door stood open. The dungeon was empty. The Doctor and all his animals were gone.

sentences.text: But he was too late.
sentences.zh: 可他还是来晚了一步。

sentences.text: The door stood open.
sentences.zh: 牢门大开着。

sentences.text: The dungeon was empty.
sentences.zh: 地牢里空无一人。

sentences.text: The Doctor and all his animals were gone.
sentences.zh: 医生和他所有的动物都不见了。

introduction.zh: 卧室里，国王又惊又怒，要这个看不见的『医生』立刻现形。波利尼西亚却笑得更大声，自称是隐身了的杜立德医生，还说到天亮之前，自有分晓。国王会相信她吗？
introduction.en: In his bedroom the angry, frightened King orders the unseen “Doctor” to show himself at once. But the parrot only laughs and says she is John Dolittle, invisible, and that before sunrise the King will see what she can do. Will he believe her?

quiz.question: What does Polynesia say will happen if the King does not let them go?
options: She will make the King and all his people sick like the monkeys.
She will take the King’s gold and ivory.
She will turn the King into a monkey.

feedback.zh: 她威胁说，要是国王不放行，她就让他和所有子民都像猴子一样病倒。
feedback.en: She threatens to make the King and all his people sick like the monkeys.

quiz.question: Why does the King hurry back to the prison?
options: He wants to apologize to the Doctor for locking him up.
He hears the Doctor and the animals singing in the dungeon.
He realizes that the Queen saw the parrot and that he has been tricked.

feedback.zh: 王后把自己看见鹦鹉从破窗钻出去的事告诉他，国王这才明白受了骗，气得赶回监狱。
feedback.en: The Queen tells him she saw the parrot leaving, so he understands he has been tricked.

grammar.excerpt: If you don’t let me and my animals travel through your kingdom, I will make you and all your people sick like the monkeys.

focus.zh: if 从句用一般现在时 don’t let 讲条件，主句用 will make 讲后果；从句里不能用 will。
focus.en: The if-clause uses the present tense don’t let for a future condition, and the main clause uses will make for the result; no will in the if-clause.

paragraphs.text: Queen Ermintrude had never in her life seen her husband so terrible as he got that night. He gnashed his teeth with rage. He called everybody a fool. He threw his tooth-brush at the palace cat. He rushed round in his night-shirt and woke up all his army and sent them into the jungle to catch the Doctor. Then he made all his servants go too—his cooks and his gardeners and his barber and Prince Bumpo’s tutor—even the Queen, who was tired from dancing in a pair of tight shoes, was packed off to help the soldiers in their search.

sentences.text: Queen Ermintrude had never in her life seen her husband so terrible as he got that night.
sentences.zh: 埃明特鲁德王后一辈子没见过丈夫像那天夜里那样可怕。

sentences.text: He gnashed his teeth with rage.
sentences.zh: 他气得咬牙切齿。

sentences.text: He called everybody a fool.
sentences.zh: 他骂所有人都是蠢货。

sentences.text: He threw his tooth-brush at the palace cat.
sentences.zh: 他把牙刷朝宫里的猫扔过去。

sentences.text: He rushed round in his night-shirt and woke up all his army and sent them into the jungle to catch the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 他穿着睡袍满屋子乱转，把整支军队都叫醒，派他们进丛林去抓医生。

sentences.text: Then he made all his servants go too—his cooks and his gardeners and his barber and Prince Bumpo’s tutor—even the Queen, who was tired from dancing in a pair of tight shoes, was packed off to help the soldiers in their search.
sentences.zh: 接着他又把所有仆人都打发去了——厨子、园丁、理发师，还有邦波王子的家庭教师——就连跳舞跳累了、鞋子又紧的王后，也被打发去帮着士兵一起搜。

hints.zh: 埃明特鲁德王后，乔利金基国王的妻子。
hints.en: Queen Ermintrude, the wife of the King of Jolliginki.

hints.zh: 咬牙切齿，形容气到极点。
hints.en: Ground his teeth together in fury.

hints.zh: 睡袍，旧时男人睡觉穿的长衫；国王就穿着它冲了出去。
hints.en: A long shirt worn in bed; the King runs out in his.

hints.zh: 邦波王子的家庭教师；邦波是国王的儿子。
hints.en: Prince Bumpo’s tutor; Bumpo is the King’s son.

paragraphs.text: All this time the Doctor and his animals were running through the forest towards the Land of the Monkeys as fast as they could go.

sentences.text: All this time the Doctor and his animals were running through the forest towards the Land of the Monkeys as fast as they could go.
sentences.zh: 这期间，医生和他的动物们一直在森林里飞奔，朝着猴子国拼命赶路。

hints.zh: 猴子国，猴子们住的地方，也是医生这趟要去的终点。
hints.en: The Land of the Monkeys, where the monkeys live and where the Doctor is heading.

paragraphs.text: Gub-Gub, with his short legs, soon got tired; and the Doctor had to carry him—which made it pretty hard when they had the trunk and the hand-bag with them as well.

sentences.text: Gub-Gub, with his short legs, soon got tired; and the Doctor had to carry him—which made it pretty hard when they had the trunk and the hand-bag with them as well.
sentences.zh: 咕咕腿短，很快就累了；医生只好抱着他——他们身边还带着大皮箱和手提包，这就更难了。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪，腿短，走不快。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s pig, whose legs are short.

introduction.zh: 那一夜，埃明特鲁德王后从没见过丈夫气成这副样子：他咬牙切齿，把牙刷扔向宫里的猫，连夜把整支军队赶进丛林。就在同一刻，杜立德医生带着动物在森林里拼命跑；咕咕腿短，很快就跑不动了。
introduction.en: Queen Ermintrude has never seen her husband so angry. That night the King throws his tooth-brush at the palace cat and sends his whole army into the jungle to catch the Doctor. The Doctor’s animals run through the forest, but Gub-Gub’s short legs soon give out.

quiz.question: What does the King throw at the palace cat?
options: A book from the palace
His tooth-brush
His night-shirt

feedback.zh: 国王气极了，抓起牙刷就朝宫里的猫扔过去；课文还写他咬牙切齿、骂所有人是蠢货。
feedback.en: The King is in such a rage that he throws his tooth-brush at the palace cat.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor have to carry Gub-Gub?
options: Gub-Gub’s legs are short and he soon gets tired
Gub-Gub has hurt one of his feet
Gub-Gub has fallen asleep on the road

feedback.zh: 咕咕腿短，很快就走累了，医生只好抱着他；他们同时还带着大皮箱和手提包，所以格外吃力。
feedback.en: Gub-Gub has short legs and soon gets tired, so the Doctor carries him — hard work with the trunk and the hand-bag as well.

grammar.excerpt: Then he made all his servants go too

focus.zh: made all his servants go：make 表示「让、使」，后面接宾语和动词原形 go，不加 to。
focus.en: Made + servants + go: make takes an object and the bare verb, with no to.

title.en: A Long Night in a Tree

paragraphs.text: The King of the Jolliginki thought it would be easy for his army to find them, because the Doctor was in a strange land and would not know his way. But he was wrong; because the monkey, Chee-Chee, knew all the paths through the jungle—better even than the King’s men did. And he led the Doctor and his pets to the very thickest part of the forest—a place where no man had ever been before—and hid them all in a big hollow tree between high rocks.

sentences.text: The King of the Jolliginki thought it would be easy for his army to find them, because the Doctor was in a strange land and would not know his way.
sentences.zh: 乔利金基国王以为他的军队找到他们很容易，因为医生身在异乡，不认得路。

sentences.text: But he was wrong; because the monkey, Chee-Chee, knew all the paths through the jungle—better even than the King’s men did.
sentences.zh: 但他错了：猴子奇奇熟悉丛林里所有的路——甚至比国王的手下还熟。

sentences.text: And he led the Doctor and his pets to the very thickest part of the forest—a place where no man had ever been before—and hid them all in a big hollow tree between high rocks.
sentences.zh: 他把医生和他的宠物们带到森林最密的地方——一个从来没有人到过的地方——把他们全藏进高岩之间一棵空心的大树里。

hints.zh: 乔利金基国王，杜立德医生一行正在逃离的那位国王。
hints.en: The King of Jolliginki, the ruler the Doctor and his animals are running from.

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子，熟悉丛林里的每一条路。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey who knows every path in the jungle.

hints.zh: 国王的手下，这里指他派出来搜山的士兵。
hints.en: The King’s men: the soldiers he has sent to search for the Doctor.

paragraphs.text: “We had better wait here,” said Chee-Chee, “till the soldiers have gone back to bed. Then we can go on into the Land of the Monkeys.”

sentences.text: “We had better wait here,” said Chee-Chee, “till the soldiers have gone back to bed.
sentences.zh: 「我们最好在这儿等着，」奇奇说，「等士兵们回去睡了。

sentences.text: Then we can go on into the Land of the Monkeys.”
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以继续赶路，进猴子国了。」

paragraphs.text: So there they stayed the whole night through.

sentences.text: So there they stayed the whole night through.
sentences.zh: 他们就这样在那儿待了整整一夜。

paragraphs.text: They often heard the King’s men searching and talking in the jungle round about. But they were quite safe, for no one knew of that hiding-place but Chee-Chee—not even the other monkeys.

sentences.text: They often heard the King’s men searching and talking in the jungle round about.
sentences.zh: 他们不时听见国王的手下在四周的丛林里搜寻、说话。

sentences.text: But they were quite safe, for no one knew of that hiding-place but Chee-Chee—not even the other monkeys.
sentences.zh: 但他们很安全，因为除了奇奇，没人知道那个藏身之处——连别的猴子也不知道。

hints.zh: 这里的 but 是「除了」，不是「但是」：除了奇奇，谁也不知道这个地方。
hints.en: Here but means “except”: nobody knew the hiding-place except Chee-Chee.

paragraphs.text: At last, when daylight began to come through the thick leaves overhead, they heard Queen Ermintrude saying in a very tired voice that it was no use looking any more—that they might as well go back and get some sleep.

sentences.text: At last, when daylight began to come through the thick leaves overhead, they heard Queen Ermintrude saying in a very tired voice that it was no use looking any more—that they might as well go back and get some sleep.
sentences.zh: 最后，当晨光开始透过头顶厚厚的树叶照下来时，他们听见埃明特鲁德王后用十分疲倦的声音说，再找下去也没用了——大家不妨回去睡一觉。

hints.target: it was no use looking any more
hints.zh: 再找下去也没用了；no use doing 表示做某事没有意义。
hints.en: There was no point in searching any longer.

paragraphs.text: As soon as the soldiers had all gone home, Chee-Chee brought the Doctor and his animals out of the hiding-place and they set off for the Land of the Monkeys.

sentences.text: As soon as the soldiers had all gone home, Chee-Chee brought the Doctor and his animals out of the hiding-place and they set off for the Land of the Monkeys.
sentences.zh: 士兵们全都回家去之后，奇奇就把医生和他的动物们从藏身处领出来，他们动身前往猴子国。

hints.zh: 出发、动身。
hints.en: Set off: started on their way.

introduction.zh: 国王以为，在自己的地盘上抓一个外乡人很容易，可他没算到带路的是猴子奇奇。追兵在林子四周搜了一整夜，说话声近得能听见。他们藏身的地方，除了奇奇，连别的猴子都不知道。天亮以后，他们还走得成吗？
introduction.en: The King thinks his army will find the Doctor easily: the man is a stranger and does not know the paths. But Chee-Chee the monkey knows every path in the jungle. All night the soldiers search and talk nearby. Only Chee-Chee knows the hiding-place. Can they get away at daylight?

quiz.question: Why was the King wrong about finding the Doctor easily?
options: The Doctor had a map of the jungle
The army went to the wrong country
Chee-Chee knew the jungle paths better than the King’s men

feedback.zh: 国王以为外乡人不认路，可奇奇熟悉丛林里所有的路，甚至比国王的手下还熟，把他们藏进了空心树。
feedback.en: The King counted on the Doctor being a stranger, but Chee-Chee knew every path and hid them in a hollow tree.

quiz.question: What did the Queen say to the soldiers when daylight came?
options: That the Doctor had been caught in the night
That it was no use looking and they might as well go back to sleep
That they must search the jungle for another week

feedback.zh: 天亮时王后疲倦地说，再找下去也没用了，大家不妨回去睡一觉——士兵们这才撤走。
feedback.en: At daylight the Queen said in a tired voice that it was no use looking any more and they might as well go back and sleep.

grammar.excerpt: We had better wait here

focus.zh: had better + 动词原形 wait：表示「最好」，是奇奇的建议，跟过去时无关。
focus.en: Had better + wait: a fixed pattern for “it would be best to”, not a past tense.

paragraphs.text: It was a long, long way; and they often got very tired—especially Gub-Gub. But when he cried they gave him milk out of the cocoanuts, which he was very fond of.

sentences.text: It was a long, long way; and they often got very tired—especially Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 路很长很长；他们常常累得不行——尤其是咕咕。

sentences.text: But when he cried they gave him milk out of the cocoanuts, which he was very fond of.
sentences.zh: 可他一哭，他们就给他喝椰子里的奶，他特别喜欢这个。

hints.zh: 椰子；cocoanut 是 coconut 的旧拼法。
hints.en: Cocoanuts: an old spelling of coconuts.

paragraphs.text: They always had plenty to eat and drink; because Chee-Chee and Polynesia knew all the different kinds of fruits and vegetables that grow in the jungle, and where to find them—like dates and figs and ground-nuts and ginger and yams. They used to make their lemonade out of the juice of wild oranges, sweetened with honey which they got from the bees’ nests in hollow trees. No matter what it was they asked for, Chee-Chee and Polynesia always seemed to be able to get it for them—or something like it. They even got the Doctor some tobacco one day, when he had finished what he had brought with him and wanted to smoke.

sentences.text: They always had plenty to eat and drink; because Chee-Chee and Polynesia knew all the different kinds of fruits and vegetables that grow in the jungle, and where to find them—like dates and figs and ground-nuts and ginger and yams.
sentences.zh: 他们总有吃不完喝不完的东西；因为奇奇和波利尼西亚认得丛林里生长的各种水果和蔬菜，也知道上哪儿去找——比如椰枣、无花果、花生、姜和山药。

sentences.text: They used to make their lemonade out of the juice of wild oranges, sweetened with honey which they got from the bees’ nests in hollow trees.
sentences.zh: 他们常拿野橙子的汁做柠檬水，再掺上从空心树里的蜂巢取来的蜂蜜。

sentences.text: No matter what it was they asked for, Chee-Chee and Polynesia always seemed to be able to get it for them—or something like it.
sentences.zh: 不管他们要什么，奇奇和波利尼西亚似乎总能弄到——或者弄到差不多的东西。

sentences.text: They even got the Doctor some tobacco one day, when he had finished what he had brought with him and wanted to smoke.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他把随身带来的烟抽完了，正想抽烟，他们甚至替他弄到了一些烟草。

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉，见多识广，认得丛林里的各种吃食。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor’s parrot, who knows the jungle and its food.

hints.zh: 山药，热带地方当粮食的块根。
hints.en: Yams: large starchy roots eaten as food in hot countries.

hints.zh: 花生，果实长在地下的坚果。
hints.en: Ground-nuts: peanuts, which grow underground.

hints.target: No matter what it was they asked for
hints.zh: 不管他们提出要什么；no matter what 引出让步从句。
hints.en: Whatever they asked for: no matter what introduces the concession.

paragraphs.text: At night they slept in tents made of palm-leaves, on thick, soft beds of dried grass. And after a while they got used to walking such a lot and did not get so tired and enjoyed the life of travel very much.

sentences.text: At night they slept in tents made of palm-leaves, on thick, soft beds of dried grass.
sentences.zh: 夜里他们睡在棕榈叶搭的帐篷里，铺着厚厚的、软软的干草床。

sentences.text: And after a while they got used to walking such a lot and did not get so tired and enjoyed the life of travel very much.
sentences.zh: 过了一阵子，他们习惯了这样长途走路，不再那么累，也很喜欢这种旅行的生活。

hints.zh: 习惯了走这么多路；get used to 后接 -ing，和 used to do（过去常做）不是一回事。
hints.en: Got used to walking: became accustomed to it; get used to takes an -ing form.

paragraphs.text: But they were always glad when the night came and they stopped for their resting-time. Then the Doctor used to make a little fire of sticks; and after they had had their supper, they would sit round it in a ring, listening to Polynesia singing songs about the sea, or to Chee-Chee telling stories of the jungle.

sentences.text: But they were always glad when the night came and they stopped for their resting-time.
sentences.zh: 不过每当夜晚来临、他们停下来歇息时，大家总是很高兴。

sentences.text: Then the Doctor used to make a little fire of sticks; and after they had had their supper, they would sit round it in a ring, listening to Polynesia singing songs about the sea, or to Chee-Chee telling stories of the jungle.
sentences.zh: 那时医生常会用树枝生起一小堆火；吃过晚饭，他们就围成一圈坐着，听波利尼西亚唱关于大海的歌，或者听奇奇讲丛林里的故事。

introduction.zh: 路很长很长，咕咕常常喊累，可每次都能喝到椰子里的奶。丛林里能吃的东西多得数不清，奇奇和波利尼西亚总能弄到——连医生想抽的烟也有。到了夜里，他们围着小小的火堆坐下来，听歌，也听故事。
introduction.en: The way is long and Gub-Gub often cries with tiredness, but there is always milk from the cocoanuts. Chee-Chee and Polynesia can find fruit, nuts and honey, and even tobacco for the Doctor. At night everyone sits round a little fire. What do they hear there?

quiz.question: What did the travellers make their lemonade from?
options: Juice of wild oranges, sweetened with honey
River water and sugar from the jungle
Milk taken out of the cocoanuts

feedback.zh: 他们把野橙子的汁挤出来当柠檬水，再加上从空心树蜂巢里取来的蜂蜜。椰子里的是奶，不是柠檬水。
feedback.en: They made lemonade from the juice of wild oranges and sweetened it with honey from bees’ nests.

quiz.question: How did they spend their evenings on the way?
options: Sleeping in tents made of palm-leaves
Searching the jungle for fruit and honey
Sitting round a fire, listening to songs and stories

feedback.zh: 晚上医生生一小堆火，大家吃过晚饭围成一圈，听波利尼西亚唱海上的歌，或听奇奇讲丛林的故事。
feedback.en: The Doctor made a little fire, and after supper they sat in a ring listening to Polynesia’s songs or Chee-Chee’s stories.

grammar.excerpt: They used to make their lemonade out of the juice of wild oranges

focus.zh: used to make：used to 后面跟动词原形，讲的是过去常常这样做。
focus.en: Used to make: used to + base verb describes a habit in the past.

paragraphs.text: And many of the tales that Chee-Chee told were very interesting. Because although the monkeys had no history-books of their own before Doctor Dolittle came to write them for them, they remember everything that happens by telling stories to their children. And Chee-Chee spoke of many things his grandmother had told him—tales of long, long, long ago, before Noah and the Flood,—of the days when men dressed in bear-skins and lived in holes in the rock and ate their mutton raw, because they did not know what cooking was—having never seen a fire. And he told them of the Great Mammoths and Lizards, as long as a train, that wandered over the mountains in those times, nibbling from the tree-tops. And often they got so interested listening, that when he had finished they found their fire had gone right out; and they had to scurry round to get more sticks and build a new one.

sentences.text: And many of the tales that Chee-Chee told were very interesting.
sentences.zh: 奇奇讲的许多故事都非常有意思。

sentences.text: Because although the monkeys had no history-books of their own before Doctor Dolittle came to write them for them, they remember everything that happens by telling stories to their children.
sentences.zh: 因为，虽说在杜立德医生来替它们写史书之前，猴子们并没有自己的史书，它们却靠把故事讲给孩子听，记住发生的一切。

sentences.text: And Chee-Chee spoke of many things his grandmother had told him—tales of long, long, long ago, before Noah and the Flood,—of the days when men dressed in bear-skins and lived in holes in the rock and ate their mutton raw, because they did not know what cooking was—having never seen a fire.
sentences.zh: 奇奇讲了许多他奶奶告诉他的事——那些很久很久很久以前、诺亚与大洪水之前的故事——讲那时候的人穿着熊皮，住在岩洞里，吃生羊肉，因为他们不懂烹调——他们从没见过火。

sentences.text: And he told them of the Great Mammoths and Lizards, as long as a train, that wandered over the mountains in those times, nibbling from the tree-tops.
sentences.zh: 他还给他们讲那些像火车一样长的巨猛犸和巨蜥，当年它们在群山中游荡，啃食树梢。

sentences.text: And often they got so interested listening, that when he had finished they found their fire had gone right out; and they had to scurry round to get more sticks and build a new one.
sentences.zh: 常常他们听得太入神，等他讲完，才发现火已经彻底灭了；他们只好赶紧四下里捡来更多树枝，重新生一堆。

hints.zh: 杜立德医生，这本书的主角，会给动物看病。
hints.en: Doctor Dolittle, the doctor who can talk to animals.

hints.zh: 诺亚与大洪水，《圣经》里的故事，这里用来指极遥远的古代。
hints.en: Noah and the Flood: the Bible story, used here to mean a very distant past.

hints.zh: 熊皮，远古的人拿它当衣服穿。
hints.en: Bear-skins: bears’ skins worn as clothes.

hints.zh: 巨猛犸和巨蜥，远古时代的庞然巨兽。
hints.en: The Great Mammoths and Lizards: giant beasts of prehistoric times.

hints.zh: 急匆匆地跑；这里指赶紧四下里捡柴。
hints.en: Scurry round: hurry about in short quick movements.

paragraphs.text: Now when the King’s army had gone back and told the King that they couldn’t find the Doctor, the King sent them out again and told them they must stay in the jungle till they caught him. So all this time, while the Doctor and his animals were going along towards the Land of the Monkeys, thinking themselves quite safe, they were still being followed by the King’s men. If Chee-Chee had known this, he would most likely have hidden them again. But he didn’t know it.

sentences.text: Now when the King’s army had gone back and told the King that they couldn’t find the Doctor, the King sent them out again and told them they must stay in the jungle till they caught him.
sentences.zh: 再说国王的军队回去报告国王说找不到医生，国王就又把他们派了出去，吩咐他们必须待在丛林里，直到抓住他为止。

sentences.text: So all this time, while the Doctor and his animals were going along towards the Land of the Monkeys, thinking themselves quite safe, they were still being followed by the King’s men.
sentences.zh: 所以这一路上，医生和他的动物们朝猴子国走，自以为很安全，其实一直被国王的手下跟着。

sentences.text: If Chee-Chee had known this, he would most likely have hidden them again.
sentences.zh: 奇奇要是知道这一点，多半会再把他们藏起来。

sentences.text: But he didn’t know it.
sentences.zh: 可他并不知道。

introduction.zh: 猴子没有史书，却记得发生过的一切——它们把事讲给孩子听。奇奇讲的是奶奶传下来的故事：大洪水以前的年月，人穿熊皮、住山洞，吃生肉，因为从没见过火。故事听得入神，火灭了都没人察觉。
introduction.en: The monkeys have no history-books, but they remember everything by telling stories to their children. Chee-Chee repeats what his grandmother told him: men in bear-skins, mammoths as long as a train. The tales are so good that the fire goes out. Are they really as safe as they think?

quiz.question: How do the monkeys remember everything that happens?
options: By drawing pictures on the rocks
By telling stories to their children
By keeping history-books of their own

feedback.zh: 猴子本来没有史书，它们靠把发生过的事讲给孩子听，一代代记下来。
feedback.en: The monkeys had no history-books; they remember what happens by telling stories to their children.

quiz.question: Why did the fire go out while Chee-Chee was talking?
options: They were listening so hard that nobody watched it
A heavy rain put it out
They had no more sticks to burn

feedback.zh: 大家听得太入神，等故事讲完才发现火已经灭了；随后他们才赶紧去捡更多树枝重新生火。
feedback.en: They were so interested in the tales that they only found the fire had gone right out when he finished; then they had to get more sticks.

grammar.excerpt: although the monkeys had no history-books of their own before Doctor Dolittle came to write them for them

focus.zh: although 引出让步从句：猴子本来没有史书；主句 they remember 前不再加 but。
focus.en: Although introduces the concession, and the main clause needs no but.

paragraphs.text: One day Chee-Chee climbed up a high rock and looked out over the tree-tops. And when he came down he said they were now quite close to the Land of the Monkeys and would soon be there.

sentences.text: One day Chee-Chee climbed up a high rock and looked out over the tree-tops.
sentences.zh: 有一天，奇奇爬上一块高岩，朝树梢外眺望。

sentences.text: And when he came down he said they were now quite close to the Land of the Monkeys and would soon be there.
sentences.zh: 他下来以后说，他们现在已经离猴子国很近了，很快就能到。

paragraphs.text: And that same evening, sure enough, they saw Chee-Chee’s cousin and a lot of other monkeys, who had not yet got sick, sitting in the trees by the edge of a swamp, looking and waiting for them. And when they saw the famous doctor really come, these monkeys made a tremendous noise, cheering and waving leaves and swinging out of the branches to greet him.

sentences.text: And that same evening, sure enough, they saw Chee-Chee’s cousin and a lot of other monkeys, who had not yet got sick, sitting in the trees by the edge of a swamp, looking and waiting for them.
sentences.zh: 就在那天傍晚，他们果然看见奇奇的表亲，还有一大群还没生病的猴子，坐在沼泽边的树上，朝他们这边望着，等着他们。

sentences.text: And when they saw the famous doctor really come, these monkeys made a tremendous noise, cheering and waving leaves and swinging out of the branches to greet him.
sentences.zh: 这些猴子见那位名医真的来了，就闹出极大的动静，欢呼着，挥动树叶，从枝头荡下来迎接他。

hints.zh: 奇奇的表亲，也是猴子；它带着一群还没生病的猴子来接他们。
hints.en: Chee-Chee’s cousin, a monkey waiting with the others who are not yet ill.

hints.zh: 果然，表示事情正像预料的那样发生了。
hints.en: Sure enough: and it happened just as expected.

hints.zh: 还没生病；猴子国正闹病，这些是还没染上的猴子。
hints.en: Not yet ill: the sickness is the reason the Doctor is coming.

paragraphs.text: They wanted to carry his bag and his trunk and everything he had—and one of the bigger ones even carried Gub-Gub who had got tired again. Then two of them rushed on in front to tell the sick monkeys that the great doctor had come at last.

sentences.text: They wanted to carry his bag and his trunk and everything he had—and one of the bigger ones even carried Gub-Gub who had got tired again.
sentences.zh: 它们要替他拿包、拿箱子，拿他所有的东西——其中一只大些的猴子还把又走累了的咕咕抱了起来。

sentences.text: Then two of them rushed on in front to tell the sick monkeys that the great doctor had come at last.
sentences.zh: 接着有两只猴子抢先跑到前面，去告诉生病的猴子们：那位了不起的医生终于来了。

paragraphs.text: But the King’s men, who were still following, had heard the noise of the monkeys cheering; and they at last knew where the Doctor was, and hastened on to catch him.

sentences.text: But the King’s men, who were still following, had heard the noise of the monkeys cheering; and they at last knew where the Doctor was, and hastened on to catch him.
sentences.zh: 可是一直跟在后面的国王手下听见了猴子们的欢呼声；他们终于知道医生在哪儿，急忙赶上去抓他。

hints.zh: 急忙赶路；hasten 是较文的说法，相当于 hurry。
hints.en: Hastened on: hurried forward; hasten is a literary word for hurry.

paragraphs.text: The big monkey carrying Gub-Gub was coming along behind slowly, and he saw the Captain of the army sneaking through the trees. So he hurried after the Doctor and told him to run.

sentences.text: The big monkey carrying Gub-Gub was coming along behind slowly, and he saw the Captain of the army sneaking through the trees.
sentences.zh: 抱着咕咕的那只大猴子慢慢跟在后面，看见军队的上尉正从树间悄悄摸过来。

sentences.text: So he hurried after the Doctor and told him to run.
sentences.zh: 于是他赶紧追上医生，叫他快跑。

hints.zh: 这支军队的上尉，一路追他们的领头人。
hints.en: The Captain of the army, who is leading the chase.

paragraphs.text: Then they all ran harder than they had ever run in their lives; and the King’s men, coming after them, began to run too; and the Captain ran hardest of all.

sentences.text: Then they all ran harder than they had ever run in their lives; and the King’s men, coming after them, began to run too; and the Captain ran hardest of all.
sentences.zh: 于是他们全都跑得比这辈子任何时候都快；国王的手下在后面追，也跟着跑起来；上尉跑得最快。

introduction.zh: 奇奇爬上高岩，往树梢外一望，说快到了。傍晚，一群还没生病的猴子果然在沼泽边等着；一看见那位名医真的来了，它们就扯开嗓子欢呼，挥着树叶从枝头荡下来迎接。这声音传得很远。
introduction.en: Chee-Chee climbs a high rock, looks out over the tree-tops and says they are nearly there. That evening a crowd of monkeys waits by a swamp. When they see the famous doctor, they cheer, wave leaves and swing down from the branches. The noise carries a long way.

quiz.question: What did the monkeys do when they saw the Doctor really come?
options: They ran away into the swamp
They asked him to wait quietly in the trees
They cheered, waved leaves and swung down from the branches

feedback.zh: 猴子们见名医真的来了，就欢呼、挥叶子、从枝头荡下来迎接他，闹出很大的动静。
feedback.en: When they saw the famous doctor really come, the monkeys cheered, waved leaves and swung out of the branches to greet him.

quiz.question: How did the King’s men find out where the Doctor was?
options: Chee-Chee went back and told them
They heard the noise of the monkeys cheering
They found the marks of the Doctor’s fire

feedback.zh: 一直跟在后面的士兵听见了猴子欢呼的声音，这才知道医生在哪儿，急忙赶上来。
feedback.en: The King’s men, still following, heard the noise of the monkeys cheering and at last knew where the Doctor was.

grammar.excerpt: So he hurried after the Doctor and told him to run

focus.zh: told him to run：tell + 人 + to do，表示叫某人做某事，这里的 to 不能省。
focus.en: Told him to run: tell + person + to + verb; the to cannot be dropped.

title.en: At the Edge of the Cliff

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor tripped over his medicine-bag and fell down in the mud, and the Captain thought he would surely catch him this time.

sentences.text: Then the Doctor tripped over his medicine-bag and fell down in the mud, and the Captain thought he would surely catch him this time.
sentences.zh: 这时医生被药箱绊了一下，摔进泥里，上尉觉得自己这回准能抓住他了。

hints.zh: 被……绊倒；trip over 后面接绊到脚的东西。
hints.en: Tripped over: caught his foot on it and fell.

paragraphs.text: But the Captain had very long ears—though his hair was very short. And as he sprang forward to take hold of the Doctor, one of his ears caught fast in a tree; and the rest of the army had to stop and help him.

sentences.text: But the Captain had very long ears—though his hair was very short.
sentences.zh: 可上尉的耳朵非常长——尽管他的头发很短。

sentences.text: And as he sprang forward to take hold of the Doctor, one of his ears caught fast in a tree; and the rest of the army had to stop and help him.
sentences.zh: 就在他纵身向前去抓医生的时候，一只耳朵牢牢卡在树上；其余的人只好停下来帮他。

hints.zh: 纵身向前扑；spring 的过去式是 sprang。
hints.en: Sprang forward: jumped forward suddenly; sprang is the past of spring.

hints.zh: 牢牢卡住，动不了。
hints.en: Caught fast: stuck and unable to move.

paragraphs.text: By this time the Doctor had picked himself up, and on they went again, running and running. And Chee-Chee shouted,

sentences.text: By this time the Doctor had picked himself up, and on they went again, running and running.
sentences.zh: 这时候医生已经爬了起来，他们又继续往前跑，跑个不停。

sentences.text: And Chee-Chee shouted,
sentences.zh: 奇奇喊道：

paragraphs.text: “It’s all right! We haven’t far to go now!”

sentences.text: “It’s all right!
sentences.zh: 「没事！

sentences.text: We haven’t far to go now!”
sentences.zh: 我们没多远了！」

paragraphs.text: But before they could get into the Land of the Monkeys, they came to a steep cliff with a river flowing below. This was the end of the Kingdom of Jolliginki; and the Land of the Monkeys was on the other side—across the river.

sentences.text: But before they could get into the Land of the Monkeys, they came to a steep cliff with a river flowing below.
sentences.zh: 可他们还没能进入猴子国，就来到一道陡崖前，崖下有条河在流。

sentences.text: This was the end of the Kingdom of Jolliginki; and the Land of the Monkeys was on the other side—across the river.
sentences.zh: 这里是乔利金基王国的尽头；猴子国就在河对岸的另一边。

paragraphs.text: And Jip, the dog, looked down over the edge of the steep, steep cliff and said,

sentences.text: And Jip, the dog, looked down over the edge of the steep, steep cliff and said,
sentences.zh: 狗吉普从陡得吓人的崖边往下望，说：

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

paragraphs.text: “Golly! How are we ever going to get across?”

sentences.text: “Golly!
sentences.zh: 「天哪！

sentences.text: How are we ever going to get across?”
sentences.zh: 我们到底要怎么过去啊？」

hints.zh: 天哪！表示惊讶的老式感叹词。
hints.en: Golly!: an old exclamation of surprise.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, dear!” said Gub-Gub. “The King’s men are quite close now—Look at them! I am afraid we are going to be taken back to prison again.” And he began to weep.

sentences.text: “Oh, dear!” said Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「唉，天哪！」咕咕说。

sentences.text: “The King’s men are quite close now—Look at them!
sentences.zh: 「国王的手下已经离得很近了——你看他们！

sentences.text: I am afraid we are going to be taken back to prison again.”
sentences.zh: 我怕我们又要被抓回监狱去了。」

sentences.text: And he began to weep.
sentences.zh: 他哭了起来。

paragraphs.text: But the big monkey who was carrying the pig dropped him on the ground and cried out to the other monkeys,

sentences.text: But the big monkey who was carrying the pig dropped him on the ground and cried out to the other monkeys,
sentences.zh: 可抱着小猪的那只大猴子把咕咕放到地上，朝其他猴子大声喊：

paragraphs.text: “Boys—a bridge! Quick!—Make a bridge! We’ve only a minute to do it. They’ve got the Captain loose, and he’s coming on like a deer. Get lively! A bridge! A bridge!”

sentences.text: “Boys—a bridge!
sentences.zh: 「伙计们——搭桥！

sentences.text: Quick!—Make a bridge!
sentences.zh: 快！——搭座桥！

sentences.text: We’ve only a minute to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们只有一分钟的时间。

sentences.text: They’ve got the Captain loose, and he’s coming on like a deer.
sentences.zh: 他们把那上尉松开了，他正像鹿一样飞奔过来。

sentences.text: Get lively!
sentences.zh: 快点儿！

sentences.text: A bridge!
sentences.zh: 搭桥！

sentences.text: A bridge!”
sentences.zh: 搭桥！」

hints.zh: 快点儿、打起精神来；催人赶快动手的口语说法。
hints.en: Get lively!: hurry up, move quickly.

introduction.zh: 医生被药箱绊倒，摔进泥里，追他的上尉眼看就要抓住他。这位上尉有一对很长的耳朵，头发却很短。而前面等着他们的，是一道陡崖，崖下是河——猴子国在河那边。
introduction.en: The Doctor trips over his medicine-bag and falls in the mud, and the Captain thinks he has him. The Captain’s ears are very long. Ahead lies a steep cliff with a river below, and the Land of the Monkeys is on the far side. How can anyone cross?

quiz.question: Why couldn’t the Captain catch the Doctor?
options: One of his long ears caught fast in a tree
He slipped and fell into the river
The Doctor hit him with the medicine-bag

feedback.zh: 上尉纵身扑过去时，一只长耳朵牢牢卡在树上；其余士兵只好停下来帮他，医生趁机跑了。
feedback.en: As he sprang forward, one of his long ears caught fast in a tree, and the rest of the army had to stop and help him.

quiz.question: What stopped the Doctor and his animals before the Land of the Monkeys?
options: A high wall round the kingdom
A thick forest with no paths through it
A steep cliff with a river flowing below

feedback.zh: 他们还没进猴子国，就到了一道陡崖前，崖下是河；猴子国在河对岸。
feedback.en: Before they could get into the Land of the Monkeys, they came to a steep cliff with a river flowing below.

grammar.excerpt: as he sprang forward to take hold of the Doctor

focus.zh: as 引出时间从句：就在他纵身扑过去的时候，卡住耳朵这件事同时发生。
focus.en: As introduces the time clause: the two things happen at the same moment.

paragraphs.text: The Doctor began to wonder what they were going to make a bridge out of, and he gazed around to see if they had any boards hidden any place.

sentences.text: The Doctor began to wonder what they were going to make a bridge out of, and he gazed around to see if they had any boards hidden any place.
sentences.zh: 医生开始纳闷，他们到底要拿什么搭桥，就四下张望，看他们是不是在哪儿藏着木板。

paragraphs.text: But when he looked back at the cliff, there, hanging across the river, was a bridge all ready for him—made of living monkeys! For while his back was turned, the monkeys—quick as a flash—had made themselves into a bridge, just by holding hands and feet.

sentences.text: But when he looked back at the cliff, there, hanging across the river, was a bridge all ready for him—made of living monkeys!
sentences.zh: 可等他回头望那道崖，河上已经横着一座为他准备好的桥——竟是用活猴子搭成的！

sentences.text: For while his back was turned, the monkeys—quick as a flash—had made themselves into a bridge, just by holding hands and feet.
sentences.zh: 原来趁他背过身去的时候，猴子们快得像闪电，手拉手、脚勾脚，把自己搭成了一座桥。

paragraphs.text: And the big one shouted to the Doctor, “Walk over! Walk over—all of you—hurry!”

sentences.text: And the big one shouted to the Doctor, “Walk over!
sentences.zh: 那只大猴子朝医生喊：「走过来！

sentences.text: Walk over—all of you—hurry!”
sentences.zh: 都走过来——你们全都过来——快！」

paragraphs.text: Gub-Gub was a bit scared, walking on such a narrow bridge at that dizzy height above the river. But he got over all right; and so did all of them.

sentences.text: Gub-Gub was a bit scared, walking on such a narrow bridge at that dizzy height above the river.
sentences.zh: 咕咕有点害怕——走这么窄的一座桥，下面离河又那么高，让人眼晕。

sentences.text: But he got over all right; and so did all of them.
sentences.zh: 不过他还是顺利过去了；其余大家也都过去了。

hints.zh: 高得让人头晕的高度。
hints.en: Dizzy height: so high that it makes you giddy.

paragraphs.text: John Dolittle was the last to cross. And just as he was getting to the other side, the King’s men came rushing up to the edge of the cliff.

sentences.text: John Dolittle was the last to cross.
sentences.zh: 约翰·杜立德最后一个过桥。

sentences.text: And just as he was getting to the other side, the King’s men came rushing up to the edge of the cliff.
sentences.zh: 就在他快要到对岸的时候，国王的手下冲到崖边来了。

paragraphs.text: Then they shook their fists and yelled with rage. For they saw they were too late. The Doctor and all his animals were safe in the Land of the Monkeys and the bridge was pulled across to the other side.

sentences.text: Then they shook their fists and yelled with rage.
sentences.zh: 他们挥着拳头，气得大叫。

sentences.text: For they saw they were too late.
sentences.zh: 因为他们看出自己来晚了。

sentences.text: The Doctor and all his animals were safe in the Land of the Monkeys and the bridge was pulled across to the other side.
sentences.zh: 医生和他的动物们已经安全地到了猴子国，那座桥也被拉到了对岸。

hints.zh: 挥拳头，表示气愤又无可奈何。
hints.en: Shook their fists: a gesture of angry helplessness.

hints.zh: 拉过去；猴子们把桥收到自己这一岸，追兵就过不来了。
hints.en: Pulled across: the monkeys dragged the bridge over to their own side.

paragraphs.text: Then Chee-Chee turned to the Doctor and said,

sentences.text: Then Chee-Chee turned to the Doctor and said,
sentences.zh: 奇奇转过身，对医生说：

paragraphs.text: “Many great explorers and gray-bearded naturalists have lain long weeks hidden in the jungle waiting to see the monkeys do that trick. But we never let a white man get a glimpse of it before. You are the first to see the famous ‘Bridge of Apes.’”

sentences.text: “Many great explorers and gray-bearded naturalists have lain long weeks hidden in the jungle waiting to see the monkeys do that trick.
sentences.zh: 「许多了不起的探险家和胡子花白的博物学家，在丛林里一藏就是好几个星期，就等着看猴子们耍这一手。

sentences.text: But we never let a white man get a glimpse of it before.
sentences.zh: 可我们从来没让一个白人瞧见过。

sentences.text: You are the first to see the famous ‘Bridge of Apes.’”
sentences.zh: 你是头一个看到这有名的『猿猴桥』的人。」

hints.zh: 胡子花白的博物学家，旧时到野外研究动植物的人。
hints.en: Gray-bearded naturalists: old scholars who study plants and animals in the wild.

hints.zh: 瞥见一眼；glimpse 指短暂地看到。
hints.en: Get a glimpse of it: see it for a moment.

hints.zh: 「猿猴桥」，猴子们对自己搭桥本领的叫法。
hints.en: “Bridge of Apes”: the monkeys’ own name for the trick.

paragraphs.text: And the Doctor felt very pleased.

sentences.text: And the Doctor felt very pleased.
sentences.zh: 医生心里非常得意。

introduction.zh: 医生四下张望，想不出他们拿什么搭桥：木板？藏起来的木头？等他回头看崖边，一座桥已经横在河上，材料却出乎他的意料。咕咕得走过这座窄桥，脚下是又高又远的河。
introduction.en: The Doctor looks around for boards. What will they build a bridge from? When he turns back to the cliff, a bridge already hangs across the river, made of something he did not expect. Gub-Gub must walk over it, high above the water. Will it hold?

quiz.question: What was the bridge across the river made of?
options: Palm-leaves tied together with grass
Living monkeys holding hands and feet
Boards hidden among the rocks

feedback.zh: 趁医生背过身，猴子们手拉手、脚勾脚，把自己搭成了一座横在河上的活桥。
feedback.en: While his back was turned, the monkeys made themselves into a bridge just by holding hands and feet.

quiz.question: What did the King’s men see when they reached the cliff?
options: The Doctor was safe on the other side and the bridge had been pulled across
The monkeys were still building the bridge
The Doctor was waiting for them at the edge

feedback.zh: 他们冲到崖边时，医生和动物们已经安全到了猴子国，桥也被拉到对岸，他们只能挥拳大喊。
feedback.en: They saw that they were too late: the Doctor and his animals were safe in the Land of the Monkeys and the bridge had been pulled across.

grammar.excerpt: just by holding hands and feet

focus.zh: by + holding：by 加动词 -ing 表示方式，说明桥是「靠」手拉脚勾搭成的。
focus.en: By + holding: by with an -ing form tells us how the bridge was made.

paragraphs.text: John Dolittle now became dreadfully, awfully busy. He found hundreds and thousands of monkeys sick—gorillas, orang-outangs, chimpanzees, dog-faced baboons, marmosettes, gray monkeys, red ones—all kinds. And many had died.

sentences.text: John Dolittle now became dreadfully, awfully busy.
sentences.zh: 约翰·杜立德这下可忙坏了，忙得昏天黑地。

sentences.text: He found hundreds and thousands of monkeys sick—gorillas, orang-outangs, chimpanzees, dog-faced baboons, marmosettes, gray monkeys, red ones—all kinds.
sentences.zh: 他发现成千上万只猴子都病了——大猩猩、红毛猩猩、黑猩猩、狗脸狒狒、小狨猴、灰猴、红猴——什么种类都有。

sentences.text: And many had died.
sentences.zh: 而且很多已经死了。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，本书的主角，那位会给动物看病的医生。
hints.en: John Dolittle, the Doctor himself: the man who can cure animals.

hints.zh: 红毛猩猩，产在东南亚的类人猿；前面的大猩猩、黑猩猩是另外几种。
hints.en: Orang-outangs: red-haired apes from South-East Asia, different from gorillas and chimpanzees.

paragraphs.text: The first thing he did was to separate the sick ones from the well ones. Then he got Chee-Chee and his cousin to build him a little house of grass. The next thing: he made all the monkeys who were still well come and be vaccinated.

sentences.text: The first thing he did was to separate the sick ones from the well ones.
sentences.zh: 他做的第一件事，是把病猴和健康的猴子分开。

sentences.text: Then he got Chee-Chee and his cousin to build him a little house of grass.
sentences.zh: 然后他叫奇奇和奇奇的表兄给他搭一间小草屋。

sentences.text: The next thing: he made all the monkeys who were still well come and be vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 接下来：他让所有还没生病的猴子都过来接种疫苗。

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子，医生的朋友。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey, one of the Doctor's friends.

paragraphs.text: And for three days and three nights the monkeys kept coming from the jungles and the valleys and the hills to the little house of grass, where the Doctor sat all day and all night, vaccinating and vaccinating.

sentences.text: And for three days and three nights the monkeys kept coming from the jungles and the valleys and the hills to the little house of grass, where the Doctor sat all day and all night, vaccinating and vaccinating.
sentences.zh: 一连三天三夜，猴子们不断从丛林里、山谷里、山岗上赶来，来到那间小草屋；医生就坐在那儿，白天黑夜不停地接种、接种。

paragraphs.text: Then he had another house made—a big one, with a lot of beds in it; and he put all the sick ones in this house.

sentences.text: Then he had another house made—a big one, with a lot of beds in it; and he put all the sick ones in this house.
sentences.zh: 接着他又让人盖了一间屋子——很大，里面放了许多张床；他把病猴全都安置在这间屋里。

paragraphs.text: But so many were sick, there were not enough well ones to do the nursing. So he sent messages to the other animals, like the lions and the leopards and the antelopes, to come and help with the nursing.

sentences.text: But so many were sick, there were not enough well ones to do the nursing.
sentences.zh: 可是病猴太多了，健康的猴子不够用，没人来做护理。

sentences.text: So he sent messages to the other animals, like the lions and the leopards and the antelopes, to come and help with the nursing.
sentences.zh: 于是他给别的动物捎信——狮子、豹子、羚羊这一类——请它们来帮忙做护理。

paragraphs.text: But the Leader of the Lions was a very proud creature. And when he came to the Doctor’s big house full of beds he seemed angry and scornful.

sentences.text: But the Leader of the Lions was a very proud creature.
sentences.zh: 可狮子首领是个非常骄傲的家伙。

sentences.text: And when he came to the Doctor’s big house full of beds he seemed angry and scornful.
sentences.zh: 他来到医生那间摆满床的大屋子时，看上去又生气又轻蔑。

paragraphs.text: “Do you dare to ask me, Sir?” he said, glaring at the Doctor. “Do you dare to ask me—ME, the King of Beasts, to wait on a lot of dirty monkeys? Why, I wouldn’t even eat them between meals!”

sentences.text: “Do you dare to ask me, Sir?” he said, glaring at the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「你敢来问我，先生？」他瞪着医生说。

sentences.text: “Do you dare to ask me—ME, the King of Beasts, to wait on a lot of dirty monkeys?
sentences.zh: 「你敢叫我——叫我这个百兽之王——去伺候一群脏兮兮的猴子？

sentences.text: Why, I wouldn’t even eat them between meals!”
sentences.zh: 哼，我连拿它们当两顿饭之间的点心都不愿意！」

hints.zh: 百兽之王，狮子的称号；他拿这个头衔给自己撑面子。
hints.en: The King of Beasts: the lion's grand title for himself.

hints.zh: 伺候、服侍，不是「等待」。
hints.en: To wait on someone means to serve them, not to wait for them.

introduction.zh: 丛林里成千上万只猴子病倒了，杜立德医生日夜不停地给它们打预防针。病猴越来越多，健康的猴子不够用，护理的人手眼看就要断了。他只好捎信去请狮子、豹子和羚羊。狮子首领会来当护士吗？
introduction.en: Thousands of monkeys are ill in the jungle, and the Doctor vaccinates them day and night. Soon there are more sick monkeys than well ones to nurse them. So he sends for the lions, the leopards and the antelopes. What will the Leader of the Lions say?

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor send messages to the lions and the leopards?
options: He wants them to carry the sick monkeys to the grass house.
He needs their help to build a second house full of beds.
Too many monkeys are sick and there are not enough well ones to nurse them.

feedback.zh: 原文说病猴太多，健康的猴子不够做护理，所以他才捎信请别的动物来帮忙；房子他已经盖好了。
feedback.en: The text says there were not enough well monkeys to do the nursing, so he sent for other animals; the houses were already built.

quiz.question: How does the Leader of the Lions feel about nursing the monkeys?
options: He thinks the leopards should be asked first.
It is beneath him, because he is the King of Beasts.
He is afraid the monkeys will bite him.

feedback.zh: 他觉得以「百兽之王」的身份去伺候一群脏猴子是丢脸的事，所以又生气又轻蔑。
feedback.en: He thinks it is shameful for the King of Beasts to wait on a lot of dirty monkeys, and he is angry and scornful.

grammar.excerpt: he made all the monkeys who were still well come and be vaccinated

focus.zh: made 后面先跟宾语 all the monkeys，再接动词原形 come：「让猴子们来」；who were still well 只是修饰宾语的定语。
focus.en: Made takes the object all the monkeys and then the bare verb come; the who-clause only describes the monkeys.

paragraphs.text: Although the lion looked very terrible, the Doctor tried hard not to seem afraid of him.

sentences.text: Although the lion looked very terrible, the Doctor tried hard not to seem afraid of him.
sentences.zh: 狮子看上去很凶，但医生还是竭力不露出怕他的样子。

paragraphs.text: “I didn’t ask you to eat them,” he said quietly. “And besides, they’re not dirty. They’ve all had a bath this morning. Your coat looks as though it needed brushing—badly. Now listen, and I’ll tell you something: the day may come when the lions get sick. And if you don’t help the other animals now, the lions may find themselves left all alone when they are in trouble. That often happens to proud people.”

sentences.text: “I didn’t ask you to eat them,” he said quietly.
sentences.zh: 「我没请你吃它们啊。」他平静地说。

sentences.text: “And besides, they’re not dirty.
sentences.zh: 「再说，它们也不脏。

sentences.text: They’ve all had a bath this morning.
sentences.zh: 今天早上它们都洗过澡了。

sentences.text: Your coat looks as though it needed brushing—badly.
sentences.zh: 倒是你的毛看上去该刷一刷了——很该刷一刷。

sentences.text: Now listen, and I’ll tell you something: the day may come when the lions get sick.
sentences.zh: 你听我说，我告诉你一件事：总有一天，狮子也会生病。

sentences.text: And if you don’t help the other animals now, the lions may find themselves left all alone when they are in trouble.
sentences.zh: 要是你现在不肯帮助别的动物，等狮子自己遇上难处，也许会发现身边一个帮手都没有。

sentences.text: That often happens to proud people.”
sentences.zh: 骄傲的家伙常常就是这个下场。」

paragraphs.text: “The lions are never in trouble—they only make trouble,” said the Leader, turning up his nose. And he stalked away into the jungle, feeling he had been rather smart and clever.

sentences.text: “The lions are never in trouble—they only make trouble,” said the Leader, turning up his nose.
sentences.zh: 「狮子从来不会遇上麻烦——狮子只制造麻烦。」首领说着，翘起了鼻子。

sentences.text: And he stalked away into the jungle, feeling he had been rather smart and clever.
sentences.zh: 他昂着头走进丛林，觉得自己刚才十分机灵、十分高明。

hints.zh: 翘起鼻子，表示瞧不起、不屑。
hints.en: Turning up his nose: showing that he thinks something is beneath him.

hints.zh: 昂着身子、迈着大步走开，带着一股傲气。
hints.en: Stalked away: walked off stiffly and proudly.

paragraphs.text: Then the leopards got proud too and said they wouldn’t help. And then of course the antelopes—although they were too shy and timid to be rude to the Doctor like the lion—they pawed the ground, and smiled foolishly, and said they had never been nurses before.

sentences.text: Then the leopards got proud too and said they wouldn’t help.
sentences.zh: 于是豹子也骄傲起来，说它们不肯帮忙。

sentences.text: And then of course the antelopes—although they were too shy and timid to be rude to the Doctor like the lion—they pawed the ground, and smiled foolishly, and said they had never been nurses before.
sentences.zh: 接着当然轮到羚羊——它们太害羞、太胆小，不敢像狮子那样对医生无礼——只是一个劲儿地刨着地，傻乎乎地笑着，说自己从来没当过护士。

hints.zh: 用蹄子刨地；动物不安、犹豫或不好意思时常这样。
hints.en: Pawed the ground: what animals do with their hooves when they are uneasy or shy.

paragraphs.text: And now the poor Doctor was worried frantic, wondering where he could get help enough to take care of all these thousands of monkeys in bed.

sentences.text: And now the poor Doctor was worried frantic, wondering where he could get help enough to take care of all these thousands of monkeys in bed.
sentences.zh: 这下可怜的医生急得发狂，不知道上哪儿才能找到足够的人手，来照看床上这成千上万只猴子。

paragraphs.text: But the Leader of the Lions, when he got back to his den, saw his wife, the Queen Lioness, come running out to meet him with her hair untidy.

sentences.text: But the Leader of the Lions, when he got back to his den, saw his wife, the Queen Lioness, come running out to meet him with her hair untidy.
sentences.zh: 可狮子首领回到自己的洞穴时，看见妻子——母狮王后——头发乱蓬蓬地跑出来迎他。

hints.zh: 母狮王后，狮子首领的妻子。
hints.en: The Queen Lioness: the Leader's wife.

hints.zh: 野兽的洞穴、窝，这里指狮子住的地方。
hints.en: A den: the cave or home of a wild animal.

paragraphs.text: “One of the cubs won’t eat,” she said. “I don’t know what to do with him. He hasn’t taken a thing since last night.”

sentences.text: “One of the cubs won’t eat,” she said.
sentences.zh: 「有一只小狮子不肯吃东西。」她说。

sentences.text: “I don’t know what to do with him.
sentences.zh: 「我拿他一点办法也没有。

sentences.text: He hasn’t taken a thing since last night.”
sentences.zh: 从昨天晚上到现在，他一口东西都没吃。」

introduction.zh: 被狮子首领一口回绝，豹子和羚羊也跟着推托，床上却还躺着几千只病猴。医生急得不知上哪儿找人。就在这时候，狮子首领回到洞里，母狮王后乱着头发跑出来迎他——出了什么事？
introduction.en: The lions, the leopards and the antelopes all refuse to nurse the sick monkeys, and the Doctor cannot think where to find help. Then the Leader goes home, and the Queen Lioness runs out to meet him, her hair untidy. What has happened?

quiz.question: What does the Doctor say may happen to the lions one day?
options: They may get sick and find nobody willing to help them.
They may lose their dens to the leopards.
They may have to leave the jungle for the plains.

feedback.zh: 医生提醒他：狮子也会生病，到那时若没人肯帮，就会孤零零的；他说骄傲的人常常如此。
feedback.en: The Doctor warns that the lions may get sick too, and if they have helped nobody they will be left all alone — as often happens to proud people.

quiz.question: What do the antelopes do when they are asked to help?
options: They laugh at the Doctor and walk away.
They agree at once and follow the leopards.
They paw the ground, smile foolishly and say they have never been nurses.

feedback.zh: 羚羊不敢像狮子那样无礼，只是刨着地、傻笑，推说从来没当过护士——其实也是不肯帮忙。
feedback.en: Too shy to be rude like the lion, the antelopes paw the ground and smile foolishly, saying they have never been nurses — which is still a refusal.

grammar.excerpt: Although the lion looked very terrible, the Doctor tried hard not to seem afraid of him

focus.zh: Although 引出让步从句「虽然狮子看上去很凶」，重点在主句：医生竭力不露怯；用了 although 就不再加 but。
focus.en: Although introduces the concession (the lion looked terrible); the main point is that the Doctor tried hard not to seem afraid.

paragraphs.text: And she began to cry and shake with nervousness—for she was a good mother, even though she was a lioness.

sentences.text: And she began to cry and shake with nervousness—for she was a good mother, even though she was a lioness.
sentences.zh: 她紧张得哭了起来，浑身发抖——虽说她只是头母狮，却是个好母亲。

paragraphs.text: So the Leader went into his den and looked at his children—two very cunning little cubs, lying on the floor. And one of them seemed quite poorly.

sentences.text: So the Leader went into his den and looked at his children—two very cunning little cubs, lying on the floor.
sentences.zh: 于是首领走进洞穴去看他的孩子——两只非常逗人喜爱的小狮子，躺在地上。

sentences.text: And one of them seemed quite poorly.
sentences.zh: 其中一只看上去病得不轻。

hints.zh: 这里不是「狡猾」，而是「逗人喜爱、机灵可爱」，形容小狮子。
hints.en: Here cunning does not mean sly: it means charming and cute, said of the cubs.

hints.zh: 形容词，「不舒服、有病」，不是「贫穷地」。
hints.en: Poorly as an adjective means unwell, not poor.

paragraphs.text: Then the lion told his wife, quite proudly, just what he had said to the Doctor. And she got so angry she nearly drove him out of the den.

sentences.text: Then the lion told his wife, quite proudly, just what he had said to the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 接着，狮子非常得意地把对医生说过的话原原本本告诉了妻子。

sentences.text: And she got so angry she nearly drove him out of the den.
sentences.zh: 她气得差点把他赶出洞穴。

paragraphs.text: “You never did have a grain of sense!” she screamed. “All the animals from here to the Indian Ocean are talking about this wonderful man, and how he can cure any kind of sickness, and how kind he is—the only man in the whole world who can talk the language of the animals! And now, now—when we have a sick baby on our hands, you must go and offend him! You great booby! Nobody but a fool is ever rude to a good doctor. You—,” and she started pulling her husband’s hair.

sentences.text: “You never did have a grain of sense!” she screamed.
sentences.zh: 「你从来就没有一丁点儿头脑！」她尖叫道。

sentences.text: “All the animals from here to the Indian Ocean are talking about this wonderful man, and how he can cure any kind of sickness, and how kind he is—the only man in the whole world who can talk the language of the animals!
sentences.zh: 「从这里到印度洋，所有的动物都在议论这位了不起的人，说他能治好任何一种病，说他多么善良——全世界唯一一个会说动物语言的人！

sentences.text: And now, now—when we have a sick baby on our hands, you must go and offend him!
sentences.zh: 可现在，就在这会儿——我们手上还有个生病的孩子，你偏去得罪他！

sentences.text: You great booby!
sentences.zh: 你这个大笨蛋！

sentences.text: Nobody but a fool is ever rude to a good doctor.
sentences.zh: 只有傻瓜才会对一位好医生无礼。

sentences.text: You—,” and she started pulling her husband’s hair.
sentences.zh: 「你——」说着，她动手扯起丈夫的头发。

hints.zh: 一丁点儿头脑、一点儿常识；grain 本义是「一粒」，极言其少。
hints.en: A grain of sense: even a tiny bit of good sense. A grain is the smallest seed.

hints.zh: 笨蛋、傻瓜，旧时骂人的话。
hints.en: Booby: an old-fashioned word for a silly fool.

paragraphs.text: “Go back to that white man at once,” she yelled, “and tell him you’re sorry. And take all the other empty-headed lions with you—and those stupid leopards and antelopes. Then do everything the Doctor tells you. Work like niggers! And perhaps he will be kind enough to come and see the cub later. Now be off!—Hurry, I tell you! You’re not fit to be a father!”

sentences.text: “Go back to that white man at once,” she yelled, “and tell him you’re sorry.
sentences.zh: 「马上回到那个白人那儿去，」她吼道，「去跟他说你错了。

sentences.text: And take all the other empty-headed lions with you—and those stupid leopards and antelopes.
sentences.zh: 把别的那些没脑子的狮子都带上——还有那些蠢豹子和蠢羚羊。

sentences.text: Then do everything the Doctor tells you.
sentences.zh: 然后医生让你做什么，你就做什么。

sentences.text: Work like niggers!
sentences.zh: 像黑奴一样干活！

sentences.text: And perhaps he will be kind enough to come and see the cub later.
sentences.zh: 也许他心肠好，过后肯来看看小狮子。

sentences.text: Now be off!—Hurry, I tell you!
sentences.zh: 快走！——我叫你快一点！

sentences.text: You’re not fit to be a father!”
sentences.zh: 你根本不配当父亲！」

hints.zh: 旧时对黑人的蔑称，原文用它形容「拼命干活」；这个词今天带有强烈的冒犯性。
hints.en: A cruel old word for black people. The book uses it to mean working like a slave; today it is deeply offensive.

paragraphs.text: And she went into the den next door, where another mother-lion lived, and told her all about it.

sentences.text: And she went into the den next door, where another mother-lion lived, and told her all about it.
sentences.zh: 随后她走进隔壁的洞穴——那里住着另一头母狮——把这件事一五一十全告诉了她。

introduction.zh: 母狮王后哭得浑身发抖：一只小狮子从昨晚起就不肯吃东西。狮子首领这才把白天怎么回绝医生的话，一五一十说了出来。王后听完，气得扯住了他的头发。她会让他怎么办？
introduction.en: The Queen Lioness is crying: one of the cubs has not eaten since last night. Then the Leader proudly tells her what he said to the Doctor. She is so angry that she pulls his hair. What will she make him do?

quiz.question: Why is the Queen Lioness so angry with her husband?
options: He has left the cub alone in the jungle all day.
Their cub is sick, and he has just offended the one man who could cure it.
He has brought a lot of noisy monkeys into the den.

feedback.zh: 她骂：家里正好有生病的孩子，你却偏偏去得罪那位能治病的医生——所以她气得扯他的头发。
feedback.en: She says that with a sick baby at home he has just gone and offended the very man who can cure any sickness.

quiz.question: What does the Queen Lioness tell her husband to do?
options: Go back to the white man and tell him he is sorry.
Wait and see whether the cub gets better by itself.
Send the leopards to say sorry in his place.

feedback.zh: 她吼着让他立刻回到白人那儿去认错，还要带上狮子、豹子、羚羊一起去帮忙。
feedback.en: She yells at him to go back to the white man at once and say he is sorry — and to take all the other lions, leopards and antelopes with him.

grammar.excerpt: she got so angry she nearly drove him out of the den

focus.zh: so angry 后面省了 that：气得（以至于）差点把他赶出去；so + 形容词再接结果。
focus.en: So angry is followed by a result clause with that left out: so angry (that) she nearly drove him out.

paragraphs.text: So the Leader of the Lions went back to the Doctor and said, “I happened to be passing this way and thought I’d look in. Got any help yet?”

sentences.text: So the Leader of the Lions went back to the Doctor and said, “I happened to be passing this way and thought I’d look in.
sentences.zh: 于是狮子首领回到医生那里，说：「我碰巧路过这儿，心想不如进来看看。

sentences.text: Got any help yet?”
sentences.zh: 找到帮手了吗？」

hints.target: happened to be passing this way
hints.zh: 碰巧路过这边；happen to do 表示「碰巧、正好」。
hints.en: Happened to be passing: it was chance — or so he says — that brought him this way.

hints.zh: 顺道进来看看、串个门。
hints.en: Look in: to drop by for a short visit.

paragraphs.text: “No,” said the Doctor. “I haven’t. And I’m dreadfully worried.”

sentences.text: “No,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「没有。」医生说。

sentences.text: “I haven’t. And I’m dreadfully worried.”
sentences.zh: 「还没有。我愁得要命。」

paragraphs.text: “Help’s pretty hard to get these days,” said the lion. “Animals don’t seem to want to work any more. You can’t blame them—in a way.... Well, seeing you’re in difficulties, I don’t mind doing what I can—just to oblige you—so long as I don’t have to wash the creatures. And I have told all the other hunting animals to come and do their share. The leopards should be here any minute now.... Oh, and by the way, we’ve got a sick cub at home. I don’t think there’s much the matter with him myself. But the wife is anxious. If you are around that way this evening, you might take a look at him, will you?”

sentences.text: “Help’s pretty hard to get these days,” said the lion.
sentences.zh: 「这年头，帮手可不好找。」狮子说。

sentences.text: “Animals don’t seem to want to work any more.
sentences.zh: 「动物们好像再也不愿意干活了。

sentences.text: You can’t blame them—in a way....
sentences.zh: 你也不能怪它们——从某种意义上说……

sentences.text: Well, seeing you’re in difficulties, I don’t mind doing what I can—just to oblige you—so long as I don’t have to wash the creatures.
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然你眼下有难处，我不介意尽力帮一把——纯粹是给你个面子——只要别让我给这些家伙洗澡就行。

sentences.text: And I have told all the other hunting animals to come and do their share.
sentences.zh: 我已经通知了别的所有食肉的动物，让它们也来尽一份力。

sentences.text: The leopards should be here any minute now....
sentences.zh: 豹子们这会儿随时就该到了……

sentences.text: Oh, and by the way, we’ve got a sick cub at home.
sentences.zh: 哦，对了，我们家有只小狮子病了。

sentences.text: I don’t think there’s much the matter with him myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己倒觉得它没什么大毛病。

sentences.text: But the wife is anxious.
sentences.zh: 可我妻子不放心。

sentences.text: If you are around that way this evening, you might take a look at him, will you?”
sentences.zh: 要是你今晚正好往那边去，不妨给他看一看，行不行？」

hints.zh: seeing (that) 是「既然、考虑到」，不是「看见」。
hints.en: Seeing (that) means “since” or “considering”: since you are in difficulties.

hints.zh: 只要，表示条件；相当于 as long as。
hints.en: So long as means “on condition that”.

hints.zh: 各尽一份力、分担自己那一份活儿。
hints.en: Do their share: each do their part of the work.

hints.zh: something the matter with sb 是「某人哪儿不舒服」；much the matter 就是「病得不轻」。
hints.en: Something the matter with someone means they are ill; much the matter means seriously ill.

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor was very happy; for all the lions and the leopards and the antelopes and the giraffes and the zebras—all the animals of the forests and the mountains and the plains—came to help him in his work. There were so many of them that he had to send some away, and only kept the cleverest.

sentences.text: Then the Doctor was very happy; for all the lions and the leopards and the antelopes and the giraffes and the zebras—all the animals of the forests and the mountains and the plains—came to help him in his work.
sentences.zh: 医生这下高兴极了；因为所有的狮子、豹子、羚羊、长颈鹿和斑马——森林、高山和平原上所有的动物——都来帮他的忙。

sentences.text: There were so many of them that he had to send some away, and only kept the cleverest.
sentences.zh: 来的动物实在太多，他只好打发走一些，只留下最聪明的。

paragraphs.text: And now very soon the monkeys began to get better. At the end of a week the big house full of beds were half empty. And at the end of the second week the last monkey had got well.

sentences.text: And now very soon the monkeys began to get better.
sentences.zh: 很快，猴子们就开始好转了。

sentences.text: At the end of a week the big house full of beds were half empty.
sentences.zh: 一个星期之后，那间摆满床的大屋子空了一半。

sentences.text: And at the end of the second week the last monkey had got well.
sentences.zh: 到第二个星期末，最后一只猴子也痊愈了。

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor’s work was done; and he was so tired he went to bed and slept for three days without even turning over.

sentences.text: Then the Doctor’s work was done; and he was so tired he went to bed and slept for three days without even turning over.
sentences.zh: 医生的活儿干完了；他累得上了床，一睡就是三天，连身都没翻一下。

introduction.zh: 狮子首领又出现在医生门口，说自己只是碰巧路过，顺便进来看看。他一边抱怨动物都不爱干活了，一边又提起家里那只不肯吃东西的小狮子。医生等得到帮手吗？
introduction.en: The Leader of the Lions turns up again, saying he happened to be passing. He grumbles that animals no longer like work — and then mentions a cub at home that will not eat. Will the Doctor ever get his helpers?

quiz.question: Why does the Leader of the Lions really come back to the Doctor?
options: He wants to borrow beds for the lions' den.
He has decided that monkeys are clean after all.
His own cub is ill at home, and his wife is anxious about it.

feedback.zh: 他嘴上说只是路过、顺便帮忙，可后来说漏了：家里有只小狮子病了，妻子不放心，还想请医生去看看。
feedback.en: He says he is only passing by, but then lets slip that there is a sick cub at home and his wife is anxious — and asks the Doctor to look at it.

quiz.question: What happens once the lion sends word to the other animals?
options: The Doctor sends the sick monkeys away to the plains.
Animals from the forests, mountains and plains come to help, and the monkeys get better.
The leopards refuse again and the Doctor works alone.

feedback.zh: 狮子、豹子、羚羊、长颈鹿、斑马都来了，人多得医生还要打发走一些；猴子很快好转，最后一只也痊愈了。
feedback.en: Lions, leopards, antelopes, giraffes and zebras all come — so many that he sends some away — and the monkeys soon get better.

grammar.excerpt: you might take a look at him, will you?

focus.zh: might take 不是「可能拿走」，而是客气的请求：用 might 把话说到很轻，句尾 will you 再确认一次。
focus.en: Might take is not about possibility here: it makes the request soft and polite, and will you asks for agreement.

paragraphs.text: Chee-Chee stood outside the Doctor’s door, keeping everybody away till he woke up. Then John Dolittle told the monkeys that he must now go back to Puddleby.

sentences.text: Chee-Chee stood outside the Doctor’s door, keeping everybody away till he woke up.
sentences.zh: 奇奇站在医生门外，挡着大家不让进去，一直到他睡醒。

sentences.text: Then John Dolittle told the monkeys that he must now go back to Puddleby.
sentences.zh: 随后，约翰·杜立德告诉猴子们，他现在必须回帕德尔比去了。

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子，医生在非洲结识的朋友。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey who became the Doctor's friend in Africa.

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，本书的主角，那位会给动物看病的医生。
hints.en: John Dolittle, the hero of the book: the doctor who can talk to animals.

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡，远在英格兰。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor's home town, far away in England.

paragraphs.text: They were very surprised at this; for they had thought that he was going to stay with them forever. And that night all the monkeys got together in the jungle to talk it over.

sentences.text: They were very surprised at this; for they had thought that he was going to stay with them forever.
sentences.zh: 他们听了非常吃惊，因为他们原以为他会永远和他们住在一起。

sentences.text: And that night all the monkeys got together in the jungle to talk it over.
sentences.zh: 那天夜里，所有的猴子聚在丛林里，商量这件事。

paragraphs.text: And the Chief Chimpanzee rose up and said,

sentences.text: And the Chief Chimpanzee rose up and said,
sentences.zh: 黑猩猩首领站起来说：

hints.zh: 黑猩猩首领，猴群里的头领。
hints.en: The Chief Chimpanzee: the leader of the chimpanzees.

paragraphs.text: “Why is it the good man is going away? Is he not happy here with us?”

sentences.text: “Why is it the good man is going away?
sentences.zh: 「这位好人为什么要走呢？

sentences.text: Is he not happy here with us?”
sentences.zh: 他跟我们在一起，难道不开心吗？」

paragraphs.text: But none of them could answer him.

sentences.text: But none of them could answer him.
sentences.zh: 可是谁也没法回答他。

paragraphs.text: Then the Grand Gorilla got up and said,

sentences.text: Then the Grand Gorilla got up and said,
sentences.zh: 接着，大猩猩长老站起身来，说：

paragraphs.text: “I think we all should go to him and ask him to stay. Perhaps if we make him a new house and a bigger bed, and promise him plenty of monkey-servants to work for him and to make life pleasant for him—perhaps then he will not wish to go.”

sentences.text: “I think we all should go to him and ask him to stay.
sentences.zh: 「我想，我们大家应该一起去找他，请他留下来。

sentences.text: Perhaps if we make him a new house and a bigger bed, and promise him plenty of monkey-servants to work for him and to make life pleasant for him—perhaps then he will not wish to go.”
sentences.zh: 也许我们给他盖座新房子、做张更大的床，再答应派许多猴子伺候他、让他的日子过得舒舒服服——也许这样，他就不想走了。」

paragraphs.text: Then Chee-Chee got up; and all the others whispered, “Sh! Look! Chee-Chee, the great Traveler, is about to speak!”

sentences.text: Then Chee-Chee got up; and all the others whispered, “Sh!
sentences.zh: 这时奇奇站起身；别的猴子都小声说：「嘘！

sentences.text: Look!
sentences.zh: 看哪！

sentences.text: Chee-Chee, the great Traveler, is about to speak!”
sentences.zh: 奇奇，这位了不起的旅行家，要讲话了！」

hints.zh: 「了不起的旅行家」，猴子们给奇奇的外号——他被带到过白人的国度，见过世面。
hints.en: “The great traveller”: the monkeys' name for Chee-Chee, who has been to the white men's land.

paragraphs.text: And Chee-Chee said to the other monkeys,

sentences.text: And Chee-Chee said to the other monkeys,
sentences.zh: 奇奇对别的猴子说：

paragraphs.text: “My friends, I am afraid it is useless to ask the Doctor to stay. He owes money in Puddleby; and he says he must go back and pay it.”

sentences.text: “My friends, I am afraid it is useless to ask the Doctor to stay.
sentences.zh: 「朋友们，恐怕请医生留下来是没有用的。

sentences.text: He owes money in Puddleby; and he says he must go back and pay it.”
sentences.zh: 他在帕德尔比欠了钱；他说他必须回去把钱还上。」

paragraphs.text: And the monkeys asked him, “What is money?”

sentences.text: And the monkeys asked him, “What is money?”
sentences.zh: 猴子们问他：「钱是什么？」

paragraphs.text: Then Chee-Chee told them that in the Land of the White Men you could get nothing without money; you could do nothing without money—that it was almost impossible to live without money.

sentences.text: Then Chee-Chee told them that in the Land of the White Men you could get nothing without money; you could do nothing without money—that it was almost impossible to live without money.
sentences.zh: 于是奇奇告诉他们：在白人的国度里，没有钱就什么也拿不到；没有钱就什么也做不成——没有钱，几乎活不下去。

hints.zh: 「白人的国度」，猴子们对欧洲的叫法。
hints.en: “The land of the white men”: how the monkeys speak of Europe.

introduction.zh: 猴子们忽然听说，医生要离开丛林，回帕德尔比去。可他们一直以为，他会永远和他们住在一起。那天夜里，全丛林的猴子聚在一起商量；黑猩猩首领问了一句话，却谁也没答上来——奇奇站起来的时候，大家都静了。
introduction.en: The monkeys hear that the Doctor is going back to Puddleby. They had thought he would stay in the jungle forever. That night they all meet in the dark to talk it over, and the Chief Chimpanzee asks a question that nobody can answer. Then Chee-Chee stands up.

quiz.question: Why are the monkeys so surprised when the Doctor says he must go back?
options: They believed he would stay with them forever.
They thought he had nowhere else to go.
They did not know who he was.

feedback.zh: 原文说他们大吃一惊，因为他们本以为医生会永远和他们住在一起；他忽然要走，完全出乎意料。
feedback.en: The text says they were very surprised, for they had thought he was going to stay with them forever.

quiz.question: What does the Grand Gorilla tell the monkeys to do?
options: Hide the Doctor's boat so that he cannot leave.
Ask the Doctor to take them all to Puddleby.
Ask the Doctor to stay, and offer him a new house and plenty of servants.

feedback.zh: 他提议大家一起去求医生留下，还许诺给他盖新房子、做更大的床、派许多猴子伺候他。
feedback.en: He suggests going to the Doctor together and offering him a new house, a bigger bed and plenty of monkey-servants.

grammar.excerpt: I am afraid it is useless to ask the Doctor to stay

focus.zh: it 是形式主语，真正的主语是后面的 to ask the Doctor to stay；useless 说的正是「请他留下」这件事。
focus.en: It is a dummy subject: the real subject is to ask the Doctor to stay, and useless describes that act.

paragraphs.text: And some of them asked, “But can you not even eat and drink without paying?”

sentences.text: And some of them asked, “But can you not even eat and drink without paying?”
sentences.zh: 有几只猴子问：「可是，难道连吃喝也非付钱不可吗？」

paragraphs.text: But Chee-Chee shook his head. And then he told them that even he, when he was with the organ-grinder, had been made to ask the children for money.

sentences.text: But Chee-Chee shook his head.
sentences.zh: 奇奇却摇了摇头。

sentences.text: And then he told them that even he, when he was with the organ-grinder, had been made to ask the children for money.
sentences.zh: 接着他告诉他们：就连他自己，当年跟着摇手摇风琴的艺人时，也被逼着向孩子们讨钱。

hints.zh: 摇手摇风琴的街头艺人；奇奇从前跟着他上街卖艺、讨钱。
hints.en: A street musician who turns a hand organ; Chee-Chee once travelled with one.

paragraphs.text: And the Chief Chimpanzee turned to the Oldest Orang-outang and said, “Cousin, surely these Men be strange creatures! Who would wish to live in such a land? My gracious, how paltry!”

sentences.text: And the Chief Chimpanzee turned to the Oldest Orang-outang and said, “Cousin, surely these Men be strange creatures!
sentences.zh: 黑猩猩首领转向最年长的红毛猩猩，说：「表亲，这些『人』真是些奇怪的家伙！

sentences.text: Who would wish to live in such a land?
sentences.zh: 谁会愿意住在这样的地方？

sentences.text: My gracious, how paltry!”
sentences.zh: 我的天，多么寒酸！」

hints.zh: 最年长的红毛猩猩；orang-outang 是旧时拼法，现在多写 orangutan。
hints.en: The oldest orang-utan; orang-outang is the old spelling of orangutan.

hints.zh: 「真是些奇怪的家伙」；这里用 be 代替 are，是旧式或方言的说法。
hints.en: “Are strange creatures”: be stands for are here, an old or dialect way of speaking.

hints.zh: 老式感叹语，「我的天哪」，表示吃惊或不以为然。
hints.en: An old-fashioned exclamation: “Good heavens!”, showing shock or scorn.

hints.zh: 本义「微不足道、寒酸」；这里笑白人为几个钱斤斤计较，实在可怜。
hints.en: Small and mean; here it mocks the white men for caring so much about money.

paragraphs.text: Then Chee-Chee said,

sentences.text: Then Chee-Chee said,
sentences.zh: 奇奇说：

paragraphs.text: “When we were coming to you we had no boat to cross the sea in and no money to buy food to eat on our journey. So a man lent us some biscuits; and we said we would pay him when we came back. And we borrowed a boat from a sailor; but it was broken on the rocks when we reached the shores of Africa. Now the Doctor says he must go back and get the sailor another boat—because the man was poor and his ship was all he had.”

sentences.text: “When we were coming to you we had no boat to cross the sea in and no money to buy food to eat on our journey.
sentences.zh: 「我们来找你们的时候，没有船渡海，也没有钱在路上买吃的。

sentences.text: So a man lent us some biscuits; and we said we would pay him when we came back.
sentences.zh: 于是有人借给我们一些饼干；我们说好等回来就还他钱。

sentences.text: And we borrowed a boat from a sailor; but it was broken on the rocks when we reached the shores of Africa.
sentences.zh: 我们还向一个水手借了条船；可我们到达非洲海岸时，船在礁石上撞坏了。

sentences.text: Now the Doctor says he must go back and get the sailor another boat—because the man was poor and his ship was all he had.”
sentences.zh: 现在医生说，他必须回去，另赔那个水手一条船——因为那人很穷，那条船就是他全部的家当。」

paragraphs.text: And the monkeys were all silent for a while, sitting quite still upon the ground and thinking hard.

sentences.text: And the monkeys were all silent for a while, sitting quite still upon the ground and thinking hard.
sentences.zh: 猴子们沉默了一会儿，一动不动地坐在地上，苦苦思索。

paragraphs.text: At last the Biggest Baboon got up and said,

sentences.text: At last the Biggest Baboon got up and said,
sentences.zh: 最后，最大的狒狒站起来说：

hints.zh: 最大的狒狒，猴群里另一位有威望的头领。
hints.en: The Biggest Baboon: another respected leader among the monkeys.

paragraphs.text: “I do not think we ought to let this good man leave our land till we have given him a fine present to take with him, so that he may know we are grateful for all that he has done for us.”

sentences.text: “I do not think we ought to let this good man leave our land till we have given him a fine present to take with him, so that he may know we are grateful for all that he has done for us.”
sentences.zh: 「我觉得，我们不该让这位好人空着手离开我们的土地；得先送他一份厚礼带回去，好让他知道，我们感激他为我们做的一切。」

paragraphs.text: And a little, tiny red monkey who was sitting up in a tree shouted down,

sentences.text: And a little, tiny red monkey who was sitting up in a tree shouted down,
sentences.zh: 一只小小的红猴子坐在树上，朝下面喊道：

introduction.zh: 在猴子们看来，白人的国度样样难以理解：连吃喝都要付钱。奇奇只好讲起自己从前跟着摇风琴艺人的日子，还有他们来非洲路上欠下的账。猴子们听完，一动不动地坐在地上，沉默了很久。
introduction.en: To the monkeys, the white men's land makes no sense: you must even pay to eat and drink. So Chee-Chee tells them about his old days on the street with the organ-grinder, and about the debts behind the journey to Africa. When he stops, the monkeys sit quite still.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor say he must go back to Puddleby?
options: The monkeys have asked him to leave their land.
He must pay his debts, and get the poor sailor another boat.
He wants to bring all his animals to Africa.

feedback.zh: 奇奇说，医生得回去还债，还要赔那个水手一条船——因为那人很穷，船就是他全部的家当。
feedback.en: Chee-Chee explains that the Doctor must pay his debts and replace the sailor's boat, because the man was poor and the ship was all he had.

quiz.question: What does Chee-Chee admit about his own past?
options: He was once made to ask children for money.
He once owned a big boat of his own.
He once lived in the London Zoo.

feedback.zh: 他说，就连他自己跟着摇风琴的艺人时，也被逼着向孩子们讨钱：在白人的国度，没有钱寸步难行。
feedback.en: He says that even he, when he was with the organ-grinder, had been made to ask the children for money.

grammar.excerpt: I do not think we ought to let this good man leave our land

focus.zh: ought to 后面接动词原形 leave，表示「应该、按理该」；否定式是 ought not to。
focus.en: Ought to takes the base verb leave and means “should”; the negative is ought not to.

paragraphs.text: “I think that too!”

sentences.text: “I think that too!”
sentences.zh: 「我也这么想！」

paragraphs.text: And then they all cried out, making a great noise, “Yes, yes. Let us give him the finest present a White Man ever had!”

sentences.text: And then they all cried out, making a great noise, “Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 于是他们一齐嚷起来，闹成一片：「对，对！

sentences.text: Let us give him the finest present a White Man ever had!”
sentences.zh: 我们送他一份白人从没收到过的最好的礼物！」

paragraphs.text: Now they began to wonder and ask one another what would be the best thing to give him. And one said, “Fifty bags of cocoanuts!” And another—“A hundred bunches of bananas!—At least he shall not have to buy his fruit in the Land Where You Pay to Eat!”

sentences.text: Now they began to wonder and ask one another what would be the best thing to give him.
sentences.zh: 他们开始琢磨，互相打听：送什么给他最好？

sentences.text: And one said, “Fifty bags of cocoanuts!”
sentences.zh: 一个说：「五十袋椰子！」

sentences.text: And another—“A hundred bunches of bananas!—At least he shall not have to buy his fruit in the Land Where You Pay to Eat!”
sentences.zh: 另一个说：「一百串香蕉！——至少在那个『吃饭要付钱的地方』，他不用再买水果了！」

hints.zh: 椰子的旧拼法，今天写作 coconuts。
hints.en: An old spelling of coconuts.
