hints.target: Land Where You Pay to Eat
hints.zh: 「吃饭要付钱的地方」，猴子们给白人国度起的绰号。
hints.en: “The land where you pay to eat”: the monkeys' nickname for the white men's country.

paragraphs.text: But Chee-Chee told them that all these things would be too heavy to carry so far and would go bad before half was eaten.

sentences.text: But Chee-Chee told them that all these things would be too heavy to carry so far and would go bad before half was eaten.
sentences.zh: 可奇奇告诉他们：这些东西太重，没法搬那么远；而且还没吃掉一半就先坏了。

paragraphs.text: “If you want to please him,” he said, “give him an animal. You may be sure he will be kind to it. Give him some rare animal they have not got in the menageries.”

sentences.text: “If you want to please him,” he said, “give him an animal.
sentences.zh: 「你们要是想让他高兴，」他说，「就送他一只动物。

sentences.text: You may be sure he will be kind to it.
sentences.zh: 你放心，他一定会好好待它。

sentences.text: Give him some rare animal they have not got in the menageries.”
sentences.zh: 送他一只稀有的动物，他们的兽苑里没有的那种。」

hints.zh: 兽苑，旧时把野兽关在笼子里供人买票参观的场所，现代动物园的前身。
hints.en: A menagerie: an old collection of wild animals kept in cages for people to look at.

paragraphs.text: And the monkeys asked him, “What are menageries?”

sentences.text: And the monkeys asked him, “What are menageries?”
sentences.zh: 猴子们问他：「兽苑是什么？」

paragraphs.text: Then Chee-Chee explained to them that menageries were places in the Land of the White Men, where animals were put in cages for people to come and look at. And the monkeys were very shocked and said to one another,

sentences.text: Then Chee-Chee explained to them that menageries were places in the Land of the White Men, where animals were put in cages for people to come and look at.
sentences.zh: 于是奇奇向他们解释：兽苑是白人国度里的地方，动物被关在笼子里，让人过来观看。

sentences.text: And the monkeys were very shocked and said to one another,
sentences.zh: 猴子们吓了一大跳，彼此说：

paragraphs.text: “These Men are like thoughtless young ones—stupid and easily amused. Sh! It is a prison he means.”

sentences.text: “These Men are like thoughtless young ones—stupid and easily amused.
sentences.zh: 「这些『人』就像不懂事的小孩子——又蠢，又容易哄。

sentences.text: Sh!
sentences.zh: 嘘！

sentences.text: It is a prison he means.”
sentences.zh: 他说的其实就是牢房。」

paragraphs.text: So then they asked Chee-Chee what rare animal it could be that they should give the Doctor—one the White Men had not seen before. And the Major of the Marmosettes asked,

sentences.text: So then they asked Chee-Chee what rare animal it could be that they should give the Doctor—one the White Men had not seen before.
sentences.zh: 于是他们问奇奇：该送医生一只什么样的稀有动物——一只白人从没见过的？

sentences.text: And the Major of the Marmosettes asked,
sentences.zh: 狨猴少校问道：

hints.zh: 狨猴少校；Major 是军衔「少校」，Marmosettes 指小狨猴。
hints.en: The Major of the Marmosettes: Major is an army rank, and marmosettes are tiny marmoset monkeys.

paragraphs.text: “Have they an iguana over there?”

sentences.text: “Have they an iguana over there?”
sentences.zh: 「他们那边有鬣蜥吗？」

paragraphs.text: But Chee-Chee said, “Yes, there is one in the London Zoo.”

sentences.text: But Chee-Chee said, “Yes, there is one in the London Zoo.”
sentences.zh: 奇奇说：「有，伦敦动物园里就有一只。」

paragraphs.text: And another asked, “Have they an okapi?”

sentences.text: And another asked, “Have they an okapi?”
sentences.zh: 另一只问：「他们有霍加狓吗？」

hints.zh: 霍加狓，非洲密林里的稀有动物，后腿像斑马，脖子像长颈鹿。
hints.en: An okapi: a rare animal of the African forest, with zebra-striped legs and a giraffe-like neck.

paragraphs.text: But Chee-Chee said, “Yes. In Belgium, where my organ-grinder took me five years ago, they had an okapi in a big city they call Antwerp.”

sentences.text: But Chee-Chee said, “Yes.
sentences.zh: 奇奇说：「有。

sentences.text: In Belgium, where my organ-grinder took me five years ago, they had an okapi in a big city they call Antwerp.”
sentences.zh: 五年前，摇风琴的艺人带我去比利时，他们那座叫安特卫普的大城里就有一只霍加狓。」

paragraphs.text: And another asked, “Have they a pushmi-pullyu?”

sentences.text: And another asked, “Have they a pushmi-pullyu?”
sentences.zh: 又一只问：「他们有『推我拉你』吗？」

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，一种稀有的双头动物；本书就用这个译名。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu: a rare two-headed animal; this is the name used for it in this book.

paragraphs.text: Then Chee-Chee said, “No. No White Man has ever seen a pushmi-pullyu. Let us give him that.”

sentences.text: Then Chee-Chee said, “No.
sentences.zh: 奇奇说：「没有。

sentences.text: No White Man has ever seen a pushmi-pullyu.
sentences.zh: 白人从没见过『推我拉你』。

sentences.text: Let us give him that.”
sentences.zh: 我们就送他这个吧。」

introduction.zh: 既然留不住医生，猴子们想送他一件礼物带走。可送什么好？香蕉和椰子顺口就能说出来，稀有的野兽似乎更体面。奇奇报出一个又一个名字，那边却都已经有了。难道白人什么都见过？
introduction.en: If the Doctor cannot stay, the monkeys want to send him away with a gift. But what? Bananas and coconuts are easy to name. A rare beast would be better — but which one? Chee-Chee names one animal after another, and each time the answer is the same.

quiz.question: Why does Chee-Chee say no to the fruit?
options: The Doctor never eats fruit.
The monkeys need the fruit for themselves.
It would be too heavy to carry, and it would go bad.

feedback.zh: 奇奇说，这些东西太重，搬不了那么远；而且还没吃掉一半，就先坏了。
feedback.en: Chee-Chee says the fruit would be too heavy to carry so far and would go bad before half of it was eaten.

quiz.question: Why do the monkeys settle on the pushmi-pullyu?
options: It is smaller and lighter than an okapi.
No white man has ever seen one.
It is the only animal they are able to catch.

feedback.zh: 鬣蜥和霍加狓白人都已经见过，只有「推我拉你」从没有白人见过，所以奇奇说就送这个。
feedback.en: The white men already have an iguana and an okapi; no white man has ever seen a pushmi-pullyu.

grammar.excerpt: menageries were places in the Land of the White Men, where animals were put in cages

focus.zh: where 从句修饰前面的 places，说明是「什么样的地方」；where 前要有表示地点的名词。
focus.en: The where-clause describes places: it tells us what kind of place it is, and it needs a place noun before it.

title.en: The Animal No One Could Catch

paragraphs.text: Pushmi-Pullyus are now extinct. That means, there aren’t any more. But long ago, when Doctor Dolittle was alive, there were some of them still left in the deepest jungles of Africa; and even then they were very, very scarce. They had no tail, but a head at each end, and sharp horns on each head. They were very shy and terribly hard to catch. The black men get most of their animals by sneaking up behind them while they are not looking. But you could not do this with the pushmi-pullyu—because, no matter which way you came towards him, he was always facing you. And besides, only one half of him slept at a time. The other head was always awake—and watching. This was why they were never caught and never seen in Zoos. Though many of the greatest huntsmen and the cleverest menagerie-keepers spent years of their lives searching through the jungles in all weathers for pushmi-pullyus, not a single one had ever been caught. Even then, years ago, he was the only animal in the world with two heads.

sentences.text: Pushmi-Pullyus are now extinct.
sentences.zh: 「推我拉你」如今已经绝种了。

sentences.text: That means, there aren’t any more.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，一只也不剩了。

sentences.text: But long ago, when Doctor Dolittle was alive, there were some of them still left in the deepest jungles of Africa; and even then they were very, very scarce.
sentences.zh: 可很久以前，杜立德医生还在世的时候，非洲最深的丛林里还剩下几只；即便在那时，它们也已经非常非常稀少了。

sentences.text: They had no tail, but a head at each end, and sharp horns on each head.
sentences.zh: 它们没有尾巴，两头各长一个脑袋，每个脑袋上都长着尖角。

sentences.text: They were very shy and terribly hard to catch.
sentences.zh: 它们非常胆小，要抓到它们难极了。

sentences.text: The black men get most of their animals by sneaking up behind them while they are not looking.
sentences.zh: 黑人捕捉动物，多半是趁它们没留意，悄悄从背后摸上去。

sentences.text: But you could not do this with the pushmi-pullyu—because, no matter which way you came towards him, he was always facing you.
sentences.zh: 可这一招对「推我拉你」不管用——因为不管你从哪一边靠近，它总是面朝着你。

sentences.text: And besides, only one half of him slept at a time.
sentences.zh: 再说，它一次只有一半身子在睡觉。

sentences.text: The other head was always awake—and watching.
sentences.zh: 另一个脑袋始终醒着——而且一直盯着看。

sentences.text: This was why they were never caught and never seen in Zoos.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，它们从没被抓到过，也从没在动物园里露过面。

sentences.text: Though many of the greatest huntsmen and the cleverest menagerie-keepers spent years of their lives searching through the jungles in all weathers for pushmi-pullyus, not a single one had ever been caught.
sentences.zh: 尽管许多最了不起的猎人和最精明的动物展览老板，一辈子花了多年时间，顶着各种天气在丛林里搜寻「推我拉你」，却连一只都没抓到过。

sentences.text: Even then, years ago, he was the only animal in the world with two heads.
sentences.zh: 即便在那么多年以前，它也是世上唯一长着两个脑袋的动物。

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，一头一尾各长一个脑袋的稀有动物，两个脑袋会朝相反方向使劲。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu: a rare animal with a head at each end, so the two heads pull opposite ways.

hints.zh: 杜立德医生，本书的主角，会说动物的话。
hints.en: Doctor Dolittle, the hero of the book, who can talk with animals.

hints.zh: 稀少的、难得见到的；very scarce 就是「少得很」。
hints.en: Rare, hard to find; very scarce means there were very few left.

hints.zh: 悄悄靠近、蹑手蹑脚地摸上去，不让对方察觉。
hints.en: Moving up quietly and secretly, so as not to be noticed.

hints.zh: menagerie 是供人参观的私家动物展览，keeper 是经营、看管它的人。
hints.en: A menagerie was a collection of wild animals kept for show; its keeper ran the show.

hints.zh: 不管天气好坏、风雨无阻。
hints.en: In every kind of weather, good or bad.

paragraphs.text: Well, the monkeys set out hunting for this animal through the forest. And after they had gone a good many miles, one of them found peculiar footprints near the edge of a river; and they knew that a pushmi-pullyu must be very near that spot.

sentences.text: Well, the monkeys set out hunting for this animal through the forest.
sentences.zh: 就这样，猴子们出发穿过森林，去寻找这种动物。

sentences.text: And after they had gone a good many miles, one of them found peculiar footprints near the edge of a river; and they knew that a pushmi-pullyu must be very near that spot.
sentences.zh: 走了好多英里以后，其中一只在河边发现了奇怪的脚印；它们知道，附近一定有一只「推我拉你」。

paragraphs.text: Then they went along the bank of the river a little way and they saw a place where the grass was high and thick; and they guessed that he was in there.

sentences.text: Then they went along the bank of the river a little way and they saw a place where the grass was high and thick; and they guessed that he was in there.
sentences.zh: 接着它们沿着河岸走了一小段，看见一处又高又密的草；它们猜想，它就在那里面。

introduction.zh: 这种动物如今已经绝种，连动物园里也见不到一只。可很久以前，非洲最深的丛林里还剩下几头。它两头各有一个脑袋，一有动静就醒。猎人们找了它一辈子，为什么连一只也没到手？
introduction.en: This animal has gone from the world; not even a zoo has one. Long ago a few still lived in the deepest African jungle. It has a head at each end and sharp horns, and it is very hard to catch. Why did the best hunters never catch one?

quiz.question: Why could no hunter sneak up behind a pushmi-pullyu?
options: Because it slept in the river all day.
Because it was always facing you, whichever way you came.
Because it could run faster than any horse.

feedback.zh: 原文说不管你从哪一边靠近，它总是面朝着你；再加上它一次只睡一半，另一个脑袋始终醒着，所以没法偷袭。
feedback.en: Whichever way you came towards it, one head was always facing you, and only half of it slept at a time.

quiz.question: What did the monkeys find near the river?
options: Strange footprints
A two-headed animal asleep in the mud
A boat tied to the bank

feedback.zh: 其中一只猴子在河边发现了奇怪的脚印，它们由此断定附近就有一只「推我拉你」。
feedback.en: One of the monkeys found peculiar footprints near the river, and from them the monkeys knew the animal was close.

grammar.excerpt: Though many of the greatest huntsmen and the cleverest menagerie-keepers spent years of their lives searching through the jungles in all weathers for pushmi-pullyus, not a single one had ever been caught.

focus.zh: Though 引出让步从句「尽管最好的猎人和动物商找了多年」，作者真正要说的在后面主句：连一只也没抓到。
focus.en: The though-clause gives in, but the point is the main clause after it: not a single one had ever been caught.

paragraphs.text: So they all joined hands and made a great circle round the high grass. The pushmi-pullyu heard them coming; and he tried hard to break through the ring of monkeys. But he couldn’t do it. When he saw that it was no use trying to escape, he sat down and waited to see what they wanted.

sentences.text: So they all joined hands and made a great circle round the high grass.
sentences.zh: 于是它们手拉手，在高草四周围成一个大圈。

sentences.text: The pushmi-pullyu heard them coming; and he tried hard to break through the ring of monkeys.
sentences.zh: 「推我拉你」听见它们过来，拼命想冲出猴子的包围圈。

sentences.text: But he couldn’t do it.
sentences.zh: 可它冲不出去。

sentences.text: When he saw that it was no use trying to escape, he sat down and waited to see what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 它看出逃跑没有用，就坐下来，等着看它们要干什么。

hints.zh: 手拉手，围成一圈，表示大家连成一道墙。
hints.en: Took each other's hands, so the monkeys made a wall of bodies.

hints.zh: ring 这里指围成一圈的猴子，也就是包围圈。
hints.en: Here a ring is the circle of monkeys round him, like a wall.

paragraphs.text: They asked him if he would go with Doctor Dolittle and be put on show in the Land of the White Men.

sentences.text: They asked him if he would go with Doctor Dolittle and be put on show in the Land of the White Men.
sentences.zh: 它们问它，愿不愿意跟杜立德医生走，到白人的国度去让人参观。

hints.target: the Land of the White Men
hints.zh: 白人的国度，指欧洲，也就是医生来的地方。
hints.en: The land of white men: Europe, the country the Doctor comes from.

paragraphs.text: But he shook both his heads hard and said, “Certainly not!”

sentences.text: But he shook both his heads hard and said, “Certainly not!”
sentences.zh: 可它两个脑袋一起使劲摇，说：「绝对不行！」

paragraphs.text: They explained to him that he would not be shut up in a menagerie but would just be looked at. They told him that the Doctor was a very kind man but hadn’t any money; and people would pay to see a two-headed animal and the Doctor would get rich and could pay for the boat he had borrowed to come to Africa in.

sentences.text: They explained to him that he would not be shut up in a menagerie but would just be looked at.
sentences.zh: 它们向它解释：它不会被关进动物展览里，只是让人看看而已。

sentences.text: They told him that the Doctor was a very kind man but hadn’t any money; and people would pay to see a two-headed animal and the Doctor would get rich and could pay for the boat he had borrowed to come to Africa in.
sentences.zh: 它们告诉它，医生是个非常好心的人，可一个钱也没有；人们会花钱来看双头动物，医生就能富起来，好还清他来非洲时借那条船欠下的钱。

hints.zh: 关起来、关在里头；不是叫人「闭嘴」。
hints.en: Locked up in a place, not told to be quiet.

paragraphs.text: But he answered, “No. You know how shy I am—I hate being stared at.” And he almost began to cry.

sentences.text: But he answered, “No.
sentences.zh: 可它回答：「不行。

sentences.text: You know how shy I am—I hate being stared at.”
sentences.zh: 你知道我有多害羞——我最讨厌被人盯着看。」

sentences.text: And he almost began to cry.
sentences.zh: 它差点就要哭出来。

paragraphs.text: Then for three days they tried to persuade him.

sentences.text: Then for three days they tried to persuade him.
sentences.zh: 接下来的三天，它们一直在劝它。

paragraphs.text: And at the end of the third day he said he would come with them and see what kind of a man the Doctor was, first.

sentences.text: And at the end of the third day he said he would come with them and see what kind of a man the Doctor was, first.
sentences.zh: 到第三天快过完的时候，它说愿意跟它们走一趟，先去看看医生是个什么样的人。

paragraphs.text: So the monkeys traveled back with the pushmi-pullyu. And when they came to where the Doctor’s little house of grass was, they knocked on the door.

sentences.text: So the monkeys traveled back with the pushmi-pullyu.
sentences.zh: 于是猴子们带着「推我拉你」往回走。

sentences.text: And when they came to where the Doctor’s little house of grass was, they knocked on the door.
sentences.zh: 它们来到医生那座小草屋前，敲了敲门。

paragraphs.text: The duck, who was packing the trunk, said, “Come in!”

sentences.text: The duck, who was packing the trunk, said, “Come in!”
sentences.zh: 正在收拾箱子的鸭子说：「进来！」

hints.zh: 大旅行箱；这里不是象鼻，也不是汽车后备箱。
hints.en: A large travelling box here, not an elephant's trunk.

introduction.zh: 猴子们手拉手，在高草四周围成一个大圈，把里面的动物圈在当中。它们把来意说了一遍：跟医生去白人那儿，让人看看它，医生就能还上借船的钱。这主意听着不难，可对方有两个脑袋——它会不会也有两个主意？
introduction.en: The monkeys join hands and make a big circle round the tall grass. They explain the plan: go with the Doctor to the land of white men and be looked at. But this animal has two heads, and maybe two minds. Will it agree?

quiz.question: Why does the pushmi-pullyu refuse to be shown to people?
options: It does not like the Doctor's boat.
It is angry with the monkeys.
It is shy and hates being stared at.

feedback.zh: 它自己说明了原因：我很害羞，最讨厌被人盯着看；说完差点哭出来。
feedback.en: It says plainly: “You know how shy I am — I hate being stared at,” and it almost begins to cry.

quiz.question: What did the monkeys promise the animal if it went with them?
options: It would be paid a little money every week.
It would not be shut up, only looked at.
It would be given a house of grass of its own.

feedback.zh: 猴子们解释：它不会被关进动物展览里，只是让人看看而已；还说了医生没钱、需要它帮忙。
feedback.en: The monkeys explain that it will not be shut up in a menagerie but will just be looked at.

grammar.excerpt: They explained to him that he would not be shut up in a menagerie but would just be looked at

focus.zh: explained 后用 that 从句转述原话，时态后退一步：will not be shut up 变成 would not be shut up。
focus.en: After explained, the that-clause reports the words, so will becomes would: would not be shut up.

title.en: How Does It Make Up Its Mind?

paragraphs.text: And Chee-Chee very proudly took the animal inside and showed him to the Doctor.

sentences.text: And Chee-Chee very proudly took the animal inside and showed him to the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 奇奇非常得意地把这动物领进屋，给医生看。

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子，这趟出门找「推我拉你」的动物里就有他。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey who led the search for the pushmi-pullyu.

paragraphs.text: “What in the world is it?” asked John Dolittle, gazing at the strange creature.

sentences.text: “What in the world is it?” asked John Dolittle, gazing at the strange creature.
sentences.zh: 「这到底是什么东西？」约翰·杜立德盯着这个奇怪的家伙问。

paragraphs.text: “Lord save us!” cried the duck. “How does it make up its mind?”

sentences.text: “Lord save us!” cried the duck.
sentences.zh: 「老天爷呀！」鸭子叫道。

sentences.text: “How does it make up its mind?”
sentences.zh: 「它可怎么拿定主意呢？」

paragraphs.text: “It doesn’t look to me as though it had any,” said Jip, the dog.

sentences.text: “It doesn’t look to me as though it had any,” said Jip, the dog.
sentences.zh: 「我看它根本不像有主意的样子。」狗吉普说。

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗，鼻子最灵。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor's dog, with the best nose of the party.

paragraphs.text: “This, Doctor,” said Chee-Chee, “is the pushmi-pullyu—the rarest animal of the African jungles, the only two-headed beast in the world! Take him home with you and your fortune’s made. People will pay any money to see him.”

sentences.text: “This, Doctor,” said Chee-Chee, “is the pushmi-pullyu—the rarest animal of the African jungles, the only two-headed beast in the world!
sentences.zh: 「医生，」奇奇说，「这就是『推我拉你』——非洲丛林里最稀有的动物，世上唯一长着两个脑袋的野兽！

sentences.text: Take him home with you and your fortune’s made.
sentences.zh: 把它带回家，你就发财了。

sentences.text: People will pay any money to see him.”
sentences.zh: 人们为了看它，多少钱都肯出。」

paragraphs.text: “But I don’t want any money,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “But I don’t want any money,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可我不要什么钱。」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “Yes, you do,” said Dab-Dab, the duck. “Don’t you remember how we had to pinch and scrape to pay the butcher’s bill in Puddleby? And how are you going to get the sailor the new boat you spoke of—unless we have the money to buy it?”

sentences.text: “Yes, you do,” said Dab-Dab, the duck.
sentences.zh: 「你当然要。」鸭子达布达布说。

sentences.text: “Don’t you remember how we had to pinch and scrape to pay the butcher’s bill in Puddleby?
sentences.zh: 「你忘了我们在帕德尔比是怎么省吃俭用，才付上肉铺的账吗？

sentences.text: And how are you going to get the sailor the new boat you spoke of—unless we have the money to buy it?”
sentences.zh: 还有你说过要给那个水手弄条新船——没有钱去买，你拿什么给他？」

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子，管着家里的账。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor's duck, who keeps an eye on the money.

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor's home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

hints.zh: 省吃俭用、一分一分地抠着花，日子过得很紧。
hints.en: To live very sparingly, saving every penny.

paragraphs.text: “I was going to make him one,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “I was going to make him one,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我本来打算给他做一条。」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “Oh, do be sensible!” cried Dab-Dab. “Where would you get all the wood and the nails to make one with?—And besides, what are we going to live on? We shall be poorer than ever when we get back. Chee-Chee’s perfectly right: take the funny-looking thing along, do!”

sentences.text: “Oh, do be sensible!” cried Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「哎呀，你讲讲道理吧！」达布达布叫道。

sentences.text: “Where would you get all the wood and the nails to make one with?—And besides, what are we going to live on?
sentences.zh: 「做船要用的木头和钉子，你上哪儿弄去？——再说，我们往后靠什么过日子？

sentences.text: We shall be poorer than ever when we get back.
sentences.zh: 等我们回去，只会比从前更穷。

sentences.text: Chee-Chee’s perfectly right: take the funny-looking thing along, do!”
sentences.zh: 奇奇说得一点没错：把这个怪模怪样的东西带上吧，带吧！」

paragraphs.text: “Well, perhaps there is something in what you say,” murmured the Doctor. “It certainly would make a nice new kind of pet. But does the er—what-do-you-call-it really want to go abroad?”

sentences.text: “Well, perhaps there is something in what you say,” murmured the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「嗯，你说的也许有点道理。」医生低声说。

sentences.text: “It certainly would make a nice new kind of pet.
sentences.zh: 「它肯定会是一种很不错的新奇宠物。

sentences.text: But does the er—what-do-you-call-it really want to go abroad?”
sentences.zh: 可这个——呃——叫什么来着——它真的愿意出国吗？」

introduction.zh: 奇奇很得意地把这个怪物领进屋。医生盯着它，半天说不清这是什么；鸭子想的却是另一件事：两个脑袋，怎么拿定一个主意？奇奇说，这东西能让人发大财。发财这件事，医生会怎么看？
introduction.en: Chee-Chee leads the strange animal into the house. The Doctor stares and cannot say what it is. The duck asks a practical question: with two heads, how does it make up its mind? Then Chee-Chee says this animal could make them rich. How will the Doctor answer?

quiz.question: Why does Chee-Chee want the Doctor to take the animal home?
options: People will pay to see it and the Doctor will get rich.
The monkeys have no room for it in the jungle.
It can show the Doctor the way back to England.

feedback.zh: 奇奇说这是最稀有的动物，把它带回家就发财了，人们为了看它多少钱都肯出。
feedback.en: Chee-Chee calls it the rarest animal and says: “Take him home with you and your fortune's made.”

quiz.question: Why does Dab-Dab think the Doctor cannot make a boat for the sailor?
options: The sailor has already bought a new boat.
The boat would be too small for the animals.
He has no wood, no nails and no money.

feedback.zh: 达布达布连问两句：木头和钉子哪儿弄？往后靠什么过日子？她要说的就是既没材料也没钱。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab asks where the wood and nails would come from, and what they would live on: no materials and no money.

grammar.excerpt: I was going to make him one

focus.zh: was going to 是 be going to 的过去式，表示当时本来的打算：他原打算自己做一条船。
focus.en: Was going to is the past of be going to: it was his plan at that time to make the boat himself.

paragraphs.text: “Yes, I’ll go,” said the pushmi-pullyu who saw at once, from the Doctor’s face, that he was a man to be trusted. “You have been so kind to the animals here—and the monkeys tell me that I am the only one who will do. But you must promise me that if I do not like it in the Land of the White Men you will send me back.”

sentences.text: “Yes, I’ll go,” said the pushmi-pullyu who saw at once, from the Doctor’s face, that he was a man to be trusted.
sentences.zh: 「好，我去。」「推我拉你」说——它从医生脸上立刻看出，这个人值得信任。

sentences.text: “You have been so kind to the animals here—and the monkeys tell me that I am the only one who will do.
sentences.zh: 「你对这里的动物这么好——猴子们也说，只有我合适。

sentences.text: But you must promise me that if I do not like it in the Land of the White Men you will send me back.”
sentences.zh: 可你得答应我：要是我在白人那儿过得不顺心，你就把我送回来。」

paragraphs.text: “Why, certainly—of course, of course,” said the Doctor. “Excuse me, surely you are related to the Deer Family, are you not?”

sentences.text: “Why, certainly—of course, of course,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「当然——当然，当然。」医生说。

sentences.text: “Excuse me, surely you are related to the Deer Family, are you not?”
sentences.zh: 「对不起，你一定和鹿家沾亲，是不是？」

hints.zh: 鹿科，动物学上的一个大类；医生在给它「归类」。
hints.en: The deer family, one group of animals; the Doctor is trying to place it.

paragraphs.text: “Yes,” said the pushmi-pullyu—“to the Abyssinian Gazelles and the Asiatic Chamois—on my mother’s side. My father’s great-grandfather was the last of the Unicorns.”

sentences.text: “Yes,” said the pushmi-pullyu—“to the Abyssinian Gazelles and the Asiatic Chamois—on my mother’s side.
sentences.zh: 「是的，」「推我拉你」说，「跟阿比西尼亚羚羊和亚洲岩羚羊——是我母亲这边的亲戚。

sentences.text: My father’s great-grandfather was the last of the Unicorns.”
sentences.zh: 我父亲的曾祖父，是最后一只独角兽。」

hints.zh: 阿比西尼亚羚羊；阿比西尼亚是埃塞俄比亚的旧称，gazelle 是一种跑得很快的羚羊。
hints.en: Gazelles from Abyssinia, the old name for Ethiopia.

hints.zh: 亚洲岩羚羊；chamois 是一种住在山上的小羚羊。
hints.en: The chamois is a small mountain antelope; this one is Asiatic.

hints.zh: 独角兽，传说中额上只长一只角的动物，早已不在世上。
hints.en: Unicorns: legendary beasts with a single horn, no longer in the world.

paragraphs.text: “Most interesting!” murmured the Doctor; and he took a book out of the trunk which Dab-Dab was packing and began turning the pages. “Let us see if Buffon says anything—”

sentences.text: “Most interesting!” murmured the Doctor; and he took a book out of the trunk which Dab-Dab was packing and began turning the pages.
sentences.zh: 「太有意思了！」医生低声说，从达布达布正在收拾的箱子里取出一本书，翻了起来。

sentences.text: “Let us see if Buffon says anything—”
sentences.zh: 「看看布丰书上有没有说——」

hints.zh: 布丰，十八世纪法国博物学家，写过一部讲各种动物的巨著。
hints.en: Buffon, an eighteenth-century French naturalist who wrote a great book on animals.

paragraphs.text: “I notice,” said the duck, “that you only talk with one of your mouths. Can’t the other head talk as well?”

sentences.text: “I notice,” said the duck, “that you only talk with one of your mouths.
sentences.zh: 「我注意到，」鸭子说，「你只用一张嘴说话。

sentences.text: Can’t the other head talk as well?”
sentences.zh: 另一个脑袋就不会说话吗？」

paragraphs.text: “Oh, yes,” said the pushmi-pullyu. “But I keep the other mouth for eating—mostly. In that way I can talk while I am eating without being rude. Our people have always been very polite.”

sentences.text: “Oh, yes,” said the pushmi-pullyu.
sentences.zh: 「哦，会的。」「推我拉你」说。

sentences.text: “But I keep the other mouth for eating—mostly.
sentences.zh: 「不过另一张嘴我留着吃饭——多半是这样。

sentences.text: In that way I can talk while I am eating without being rude.
sentences.zh: 这样我就能一边吃一边说话，也不算失礼。

sentences.text: Our people have always been very polite.”
sentences.zh: 我们这一族一向很讲礼貌。」

paragraphs.text: When the packing was finished and everything was ready to start, the monkeys gave a grand party for the Doctor, and all the animals of the jungle came. And they had pineapples and mangoes and honey and all sorts of good things to eat and drink.

sentences.text: When the packing was finished and everything was ready to start, the monkeys gave a grand party for the Doctor, and all the animals of the jungle came.
sentences.zh: 行李收拾好、一切都准备出发的时候，猴子们为医生办了一场盛大的宴会，丛林里的动物都来了。

sentences.text: And they had pineapples and mangoes and honey and all sorts of good things to eat and drink.
sentences.zh: 宴上有菠萝、芒果、蜂蜜，还有各种各样好吃的、好喝的。

introduction.zh: 医生已经准备动身，这头动物却还有话要说：它只提一个条件——要是白人那儿的生活不合心意，医生就得把它送回来。话刚说完，医生又盯住它的长相，问了个怪问题：你是不是跟鹿家沾亲？
introduction.en: The Doctor is ready to start, but the animal has something to ask: if it does not like life in the land of white men, the Doctor must send it back. He hears it out, then looks at it again and asks: are you related to the Deer Family?

quiz.question: What does the pushmi-pullyu ask the Doctor to promise?
options: To let it sleep inside the trunk.
To send it back if it does not like the new land.
To find its family in Abyssinia.

feedback.zh: 它答应去，但先讲条件：要是白人的地方不合心意，医生得把它送回来。
feedback.en: It will go, but only if the Doctor promises to send it back when it does not like the land of white men.

quiz.question: Why does it keep one mouth for eating?
options: So that it can talk while eating without being rude.
Because one of the mouths is smaller than the other.
Because it can only taste food with that mouth.

feedback.zh: 它的理由是：这样就能边吃边说话，不失礼；它还说它们这一族一向很讲礼貌。
feedback.en: It keeps one mouth for food so that it can talk while eating and still be polite.

grammar.excerpt: if I do not like it in the Land of the White Men you will send me back

focus.zh: if 从句讲将来的条件，却用一般现在时 do not like；主句才用 will send me back。
focus.en: The if-clause talks about the future but takes the present tense, do not like; only the main clause uses will.

paragraphs.text: After they had all finished eating, the Doctor got up and said,

sentences.text: After they had all finished eating, the Doctor got up and said,
sentences.zh: 大家吃完以后，医生站起来说：

paragraphs.text: “My friends: I am not clever at speaking long words after dinner, like some men; and I have just eaten many fruits and much honey. But I wish to tell you that I am very sad at leaving your beautiful country. Because I have things to do in the Land of the White Men, I must go. After I have gone, remember never to let the flies settle on your food before you eat it; and do not sleep on the ground when the rains are coming. I—er—er—I hope you will all live happily ever after.”

sentences.text: “My friends: I am not clever at speaking long words after dinner, like some men; and I have just eaten many fruits and much honey.
sentences.zh: 「朋友们：我不像有些人那样，会在饭后讲一大套漂亮话；再说，我刚吃了许多水果和许多蜂蜜。

sentences.text: But I wish to tell you that I am very sad at leaving your beautiful country.
sentences.zh: 不过我想告诉你们：要离开你们这美丽的国家，我心里非常难过。

sentences.text: Because I have things to do in the Land of the White Men, I must go.
sentences.zh: 因为我在白人那边还有事情要办，必须得走。

sentences.text: After I have gone, remember never to let the flies settle on your food before you eat it; and do not sleep on the ground when the rains are coming.
sentences.zh: 我走以后，记住：吃东西之前，千万别让苍蝇落在食物上；雨季快来的时候，别睡在地上。

sentences.text: I—er—er—I hope you will all live happily ever after.”
sentences.zh: 我——呃——呃——祝你们大家从此都过得幸福。」

hints.zh: 童话结尾的老话「从此幸福地生活下去」；医生用它来祝福，带点笨拙的可爱。
hints.en: The old fairy-tale ending, “and they lived happily ever after”; the Doctor uses it as a blessing.

paragraphs.text: When the Doctor stopped speaking and sat down, all the monkeys clapped their hands a long time and said to one another, “Let it be remembered always among our people that he sat and ate with us, here, under the trees. For surely he is the Greatest of Men!”

sentences.text: When the Doctor stopped speaking and sat down, all the monkeys clapped their hands a long time and said to one another, “Let it be remembered always among our people that he sat and ate with us, here, under the trees.
sentences.zh: 医生讲完坐下，猴子们久久地拍手，彼此说：「让我们族人永远记住：他曾在这里，就在树下，和我们坐在一起吃饭。

sentences.text: For surely he is the Greatest of Men!”
sentences.zh: 因为他确实是人类中最伟大的一位！」

paragraphs.text: And the Grand Gorilla, who had the strength of seven horses in his hairy arms, rolled a great rock up to the head of the table and said,

sentences.text: And the Grand Gorilla, who had the strength of seven horses in his hairy arms, rolled a great rock up to the head of the table and said,
sentences.zh: 那位手臂毛茸茸、力气顶得上七匹马的大猩猩，把一块大石头滚到桌子的一头，说：

hints.zh: 大猩猩首领；Grand 是尊称，猴子国里地位最高的那位。
hints.en: The Grand Gorilla: the chief of the gorillas, Grand being a title of respect.

paragraphs.text: “This stone for all time shall mark the spot.”

sentences.text: “This stone for all time shall mark the spot.”
sentences.zh: 「这块石头将永远标记这个地方。」

hints.zh: 永远、千秋万代，语气比 forever 更郑重。
hints.en: For ever and always; a more solemn way of saying forever.

paragraphs.text: And even to this day, in the heart of the jungle, that stone still is there. And monkey-mothers, passing through the forest with their families, still point down at it from the branches and whisper to their children, “Sh! There it is—look—where the Good White Man sat and ate food with us in the Year of the Great Sickness!”

sentences.text: And even to this day, in the heart of the jungle, that stone still is there.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，在丛林深处，那块石头还在那里。

sentences.text: And monkey-mothers, passing through the forest with their families, still point down at it from the branches and whisper to their children, “Sh!
sentences.zh: 猴妈妈带着一家子穿过森林时，还会从枝头往下指着它，小声对孩子说：「嘘！

sentences.text: There it is—look—where the Good White Man sat and ate food with us in the Year of the Great Sickness!”
sentences.zh: 就在那儿——你看——那位好心的白人就是在这儿，和我们一起吃了饭，那是在大瘟疫那一年！」

hints.target: the Year of the Great Sickness
hints.zh: 大瘟疫那一年，指前文那场差点毁掉猴子国的重病。
hints.en: The Year of the Great Sickness: the plague that nearly killed the monkeys earlier in the story.

paragraphs.text: Then, when the party was over, the Doctor and his pets started out to go back to the seashore. And all the monkeys went with him as far as the edge of their country, carrying his trunk and bags, to see him off.

sentences.text: Then, when the party was over, the Doctor and his pets started out to go back to the seashore.
sentences.zh: 宴会结束后，医生和他的动物们动身回海边去。

sentences.text: And all the monkeys went with him as far as the edge of their country, carrying his trunk and bags, to see him off.
sentences.zh: 所有的猴子都替他拎着箱子和口袋，一直送他到他们国度的边上，为他送行。

hints.zh: 送行、送别，在出发的地方陪一会儿再告别。
hints.en: To see someone off: to go with them to the place they leave from.

introduction.zh: 宴会快散了，医生站起来道别。他说自己不擅长饭后讲长话，只留下两句要紧的叮嘱：别让苍蝇落在食物上，雨季别睡在地上。猴子们听完，久久地拍手；大猩猩还滚来一块大石头。它要在石头上说什么？
introduction.en: The party ends, and the Doctor stands up to say goodbye. He is no good at long speeches, so he gives the animals just two pieces of advice. The monkeys clap for a long time, and the Grand Gorilla rolls a stone over. What will he say?

quiz.question: What two pieces of advice does the Doctor give the animals?
options: Wash all their fruit, and stay in the trees at night.
Share their honey, and look after the old monkeys.
Keep flies off their food, and do not sleep on the ground in the rains.

feedback.zh: 医生临走只叮嘱两件事：吃东西前别让苍蝇落在食物上，雨季快来时别睡在地上。
feedback.en: He tells them never to let flies settle on their food before eating, and not to sleep on the ground when the rains come.

quiz.question: What does the Grand Gorilla do at the end of the party?
options: He carries the Doctor's trunk down to the sea.
He rolls a great rock to the head of the table.
He makes a long speech about the Doctor.

feedback.zh: 是大猩猩把一块大石头滚到桌子一头，说这石头将永远标记这个地方；搬箱子送行的是猴子们。
feedback.en: It is the Grand Gorilla who rolls the rock to the table and says it will mark the spot; the monkeys carry the trunk.

grammar.excerpt: the Grand Gorilla, who had the strength of seven horses in his hairy arms

focus.zh: 逗号后的 who 从句是非限制性定语，只补充大猩猩的力气，并不用来限定是「哪一只」。
focus.en: The comma plus who adds extra information about the gorilla; it does not pick out which one.

paragraphs.text: By the edge of the river they stopped and said farewell.

sentences.text: By the edge of the river they stopped and said farewell.
sentences.zh: 到了河边，他们停下脚步，互相道别。

paragraphs.text: This took a long time, because all those thousands of monkeys wanted to shake John Dolittle by the hand.

sentences.text: This took a long time, because all those thousands of monkeys wanted to shake John Dolittle by the hand.
sentences.zh: 这道别花了很长时间，因为那成千上万只猴子都想跟约翰·杜立德握握手。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，本书的主角，一位能给动物看病的医生。
hints.en: John Dolittle, the Doctor who can talk to animals and cure them.

paragraphs.text: Afterwards, when the Doctor and his pets were going on alone, Polynesia said,

sentences.text: Afterwards, when the Doctor and his pets were going on alone, Polynesia said,
sentences.zh: 之后，医生带着宠物们独自上路，波利尼西亚说：

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉，会说人话，也最爱出主意。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor’s parrot, who can talk and loves to make plans.

paragraphs.text: “We must tread softly and talk low as we go through the land of the Jolliginki. If the King should hear us, he will send his soldiers to catch us again; for I am sure he is still very angry over the trick I played on him.”

sentences.text: “We must tread softly and talk low as we go through the land of the Jolliginki.
sentences.zh: 「穿过乔利金基的地界时，咱们走路要轻，说话要低声。

sentences.text: If the King should hear us, he will send his soldiers to catch us again; for I am sure he is still very angry over the trick I played on him.”
sentences.zh: 要是让国王听见，他又会派士兵来抓咱们；我敢肯定，他为上次我捉弄他那件事还在生气。」

hints.zh: 乔利金基，非洲的一个王国，国王先前把医生一行关进过牢里。
hints.en: Jolliginki, the African kingdom whose King once locked the Doctor up.

hints.target: the trick I played on him
hints.zh: 我捉弄他的那件事；指波利尼西亚装成隐身医生吓国王，让他开牢放人。
hints.en: The trick she played on him: she pretended to be the invisible Doctor and frightened the King into opening the prison.

paragraphs.text: “What I am wondering,” said the Doctor, “is where we are going to get another boat to go home in.... Oh well, perhaps we’ll find one lying about on the beach that nobody is using. ‘Never lift your foot till you come to the stile.’”

sentences.text: “What I am wondering,” said the Doctor, “is where we are going to get another boat to go home in....
sentences.zh: 「我一直在想，」医生说，「咱们上哪儿再弄一条船回家去……

sentences.text: Oh well, perhaps we’ll find one lying about on the beach that nobody is using. ‘Never lift your foot till you come to the stile.’”
sentences.zh: 唉，好吧，也许海滩上就停着一条没人用的船。『没走到栅门，就别急着抬脚。』」

hints.target: Never lift your foot till you come to the stile
hints.zh: 一句老话，字面是「没走到栅门前，别抬脚跨过去」；意思是先别为还没到的难关发愁。
hints.en: An old saying: don’t step over the gate before you reach it — don’t worry about a trouble that has not come yet.

paragraphs.text: One day, while they were passing through a very thick part of the forest, Chee-Chee went ahead of them to look for cocoanuts. And while he was away, the Doctor and the rest of the animals, who did not know the jungle-paths so well, got lost in the deep woods. They wandered around and around but could not find their way down to the seashore.

sentences.text: One day, while they were passing through a very thick part of the forest, Chee-Chee went ahead of them to look for cocoanuts.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他们正穿过森林里枝叶最密的一片地方，奇奇走到前面去给大家找椰子。

sentences.text: And while he was away, the Doctor and the rest of the animals, who did not know the jungle-paths so well, got lost in the deep woods.
sentences.zh: 就在他离开的时候，医生和其余那些不太认得丛林小路的动物，在密林深处迷了路。

sentences.text: They wandered around and around but could not find their way down to the seashore.
sentences.zh: 他们转来转去，怎么也找不到下山去海边的路。

hints.zh: 奇奇，医生养的那只猴子，最认得丛林里的路。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the Doctor’s monkey, who knows the jungle paths best.

introduction.zh: 和几千只猴子一一告过别，医生带着宠物独自上路，要悄悄穿过乔利金基。波利尼西亚压低声音提醒：国王为那次捉弄还在生气。可医生心里挂着另一件事——回帕德尔比的船，到哪里去找？
introduction.en: After saying goodbye to thousands of monkeys, the Doctor and his pets set off alone. Polynesia warns them to keep quiet: the King is still angry. But the Doctor has another worry — where will they find a boat to take them home?

quiz.question: Why does it take so long to say goodbye at the river?
options: The monkeys are too sick to let him go.
The Doctor has lost his trunk near the water.
Thousands of monkeys want to shake the Doctor’s hand.

feedback.zh: 原文说这道别花了很长时间，因为成千上万只猴子都想跟约翰·杜立德握手。
feedback.en: The text says it took a long time because all those thousands of monkeys wanted to shake John Dolittle by the hand.

quiz.question: What is the Doctor wondering about as they go on alone?
options: Whether the King is still angry with them.
How to pay the monkeys for their help.
Where they will get another boat to go home in.

feedback.zh: 医生想的是「上哪儿再弄一条船回家去」；国王生不生气是波利尼西亚担心的事。
feedback.en: The Doctor wonders where they are going to get another boat to go home in; it is Polynesia who worries about the angry King.

grammar.excerpt: We must tread softly and talk low as we go through the land of the Jolliginki

focus.zh: as 在这里是「当……的时候」，引出同时发生的事：穿过乔利金基的整段时间都得放轻脚步、压低声音。
focus.en: As here means “while”: during the whole time they cross Jolliginki they must walk softly and talk low.

paragraphs.text: Chee-Chee, when he could not see them anywhere, was terribly upset. He climbed high trees and looked out from the top branches to try and see the Doctor’s high hat; he waved and shouted; he called to all the animals by name. But it was no use. They seemed to have disappeared altogether.

sentences.text: Chee-Chee, when he could not see them anywhere, was terribly upset.
sentences.zh: 奇奇四处都看不见他们，急得不得了。

sentences.text: He climbed high trees and looked out from the top branches to try and see the Doctor’s high hat; he waved and shouted; he called to all the animals by name.
sentences.zh: 他爬上高树，从树梢上张望，想看见医生的高礼帽；他又挥手又喊叫，把每只动物的名字都叫了一遍。

sentences.text: But it was no use.
sentences.zh: 可是没有用。

sentences.text: They seemed to have disappeared altogether.
sentences.zh: 他们好像完完全全消失了。

paragraphs.text: Indeed they had lost their way very badly. They had strayed a long way off the path, and the jungle was so thick with bushes and creepers and vines that sometimes they could hardly move at all, and the Doctor had to take out his pocket-knife and cut his way along. They stumbled into wet, boggy places; they got all tangled up in thick convolvulus-runners; they scratched themselves on thorns, and twice they nearly lost the medicine-bag in the under-brush. There seemed no end to their troubles; and nowhere could they come upon a path.

sentences.text: Indeed they had lost their way very badly.
sentences.zh: 他们的确是迷得厉害。

sentences.text: They had strayed a long way off the path, and the jungle was so thick with bushes and creepers and vines that sometimes they could hardly move at all, and the Doctor had to take out his pocket-knife and cut his way along.
sentences.zh: 他们早已偏离小路很远，丛林里灌木、爬藤和藤蔓密得有时几乎挪不动步，医生只好掏出小折刀，一路砍出一条道来。

sentences.text: They stumbled into wet, boggy places; they got all tangled up in thick convolvulus-runners; they scratched themselves on thorns, and twice they nearly lost the medicine-bag in the under-brush.
sentences.zh: 他们跌进湿软的泥沼；被粗粗的旋花藤缠住；让荆棘划破了皮；还有两次差点把药箱丢在灌木丛里。

sentences.text: There seemed no end to their troubles; and nowhere could they come upon a path.
sentences.zh: 他们的麻烦好像没完没了，哪儿也碰不上一条路。

hints.zh: 旋花，一种缠着别的植物往上爬的野草；runners 是它伸出去的藤。
hints.en: Convolvulus is a climbing weed; its runners are the long stems it puts out.

hints.zh: 即 underbrush，树林下层的灌木和杂草。
hints.en: Underbrush: the bushes and weeds growing low in the wood.

paragraphs.text: At last, after blundering about like this for many days, getting their clothes torn and their faces covered with mud, they walked right into the King’s back-garden by mistake. The King’s men came running up at once and caught them.

sentences.text: At last, after blundering about like this for many days, getting their clothes torn and their faces covered with mud, they walked right into the King’s back-garden by mistake.
sentences.zh: 就这样乱撞了许多天，衣服扯破了，脸上糊满了泥，最后他们竟糊里糊涂一头闯进了国王的后花园。

sentences.text: The King’s men came running up at once and caught them.
sentences.zh: 国王的手下立刻跑过来，把他们抓住了。

hints.zh: 跌跌撞撞地乱走、瞎撞；指他们在林子里没有方向地乱转了许多天。
hints.en: Blundering about means moving on clumsily with no idea of the way.

hints.zh: 国王手下的士兵、卫兵。
hints.en: The King’s men: the King’s soldiers and guards.

paragraphs.text: But Polynesia flew into a tree in the garden, without anybody seeing her, and hid herself. The Doctor and the rest were taken before the King.

sentences.text: But Polynesia flew into a tree in the garden, without anybody seeing her, and hid herself.
sentences.zh: 可波利尼西亚飞进了花园里的一棵树，谁也没看见，就躲了起来。

sentences.text: The Doctor and the rest were taken before the King.
sentences.zh: 医生和其他动物被带到了国王面前。

introduction.zh: 奇奇爬上高树，喊着每只动物的名字，可林子里一点回音也没有。医生一行越走越偏，藤蔓缠脚，泥沼陷腿，还差点丢了药箱。林中没有路，他们只能往前闯——前面等着的是什么？
introduction.en: Chee-Chee climbs the tallest trees and calls every animal by name, but nothing answers. Meanwhile the Doctor and the others push deeper into the jungle, tangled in vines and stuck in mud. There is no path anywhere. What waits for them up ahead?

quiz.question: What happens after the Doctor and the animals wander for many days?
options: They find a path down to the seashore.
They walk into the King’s back-garden by mistake.
Chee-Chee finds them and leads them back.

feedback.zh: 他们在林子里乱撞了许多天，最后「糊里糊涂」闯进了国王的后花园；海边一直没找到。
feedback.en: After many days of blundering about they walked right into the King’s back-garden by mistake; they never found the seashore.

quiz.question: What does Polynesia do when the others are caught?
options: She calls the monkeys to come and help.
She flies into a tree and hides where nobody sees her.
She flies off to look for Chee-Chee.

feedback.zh: 原文说波利尼西亚飞进花园里的一棵树，谁也没看见，就躲了起来，所以没被抓走。
feedback.en: The parrot flew into a tree in the garden without anybody seeing her and hid herself, so she was not caught.

grammar.excerpt: the jungle was so thick with bushes and creepers and vines that sometimes they could hardly move at all

focus.zh: so + 形容词 + that 引出结果：密到「常常几乎挪不动步」的地步；thick 后面先接 with 短语，再接 that 从句。
focus.en: So thick … that introduces the result: the jungle was thick to the point that they could hardly move; thick takes a with-phrase before the that-clause.

paragraphs.text: “Ha, ha!” cried the King. “So you are caught again! This time you shall not escape. Take them all back to prison and put double locks on the door. This White Man shall scrub my kitchen-floor for the rest of his life!”

sentences.text: “Ha, ha!” cried the King.
sentences.zh: 「哈，哈！」国王大叫。

sentences.text: “So you are caught again!
sentences.zh: 「这么说你们又被抓住了！

sentences.text: This time you shall not escape.
sentences.zh: 这一回你们可跑不掉了。

sentences.text: Take them all back to prison and put double locks on the door.
sentences.zh: 把他们统统带回牢里，门上再加两道锁。

sentences.text: This White Man shall scrub my kitchen-floor for the rest of his life!”
sentences.zh: 这个白人得给我擦一辈子的厨房地板！」

hints.zh: 国王口中的「这个白人」，指的是杜立德医生。
hints.en: “This White Man” is how the King speaks of Doctor Dolittle.

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor and his pets were led back to prison and locked up. And the Doctor was told that in the morning he must begin scrubbing the kitchen-floor.

sentences.text: So the Doctor and his pets were led back to prison and locked up.
sentences.zh: 于是医生和他的宠物们被带回牢房关了起来。

sentences.text: And the Doctor was told that in the morning he must begin scrubbing the kitchen-floor.
sentences.zh: 医生还被告知，第二天早上就得开始擦厨房地板。

paragraphs.text: They were all very unhappy.

sentences.text: They were all very unhappy.
sentences.zh: 他们都愁坏了。

paragraphs.text: “This is a great nuisance,” said the Doctor. “I really must get back to Puddleby. That poor sailor will think I’ve stolen his ship if I don’t get home soon.... I wonder if those hinges are loose.”

sentences.text: “This is a great nuisance,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「真是麻烦透了，」医生说。

sentences.text: “I really must get back to Puddleby.
sentences.zh: 「我真得回帕德尔比去。

sentences.text: That poor sailor will think I’ve stolen his ship if I don’t get home soon....
sentences.zh: 要是不能早点回去，那个可怜的水手会以为我把他的船偷走了……

sentences.text: I wonder if those hinges are loose.”
sentences.zh: 不知道那几副合页松不松。」

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor’s home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

hints.zh: 那个可怜的水手；指把船借给医生的人，船在非洲海岸撞坏了。
hints.en: The sailor who lent the Doctor his boat — it was broken on the rocks when they reached Africa.

paragraphs.text: But the door was very strong and firmly locked. There seemed no chance of getting out. Then Gub-Gub began to cry again.

sentences.text: But the door was very strong and firmly locked.
sentences.zh: 可牢门又结实，锁得又牢。

sentences.text: There seemed no chance of getting out.
sentences.zh: 看样子是没机会出去了。

sentences.text: Then Gub-Gub began to cry again.
sentences.zh: 这时咕咕又哭了起来。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生养的小猪，一着急就哭。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s little pig, who cries whenever he is frightened.

paragraphs.text: All this time Polynesia was still sitting in the tree in the palace-garden. She was saying nothing and blinking her eyes.

sentences.text: All this time Polynesia was still sitting in the tree in the palace-garden.
sentences.zh: 这工夫，波利尼西亚一直坐在王宫花园的那棵树上。

sentences.text: She was saying nothing and blinking her eyes.
sentences.zh: 她一声不响，只是眨着眼睛。

paragraphs.text: This was always a very bad sign with Polynesia. Whenever she said nothing and blinked her eyes, it meant that somebody had been making trouble, and she was thinking out some way to put things right. People who made trouble for Polynesia or her friends were nearly always sorry for it afterwards.

sentences.text: This was always a very bad sign with Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 在波利尼西亚身上，这可是个很坏的兆头。

sentences.text: Whenever she said nothing and blinked her eyes, it meant that somebody had been making trouble, and she was thinking out some way to put things right.
sentences.zh: 每当她一声不响、眨着眼睛，就说明有人闯了祸，而她正在琢磨什么法子把事情扳回来。

sentences.text: People who made trouble for Polynesia or her friends were nearly always sorry for it afterwards.
sentences.zh: 给波利尼西亚或她的朋友添麻烦的人，事后几乎总是要后悔的。

hints.zh: 把事情摆平、纠正过来；这里指想法子把大家救出来。
hints.en: Put things right: to fix the trouble and make it good again.

paragraphs.text: Presently she spied Chee-Chee swinging through the trees still looking for the Doctor. When Chee-Chee saw her, he came into her tree and asked her what had become of him.

sentences.text: Presently she spied Chee-Chee swinging through the trees still looking for the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，她瞧见奇奇在树间荡来荡去，还在找医生。

sentences.text: When Chee-Chee saw her, he came into her tree and asked her what had become of him.
sentences.zh: 奇奇一看见她，就落到她那棵树上，问她医生到底怎么样了。

introduction.zh: 国王大笑，吩咐给牢门加上双锁，还让这位「白人」一辈子给他擦厨房地板。医生惦记着帕德尔比，还有那位会把船当成被偷了的水手。牢门结实得很。而花园的树上，波利尼西亚一声不响，只是眨眼。
introduction.en: The King laughs and orders double locks on the prison door. The Doctor will scrub the kitchen floor for the rest of his life, and he still worries about the sailor whose ship he borrowed. Outside, Polynesia sits in a garden tree, silent, blinking her eyes.

quiz.question: What does the King say the Doctor must do?
options: Write a book about the animals of the jungle.
Scrub the kitchen-floor for the rest of his life.
Show the King where the gold is hidden.

feedback.zh: 国王下令把牢门加双锁，还说这个白人得给他擦一辈子的厨房地板。
feedback.en: The King orders double locks on the door and says the White Man shall scrub his kitchen-floor for the rest of his life.

quiz.question: What does it mean when Polynesia says nothing and blinks her eyes?
options: She is too tired to speak.
She is angry with the Doctor.
She is thinking out a way to put things right.

feedback.zh: 原文解释：她一声不响、眨着眼睛，就说明有人闯了祸，她正在琢磨法子把事情扳回来——所以这是个「很坏的兆头」。
feedback.en: The text explains that whenever she is silent and blinks, somebody has made trouble and she is thinking out some way to put things right.

grammar.excerpt: This time you shall not escape.

focus.zh: shall 用在第二、三人称，表示说话人的意志和命令：国王是在宣告「你们这次逃不掉」，不是单纯讲将来。
focus.en: Shall with you or he does not simply talk about the future: it shows the speaker’s will — the King is declaring that they will not get away.

paragraphs.text: “The Doctor and all the animals have been caught by the King’s men and locked up again,” whispered Polynesia. “We lost our way in the jungle and blundered into the palace-garden by mistake.”

sentences.text: “The Doctor and all the animals have been caught by the King’s men and locked up again,” whispered Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「医生和所有的动物都被国王的手下抓住，又关起来了，」波利尼西亚小声说。

sentences.text: “We lost our way in the jungle and blundered into the palace-garden by mistake.”
sentences.zh: 「我们在丛林里迷了路，稀里糊涂闯进了王宫花园。」

paragraphs.text: “But couldn’t you guide them?” asked Chee-Chee; and he began to scold the parrot for letting them get lost while he was away looking for the cocoanuts.

sentences.text: “But couldn’t you guide them?” asked Chee-Chee; and he began to scold the parrot for letting them get lost while he was away looking for the cocoanuts.
sentences.zh: 「可你不会给他们带路吗？」奇奇问；接着他就数落起鹦鹉来：他不过离开去找椰子，她竟让他们迷了路。

hints.zh: scold sb for sth 是为某事数落、责怪某人；这里奇奇怪波利尼西亚没把大家带好。
hints.en: To scold somebody for something is to tell them off about it; Chee-Chee blames the parrot for losing the way.

paragraphs.text: “It was all that stupid pig’s fault,” said Polynesia. “He would keep running off the path hunting for ginger-roots. And I was kept so busy catching him and bringing him back, that I turned to the left, instead of the right, when we reached the swamp.—Sh!—Look! There’s Prince Bumpo coming into the garden! He must not see us.—Don’t move, whatever you do!”

sentences.text: “It was all that stupid pig’s fault,” said Polynesia.
sentences.zh: 「全怪那头笨猪，」波利尼西亚说。

sentences.text: “He would keep running off the path hunting for ginger-roots.
sentences.zh: 「他老是跑出小路去找姜根。

sentences.text: And I was kept so busy catching him and bringing him back, that I turned to the left, instead of the right, when we reached the swamp.—Sh!—Look!
sentences.zh: 我忙着追他、把他带回来，走到沼泽那儿就拐错了，该往右却往左了。——嘘！——看！

sentences.text: There’s Prince Bumpo coming into the garden!
sentences.zh: 邦波王子正走进花园呢！

sentences.text: He must not see us.—Don’t move, whatever you do!”
sentences.zh: 绝不能让他看见咱们。——不管怎么样，都别动！」

hints.zh: 姜的根茎，咕咕跑出小路去找的就是这东西。
hints.en: Ginger-roots: the root of the ginger plant, which Gub-Gub was hunting for.

hints.zh: 邦波王子，乔利金基国王的儿子，也就是「黑王子」。
hints.en: Prince Bumpo, the son of the King of Jolliginki — the Black Prince.

paragraphs.text: And there, sure enough, was Prince Bumpo, the King’s son, opening the garden-gate. He carried a book of fairy-tales under his arm. He came strolling down the gravel-walk, humming a sad song, till he reached a stone seat right under the tree where the parrot and the monkey were hiding. Then he lay down on the seat and began reading the fairy-stories to himself.

sentences.text: And there, sure enough, was Prince Bumpo, the King’s son, opening the garden-gate.
sentences.zh: 果然，国王的儿子邦波王子正在打开花园的门。

sentences.text: He carried a book of fairy-tales under his arm.
sentences.zh: 他胳膊下夹着一本童话书。

sentences.text: He came strolling down the gravel-walk, humming a sad song, till he reached a stone seat right under the tree where the parrot and the monkey were hiding.
sentences.zh: 他顺着碎石小路慢慢走来，哼着一支忧伤的歌，一直走到鹦鹉和猴子藏身的那棵树下的一张石凳前。

sentences.text: Then he lay down on the seat and began reading the fairy-stories to himself.
sentences.zh: 然后他在石凳上躺下，自己看起童话来。

hints.zh: 果然、果不其然；表示事情正像刚才说的那样发生了。
hints.en: Sure enough means “just as expected”: it happened exactly as she had said.

paragraphs.text: Chee-Chee and Polynesia watched him, keeping very quiet and still.

sentences.text: Chee-Chee and Polynesia watched him, keeping very quiet and still.
sentences.zh: 奇奇和波利尼西亚看着他，一动不动，一声不响。

paragraphs.text: After a while the King’s son laid the book down and sighed a weary sigh.

sentences.text: After a while the King’s son laid the book down and sighed a weary sigh.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，国王的儿子放下书，疲倦地叹了口气。

introduction.zh: 奇奇终于找到波利尼西亚，才知道大家又落进了国王手里，忍不住埋怨她没带好路。波利尼西亚把责任推给咕咕，话没说完，忽然压低声音：有人进花园了。两个藏在树上的家伙，只好一动不动。
introduction.en: Chee-Chee finds Polynesia at last and hears what happened. He scolds her for losing the way; she blames Gub-Gub for running off. Then she stops short: someone is coming into the garden. Two watchers up in the tree hold their breath.

quiz.question: What does Polynesia blame for their losing the way?
options: Gub-Gub, who kept running off the path.
The King’s men, who blocked the path.
Chee-Chee, who was away too long.

feedback.zh: 波利尼西亚说全怪那头笨猪：他老是跑出小路去找姜根，她忙着追他，走到沼泽就拐错了方向。
feedback.en: Polynesia says it was all the stupid pig’s fault: he kept running off the path for ginger-roots, and while she chased him she turned the wrong way at the swamp.

quiz.question: What does Prince Bumpo do when he reaches the stone seat?
options: He falls asleep and drops his book on the ground.
He lies down and reads his fairy-stories to himself.
He calls out to the parrot up in the tree.

feedback.zh: 他哼着歌走到树下，在石凳上躺下，自己看起童话来；他并没有发现树上的两个家伙。
feedback.en: He lies down on the seat under the tree and begins reading the fairy-stories to himself; he never notices who is hiding above him.

grammar.excerpt: He would keep running off the path hunting for ginger-roots

focus.zh: would + 动词原形表示过去反复发生的事，这里带抱怨语气：他老是跑出小路；keep + -ing 又强调没完没了。
focus.en: Would + base verb describes something that kept happening in the past, with a note of complaint: he would keep running off the path.

title.en: A Prince Who Wants to Be White

paragraphs.text: “If I were only a white prince!” said he, with a dreamy, far-away look in his eyes.

sentences.text: “If I were only a white prince!” said he, with a dreamy, far-away look in his eyes.
sentences.zh: 「我要是个白人王子就好了！」他说，眼里带着一种做梦似的、飘远的神情。

paragraphs.text: Then the parrot, talking in a small, high voice like a little girl, said aloud,

sentences.text: Then the parrot, talking in a small, high voice like a little girl, said aloud,
sentences.zh: 这时，鹦鹉用又细又高的声音，像个小姑娘似的，大声说：

paragraphs.text: “Bumpo, some one might turn thee into a white prince perchance.”

sentences.text: “Bumpo, some one might turn thee into a white prince perchance.”
sentences.zh: 「邦波，说不定有人能把你变成白人王子呢。」

hints.zh: 古英语里「你」的宾格，相当于现在的 you；下文 thou、thy、sayest 也是古语。
hints.en: Thee is the old object form of “you”; thou, thy and sayest later in the chapter are old forms too.

paragraphs.text: The King’s son started up off the seat and looked all around.

sentences.text: The King’s son started up off the seat and looked all around.
sentences.zh: 国王的儿子从石凳上猛地跳起来，四下张望。

hints.zh: start up 这里不是「开始」，而是「猛地站起、惊起」。
hints.en: Started up does not mean “began”: he jumped up suddenly from the seat.

paragraphs.text: “What is this I hear?” he cried. “Methought the sweet music of a fairy’s silver voice rang from yonder bower! Strange!”

sentences.text: “What is this I hear?” he cried.
sentences.zh: 「我听见的是什么？」他叫道。

sentences.text: “Methought the sweet music of a fairy’s silver voice rang from yonder bower!
sentences.zh: 「我仿佛听见仙女的银铃般的声音，从那边的树荫里传来甜美的乐音！

sentences.text: Strange!”
sentences.zh: 真怪！」

hints.zh: 古语，等于 it seemed to me / I thought，「我仿佛觉得」。
hints.en: Methought is old English for “it seemed to me”, or “I thought”.

paragraphs.text: “Worthy Prince,” said Polynesia, keeping very still so Bumpo couldn’t see her, “thou sayest winged words of truth. For ’tis I, Tripsitinka, the Queen of the Fairies, that speak to thee. I am hiding in a rose-bud.”

sentences.text: “Worthy Prince,” said Polynesia, keeping very still so Bumpo couldn’t see her, “thou sayest winged words of truth.
sentences.zh: 「尊贵的王子，」波利尼西亚一动不动，好让邦波看不见她，「你说的是带着翅膀的真话。

sentences.text: For ’tis I, Tripsitinka, the Queen of the Fairies, that speak to thee.
sentences.zh: 因为跟你说话的正是我，仙女皇后特里普西廷卡。

sentences.text: I am hiding in a rose-bud.”
sentences.zh: 我藏在一朵玫瑰花苞里。」

hints.zh: 字面是「长翅膀的真话」；古语里「有翼的话」指真切、会飞快传开的话。
hints.en: Winged words are words that fly: in old poetry it means words that are true and quickly spread.

hints.zh: 特里普西廷卡，波利尼西亚临时编出来的仙女皇后名号。
hints.en: Tripsitinka, the name Polynesia makes up for the Queen of the Fairies.

paragraphs.text: “Oh tell me, Fairy-Queen,” cried Bumpo, clasping his hands in joy, “who is it can turn me white?”

sentences.text: “Oh tell me, Fairy-Queen,” cried Bumpo, clasping his hands in joy, “who is it can turn me white?”
sentences.zh: 「哦，告诉我吧，仙女皇后，」邦波高兴得双手紧握，叫道，「谁能把我变成白人？」

paragraphs.text: “In thy father’s prison,” said the parrot, “there lies a famous wizard, John Dolittle by name. Many things he knows of medicine and magic, and mighty deeds has he performed. Yet thy kingly father leaves him languishing long and lingering hours. Go to him, brave Bumpo, secretly, when the sun has set; and behold, thou shalt be made the whitest prince that ever won fair lady! I have said enough. I must now go back to Fairyland. Farewell!”

sentences.text: “In thy father’s prison,” said the parrot, “there lies a famous wizard, John Dolittle by name.
sentences.zh: 「在你父亲的牢里，」鹦鹉说，「关着一位有名的魔法师，名叫约翰·杜立德。

sentences.text: Many things he knows of medicine and magic, and mighty deeds has he performed.
sentences.zh: 他懂得许多医道和法术，还干过了不起的大事。

sentences.text: Yet thy kingly father leaves him languishing long and lingering hours.
sentences.zh: 可你那位当国王的父亲，却让他一天天憔悴下去。

sentences.text: Go to him, brave Bumpo, secretly, when the sun has set; and behold, thou shalt be made the whitest prince that ever won fair lady!
sentences.zh: 勇敢的邦波，等太阳落了，你悄悄去找他；到时候，你就会变成有史以来赢得美人芳心的最白的王子！

sentences.text: I have said enough.
sentences.zh: 我说得够多了。

sentences.text: I must now go back to Fairyland.
sentences.zh: 我现在得回仙境去了。

sentences.text: Farewell!”
sentences.zh: 再见了！」

hints.zh: 日渐消瘦、苦苦熬着；指医生被关在牢里受折磨。
hints.en: Languishing means growing weak and miserable, as the Doctor does in prison.

paragraphs.text: “Farewell!” cried the Prince. “A thousand thanks, good Tripsitinka!”

sentences.text: “Farewell!” cried the Prince.
sentences.zh: 「再见！」王子叫道。

sentences.text: “A thousand thanks, good Tripsitinka!”
sentences.zh: 「万分感谢你，好心的特里普西廷卡！」

paragraphs.text: And he sat down on the seat again with a smile upon his face, waiting for the sun to set.

sentences.text: And he sat down on the seat again with a smile upon his face, waiting for the sun to set.
sentences.zh: 他又在石凳上坐下，脸上带着微笑，等着太阳落山。

introduction.zh: 国王的儿子邦波坐在树下，合上童话书，叹着气说：要是我是位白人王子就好了。忽然，一个又细又高的声音从树上传下来，自称是仙女皇后。王子四下张望——他信了吗？
introduction.en: The King’s son sits under the tree, closes his book of fairy-tales and sighs: if only he were a white prince! Then a small, high voice comes down from the leaves. It says it is the Queen of the Fairies. The Prince looks around — does he believe it?

quiz.question: What does the King’s son wish for?
options: To be a white prince.
To be King of the Jolliginki.
To catch the two-headed animal.

feedback.zh: 他合上书叹气，说的是「我要是个白人王子就好了」；他想要的是换个身份，不是王位。
feedback.en: He sighs and says, “If I were only a white prince!” — what he wants is to be someone else, not to take his father’s throne.

quiz.question: What does the voice tell Bumpo to do?
options: Go secretly to the wizard in the prison after sunset.
Bring a rose to the fairy queen at once.
Ask his father to set the wizard free.

feedback.zh: 「仙女」让他等太阳落山后悄悄去找牢里的魔法师约翰·杜立德，说那就能变白；还特意说「我藏在玫瑰花苞里」，没让他送花。
feedback.en: She tells him to go secretly to the wizard John Dolittle in his father’s prison when the sun has set; the rose-bud is only where she says she is hiding.

grammar.excerpt: If I were only a white prince!

focus.zh: if only + 过去式表示与现在相反的愿望：要是我是白人王子就好了；were 是虚拟语气，这里只有从句，主句省略了。
focus.en: If only + past tense expresses a wish about now that is not true: if only I were a white prince. Were is the unreal form, and the main clause is left out.

paragraphs.text: Very, very quietly, making sure that no one should see her, Polynesia then slipped out at the back of the tree and flew across to the prison.

sentences.text: Very, very quietly, making sure that no one should see her, Polynesia then slipped out at the back of the tree and flew across to the prison.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚非常非常轻地溜到树后，确认没有人会看见她，然后飞过夜空，到了牢房那边。

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，那只鹦鹉；她一直替医生出主意。
hints.en: Polynesia, the parrot, who is always full of plans.

paragraphs.text: She found Gub-Gub poking his nose through the bars of the window, trying to sniff the cooking-smells that came from the palace-kitchen. She told the pig to bring the Doctor to the window because she wanted to speak to him. So Gub-Gub went and woke the Doctor who was taking a nap.

sentences.text: She found Gub-Gub poking his nose through the bars of the window, trying to sniff the cooking-smells that came from the palace-kitchen.
sentences.zh: 她发现咕咕正把鼻子从窗栏缝里伸出去，想闻从王宫厨房飘来的饭菜香味。

sentences.text: She told the pig to bring the Doctor to the window because she wanted to speak to him.
sentences.zh: 她让这头小猪把医生带到窗边来，因为她有话要跟他说。

sentences.text: So Gub-Gub went and woke the Doctor who was taking a nap.
sentences.zh: 于是咕咕走过去，叫醒了正在打盹的医生。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的宠物小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor's little pig.

paragraphs.text: “Listen,” whispered the parrot, when John Dolittle’s face appeared: “Prince Bumpo is coming here to-night to see you. And you’ve got to find some way to turn him white. But be sure to make him promise you first that he will open the prison-door and find a ship for you to cross the sea in.”

sentences.text: “Listen,” whispered the parrot, when John Dolittle’s face appeared: “Prince Bumpo is coming here to-night to see you.
sentences.zh: 「听着，」约翰·杜立德的脸一出现在窗口，鹦鹉就小声说，「邦波王子今晚要到这里来看你。

sentences.text: And you’ve got to find some way to turn him white.
sentences.zh: 你得想个办法，把他变成白人。

sentences.text: But be sure to make him promise you first that he will open the prison-door and find a ship for you to cross the sea in.”
sentences.zh: 不过你一定要先让他答应你：他会打开牢门，再给你找一条能渡海的船。」

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，就是杜立德医生；鹦鹉叫他的全名。
hints.en: John Dolittle, the Doctor himself; the parrot uses his full name.

hints.zh: 邦波王子，乔利金基国王的儿子。
hints.en: Prince Bumpo, the son of the King of Jolliginki.

paragraphs.text: “This is all very well,” said the Doctor. “But it isn’t so easy to turn a black man white. You speak as though he were a dress to be re-dyed. It’s not so simple. ‘Shall the leopard change his spots, or the Ethiopian his skin,’ you know?”

sentences.text: “This is all very well,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「这话倒是不错，」医生说。

sentences.text: “But it isn’t so easy to turn a black man white.
sentences.zh: 「可把一个黑人变成白人，没那么容易。

sentences.text: You speak as though he were a dress to be re-dyed.
sentences.zh: 你说得好像他是一件可以重新染色的衣服。

sentences.text: It’s not so simple. ‘Shall the leopard change his spots, or the Ethiopian his skin,’ you know?”
sentences.zh: 事情没这么简单。你知道的，『豹子岂能改变斑点，埃塞俄比亚人岂能改变肤色』？」

hints.zh: 埃塞俄比亚人；医生引的是《圣经》里的老话，意思是本性难移。
hints.en: An Ethiopian; the Doctor quotes an old Bible saying about how no one can change his nature.

paragraphs.text: “I don’t know anything about that,” said Polynesia impatiently. “But you must turn this coon white. Think of a way—think hard. You’ve got plenty of medicines left in the bag. He’ll do anything for you if you change his color. It is your only chance to get out of prison.”

sentences.text: “I don’t know anything about that,” said Polynesia impatiently.
sentences.zh: 「那些我都不懂，」波利尼西亚不耐烦地说。

sentences.text: “But you must turn this coon white.
sentences.zh: 「可你必须把这个黑人变成白人。

sentences.text: Think of a way—think hard.
sentences.zh: 想个办法——好好想。

sentences.text: You’ve got plenty of medicines left in the bag.
sentences.zh: 你袋子里还剩着好多药呢。

sentences.text: He’ll do anything for you if you change his color.
sentences.zh: 只要你改了他的颜色，他什么都肯为你做。

sentences.text: It is your only chance to get out of prison.”
sentences.zh: 这是你逃出牢房的唯一机会。」

hints.zh: 旧时对黑人的蔑称，粗鲁且带侮辱；今天这样说会冒犯别人。
hints.en: An old, insulting word for a Black man. It was used casually in the book's time, but it is offensive and is not used today.

introduction.zh: 夜里，鹦鹉波利尼西亚悄悄从树后溜出去，飞到牢房窗边。她压低声音告诉杜立德医生一件事，还要他先让对方许下一个承诺。医生听完，为什么直摇头？
introduction.en: Late at night the parrot Polynesia slips away to the prison window. She wakes the Doctor with a plan, but he must first make the Prince promise something. Why does the Doctor shake his head?

quiz.question: What does Polynesia say the Doctor must do to Prince Bumpo?
options: Find some way to turn him white
Send him back to his father
Teach him to speak to animals

feedback.zh: 鹦鹉明确说「你得想个办法，把他变成白人」，这是她半夜飞来的目的。
feedback.en: The parrot says straight out: you must find some way to turn him white.

quiz.question: What must the Doctor make the Prince promise before anything else?
options: To give him half of the kingdom
To keep the whole plan a secret from the King
To open the prison-door and find a ship for him

feedback.zh: 波利尼西亚叮嘱他先要这个承诺：打开牢门，再找一条渡海的船。半个王国是王子自己后来提出的。
feedback.en: Polynesia tells him to get the promise first: the prison-door open and a ship to cross the sea. The half kingdom is the Prince's own offer, made later.

grammar.excerpt: you’ve got to find some way to turn him white

focus.zh: you’ve got to 是口语的「必须、非做不可」，比 must 更像在说没有别的路；后面跟动词原形 find。
focus.en: You’ve got to means you must, with no other way out; it takes the base verb find.

paragraphs.text: “Well, I suppose it might be possible,” said the Doctor. “Let me see—,” and he went over to his medicine-bag, murmuring something about “liberated chlorine on animal-pigment—perhaps zinc-ointment, as a temporary measure, spread thick—”

sentences.text: “Well, I suppose it might be possible,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「嗯，我想这也许办得到，」医生说。

sentences.text: “Let me see—,” and he went over to his medicine-bag, murmuring something about “liberated chlorine on animal-pigment—perhaps zinc-ointment, as a temporary measure, spread thick—”
sentences.zh: 「让我看看——」他走到药袋旁，嘴里咕哝着『用游离氯作用于动物色素——也许可以用锌软膏，作为临时办法，厚厚地涂一层——』

hints.zh: 锌软膏，一种外用药膏；医生念的这一串是化学名词，听着很唬人。
hints.en: Zinc ointment, a real skin medicine. The Doctor is muttering chemical-sounding words that impress his patient.

paragraphs.text: Well, that night Prince Bumpo came secretly to the Doctor in prison and said to him,

sentences.text: Well, that night Prince Bumpo came secretly to the Doctor in prison and said to him,
sentences.zh: 那天夜里，邦波王子果然悄悄来到牢房，对医生说：

paragraphs.text: “White Man, I am an unhappy prince. Years ago I went in search of The Sleeping Beauty, whom I had read of in a book. And having traveled through the world many days, I at last found her and kissed the lady very gently to awaken her—as the book said I should. ’Tis true indeed that she awoke. But when she saw my face she cried out, ‘Oh, he’s black!’ And she ran away and wouldn’t marry me—but went to sleep again somewhere else. So I came back, full of sadness, to my father’s kingdom. Now I hear that you are a wonderful magician and have many powerful potions. So I come to you for help. If you will turn me white, so that I may go back to The Sleeping Beauty, I will give you half my kingdom and anything besides you ask.”

sentences.text: “White Man, I am an unhappy prince.
sentences.zh: 「白人，我是一个不快乐的王子。

sentences.text: Years ago I went in search of The Sleeping Beauty, whom I had read of in a book.
sentences.zh: 很多年前，我去寻找睡美人——我是在一本书里读到她的。

sentences.text: And having traveled through the world many days, I at last found her and kissed the lady very gently to awaken her—as the book said I should. ’Tis true indeed that she awoke.
sentences.zh: 我在世上走了许多天，终于找到了她，轻轻地吻了这位小姐，把她唤醒——就像书里说的那样。她确实醒了。

sentences.text: But when she saw my face she cried out, ‘Oh, he’s black!’
sentences.zh: 可她一看见我的脸就喊起来：『哦，他是黑人！』

sentences.text: And she ran away and wouldn’t marry me—but went to sleep again somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 她跑掉了，不肯嫁给我——又到别的地方睡过去了。

sentences.text: So I came back, full of sadness, to my father’s kingdom.
sentences.zh: 于是我满心悲伤，回到我父亲的王国。

sentences.text: Now I hear that you are a wonderful magician and have many powerful potions.
sentences.zh: 现在我听说你是一位了不起的魔法师，有许多法力强大的药水。

sentences.text: So I come to you for help.
sentences.zh: 所以我来求你帮忙。

sentences.text: If you will turn me white, so that I may go back to The Sleeping Beauty, I will give you half my kingdom and anything besides you ask.”
sentences.zh: 如果你能把我变成白人，让我可以回到睡美人身边，我就把半个王国给你，另外你要什么都可以。」

hints.zh: 白人；邦波这样称呼医生，是他对远方来客的叫法。
hints.en: “White Man”: how Bumpo addresses the Doctor.

hints.zh: 睡美人，那个被吻醒就会醒来的公主。
hints.en: The Sleeping Beauty, the princess who wakes when she is kissed.

hints.zh: ’Tis 是 it is 的旧写法；王子说话带着古书的味道。
hints.en: ’Tis is an old way of saying “it is”, which suits the Prince's bookish way of talking.

hints.zh: 药水、汤剂；在童话里常指有魔力的药。
hints.en: Potions: liquid medicines, the magic kind in a fairy tale.

paragraphs.text: “Prince Bumpo,” said the Doctor, looking thoughtfully at the bottles in his medicine-bag, “supposing I made your hair a nice blonde color—would not that do instead to make you happy?”

sentences.text: “Prince Bumpo,” said the Doctor, looking thoughtfully at the bottles in his medicine-bag, “supposing I made your hair a nice blonde color—would not that do instead to make you happy?”
sentences.zh: 「邦波王子，」医生若有所思地看着药袋里的瓶子说，「假如我把你的头发变成好看的金黄色——这样就不能让你高兴了吗？」

introduction.zh: 那天深夜，邦波王子真的悄悄来到牢房。他讲起自己寻找睡美人的经历，还许下半个王国作报酬。杜立德医生听完，先提了一个只改头发颜色的小提议——这能行吗？
introduction.en: That night Prince Bumpo comes secretly to the prison and tells the Doctor his story about the Sleeping Beauty. He offers half a kingdom. The Doctor makes one small, strange offer of his own: what if only the hair changed colour?

quiz.question: Why does Prince Bumpo come to the Doctor?
options: He wants to buy the Doctor's medicine-bag
He wants the Doctor to turn him white
He wants medicine for his sick father

feedback.zh: 王子承诺：只要医生把他变成白人，他就给半个王国。「白人」是他一路说下来最在意的事。
feedback.en: The Prince promises half his kingdom if the Doctor will turn him white — being white is all he cares about.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor suggest instead of turning him white?
options: Making his hair a nice blonde colour
Giving him a new suit of clothes
Making his eyes blue for him

feedback.zh: 医生先退一步，提出只把头发改成金黄色，问他这样能不能让他高兴。蓝眼睛是王子自己后来提的。
feedback.en: The Doctor first offers something smaller: nice blonde hair. The blue eyes are Bumpo's own idea, raised later.

grammar.excerpt: The Sleeping Beauty, whom I had read of in a book

focus.zh: whom 指前面的 the Sleeping Beauty，在从句里作 read of 的宾语；介词 of 留在从句末尾。
focus.en: Whom stands for the Sleeping Beauty and is the object of read of; the preposition of stays at the end of the clause.

paragraphs.text: “No,” said Bumpo. “Nothing else will satisfy me. I must be a white prince.”

sentences.text: “No,” said Bumpo.
sentences.zh: 「不行，」邦波说。

sentences.text: “Nothing else will satisfy me.
sentences.zh: 「别的都不能让我满意。

sentences.text: I must be a white prince.”
sentences.zh: 我必须做一个白人王子。」

paragraphs.text: “You know it is very hard to change the color of a prince,” said the Doctor—“one of the hardest things a magician can do. You only want your face white, do you not?”

sentences.text: “You know it is very hard to change the color of a prince,” said the Doctor—“one of the hardest things a magician can do.
sentences.zh: 「你知道，要改变一个王子的肤色是很难的，」医生说，「这是魔法师最难办到的事情之一。

sentences.text: You only want your face white, do you not?”
sentences.zh: 你只想要脸变白，对不对？」

paragraphs.text: “Yes, that is all,” said Bumpo. “Because I shall wear shining armor and gauntlets of steel, like the other white princes, and ride on a horse.”

sentences.text: “Yes, that is all,” said Bumpo.
sentences.zh: 「对，就这些，」邦波说。

sentences.text: “Because I shall wear shining armor and gauntlets of steel, like the other white princes, and ride on a horse.”
sentences.zh: 「因为我要穿上发亮的盔甲，戴上钢护手，像别的白人王子那样，骑在马上。」

hints.zh: 钢制护手，骑士盔甲里护住手和手腕的那一部分。
hints.en: Gauntlets of steel: the armoured gloves that cover a knight's hands and wrists.

paragraphs.text: “Must your face be white all over?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Must your face be white all over?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「你的脸必须整张都变白吗？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “Yes, all over,” said Bumpo—“and I would like my eyes blue too, but I suppose that would be very hard to do.”

sentences.text: “Yes, all over,” said Bumpo—“and I would like my eyes blue too, but I suppose that would be very hard to do.”
sentences.zh: 「对，整张都要白，」邦波说，「我还希望眼睛也是蓝的，不过我想那大概很难办到。」

hints.zh: all over 指「整张、到处」，这里说整张脸都要白。
hints.en: All over means “every part”: the whole face, not just one place.

paragraphs.text: “Yes, it would,” said the Doctor quickly. “Well, I will do what I can for you. You will have to be very patient though—you know with some medicines you can never be very sure. I might have to try two or three times. You have a strong skin—yes? Well that’s all right. Now come over here by the light—Oh, but before I do anything, you must first go down to the beach and get a ship ready, with food in it, to take me across the sea. Do not speak a word of this to any one. And when I have done as you ask, you must let me and all my animals out of prison. Promise—by the crown of Jolliginki!”

sentences.text: “Yes, it would,” said the Doctor quickly.
sentences.zh: 「是的，很难，」医生赶快说。

sentences.text: “Well, I will do what I can for you.
sentences.zh: 「好吧，我尽力替你想办法。

sentences.text: You will have to be very patient though—you know with some medicines you can never be very sure.
sentences.zh: 不过你得非常有耐心——你知道，用某些药，谁也说不准。

sentences.text: I might have to try two or three times.
sentences.zh: 我可能要试上两三次。

sentences.text: You have a strong skin—yes?
sentences.zh: 你的皮肤很结实——是不是？

sentences.text: Well that’s all right.
sentences.zh: 那就好。

sentences.text: Now come over here by the light—Oh, but before I do anything, you must first go down to the beach and get a ship ready, with food in it, to take me across the sea.
sentences.zh: 现在到亮处来——哦，不过在我动手之前，你得先到海边去，准备一条船，船上备好食物，送我渡海。

sentences.text: Do not speak a word of this to any one.
sentences.zh: 这件事一个字也不许跟别人说。

sentences.text: And when I have done as you ask, you must let me and all my animals out of prison.
sentences.zh: 等我照你的要求做完了，你就得放我跟我所有的动物出牢房。

sentences.text: Promise—by the crown of Jolliginki!”
sentences.zh: 发誓——以乔利金基的王冠发誓！」

hints.zh: 乔利金基，邦波父亲的王国，医生一行就被关在这里；以王冠起誓是他们最重的誓言。
hints.en: Jolliginki, the kingdom of Bumpo's father, where the Doctor is locked up. Swearing by its crown is the strongest promise there is.

introduction.zh: 王子不要金发，只要一张白脸，还顺带想要一双蓝眼睛。杜立德医生叹了口气，没有立刻动手：要试，得先谈好一条备好食物的船，和一句以王冠起的誓。
introduction.en: The Prince does not want golden hair; he wants a white face, and blue eyes as well. The Doctor sighs. Before he tries anything, he wants two things settled: a ship stocked with food, and an oath sworn on the crown.

quiz.question: What does the Prince say when the Doctor offers to change his hair?
options: He agrees to try it first
He asks for a beard as well
Nothing else will satisfy him

feedback.zh: 他一口回绝：「别的都不能让我满意，我必须做一个白人王子。」
feedback.en: He refuses at once: nothing else will satisfy him — he must be a white prince.

quiz.question: What must happen before the Doctor will begin?
options: Bumpo must bring the crown to the prison
A ship with food must be ready at the beach
The King must say yes to the plan

feedback.zh: 医生的条件是：先备好一条带食物的船，事成之后还要放他和动物们出牢房。
feedback.en: The Doctor's terms: a ship with food ready first, and after the job, freedom for himself and all his animals.

grammar.excerpt: one of the hardest things a magician can do

focus.zh: the hardest 是最高级；things 后面省掉了关系代词，a magician can do 直接修饰 things。
focus.en: The hardest is a superlative; the relative pronoun after things is left out, so a magician can do describes the things.

paragraphs.text: So the Prince promised and went away to get a ship ready at the seashore.

sentences.text: So the Prince promised and went away to get a ship ready at the seashore.
sentences.zh: 王子就发了誓，离开去海边准备船。

paragraphs.text: When he came back and said that it was done, the Doctor asked Dab-Dab to bring a basin. Then he mixed a lot of medicines in the basin and told Bumpo to dip his face in it.

sentences.text: When he came back and said that it was done, the Doctor asked Dab-Dab to bring a basin.
sentences.zh: 等他回来，说船已经备好，医生就请达布达布拿一个盆来。

sentences.text: Then he mixed a lot of medicines in the basin and told Bumpo to dip his face in it.
sentences.zh: 然后他把许多药调进盆里，让邦波把脸浸进去。

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor's duck.

paragraphs.text: The Prince leaned down and put his face in—right up to the ears.

sentences.text: The Prince leaned down and put his face in—right up to the ears.
sentences.zh: 王子俯下身，把脸浸了进去——一直浸到耳朵。

paragraphs.text: He held it there a long time—so long that the Doctor seemed to get dreadfully anxious and fidgety, standing first on one leg and then on the other, looking at all the bottles he had used for the mixture, and reading the labels on them again and again. A strong smell filled the prison, like the smell of brown paper burning.

sentences.text: He held it there a long time—so long that the Doctor seemed to get dreadfully anxious and fidgety, standing first on one leg and then on the other, looking at all the bottles he had used for the mixture, and reading the labels on them again and again.
sentences.zh: 他在里面憋了很久——久到医生显得非常紧张、坐立不安，一会儿用这条腿站，一会儿换那条腿，还去看他调药时用过的那些瓶子，把上面的标签读了一遍又一遍。

sentences.text: A strong smell filled the prison, like the smell of brown paper burning.
