sentences.zh: 牢房里弥漫着一股浓烈的气味，像牛皮纸烧着了的味道。

hints.zh: 坐立不安、烦躁地动来动去。
hints.en: Fidgety: unable to keep still because you are nervous.

hints.zh: 棕色包装纸、牛皮纸；烧起来有股特别的气味。
hints.en: Brown paper, the thick wrapping paper; it has a smell of its own when it burns.

paragraphs.text: At last the Prince lifted his face up out of the basin, breathing very hard. And all the animals cried out in surprise.

sentences.text: At last the Prince lifted his face up out of the basin, breathing very hard.
sentences.zh: 最后，王子把脸从盆里抬起来，喘得很厉害。

sentences.text: And all the animals cried out in surprise.
sentences.zh: 所有的动物都惊讶地叫了起来。

paragraphs.text: For the Prince’s face had turned as white as snow, and his eyes, which had been mud-colored, were a manly gray!

sentences.text: For the Prince’s face had turned as white as snow, and his eyes, which had been mud-colored, were a manly gray!
sentences.zh: 因为王子的脸已经变得像雪一样白，他那双原本泥色的眼睛，也成了英气十足的灰色！

hints.zh: 泥色的，土褐色的；说他原来的肤色。
hints.en: Mud-coloured: the colour of mud, his old skin colour.

paragraphs.text: When John Dolittle lent him a little looking-glass to see himself in, he sang for joy and began dancing around the prison. But the Doctor asked him not to make so much noise about it; and when he had closed his medicine-bag in a hurry he told him to open the prison-door.

sentences.text: When John Dolittle lent him a little looking-glass to see himself in, he sang for joy and began dancing around the prison.
sentences.zh: 约翰·杜立德借给他一面小镜子照自己，他高兴得唱起歌来，在牢房里跳起舞。

sentences.text: But the Doctor asked him not to make so much noise about it; and when he had closed his medicine-bag in a hurry he told him to open the prison-door.
sentences.zh: 可医生让他别为这事弄出这么大动静；医生匆匆合上药袋，然后叫他打开牢门。

hints.zh: 镜子的旧说法，等于 mirror。
hints.en: Looking-glass: an old word for a mirror.

introduction.zh: 王子备好了船。杜立德医生把许多药水倒进盆里，让邦波把脸埋进去。等的时间太久了，医生一条腿换一条腿地站着，反复读瓶子上的标签——这一盆东西会弄出什么结果？
introduction.en: The ship is ready. The Doctor pours his medicines into a basin and tells Bumpo to put his face in. The wait is long, and the Doctor shifts from one leg to the other, reading the labels over and over. What will come out of that basin?

quiz.question: What did the animals see when the Prince lifted his face out of the basin?
options: His face had turned as white as snow
Only his hair had changed colour
Nothing had changed at all

feedback.zh: 原文说他脸白得像雪，原本泥色的眼睛也变成了灰色，所以动物们惊叫起来。
feedback.en: His face had turned as white as snow and his mud-coloured eyes were grey, so the animals cried out.

quiz.question: What was the Doctor doing while the Prince kept his face in the basin?
options: Reading a book by the prison window
Mixing a second basin of medicine
Standing first on one leg and then on the other

feedback.zh: 他紧张得坐立不安，一条腿换一条腿地站，还把用过的瓶子标签读了一遍又一遍。
feedback.en: He was dreadfully fidgety — one leg, then the other — and read the labels on his bottles again and again.

grammar.excerpt: so long that the Doctor seemed to get dreadfully anxious and fidgety

focus.zh: so + 形容词 + that 从句：that 后面说明「久」到什么结果——医生都紧张得坐立不安了。
focus.en: So + adjective + that-clause: the that-clause gives the result — he held it so long that the Doctor grew anxious.

paragraphs.text: Bumpo begged that he might keep the looking-glass, as it was the only one in the Kingdom of Jolliginki, and he wanted to look at himself all day long. But the Doctor said he needed it to shave with.

sentences.text: Bumpo begged that he might keep the looking-glass, as it was the only one in the Kingdom of Jolliginki, and he wanted to look at himself all day long.
sentences.zh: 邦波求他把镜子留下，因为这是乔利金基王国唯一的一面镜子，他想整天照着自己看。

sentences.text: But the Doctor said he needed it to shave with.
sentences.zh: 可医生说他刮胡子要用它。

paragraphs.text: Then the Prince, taking a bunch of copper keys from his pocket, undid the great double locks. And the Doctor with all his animals ran as fast as they could down to the seashore; while Bumpo leaned against the wall of the empty dungeon, smiling after them happily, his big face shining like polished ivory in the light of the moon.

sentences.text: Then the Prince, taking a bunch of copper keys from his pocket, undid the great double locks.
sentences.zh: 王子从口袋里掏出一串铜钥匙，打开了那两把大锁。

sentences.text: And the Doctor with all his animals ran as fast as they could down to the seashore; while Bumpo leaned against the wall of the empty dungeon, smiling after them happily, his big face shining like polished ivory in the light of the moon.
sentences.zh: 医生带着所有的动物，尽快往海边跑去；邦波则靠在空牢房的墙上，快活地朝他们的背影笑，他那张大脸在月光下像磨光的象牙一样发亮。

hints.zh: 地牢，城堡或王宫里关人的牢房。
hints.en: A dungeon: the prison room inside a castle or palace.

hints.zh: 象牙；磨光以后会发亮。
hints.en: Ivory: elephant tusk, which shines when it is polished.

paragraphs.text: When they came to the beach they saw Polynesia and Chee-Chee waiting for them on the rocks near the ship.

sentences.text: When they came to the beach they saw Polynesia and Chee-Chee waiting for them on the rocks near the ship.
sentences.zh: 他们到了海滩，看见波利尼西亚和奇奇在船边的岩石上等着他们。

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey.

paragraphs.text: “I feel sorry about Bumpo,” said the Doctor. “I am afraid that medicine I used will never last. Most likely he will be as black as ever when he wakes up in the morning—that’s one reason why I didn’t like to leave the mirror with him. But then again, he might stay white—I had never used that mixture before. To tell the truth, I was surprised, myself, that it worked so well. But I had to do something, didn’t I?—I couldn’t possibly scrub the King’s kitchen for the rest of my life. It was such a dirty kitchen!—I could see it from the prison-window.—Well, well!—Poor Bumpo!”

sentences.text: “I feel sorry about Bumpo,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我心里挺为邦波难过，」医生说。

sentences.text: “I am afraid that medicine I used will never last.
sentences.zh: 「我怕我用的那种药撑不了多久。

sentences.text: Most likely he will be as black as ever when he wakes up in the morning—that’s one reason why I didn’t like to leave the mirror with him.
sentences.zh: 等他早上醒来，多半还是跟以前一样黑——这也是我不愿意把镜子留给他的一个原因。

sentences.text: But then again, he might stay white—I had never used that mixture before.
sentences.zh: 不过话又说回来，他也可能一直白下去——那种药我以前从没配过。

sentences.text: To tell the truth, I was surprised, myself, that it worked so well.
sentences.zh: 说实话，它效果这么好，连我自己都吃了一惊。

sentences.text: But I had to do something, didn’t I?—I couldn’t possibly scrub the King’s kitchen for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 可我总得想个办法，不是吗？——我总不能给国王擦一辈子厨房。

sentences.text: It was such a dirty kitchen!—I could see it from the prison-window.—Well, well!—Poor Bumpo!”
sentences.zh: 那厨房脏成那样！——我从牢房窗户里就看得见。——唉，唉！——可怜的邦波！」

hints.zh: 说实话、老实说；用在句首，表示下面说的是真心话。
hints.en: To tell the truth: said before an honest admission.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, of course he will know we were just joking with him,” said the parrot.

sentences.text: “Oh, of course he will know we were just joking with him,” said the parrot.
sentences.zh: 「哦，他当然会明白我们只是跟他开了个玩笑，」鹦鹉说。

introduction.zh: 邦波抱着镜子舍不得还，医生却说他刮胡子要用。牢门开了，人和动物一起往海边跑；奇怪的是，医生一边跑一边回头，脸上没有多少高兴的样子。他在担心什么？
introduction.en: Bumpo cannot bear to give up the looking-glass, but the Doctor says he needs it to shave. Then the prison door is open and everyone runs for the shore. The Doctor, though, keeps looking back, and his face is not happy. What is he afraid of?

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor refuse to leave the looking-glass with Bumpo?
options: He says it is worth a lot of money
He says he needs it to shave with
He says it belongs to the King

feedback.zh: 医生当场给的理由很平常：他刮胡子要用这面镜子。
feedback.en: His reason is a very ordinary one: he needs it to shave with.

quiz.question: What is the Doctor afraid of as they leave the prison?
options: That the medicine will not last and Bumpo will turn black again
That the King's soldiers are running after them
That Bumpo will not keep his promise about the ship

feedback.zh: 他直说「我怕我用的那种药撑不了多久」，还猜想王子早上醒来多半又变回原来的样子。
feedback.en: He says he is afraid the medicine will never last, and thinks Bumpo will most likely be as black as ever by morning.

grammar.excerpt: Bumpo begged that he might keep the looking-glass

focus.zh: begged 后面接 that 从句，用来说明他求的是什么；从句里的 might 让请求听起来更委婉。
focus.en: Begged is followed by a that-clause saying what he asked for; might makes the request softer.

paragraphs.text: “They had no business to lock us up,” said Dab-Dab, waggling her tail angrily. “We never did them any harm. Serve him right, if he does turn black again! I hope it’s a dark black.”

sentences.text: “They had no business to lock us up,” said Dab-Dab, waggling her tail angrily.
sentences.zh: 「他们根本没道理把我们关起来，」达布达布气呼呼地摇着尾巴说。

sentences.text: “We never did them any harm.
sentences.zh: 「我们从没害过他们。

sentences.text: Serve him right, if he does turn black again!
sentences.zh: 他要是又变回黑人，那是他活该！

sentences.text: I hope it’s a dark black.”
sentences.zh: 我希望黑得不能再黑。」

hints.zh: have no business to do 意思是「没有权利、根本不该做某事」。
hints.en: Had no business to lock us up: they had no right to lock us up.

hints.zh: 他活该、他自找的；表示某人受惩罚是应得的。
hints.en: Serve him right: he deserves it.

paragraphs.text: “But he didn’t have anything to do with it,” said the Doctor. “It was the King, his father, who had us locked up—it wasn’t Bumpo’s fault.... I wonder if I ought to go back and apologize—Oh, well—I’ll send him some candy when I get to Puddleby. And who knows?—he may stay white after all.”

sentences.text: “But he didn’t have anything to do with it,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可这事跟他没关系，」医生说。

sentences.text: “It was the King, his father, who had us locked up—it wasn’t Bumpo’s fault....
sentences.zh: 「把我们关起来的是他父亲，国王——这不是邦波的错……

sentences.text: I wonder if I ought to go back and apologize—Oh, well—I’ll send him some candy when I get to Puddleby.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我是不是该回去道个歉——唉，算了——等我回到帕德尔比，给他寄点糖果吧。

sentences.text: And who knows?—he may stay white after all.”
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？——说不定他真的一直白下去了。」

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor's home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

paragraphs.text: “The Sleeping Beauty would never have him, even if he did,” said Dab-Dab. “He looked better the way he was, I thought. But he’d never be anything but ugly, no matter what color he was made.”

sentences.text: “The Sleeping Beauty would never have him, even if he did,” said Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「就算他真的一直白着，睡美人也不会要他，」达布达布说。

sentences.text: “He looked better the way he was, I thought.
sentences.zh: 「我倒觉得他原来的样子更好看。

sentences.text: But he’d never be anything but ugly, no matter what color he was made.”
sentences.zh: 可不管把他弄成什么颜色，他也只会是个丑样子。」

paragraphs.text: “Still, he had a good heart,” said the Doctor—“romantic, of course—but a good heart. After all, ‘handsome is as handsome does.’”

sentences.text: “Still, he had a good heart,” said the Doctor—“romantic, of course—but a good heart.
sentences.zh: 「不过，他心肠好，」医生说，「当然，有点爱幻想——可心肠是好的。

sentences.text: After all, ‘handsome is as handsome does.’”
sentences.zh: 说到底，『人好看不好看，要看人做的事』嘛。」

paragraphs.text: “I don’t believe the poor booby found The Sleeping Beauty at all,” said Jip, the dog. “Most likely he kissed some farmer’s fat wife who was taking a snooze under an apple-tree. Can’t blame her for getting scared! I wonder who he’ll go and kiss this time. Silly business!”

sentences.text: “I don’t believe the poor booby found The Sleeping Beauty at all,” said Jip, the dog.
sentences.zh: 「我看这个可怜的傻瓜根本没找到睡美人，」狗吉普说。

sentences.text: “Most likely he kissed some farmer’s fat wife who was taking a snooze under an apple-tree.
sentences.zh: 「多半是他吻了哪个农夫家的胖老婆——那人正在苹果树下打盹呢。

sentences.text: Can’t blame her for getting scared!
sentences.zh: 她被吓着，也不能怪她！

sentences.text: I wonder who he’ll go and kiss this time.
sentences.zh: 不知道这一回他又要去吻谁。

sentences.text: Silly business!”
sentences.zh: 荒唐事！」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor's dog.

paragraphs.text: Then the pushmi-pullyu, the white mouse, Gub-Gub, Dab-Dab, Jip and the owl, Too-Too, went on to the ship with the Doctor. But Chee-Chee, Polynesia and the crocodile stayed behind, because Africa was their proper home, the land where they were born.

sentences.text: Then the pushmi-pullyu, the white mouse, Gub-Gub, Dab-Dab, Jip and the owl, Too-Too, went on to the ship with the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 于是「推我拉你」、白鼠、咕咕、达布达布、吉普和猫头鹰图图，跟着医生上了船。

sentences.text: But Chee-Chee, Polynesia and the crocodile stayed behind, because Africa was their proper home, the land where they were born.
sentences.zh: 但奇奇、波利尼西亚和鳄鱼留了下来，因为非洲才是它们真正的家，是它们出生的土地。

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor's owl.

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，那只两头动物，一头说话一头吃草。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu, the two-headed animal, with a head at each end.

introduction.zh: 到了海边，动物们为邦波的事争了起来：鸭子气得直摇尾巴，狗讲了个不太好听的猜测，医生替王子说了句好话。上船之前，还有一件事没定下来——谁跟医生回帕德尔比，谁留在非洲？
introduction.en: At the shore the animals argue about Bumpo: the duck is angry, the dog makes a rude guess, and the Doctor says a kind word for the Prince. Before they sail, one thing is still open — who will go to Puddleby, and who will stay in Africa?

quiz.question: Who does the Doctor say was really to blame for locking them up?
options: Bumpo himself
The parrot, Polynesia
The King, Bumpo's father

feedback.zh: 医生点明：下令关人的是邦波的父亲国王，所以这不是邦波的错。
feedback.en: The Doctor points out that it was the King, Bumpo's father, who had them locked up.

quiz.question: What does Dab-Dab think of the Prince's looks?
options: He has always been handsome
He looked better the way he was
He is much handsomer now that he is white

feedback.zh: 达布达布说「我倒觉得他原来的样子更好看」，还说不管什么颜色他都是丑的。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab says he looked better the way he was, and that he would be ugly in any colour.

grammar.excerpt: It was the King, his father, who had us locked up

focus.zh: had us locked up 是 have + 宾语 + 过去分词：不是国王自己锁门，而是叫人把我们关了起来。
focus.en: Had us locked up is have + object + past participle: someone else did the locking, not the King himself.

paragraphs.text: And when the Doctor stood upon the boat, he looked over the side across the water. And then he remembered that they had no one with them to guide them back to Puddleby.

sentences.text: And when the Doctor stood upon the boat, he looked over the side across the water.
sentences.zh: 医生站在船上，从船边望过水面。

sentences.text: And then he remembered that they had no one with them to guide them back to Puddleby.
sentences.zh: 这时他想起，身边没有人能带他们回帕德尔比。

paragraphs.text: The wide, wide sea looked terribly big and lonesome in the moonlight; and he began to wonder if they would lose their way when they passed out of sight of land.

sentences.text: The wide, wide sea looked terribly big and lonesome in the moonlight; and he began to wonder if they would lose their way when they passed out of sight of land.
sentences.zh: 月光下，茫茫大海显得又大又孤单；他开始担心，等驶到看不见陆地的地方，他们会不会迷路。

hints.zh: 看不见陆地的地方，也就是远离海岸的洋面。
hints.en: Out of sight of land: far from the coast, with no land in view.

paragraphs.text: But even while he was wondering, they heard a strange whispering noise, high in the air, coming through the night. And the animals all stopped saying Good-by and listened.

sentences.text: But even while he was wondering, they heard a strange whispering noise, high in the air, coming through the night.
sentences.zh: 就在他担心的时候，他们听见高空中有一种奇怪的沙沙声，透过夜色传来。

sentences.text: And the animals all stopped saying Good-by and listened.
sentences.zh: 动物们都停下道别，侧耳倾听。

hints.zh: 低低的沙沙声，像有人贴着耳朵说悄悄话。
hints.en: A whispering noise: a soft, rustling sound, like whispers.

paragraphs.text: The noise grew louder and bigger. It seemed to be coming nearer to them—a sound like the Autumn wind blowing through the leaves of a poplar-tree, or a great, great rain beating down upon a roof.

sentences.text: The noise grew louder and bigger.
sentences.zh: 那声音越来越响，越来越大。

sentences.text: It seemed to be coming nearer to them—a sound like the Autumn wind blowing through the leaves of a poplar-tree, or a great, great rain beating down upon a roof.
sentences.zh: 它好像正在靠近他们——像秋风穿过白杨树的叶子，又像一场极大的雨打在屋顶上。

hints.zh: 白杨树，叶子又薄又密，风一吹就沙沙响。
hints.en: A poplar-tree, whose thin leaves rustle in the wind.

paragraphs.text: And Jip, with his nose pointing and his tail quite straight, said,

sentences.text: And Jip, with his nose pointing and his tail quite straight, said,
sentences.zh: 吉普把鼻子朝前指着，尾巴伸得笔直，说：

paragraphs.text: “Birds!—millions of them—flying fast—that’s it!”

sentences.text: “Birds!—millions of them—flying fast—that’s it!”
sentences.zh: 「鸟！——几百万只——飞得很快——就是它！」

paragraphs.text: And then they all looked up. And there, streaming across the face of the moon, like a huge swarm of tiny ants, they could see thousands and thousands of little birds. Soon the whole sky seemed full of them, and still more kept coming—more and more. There were so many that for a little they covered the whole moon so it could not shine, and the sea grew dark and black—like when a storm-cloud passes over the sun.

sentences.text: And then they all looked up.
sentences.zh: 于是他们全都抬起头来。

sentences.text: And there, streaming across the face of the moon, like a huge swarm of tiny ants, they could see thousands and thousands of little birds.
sentences.zh: 只见成千上万的小鸟像一大群小蚂蚁一样，从月亮前面流过。

sentences.text: Soon the whole sky seemed full of them, and still more kept coming—more and more.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，整个天空好像都装满了鸟，还有更多的不断飞来——越来越多。

sentences.text: There were so many that for a little they covered the whole moon so it could not shine, and the sea grew dark and black—like when a storm-cloud passes over the sun.
sentences.zh: 鸟多得一时把整个月亮都遮住了，月亮照不出来，海面变得又暗又黑——就像乌云遮住太阳的时候。

hints.zh: 一大群（飞虫、鸟），密密集集地一起动。
hints.en: A swarm: a very large group of small flying creatures moving together.

introduction.zh: 船离了岸，四面的海又大又空。医生忽然想起：回帕德尔比这一路，没有人替他们带路。就在这时，高高的夜空中传来一阵沙沙的怪声，越来越近——那是风，是雨，还是别的什么？
introduction.en: The ship leaves the shore, and the sea looks huge and empty. Then the Doctor remembers: no one on board can guide them back to Puddleby. Just then a strange rustling comes out of the high night sky, closer and closer. Wind? Rain? Something else?

quiz.question: What is the Doctor worried about at first?
options: That they will lose their way at sea
That they will run out of food
That the ship is too small for the animals

feedback.zh: 他担心驶出看得见陆地的地方以后会迷路，因为船上没人认识回帕德尔比的路。
feedback.en: He wonders if they will lose their way once they pass out of sight of land — nobody on board knows the way home.

quiz.question: What does Jip say the noise is?
options: A storm coming over the sea
The wind in the trees on shore
Millions of birds flying fast

feedback.zh: 吉普鼻子朝前、尾巴笔直，喊出「鸟！——几百万只——飞得很快」。
feedback.en: With his nose pointing and his tail straight, Jip calls out: birds, millions of them, flying fast.

grammar.excerpt: they heard a strange whispering noise, high in the air, coming through the night

focus.zh: heard + 宾语 + coming：coming 是现在分词，补出声音正从夜空传来，不是句子的谓语。
focus.en: Heard + object + coming: the -ing form shows the noise coming through the night; it is not the main verb.

paragraphs.text: And presently all these birds came down close, skimming over the water and the land; and the night-sky was left clear above, and the moon shone as before. Still never a call nor a cry nor a song they made—no sound but this great rustling of feathers which grew greater now than ever. When they began to settle on the sands, along the ropes of the ship—anywhere and everywhere except the trees—the Doctor could see that they had blue wings and white breasts and very short, feathered legs. As soon as they had all found a place to sit, suddenly, there was no noise left anywhere—all was quiet; all was still.

sentences.text: And presently all these birds came down close, skimming over the water and the land; and the night-sky was left clear above, and the moon shone as before.
sentences.zh: 不久，这些鸟都低低地飞下来，掠过水面和地面；上方的夜空又清朗了，月亮照旧亮着。

sentences.text: Still never a call nor a cry nor a song they made—no sound but this great rustling of feathers which grew greater now than ever.
sentences.zh: 它们仍旧不叫、不喊、不唱——除了那巨大的羽毛沙沙声，一点声音也没有，这声音此刻比先前更响了。

sentences.text: When they began to settle on the sands, along the ropes of the ship—anywhere and everywhere except the trees—the Doctor could see that they had blue wings and white breasts and very short, feathered legs.
sentences.zh: 当它们开始落在沙滩上、船上的缆绳上——到处都落，就是不上树——医生看清了：它们有蓝色的翅膀、白色的胸脯，还有长着羽毛的短短的腿。

sentences.text: As soon as they had all found a place to sit, suddenly, there was no noise left anywhere—all was quiet; all was still.
sentences.zh: 它们刚全都找到落脚的地方，忽然，四下里一点声音都没有了——一切都安静下来，一切都静住了。

hints.zh: 掠过、贴着表面飞过；skimming over the water 就是贴着水面飞。
hints.en: Skimming: flying just above the surface, almost touching it.

paragraphs.text: And in the silent moonlight John Dolittle spoke:

sentences.text: And in the silent moonlight John Dolittle spoke:
sentences.zh: 在静静的月光里，约翰·杜立德开口了：

paragraphs.text: “I had no idea that we had been in Africa so long. It will be nearly Summer when we get home. For these are the swallows going back. Swallows, I thank you for waiting for us. It is very thoughtful of you. Now we need not be afraid that we will lose our way upon the sea.... Pull up the anchor and set the sail!”

sentences.text: “I had no idea that we had been in Africa so long.
sentences.zh: 「我一点也没想到我们在非洲待了这么久。

sentences.text: It will be nearly Summer when we get home.
sentences.zh: 等我们到家，差不多就是夏天了。

sentences.text: For these are the swallows going back.
sentences.zh: 因为这些都是往回飞的燕子。

sentences.text: Swallows, I thank you for waiting for us.
sentences.zh: 燕子们，谢谢你们等我们。

sentences.text: It is very thoughtful of you.
sentences.zh: 你们想得真周到。

sentences.text: Now we need not be afraid that we will lose our way upon the sea....
sentences.zh: 现在我们不必担心在海上迷路了……

sentences.text: Pull up the anchor and set the sail!”
sentences.zh: 起锚，扬帆！」

hints.zh: 燕子；它们每年秋天成群飞往温暖的地方，春天再飞回来。
hints.en: Swallows: small birds that fly off to warm lands each year and come back in spring.

hints.zh: 这里不是「爱思考」，而是「体贴、替别人着想」。
hints.en: Thoughtful here does not mean “clever”: it means kind and considerate.

hints.zh: 起锚，把锚从水底拉上来，准备开船。
hints.en: Pull up the anchor: lift it out of the water so the ship can sail.

paragraphs.text: When the ship moved out upon the water, those who stayed behind, Chee-Chee, Polynesia and the crocodile, grew terribly sad. For never in their lives had they known any one they liked so well as Doctor John Dolittle of Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

sentences.text: When the ship moved out upon the water, those who stayed behind, Chee-Chee, Polynesia and the crocodile, grew terribly sad.
sentences.zh: 船驶到水面上，留下来的奇奇、波利尼西亚和鳄鱼难过极了。

sentences.text: For never in their lives had they known any one they liked so well as Doctor John Dolittle of Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.
sentences.zh: 因为他们这辈子从没遇到过像沼泽边的帕德尔比镇约翰·杜立德医生这样让他们喜欢的人。

paragraphs.text: And after they had called Good-by to him again and again and again, they still stood there upon the rocks, crying bitterly and waving till the ship was out of sight.

sentences.text: And after they had called Good-by to him again and again and again, they still stood there upon the rocks, crying bitterly and waving till the ship was out of sight.
sentences.zh: 他们一遍又一遍地向他喊「再见」，之后仍旧站在岩石上，痛哭着挥手，直到船看不见为止。

hints.zh: 哭得很伤心；bitterly 在这里表示痛苦、难受的程度。
hints.en: Crying bitterly: crying hard, in deep sorrow.

introduction.zh: 它们落下来了，落在沙滩上、缆绳上，却一片树叶也不碰；蓝翅膀，白胸脯，短腿上长着羽毛。杜立德医生在月光里抬头看着它们，说了一句让人放心的话——这些鸟要往哪里去？
introduction.en: Down they come — on the sands, on the ship's ropes, anywhere but the trees: blue wings, white breasts, short feathered legs. In the moonlight the Doctor speaks to them, and what he says makes everyone feel safe. Where are these birds going?

quiz.question: What kind of birds are they?
options: Birds that escaped from the King's palace
Swallows flying back home
Sea-birds from a near island

feedback.zh: 医生说出答案：「这些都是往回飞的燕子」，还说自己没想到在非洲待了这么久。
feedback.en: The Doctor names them: these are the swallows going back. He had not known they had been in Africa so long.

quiz.question: Why is the Doctor glad to see the birds?
options: They can show the ship the way home
They will bring food for the animals
They will sing the animals to sleep

feedback.zh: 他说「现在我们不必担心在海上迷路了」，随后就叫人起锚扬帆。
feedback.en: He says they need not be afraid of losing their way on the sea, and then orders the anchor up.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as they had all found a place to sit

focus.zh: as soon as 引导时间从句，意思是「一……就……」；从句用过去完成时，主句的事紧接着发生。
focus.en: As soon as introduces the time clause: the moment they had all found a seat, the next thing happened.

paragraphs.text: Sailing homeward, the Doctor’s ship had to pass the coast of Barbary. This coast is the seashore of the Great Desert. It is a wild, lonely place—all sand and stones. And it was here that the Barbary pirates lived.

sentences.text: Sailing homeward, the Doctor’s ship had to pass the coast of Barbary.
sentences.zh: 杜立德医生的船在返航途中，不得不经过巴巴里海岸。

sentences.text: This coast is the seashore of the Great Desert.
sentences.zh: 这段海岸是大沙漠边上的海滨。

sentences.text: It is a wild, lonely place—all sand and stones.
sentences.zh: 那是个荒凉、孤寂的地方——除了沙子就是石头。

sentences.text: And it was here that the Barbary pirates lived.
sentences.zh: 而巴巴里海盗就住在这里。

hints.zh: 巴巴里，北非地中海沿岸一带；本书里是海盗出没的海岸。
hints.en: Barbary: the north coast of Africa, in this book a shore where pirates live.

hints.zh: 大沙漠，指撒哈拉沙漠；这片海岸就是它的边缘。
hints.en: The Great Desert: the Sahara, whose edge is this coast.

paragraphs.text: These pirates, a bad lot of men, used to wait for sailors to be shipwrecked on their shores. And often, if they saw a boat passing, they would come out in their fast sailing-ships and chase it. When they caught a boat like this at sea, they would steal everything on it; and after they had taken the people off they would sink the ship and sail back to Barbary singing songs and feeling proud of the mischief they had done. Then they used to make the people they had caught write home to their friends for money. And if the friends sent no money, the pirates often threw the people into the sea.

sentences.text: These pirates, a bad lot of men, used to wait for sailors to be shipwrecked on their shores.
sentences.zh: 这些海盗是一伙坏蛋，过去常常等着水手在他们的海岸上遇难。

sentences.text: And often, if they saw a boat passing, they would come out in their fast sailing-ships and chase it.
sentences.zh: 而且常常是这样：他们一看见有船经过，就驾着快帆船冲出来追赶。

sentences.text: When they caught a boat like this at sea, they would steal everything on it; and after they had taken the people off they would sink the ship and sail back to Barbary singing songs and feeling proud of the mischief they had done.
sentences.zh: 他们在海上截住这样一条船，就把船上的东西全部抢走；把人带走之后，再把船弄沉，然后唱着歌驶回巴巴里，为自己干的坏事得意洋洋。

sentences.text: Then they used to make the people they had caught write home to their friends for money.
sentences.zh: 接着他们又逼着抓来的人写信回家，向亲友要钱。

sentences.text: And if the friends sent no money, the pirates often threw the people into the sea.
sentences.zh: 要是亲友不寄钱来，海盗就常常把人扔进海里。

hints.zh: 一伙坏蛋；lot 这里指「一群人」，不是「许多」。
hints.en: A bad lot of men means a bad bunch of men; lot here is a group of people.

hints.zh: 这里指伤人性命的恶行、祸害，不只是「恶作剧」。
hints.en: Here mischief means real harm done to people, not a small prank.

paragraphs.text: Now one sunshiny day the Doctor and Dab-Dab were walking up and down on the ship for exercise; a nice fresh wind was blowing the boat along, and everybody was happy. Presently Dab-Dab saw the sail of another ship a long way behind them on the edge of the sea. It was a red sail.

sentences.text: Now one sunshiny day the Doctor and Dab-Dab were walking up and down on the ship for exercise; a nice fresh wind was blowing the boat along, and everybody was happy.
sentences.zh: 有一天阳光很好，医生和达布达布在船上走来走去活动身体；一阵清爽的风吹着船往前走，大家都很高兴。

sentences.text: Presently Dab-Dab saw the sail of another ship a long way behind them on the edge of the sea.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，达布达布看见他们身后很远的海天交界处，出现了另一条船的帆。

sentences.text: It was a red sail.
sentences.zh: 那是一张红帆。

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

introduction.zh: 船正往家开，却必须从巴巴里海岸经过。那里只有沙子和石头，还住着一伙专靠过往船只发财的海盗。这一次，杜立德医生的船能从这片海岸平安开过去吗？
introduction.en: The Doctor’s ship is sailing home, but the way home runs past the coast of Barbary, a lonely shore of sand and stone where pirates live. Can the Doctor’s little ship get past them safely?

quiz.question: Why did the Barbary pirates wait on their shores?
options: To keep other boats away from the coast.
To sell food and water to passing ships.
To catch sailors whose ships were wrecked there.

feedback.zh: 原文说这些海盗过去常常等着水手在他们的海岸上遇难，好下手抓人。
feedback.en: The text says the pirates used to wait for sailors to be shipwrecked on their shores.

quiz.question: What did Dab-Dab see far behind the ship?
options: A dark line of rocks.
Another flock of birds.
A sail, and it was red.

feedback.zh: 达布达布看见身后很远的海上有另一条船的帆，下一句点明那是红帆。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab saw the sail of another ship far behind them, and it was red.

grammar.excerpt: used to wait for sailors to be shipwrecked on their shores

focus.zh: used to wait 表示过去经常这样做；used to 后面跟动词原形，本段后面的 used to make 同理。
focus.en: Used to wait means they did this again and again in the past; used to takes the base verb, as in used to make later.

paragraphs.text: “I don’t like the look of that sail,” said Dab-Dab. “I have a feeling it isn’t a friendly ship. I am afraid there is more trouble coming to us.”

sentences.text: “I don’t like the look of that sail,” said Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「我不喜欢那张帆的样子。」达布达布说。

sentences.text: “I have a feeling it isn’t a friendly ship.
sentences.zh: 「我总觉得那不是一条友善的船。

sentences.text: I am afraid there is more trouble coming to us.”
sentences.zh: 我怕又有麻烦要找上门来了。」

hints.zh: 「那张帆的样子」——由帆推想那是一条什么船、船上是什么人。
hints.en: The look of that sail: what the sail makes her think of the ship and the men on it.

hints.zh: 我有种感觉、我总觉得；后面常接一个说不清理由的判断。
hints.en: I have a feeling: I sense it, though I cannot prove it.

paragraphs.text: Jip, who was lying near taking a nap in the sun, began to growl and talk in his sleep.

sentences.text: Jip, who was lying near taking a nap in the sun, began to growl and talk in his sleep.
sentences.zh: 吉普正躺在旁边晒太阳打盹，忽然开始低声吼叫，还在睡梦里说起话来。

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

paragraphs.text: “I smell roast beef cooking,” he mumbled—“underdone roast beef—with brown gravy over it.”

sentences.text: “I smell roast beef cooking,” he mumbled—“underdone roast beef—with brown gravy over it.”
sentences.zh: 「我闻到烤牛肉的味儿了，」他含含糊糊地说——「半生不熟的烤牛肉——上面还浇着棕色肉汁。」

paragraphs.text: “Good gracious!” cried the Doctor. “What’s the matter with the dog? Is he smelling in his sleep—as well as talking?”

sentences.text: “Good gracious!” cried the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「天哪！」医生叫道。

sentences.text: “What’s the matter with the dog?
sentences.zh: 「这狗怎么了？

sentences.text: Is he smelling in his sleep—as well as talking?”
sentences.zh: 他不但说梦话，还在梦里闻味儿吗？」

hints.zh: 天哪！表示吃惊的感叹语，旧时说法。
hints.en: Good gracious: an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise.

paragraphs.text: “I suppose he is,” said Dab-Dab. “All dogs can smell in their sleep.”

sentences.text: “I suppose he is,” said Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「我看是的。」达布达布说。

sentences.text: “All dogs can smell in their sleep.”
sentences.zh: 「狗在睡梦里都能闻见味道。」

paragraphs.text: “But what is he smelling?” asked the Doctor. “There is no roast beef cooking on our ship.”

sentences.text: “But what is he smelling?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可他闻到的是什么？」医生问。

sentences.text: “There is no roast beef cooking on our ship.”
sentences.zh: 「我们船上没有在烤牛肉呀。」

paragraphs.text: “No,” said Dab-Dab. “The roast beef must be on that other ship over there.”

sentences.text: “No,” said Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「是没有。」达布达布说。

sentences.text: “The roast beef must be on that other ship over there.”
sentences.zh: 「烤牛肉一定在那边的另一条船上。」

paragraphs.text: “But that’s ten miles away,” said the Doctor. “He couldn’t smell that far surely!”

sentences.text: “But that’s ten miles away,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可那船离我们有十英里远，」医生说。

sentences.text: “He couldn’t smell that far surely!”
sentences.zh: 「他总不能闻到那么远吧！」

paragraphs.text: “Oh, yes, he could,” said Dab-Dab. “You ask him.”

sentences.text: “Oh, yes, he could,” said Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「哦，他闻得到。」达布达布说。

sentences.text: “You ask him.”
sentences.zh: 「你问问他好了。」

paragraphs.text: Then Jip, still fast asleep, began to growl again and his lip curled up angrily, showing his clean, white teeth.

sentences.text: Then Jip, still fast asleep, began to growl again and his lip curled up angrily, showing his clean, white teeth.
sentences.zh: 这时吉普仍然睡得很沉，又开始低吼，嘴唇气呼呼地往上翻，露出干净的白牙。

hints.zh: 睡得很沉；这里的 fast 不是「快」，而是「牢牢地、深深地」。
hints.en: Fast asleep means deeply asleep; fast here does not mean quickly.

paragraphs.text: “I smell bad men,” he growled—“the worst men I ever smelt. I smell trouble. I smell a fight—six bad scoundrels fighting against one brave man. I want to help him. Woof—oo—WOOF!” Then he barked, loud, and woke himself up with a surprised look on his face.

sentences.text: “I smell bad men,” he growled—“the worst men I ever smelt.
sentences.zh: 「我闻到坏人，」他低吼着——「是我闻到过的最坏的人。

sentences.text: I smell trouble.
sentences.zh: 我闻到麻烦。

sentences.text: I smell a fight—six bad scoundrels fighting against one brave man.
sentences.zh: 我闻到一场打斗——六个坏蛋在围攻一个勇敢的人。

sentences.text: I want to help him.
sentences.zh: 我想去帮他。

sentences.text: Woof—oo—WOOF!”
Then he barked, loud, and woke himself up with a surprised look on his face.
sentences.zh: 接着他大声叫了起来，把自己惊醒了，脸上露出吃惊的表情。

hints.zh: smell 的过去式（英式不规则形式），这里指「闻到过」；它和名词「胡瓜鱼」同形，别弄混。
hints.en: Smelt is the British past form of smell: the worst men I ever smelt.

introduction.zh: 甲板上，吉普晒着太阳睡着了，却在梦里说起话来。医生看得很清楚：船上什么也没有煮，可达布达布一点也不觉得奇怪。一条狗在梦里能闻到多远的东西？他闻到的又是什么？
introduction.en: Jip is asleep in the sun on deck, but he is talking in his sleep. Nothing is cooking on the ship, yet Dab-Dab is not surprised at all. How far can a dog smell while he is dreaming, and what is out there?

quiz.question: What is strange about Jip on deck?
options: He barks angrily at Dab-Dab.
He growls and talks while he is fast asleep.
He refuses to lie down in the sun.

feedback.zh: 吉普躺在太阳下打盹，却开始低吼、说梦话，医生才觉得奇怪。
feedback.en: Jip was taking a nap in the sun, yet he began to growl and talk in his sleep.

quiz.question: What does Jip smell the second time he growls?
options: A storm coming across the sea.
Roast beef with brown gravy.
Six bad men fighting one brave man.

feedback.zh: 他第二次开口时说的是「六个坏蛋在围攻一个勇敢的人」，还说自己想去帮忙。
feedback.en: The second time he speaks of six bad scoundrels fighting one brave man, and he wants to help.

grammar.excerpt: Jip, who was lying near taking a nap in the sun, began to growl

focus.zh: 两个逗号之间的 who 从句只是补充说明吉普当时在做什么，去掉不影响句子；主句的动词是 began。
focus.en: The who-clause sits between commas and only adds information about Jip; the main verb is began.

paragraphs.text: “See!” cried Dab-Dab. “That boat is nearer now. You can count its three big sails—all red. Whoever it is, they are coming after us.... I wonder who they are.”

sentences.text: “See!” cried Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「看！」达布达布叫道。

sentences.text: “That boat is nearer now.
sentences.zh: 「那条船现在更近了。

sentences.text: You can count its three big sails—all red.
sentences.zh: 你能数清它那三张大帆——全是红的。

sentences.text: Whoever it is, they are coming after us....
sentences.zh: 不管那是谁，他们都在追我们……

sentences.text: I wonder who they are.”
sentences.zh: 真不知道他们是什么人。」

paragraphs.text: “They are bad sailors,” said Jip; “and their ship is very swift. They are surely the pirates of Barbary.”

sentences.text: “They are bad sailors,” said Jip; “and their ship is very swift.
sentences.zh: 「他们不是好水手，」吉普说；「而且他们的船非常快。

sentences.text: They are surely the pirates of Barbary.”
sentences.zh: 他们肯定是巴巴里的海盗。」

paragraphs.text: “Well, we must put up more sails on our boat,” said the Doctor, “so we can go faster and get away from them. Run downstairs, Jip, and fetch me all the sails you see.”

sentences.text: “Well, we must put up more sails on our boat,” said the Doctor, “so we can go faster and get away from them.
sentences.zh: 「那好，我们得在船上多挂几张帆，」医生说，「这样就能走快些，甩开他们。

sentences.text: Run downstairs, Jip, and fetch me all the sails you see.”
sentences.zh: 吉普，你快下去，把你看见的帆都给我搬来。」

hints.zh: put up 这里指把帆升起来、挂到桅杆上，不是「建造」。
hints.en: Put up sails means raise them on the masts, not build them.

paragraphs.text: The dog hurried downstairs and dragged up every sail he could find.

sentences.text: The dog hurried downstairs and dragged up every sail he could find.
sentences.zh: 狗急忙下了舱，把他能找到的帆一张张拖了上来。

paragraphs.text: But even when all these were put up on the masts to catch the wind, the boat did not go nearly as fast as the pirates’—which kept coming on behind, closer and closer.

sentences.text: But even when all these were put up on the masts to catch the wind, the boat did not go nearly as fast as the pirates’—which kept coming on behind, closer and closer.
sentences.zh: 可是，尽管把这些帆全都挂上桅杆去兜风，船还是远不如海盗船快——那条船一直跟在后面，越来越近。

paragraphs.text: “This is a poor ship the Prince gave us,” said Gub-Gub, the pig—“the slowest he could find, I should think. Might as well try to win a race in a soup-tureen as hope to get away from them in this old barge. Look how near they are now!—You can see the mustaches on the faces of the men—six of them. What are we going to do?”

sentences.text: “This is a poor ship the Prince gave us,” said Gub-Gub, the pig—“the slowest he could find, I should think.
sentences.zh: 「王子给我们的这是条破船，」小猪咕咕说——「我看这是他找得到的最慢的一条。

sentences.text: Might as well try to win a race in a soup-tureen as hope to get away from them in this old barge.
sentences.zh: 想靠这条又旧又笨的船甩掉他们，就跟想在汤盆里赛船取胜差不多。

sentences.text: Look how near they are now!—You can see the mustaches on the faces of the men—six of them.
sentences.zh: 看看他们现在多近！——都能看清那些人脸上的胡子了——一共六个。

sentences.text: What are we going to do?”
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么办呢？」

hints.zh: 王子，指乔利金基国王的儿子邦波王子；这条船是他给的。
hints.en: The Prince: Prince Bumpo, the King of Jolliginki’s son, who gave them this ship.

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s pig.

hints.zh: Might as well … as … 是「与其……还不如……」：两种做法一样没指望。
hints.en: Might as well … as … means one plan is as hopeless as the other.

hints.zh: 带盖的大汤盆；「在汤盆里赛船」是句挖苦话，形容绝不可能赢。
hints.en: A soup-tureen is a big covered soup bowl; a race in one is a joke about a hopeless try.

hints.zh: 本指平底货船，这里指又大又笨、走不快的旧船。
hints.en: A barge is a flat goods boat; here it means a big, clumsy old ship.

introduction.zh: 挂了红帆的船越来越近，甲板上的人已经能看清对面水手的样子。医生让人把船上所有的帆都挂起来，可这条船实在太慢。帆都挂满了，还有别的办法吗？
introduction.en: The ship with the red sails is much nearer now. The Doctor has every sail on his own boat put up, but the boat the Prince gave them is old and slow. With all the sails full of wind, what else can they try?

quiz.question: What does the Doctor tell Jip to do?
options: Fetch all the sails he can find.
Throw the extra ropes overboard.
Wake the other animals below.

feedback.zh: 医生让吉普下到舱里，把所有能看见的帆都搬上来，好让船走快些。
feedback.en: The Doctor tells Jip to run downstairs and fetch every sail he can see.

quiz.question: What shows that the pirate ship is very close?
options: You can see the mustaches on the men’s faces.
You can count the animals on its deck.
You can hear the pirates singing.

feedback.zh: 咕咕说近得能看清那些人脸上的胡子，六个人都数得出来，可见已经追到眼前。
feedback.en: Gub-Gub says you can see the mustaches on the men’s faces, so the pirate ship is almost upon them.

grammar.excerpt: the boat did not go nearly as fast as the pirates’

focus.zh: not nearly as fast as 就是「远不如……快」：nearly 加重否定，被比较的是海盗船。
focus.en: Not nearly as fast as means much slower than; nearly makes the negative stronger, and the pirates’ ship is the thing compared.

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor asked Dab-Dab to fly up and tell the swallows that pirates were coming after them in a swift ship, and what should he do about it.

sentences.text: Then the Doctor asked Dab-Dab to fly up and tell the swallows that pirates were coming after them in a swift ship, and what should he do about it.
sentences.zh: 于是医生请达布达布飞上天去告诉燕子们：有海盗乘着快船追来了，他该怎么办才好。

paragraphs.text: When the swallows heard this, they all came down on to the Doctor’s ship; and they told him to unravel some pieces of long rope and make them into a lot of thin strings as quickly as he could. Then the ends of these strings were tied on to the front of the ship; and the swallows took hold of the strings with their feet and flew off, pulling the boat along.

sentences.text: When the swallows heard this, they all came down on to the Doctor’s ship; and they told him to unravel some pieces of long rope and make them into a lot of thin strings as quickly as he could.
sentences.zh: 燕子们听了，全都落到医生的船上；它们让他把几段长绳拆开，尽快搓成许多细绳。

sentences.text: Then the ends of these strings were tied on to the front of the ship; and the swallows took hold of the strings with their feet and flew off, pulling the boat along.
sentences.zh: 然后这些细绳的一头被系在船头；燕子们用脚抓住绳子，一齐飞起来，拉着船往前走。

hints.zh: 拆开、把绳子拆散成一股股细线；不是「解开谜团」。
hints.en: Unravel here means to pull the twisted rope apart into thin threads.

hints.zh: 抓住、握住；take hold of 就是「用手（或脚）抓牢」。
hints.en: Took hold of means gripped the strings with their feet.

paragraphs.text: And although swallows are not very strong when only one or two are by themselves, it is different when there are a great lot of them together. And there, tied to the Doctor’s ship, were a thousand strings; and two thousand swallows were pulling on each string—all terribly swift fliers.

sentences.text: And although swallows are not very strong when only one or two are by themselves, it is different when there are a great lot of them together.
sentences.zh: 燕子只有一两只时力气并不大，可要是一大群凑在一起，情形就不一样了。

sentences.text: And there, tied to the Doctor’s ship, were a thousand strings; and two thousand swallows were pulling on each string—all terribly swift fliers.
sentences.zh: 就这样，医生的船上系着一千根细绳；每一根绳子上都有两千只燕子在拉——它们全是飞得极快的鸟儿。

paragraphs.text: And in a moment the Doctor found himself traveling so fast he had to hold his hat on with both hands; for he felt as though the ship itself were flying through waves that frothed and boiled with speed.

sentences.text: And in a moment the Doctor found himself traveling so fast he had to hold his hat on with both hands; for he felt as though the ship itself were flying through waves that frothed and boiled with speed.
sentences.zh: 转眼间，医生发现自己走得飞快，只好用两只手按住帽子；他觉得整条船仿佛在飞，穿过被速度搅得翻腾起沫的海浪。

hints.zh: 好像、仿佛；后面常用 were 表示「并不是真的」，是想象的说法。
hints.en: As though means as if; the were shows it is only how it felt, not real.

hints.zh: 翻起白沫、像开了锅一样翻滚；形容船速太快，把海浪搅得沸腾。
hints.en: Frothed and boiled: the waves turned white and churned as if boiling, because of the speed.

paragraphs.text: And all the animals on the ship began to laugh and dance about in the rushing air, for when they looked back at the pirates’ ship, they could see that it was growing smaller now, instead of bigger. The red sails were being left far, far behind.

sentences.text: And all the animals on the ship began to laugh and dance about in the rushing air, for when they looked back at the pirates’ ship, they could see that it was growing smaller now, instead of bigger.
sentences.zh: 船上的动物们都笑了起来，在呼呼疾吹的风里蹦跳，因为它们回头望海盗船时，能看见那船正在变小，而不是变大。

sentences.text: The red sails were being left far, far behind.
sentences.zh: 红帆被远远地甩在了后面。

introduction.zh: 海盗船越逼越近，医生把最后的指望放到天上——他请达布达布去找那群燕子。燕子们落满了甲板，好像有什么主意。一群小小的鸟，能拿一条船怎么办？
introduction.en: The pirates are close behind, so the Doctor turns to the sky and sends Dab-Dab to find the swallows. Soon the little birds are all over the deck, and they seem to have a plan. What can a flock of small birds do for a ship?

quiz.question: What do the swallows ask the Doctor to do?
options: Unravel long ropes into many thin strings.
Put up more sails on the masts.
Send Dab-Dab back into the sky.

feedback.zh: 燕子让他把几段长绳拆开，尽快做成许多细绳，它们好抓住绳子拉船。
feedback.en: The swallows tell him to unravel long pieces of rope into many thin strings.

quiz.question: How does the Doctor know the ship is going very fast?
options: The pirates’ ship is getting bigger.
He has to hold his hat on with both hands.
The animals have stopped laughing.

feedback.zh: 船快得他不得不用两只手按住帽子，他自己也觉得整条船像在飞。
feedback.en: He has to hold his hat on with both hands, and he feels as if the ship itself were flying.

grammar.excerpt: the Doctor found himself traveling so fast he had to hold his hat on with both hands

focus.zh: so fast 后面省略了 that，引出结果：快得他必须用两只手按住帽子。
focus.en: So fast introduces a result, with that left out: so fast that he had to hold his hat on.

paragraphs.text: Dragging a ship through the sea is hard work. And after two or three hours the swallows began to get tired in the wings and short of breath. Then they sent a message down to the Doctor to say that they would have to take a rest soon; and that they would pull the boat over to an island not far off, and hide it in a deep bay till they had got breath enough to go on.

sentences.text: Dragging a ship through the sea is hard work.
sentences.zh: 拖着一条船在海上走，是件苦差事。

sentences.text: And after two or three hours the swallows began to get tired in the wings and short of breath.
sentences.zh: 过了两三个钟头，燕子们的翅膀开始发酸，气也喘不上来了。

sentences.text: Then they sent a message down to the Doctor to say that they would have to take a rest soon; and that they would pull the boat over to an island not far off, and hide it in a deep bay till they had got breath enough to go on.
sentences.zh: 于是它们给下面的医生送了个信儿，说它们很快就得歇一歇；它们要把船拖到不远处的一座岛边，藏进一个深深的海湾里，等缓过气来再往前走。

hints.zh: 喘不上气、气短，是累极了的样子。
hints.en: Short of breath: unable to breathe easily because you are worn out.

paragraphs.text: And presently the Doctor saw the island they had spoken of. It had a very beautiful, high, green mountain in the middle of it.

sentences.text: And presently the Doctor saw the island they had spoken of.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，医生就看见了它们说的那座岛。

sentences.text: It had a very beautiful, high, green mountain in the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 岛中央有一座很高的青山，非常好看。

hints.zh: 这里是「不久、过了一会儿」，不是现代英语里「目前」的意思。
hints.en: Here it means soon, after a short time — not “at present”.

paragraphs.text: When the ship had sailed safely into the bay where it could not be seen from the open sea, the Doctor said he would get off on to the island to look for water—because there was none left to drink on his ship. And he told all the animals to get out too and romp on the grass to stretch their legs.

sentences.text: When the ship had sailed safely into the bay where it could not be seen from the open sea, the Doctor said he would get off on to the island to look for water—because there was none left to drink on his ship.
sentences.zh: 等船稳稳地驶进那个从外海看不见的海湾，医生说他得上岛去找水——因为船上已经没有喝的水了。

sentences.text: And he told all the animals to get out too and romp on the grass to stretch their legs.
sentences.zh: 他又叫所有的动物也下船，到草地上撒欢，活动活动腿脚。

hints.zh: 活动活动腿脚：坐久了或关久了，走一走松快一下。
hints.en: To stretch your legs: to walk about and loosen up after sitting still.

paragraphs.text: Now as they were getting off, the Doctor noticed that a whole lot of rats were coming up from downstairs and leaving the ship as well. Jip started to run after them, because chasing rats had always been his favorite game. But the Doctor told him to stop.

sentences.text: Now as they were getting off, the Doctor noticed that a whole lot of rats were coming up from downstairs and leaving the ship as well.
sentences.zh: 就在大家下船的时候，医生注意到一大群老鼠正从底舱爬上来，也要离开这条船。

sentences.text: Jip started to run after them, because chasing rats had always been his favorite game.
sentences.zh: 吉普拔腿就追，因为追老鼠向来是他最喜欢的游戏。

sentences.text: But the Doctor told him to stop.
sentences.zh: 可医生叫他停下。

hints.zh: 在船上指下面的底舱，不是房子里的「楼下」。
hints.en: On a ship, downstairs means the lower decks, below the deck you stand on.

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

introduction.zh: 燕子拖着船飞了两三个钟头，翅膀酸了，气也短了，只好把船拖进一座岛的海湾里歇脚。医生正要带动物们下船找水，却发现一大群老鼠也从底舱爬上来，急着要离开。这条船到底出了什么事？
introduction.en: The swallows have pulled the ship for hours and their wings are tired, so they hide it in a deep bay beside a green island. The Doctor goes ashore for water. Then he sees the rats coming up from below, leaving too. Why would rats leave a ship?

quiz.question: Why do the swallows want to stop and rest?
options: They want to look for water on the island.
They are afraid of the rats on the ship.
Their wings are tired and they are short of breath.

feedback.zh: 原文说飞了两三个钟头后，燕子「翅膀发酸、喘不上气」，所以它们传话给医生，说得先歇一歇。
feedback.en: After two or three hours the swallows were tired in the wings and short of breath, so they sent word that they must rest soon.

quiz.question: What does Jip do when he sees the rats leaving the ship?
options: He runs to tell the swallows.
He starts to run after them.
He hides behind the Doctor.

feedback.zh: 追老鼠一向是吉普最爱的游戏，所以他立刻追了上去；医生随后叫他停下。
feedback.en: Chasing rats was Jip’s favourite game, so he started to run after them, and the Doctor told him to stop.

grammar.excerpt: Dragging a ship through the sea is hard work

focus.zh: Dragging a ship through the sea 是动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数 is；说的是「拖船」这件事本身。
focus.en: Dragging a ship through the sea is an -ing phrase as the subject, so the verb is the singular is.

title.en: Who Would Stay on a Sinking Ship

paragraphs.text: And one big black rat, who seemed to want to say something to the Doctor, now crept forward timidly along the rail, watching the dog out of the corner of his eye. And after he had coughed nervously two or three times, and cleaned his whiskers and wiped his mouth, he said,

sentences.text: And one big black rat, who seemed to want to say something to the Doctor, now crept forward timidly along the rail, watching the dog out of the corner of his eye.
sentences.zh: 这时，一只大黑老鼠沿着船舷怯生生地往前爬，眼睛还瞟着那条狗——看样子它想跟医生说点什么。

sentences.text: And after he had coughed nervously two or three times, and cleaned his whiskers and wiped his mouth, he said,
sentences.zh: 它紧张地咳了两三声，理了理胡须，又抹了抹嘴，然后说：

hints.target: out of the corner of his eye
hints.zh: 用眼角余光瞟着：不扭头也看得见，是提防的样子。
hints.en: Out of the corner of his eye: watching sideways, without turning his head.

paragraphs.text: “Ahem—er—you know of course that all ships have rats in them, Doctor, do you not?”

sentences.text: “Ahem—er—you know of course that all ships have rats in them, Doctor, do you not?”
sentences.zh: 「嗯——呃——你当然知道，每条船上都有老鼠吧，医生？」

hints.zh: 清嗓子的一声「咳」，开口前用来引起注意，也表示有点迟疑。
hints.en: Ahem: a cough to clear the throat, used to draw attention before speaking.

paragraphs.text: And the Doctor said, “Yes.”

sentences.text: And the Doctor said, “Yes.”
sentences.zh: 医生说：「是的。」

paragraphs.text: “And you have heard that rats always leave a sinking ship?”

sentences.text: “And you have heard that rats always leave a sinking ship?”
sentences.zh: 「你也听说过，老鼠总是离开要沉的船吧？」

paragraphs.text: “Yes,” said the Doctor—“so I’ve been told.”

sentences.text: “Yes,” said the Doctor—“so I’ve been told.”
sentences.zh: 「是的，」医生说，「人家是这么告诉我的。」

paragraphs.text: “People,” said the rat, “always speak of it with a sneer—as though it were something disgraceful. But you can’t blame us, can you? After all, who would stay on a sinking ship, if he could get off it?”

sentences.text: “People,” said the rat, “always speak of it with a sneer—as though it were something disgraceful.
sentences.zh: 「人们，」老鼠说，「提起这事总带着讥笑——好像那是什么丢脸的事。

sentences.text: But you can’t blame us, can you?
sentences.zh: 可这不能怪我们，是不是？

sentences.text: After all, who would stay on a sinking ship, if he could get off it?”
sentences.zh: 说到底，只要能下船，谁还肯留在一条要沉的船上呢？」

hints.zh: 带着讥笑、撇着嘴，一副看不起人的样子。
hints.en: With a sneer: with a look or tone that shows contempt.

hints.zh: 「说到底、毕竟」，用来补上一个站得住的理由。
hints.en: After all: used to add the reason that settles the matter.

paragraphs.text: “It’s very natural,” said the Doctor—“very natural. I quite understand.... Was there—Was there anything else you wished to say?”

sentences.text: “It’s very natural,” said the Doctor—“very natural.
sentences.zh: 「这很自然，」医生说，「非常自然。

sentences.text: I quite understand....
sentences.zh: 我完全明白……

sentences.text: Was there—Was there anything else you wished to say?”
sentences.zh: 还有——还有别的什么想跟我说吗？」

paragraphs.text: “Yes,” said the rat. “I’ve come to tell you that we are leaving this one. But we wanted to warn you before we go. This is a bad ship you have here. It isn’t safe. The sides aren’t strong enough. Its boards are rotten. Before to-morrow night it will sink to the bottom of the sea.”

sentences.text: “Yes,” said the rat.
sentences.zh: 「有，」老鼠说。

sentences.text: “I’ve come to tell you that we are leaving this one.
sentences.zh: 「我来是要告诉你，我们要离开这一条了。

sentences.text: But we wanted to warn you before we go.
sentences.zh: 可我们走之前，想先给你提个醒。

sentences.text: This is a bad ship you have here.
sentences.zh: 你这条船是条坏船。

sentences.text: It isn’t safe.
sentences.zh: 它不安全。

sentences.text: The sides aren’t strong enough.
sentences.zh: 船帮不够结实。

sentences.text: Its boards are rotten.
sentences.zh: 船板都烂了。

sentences.text: Before to-morrow night it will sink to the bottom of the sea.”
sentences.zh: 明天夜里之前，它就会沉到海底去。」

hints.zh: 这里指船的两侧、船帮，不是「边」或「方面」。
hints.en: The sides here are the ship’s sides, the planks of the hull.

paragraphs.text: “But how do you know?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “But how do you know?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可你怎么知道？」医生问。

introduction.zh: 一只大黑老鼠沿着船舷怯生生地爬过来，眼睛一直瞟着吉普，看样子有话要跟医生说。它先提起人们常拿来取笑老鼠的那句老话，说自己并不觉得丢脸。绕了这么大圈子，它究竟要说什么？
introduction.en: A big black rat creeps along the rail, one eye on Jip. It has something to say to the Doctor, but it begins with a careful question about rats and ships, and about the sneer people use. It takes its time. What is it working up to?

quiz.question: How do people usually speak about rats leaving a sinking ship?
options: With a sneer, as if it were shameful.
With thanks to the rats for the warning.
As if it were a funny story.

feedback.zh: 老鼠说，人们提起这事总带着讥笑，好像那是什么丢脸的事——它正是为这句话替老鼠辩白。
feedback.en: The rat says people always speak of it with a sneer, as though it were something disgraceful, and that is what it wants to answer.

quiz.question: What does the rat say will happen to the ship?
options: It will need new boards before it can sail again.
It will be left on the island for the rats.
It will sink before tomorrow night.

feedback.zh: 老鼠说船板烂了、船帮不够结实，末了明说：明天夜里之前，这条船会沉到海底。
feedback.en: The rat says the boards are rotten and the sides are not strong enough, and ends by saying the ship will sink to the bottom before tomorrow night.

grammar.excerpt: you know of course that all ships have rats in them, Doctor, do you not

focus.zh: 前面是肯定陈述，句尾就挂否定的小问句 do you not（即 don’t you），老鼠在小心地请医生点头。
focus.en: The statement is positive, so the tag is negative: do you not, that is don’t you.

paragraphs.text: “We always know,” answered the rat. “The tips of our tails get that tingly feeling—like when your foot’s asleep. This morning, at six o’clock, while I was getting breakfast, my tail suddenly began to tingle. At first I thought it was my rheumatism coming back. So I went and asked my aunt how she felt—you remember her?—the long, piebald rat, rather skinny, who came to see you in Puddleby last Spring with jaundice? Well—and she said her tail was tingling like everything! Then we knew, for sure, that this boat was going to sink in less than two days; and we all made up our minds to leave it as soon as we got near enough to any land. It’s a bad ship, Doctor. Don’t sail in it any more, or you’ll be surely drowned.... Good-by! We are now going to look for a good place to live on this island.”

sentences.text: “We always know,” answered the rat.
sentences.zh: 「我们一向知道，」老鼠回答。

sentences.text: “The tips of our tails get that tingly feeling—like when your foot’s asleep.
sentences.zh: 「我们尾巴尖儿会发麻——就像你的脚坐麻了那样。

sentences.text: This morning, at six o’clock, while I was getting breakfast, my tail suddenly began to tingle.
sentences.zh: 今天早上六点，我正在弄早饭，尾巴忽然就麻了起来。

sentences.text: At first I thought it was my rheumatism coming back.
sentences.zh: 起初我以为是我的风湿病又犯了。

sentences.text: So I went and asked my aunt how she felt—you remember her?—the long, piebald rat, rather skinny, who came to see you in Puddleby last Spring with jaundice?
sentences.zh: 于是我去问我姑妈感觉怎么样——你还记得她吧？——就是那只又长又瘦、花斑毛的老鼠，去年春天得了黄疸，到帕德尔比来找你看病的那只？

sentences.text: Well—and she said her tail was tingling like everything!
sentences.zh: 嗐——她说她的尾巴麻得没法说！

sentences.text: Then we knew, for sure, that this boat was going to sink in less than two days; and we all made up our minds to leave it as soon as we got near enough to any land.
sentences.zh: 于是我们断定，这条船不到两天就要沉；大家也拿定了主意，一靠近陆地就离开它。

sentences.text: It’s a bad ship, Doctor.
sentences.zh: 这是条坏船，医生。

sentences.text: Don’t sail in it any more, or you’ll be surely drowned....
sentences.zh: 别再坐它出海了，不然你一定会淹死……

sentences.text: Good-by!
sentences.zh: 再见！

sentences.text: We are now going to look for a good place to live on this island.”
sentences.zh: 我们这就去找个能安家的好地方，就在这座岛上。」

hints.zh: 脚坐麻了；asleep 在这里不是「睡着」，而是压久了发麻、没知觉。
hints.en: A foot that has gone to sleep is numb and tingling, not really sleeping.

hints.zh: 花斑的：毛色深浅不一，一块一块的。
hints.en: Piebald: having patches of two colours, here in the rat’s fur.

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡；老鼠说的是去年春天姑妈去那儿找他看病。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor’s home town, where the aunt came to see him last spring.

hints.zh: 拿定主意、下了决心（make up one’s mind）。
hints.en: Made up our minds: decided.

paragraphs.text: “Good-by!” said the Doctor. “And thank you very much for coming to tell me. Very considerate of you—very! Give my regards to your aunt. I remember her perfectly.... Leave that rat alone, Jip! Come here! Lie down!”

sentences.text: “Good-by!” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「再见！」医生说。

sentences.text: “And thank you very much for coming to tell me.
sentences.zh: 「多谢你专门跑来告诉我。

sentences.text: Very considerate of you—very!
sentences.zh: 你想得真周到——真周到！

sentences.text: Give my regards to your aunt.
sentences.zh: 替我问候你姑妈。

sentences.text: I remember her perfectly....
sentences.zh: 我记得她，记得一清二楚……

sentences.text: Leave that rat alone, Jip!
sentences.zh: 别碰那只老鼠，吉普！

sentences.text: Come here!
sentences.zh: 过来！

sentences.text: Lie down!”
sentences.zh: 趴下！」

paragraphs.text: So then the Doctor and all his animals went off, carrying pails and saucepans, to look for water on the island, while the swallows took their rest.

sentences.text: So then the Doctor and all his animals went off, carrying pails and saucepans, to look for water on the island, while the swallows took their rest.
sentences.zh: 于是医生带着他所有的动物，提着水桶和锅子，上岛找水去了；燕子们就在原地歇着。

paragraphs.text: “I wonder what is the name of this island,” said the Doctor, as he was climbing up the mountainside. “It seems a pleasant place. What a lot of birds there are!”

sentences.text: “I wonder what is the name of this island,” said the Doctor, as he was climbing up the mountainside.
sentences.zh: 「不知道这座岛叫什么名字，」医生一边往山坡上爬，一边说。

sentences.text: “It seems a pleasant place.
sentences.zh: 「这地方看着挺讨人喜欢。

sentences.text: What a lot of birds there are!”
sentences.zh: 鸟真多啊！」

paragraphs.text: “Why, these are the Canary Islands,” said Dab-Dab. “Don’t you hear the canaries singing?”

sentences.text: “Why, these are the Canary Islands,” said Dab-Dab.
sentences.zh: 「哎呀，这里是加那利群岛呀，」达布达布说。

sentences.text: “Don’t you hear the canaries singing?”
sentences.zh: 「你没听见金丝雀在唱歌吗？」

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

hints.zh: 加那利群岛，非洲西北岸外的一串岛；金丝雀（canary）这种鸟就得名于此。
hints.en: The Canary Islands, off the north-west coast of Africa; the canary bird is named after them.

introduction.zh: 老鼠讲起它们判断沉船的法子：尾巴尖会发麻，就像脚坐麻了一样。它还把姑妈搬了出来，说姑妈早就有过这种麻劲儿。讲完这些，医生提着水桶往山上走，忽然很想知道：这座岛叫什么名字？
introduction.en: The rat explains how rats know a ship will sink: their tails begin to tingle, like a foot that has gone to sleep. Its aunt felt it too. Later, up the mountainside with his pails, the Doctor wonders: what is this island called?

quiz.question: How do the rats know that a ship is going to sink?
options: They keep watch on the water in the bottom of the ship.
The tips of their tails begin to tingle.
They hear the boards cracking at night.

feedback.zh: 老鼠说它们的尾巴尖会发麻，就像脚坐麻了一样；它自己的尾巴那天早上六点就忽然麻了起来。
feedback.en: The rat says the tips of their tails get a tingly feeling, like a foot that has gone to sleep; its own tail began to tingle at six that morning.

quiz.question: How does the Doctor answer the rat’s warning?
options: He thanks it and sends his regards to its aunt.
He laughs and says rats are always afraid.
He asks the rat to stay on the ship with him.

feedback.zh: 医生连声道谢，说它想得周到，还让它代问姑妈好——他记得那只老鼠，记得一清二楚。
feedback.en: The Doctor thanks the rat for coming to tell him, calls it very considerate, and asks it to give his regards to its aunt.

grammar.excerpt: Don’t you hear the canaries singing

focus.zh: hear the canaries singing 是 hear + 宾语 + 现在分词：听见金丝雀正在唱，不是听它们唱完。
focus.en: Hear the canaries singing is hear + object + -ing: the singing is going on while he listens.

paragraphs.text: The Doctor stopped and listened.

sentences.text: The Doctor stopped and listened.
sentences.zh: 医生停下来听了听。

paragraphs.text: “Why, to be sure—of course!” he said. “How stupid of me! I wonder if they can tell us where to find water.”

sentences.text: “Why, to be sure—of course!” he said.
sentences.zh: 「哎呀，可不是嘛——当然！」他说。

sentences.text: “How stupid of me!
sentences.zh: 「我怎么这么笨！

sentences.text: I wonder if they can tell us where to find water.”
sentences.zh: 不知道它们能不能告诉我们哪儿能找到水。」

paragraphs.text: And presently the canaries, who had heard all about Doctor Dolittle from birds of passage, came and led him to a beautiful spring of cool, clear water where the canaries used to take their bath; and they showed him lovely meadows where the bird-seed grew and all the other sights of their island.

sentences.text: And presently the canaries, who had heard all about Doctor Dolittle from birds of passage, came and led him to a beautiful spring of cool, clear water where the canaries used to take their bath; and they showed him lovely meadows where the bird-seed grew and all the other sights of their island.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，金丝雀们来了——它们早从过路的鸟那里听说了杜立德医生的事——把他领到一眼清凉澄澈的泉水边，那是金丝雀们常来洗澡的地方；又带他看了长着鸟食草籽的美丽草地，还有岛上别的种种景致。

hints.zh: 候鸟：随季节迁徙的鸟；这里指把医生的名声传过来的过路鸟。
hints.en: Birds of passage: migrating birds, here the travellers who carried the news of the Doctor.

hints.zh: 杜立德医生，就是主角本人；金丝雀是从过路的鸟那里听说他的。
hints.en: Doctor Dolittle, the Doctor himself; the canaries had heard of him from passing birds.

paragraphs.text: And the pushmi-pullyu was glad they had come; because he liked the green grass so much better than the dried apples he had been eating on the ship. And Gub-Gub squeaked for joy when he found a whole valley full of wild sugar-cane.

sentences.text: And the pushmi-pullyu was glad they had come; because he liked the green grass so much better than the dried apples he had been eating on the ship.
sentences.zh: 「推我拉你」很高兴他们来了；因为比起在船上一直吃的干苹果，他太喜欢这青草了。

sentences.text: And Gub-Gub squeaked for joy when he found a whole valley full of wild sugar-cane.
sentences.zh: 咕咕发现整整一个山谷都长满野甘蔗，高兴得直叫。

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，那头两头各有一个脑袋的双头动物。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu, the two-headed animal with a head at each end.

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的宠物小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s pet pig.

paragraphs.text: A little later, when they had all had plenty to eat and drink, and were lying on their backs while the canaries sang for them, two of the swallows came hurrying up, very flustered and excited.

sentences.text: A little later, when they had all had plenty to eat and drink, and were lying on their backs while the canaries sang for them, two of the swallows came hurrying up, very flustered and excited.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，大家吃饱喝足，正仰面躺着听金丝雀唱歌，两只燕子慌慌张张、急急忙忙地飞了过来。

paragraphs.text: “Doctor!” they cried, “the pirates have come into the bay; and they’ve all got on to your ship. They are downstairs looking for things to steal. They have left their own ship with nobody on it. If you hurry and come down to the shore, you can get on to their ship—which is very fast—and escape. But you’ll have to hurry.”

sentences.text: “Doctor!” they cried, “the pirates have come into the bay; and they’ve all got on to your ship.
sentences.zh: 「医生！」它们叫道，「海盗进了海湾，他们全都上了你的船。

sentences.text: They are downstairs looking for things to steal.
sentences.zh: 他们正在底舱里翻找能偷的东西。

sentences.text: They have left their own ship with nobody on it.
sentences.zh: 他们把自己的船丢下了，船上一个人也没有。

sentences.text: If you hurry and come down to the shore, you can get on to their ship—which is very fast—and escape.
sentences.zh: 你要是赶紧下到岸边，就能上他们的船——他们的船快得很——然后逃走。

sentences.text: But you’ll have to hurry.”
sentences.zh: 不过你得快点儿。」

paragraphs.text: “That’s a good idea,” said the Doctor—“splendid!”

sentences.text: “That’s a good idea,” said the Doctor—“splendid!”
sentences.zh: 「这主意好，」医生说，「太好了！」

paragraphs.text: And he called his animals together at once, said Good-by to the canaries and ran down to the beach.

sentences.text: And he called his animals together at once, said Good-by to the canaries and ran down to the beach.
sentences.zh: 他马上把动物们叫到一起，跟金丝雀道了别，就往海滩跑去。

paragraphs.text: When they reached the shore they saw the pirate-ship, with the three red sails, standing in the water; and—just as the swallows had said—there was nobody on it; all the pirates were downstairs in the Doctor’s ship, looking for things to steal.

sentences.text: When they reached the shore they saw the pirate-ship, with the three red sails, standing in the water; and—just as the swallows had said—there was nobody on it; all the pirates were downstairs in the Doctor’s ship, looking for things to steal.
sentences.zh: 到了岸边，他们看见那条挂着三面红帆的海盗船停在水上；果然像燕子说的那样，船上一个人也没有——海盗们全在医生的船底舱里，翻找能偷的东西。

hints.zh: 挂着三面红帆——那是海盗船的标志，前文就见过这条船。
hints.en: The three red sails mark the pirate ship that has appeared before in the story.

hints.zh: 船「停在水上」；stand 这里指船停着不动，不是「站着」。
hints.en: Standing here means the ship lies still in the water, not that it is on its feet.

paragraphs.text: So John Dolittle told his animals to walk very softly and they all crept on to the pirate-ship.

sentences.text: So John Dolittle told his animals to walk very softly and they all crept on to the pirate-ship.
sentences.zh: 于是约翰·杜立德叫动物们走路轻一些，大家就都悄悄爬上了海盗船。

introduction.zh: 金丝雀把医生领到一眼清凉的泉水边，又带他看了长满鸟食草籽的草地。「推我拉你」和咕咕总算吃上了新鲜草料。大家正躺在草地上听鸟唱歌，两只燕子慌慌张张地飞了过来，说海湾里出了事。
introduction.en: The canaries lead the Doctor to a cool spring and to meadows full of bird-seed. The pushmi-pullyu and Gub-Gub feast on fresh grass and sugar-cane, and everyone lies in the sun while the birds sing. Then two swallows rush up, flustered and breathless. Something has happened in the bay.

quiz.question: What do the canaries do for the Doctor?
options: They carry his pails back to the ship.
They fly off to look for the pirates.
They lead him to a spring and show him their meadows.

feedback.zh: 金丝雀把他领到一眼清凉的泉水边，又带他看了长着鸟食草籽的草地和岛上别的景致。
feedback.en: The canaries lead him to a beautiful spring of cool, clear water and show him the meadows where the bird-seed grows.

quiz.question: What are the pirates doing on the Doctor’s ship?
options: They are chasing the canaries on the island.
They are downstairs looking for things to steal.
They are waiting on deck to meet the Doctor.

feedback.zh: 燕子说海盗进了海湾，全上了医生的船，正在底舱翻找能偷的东西——所以他们自己的船空着。
feedback.en: The swallows say the pirates have come into the bay and are all on the Doctor’s ship, downstairs looking for things to steal.

grammar.excerpt: If you hurry and come down to the shore, you can get on to their ship

focus.zh: if 从句用现在时 hurry、come，主句用 can + 动词原形，讲「只要……就能……」的真实条件。
focus.en: The if-clause uses the present tense (hurry, come) and the main clause uses can + base verb for a real condition.

paragraphs.text: Everything would have gone all right if the pig had not caught a cold in his head while eating the damp sugar-cane on the island. This is what happened:

sentences.text: Everything would have gone all right if the pig had not caught a cold in his head while eating the damp sugar-cane on the island.
sentences.zh: 要不是那头小猪在岛上吃潮湿的甘蔗时受了凉，本来一切都会顺顺当当的。

sentences.text: This is what happened:
sentences.zh: 事情是这样发生的：

paragraphs.text: After they had pulled up the anchor without a sound, and were moving the ship very, very carefully out of the bay, Gub-Gub suddenly sneezed so loud that the pirates on the other ship came rushing upstairs to see what the noise was.

sentences.text: After they had pulled up the anchor without a sound, and were moving the ship very, very carefully out of the bay, Gub-Gub suddenly sneezed so loud that the pirates on the other ship came rushing upstairs to see what the noise was.
sentences.zh: 他们一声不响地起了锚，正把船小心翼翼地从海湾里开出去，咕咕忽然打了个喷嚏，响得另一条船上的海盗都冲上楼来，看看是什么声音。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生养的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s little pig.

paragraphs.text: As soon as they saw that the Doctor was escaping, they sailed the other boat right across the entrance to the bay so that the Doctor could not get out into the open sea.

sentences.text: As soon as they saw that the Doctor was escaping, they sailed the other boat right across the entrance to the bay so that the Doctor could not get out into the open sea.
sentences.zh: 他们一看医生要逃走，就把另一条船横着驶到湾口，好让医生出不了外海。

paragraphs.text: Then the leader of these bad men (who called himself “Ben Ali, The Dragon”) shook his fist at the Doctor and shouted across the water,

sentences.text: Then the leader of these bad men (who called himself “Ben Ali, The Dragon”) shook his fist at the Doctor and shouted across the water,
sentences.zh: 于是这些坏人的头子（他自称「本·阿里，巨龙」）冲医生挥着拳头，隔着水大喊：

hints.zh: 本·阿里，这伙海盗的头子，诨号「巴巴里巨龙」。
hints.en: Ben Ali, the chief of these pirates, who calls himself the Dragon.

paragraphs.text: “Ha! Ha! You are caught, my fine friend! You were going to run off in my ship, eh? But you are not a good enough sailor to beat Ben Ali, the Barbary Dragon. I want that duck you’ve got—and the pig too. We’ll have pork-chops and roast duck for supper to-night. And before I let you go home, you must make your friends send me a trunk-full of gold.”

sentences.text: “Ha!
Ha!
sentences.zh: 哈！

sentences.text: You are caught, my fine friend!
sentences.zh: 你被逮住了，我的好朋友！

sentences.text: You were going to run off in my ship, eh?
sentences.zh: 你打算坐着我的船溜走，是吧？

sentences.text: But you are not a good enough sailor to beat Ben Ali, the Barbary Dragon.
sentences.zh: 可你的航海本事还不够好，斗不过巴巴里巨龙本·阿里。

sentences.text: I want that duck you’ve got—and the pig too.
sentences.zh: 我要你那只鸭子——还有那头猪。

sentences.text: We’ll have pork-chops and roast duck for supper to-night.
sentences.zh: 今儿晚饭我们就吃猪排和烤鸭。

sentences.text: And before I let you go home, you must make your friends send me a trunk-full of gold.”
sentences.zh: 在我放你回家之前，你得让你的朋友们给我送一箱子黄金来。」

hints.zh: 巴巴里巨龙，本·阿里的诨名；巴巴里指北非海岸一带。
hints.en: The Barbary Dragon: Ben Ali’s nickname; Barbary is the old name for the North African coast.

paragraphs.text: Poor Gub-Gub began to weep; and Dab-Dab made ready to fly to save her life. But the owl, Too-Too, whispered to the Doctor,

sentences.text: Poor Gub-Gub began to weep; and Dab-Dab made ready to fly to save her life.
sentences.zh: 可怜的咕咕哭了起来；达布达布准备飞走逃命。

sentences.text: But the owl, Too-Too, whispered to the Doctor,
sentences.zh: 可是猫头鹰图图对医生低声说：

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor’s owl.

paragraphs.text: “Keep him talking, Doctor. Be pleasant to him. Our old ship is bound to sink soon—the rats said it would be at the bottom of the sea before to-morrow-night—and the rats are never wrong. Be pleasant, till the ship sinks under him. Keep him talking.”

sentences.text: “Keep him talking, Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「一直跟他说话，医生。

sentences.text: Be pleasant to him.
sentences.zh: 对他客气些。

sentences.text: Our old ship is bound to sink soon—the rats said it would be at the bottom of the sea before to-morrow-night—and the rats are never wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们这条旧船很快就要沉了——老鼠们说，明天夜里之前它就会沉到海底——老鼠从没说错过。

sentences.text: Be pleasant, till the ship sinks under him.
sentences.zh: 对他客气些，一直拖到船在他脚下沉下去。

sentences.text: Keep him talking.”
sentences.zh: 一直跟他说话。」

hints.zh: be bound to + 动词，意思是「一定会、必定」：这条船非沉不可。
hints.en: Be bound to do something means it is certain to happen: the ship is sure to sink.

introduction.zh: 黑夜里，医生和动物们悄悄起了锚，想把船开出海湾。偏偏这时，小猪咕咕打了一个响得不能再响的喷嚏。湾口被另一条船堵住了，海盗头子隔着水喊话，说要拿鸭子和猪当晚饭。这一船人还能悄悄走掉吗？
introduction.en: In the dark the Doctor and his animals pull up the anchor without a sound. Then Gub-Gub sneezes. The pirates block the harbour mouth, and their chief shouts across the water that he wants duck and pork for supper. Can anyone still slip away?

quiz.question: Why do the pirates on the other ship come rushing upstairs?
options: Gub-Gub sneezes very loudly.
They hear the anchor being pulled up.
The Doctor calls out to them.

feedback.zh: 原文说咕咕一个喷嚏响得让另一条船上的海盗都冲上楼来看是什么声音，悄悄逃走就这么暴露了。
feedback.en: Gub-Gub’s sneeze was so loud that the pirates on the other ship rushed upstairs to see what the noise was.

quiz.question: Why does Too-Too tell the Doctor to keep talking and be pleasant?
options: Because the pirates will get tired and sail away.
Because another ship is coming to help them.
Because their old ship is sure to sink soon.

feedback.zh: 图图说旧船很快会沉，老鼠讲过明天夜里之前它就到海底，所以要医生拖延时间，等船在海盗脚下沉掉。
feedback.en: Too-Too says the old ship is bound to sink before the next night, so the Doctor should keep the pirate talking until it goes down under him.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as they saw that the Doctor was escaping

focus.zh: as soon as 引出先发生的事：他们一看出医生要逃，主句紧接着讲海盗马上把船横到湾口。
focus.en: As soon as marks the first event: the moment they saw the Doctor escaping, the pirates blocked the bay.

paragraphs.text: “What, until to-morrow night!” said the Doctor. “Well, I’ll do my best.... Let me see—What shall I talk about?”

sentences.text: “What, until to-morrow night!” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「什么，要到明天夜里！」医生说。

sentences.text: “Well, I’ll do my best....
sentences.zh: 「好吧，我尽力而为……

sentences.text: Let me see—What shall I talk about?”
sentences.zh: 让我想想——我该说些什么呢？」

paragraphs.text: “Oh, let them come on,” said Jip. “We can fight the dirty rascals. There are only six of them. Let them come on. I’d love to tell that collie next door, when we get home, that I had bitten a real pirate. Let ’em come. We can fight them.”

sentences.text: “Oh, let them come on,” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「噢，让他们来吧，」吉普说。

sentences.text: “We can fight the dirty rascals.
sentences.zh: 「我们能收拾这些脏兮兮的坏蛋。

sentences.text: There are only six of them.
sentences.zh: 他们只有六个人。

sentences.text: Let them come on.
sentences.zh: 让他们来吧。

sentences.text: I’d love to tell that collie next door, when we get home, that I had bitten a real pirate.
sentences.zh: 等我们回了家，我真想告诉隔壁那条牧羊犬，我咬过一个真正的海盗。

sentences.text: Let ’em come.
sentences.zh: 让他们来吧。

sentences.text: We can fight them.”
sentences.zh: 我们能打赢他们。」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

hints.zh: ’em 是 them 的口语缩写，Let ’em come 就是「让他们来吧」，比 Let them come 更随意。
hints.en: ’Em is a spoken short form of them: let ’em come means let them come.

paragraphs.text: “But they have pistols and swords,” said the Doctor. “No, that would never do. I must talk to him.... Look here, Ben Ali—”

sentences.text: “But they have pistols and swords,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可他们有手枪和刀，」医生说。

sentences.text: “No, that would never do.
sentences.zh: 「不行，那可不行。

sentences.text: I must talk to him....
sentences.zh: 我得跟他谈谈……

sentences.text: Look here, Ben Ali—”
sentences.zh: 你听着，本·阿里——」

paragraphs.text: But before the Doctor could say any more, the pirates began to sail the ship nearer, laughing with glee, and saying one to another, “Who shall be the first to catch the pig?”

sentences.text: But before the Doctor could say any more, the pirates began to sail the ship nearer, laughing with glee, and saying one to another, “Who shall be the first to catch the pig?”
sentences.zh: 可医生还没再说下去，海盗们已经把船驶得更近，兴高采烈地笑着，互相问：「谁第一个去抓那头猪？」

paragraphs.text: Poor Gub-Gub was dreadfully frightened; and the pushmi-pullyu began to sharpen his horns for a fight by rubbing them on the mast of the ship; while Jip kept springing into the air and barking and calling Ben Ali bad names in dog-language.

sentences.text: Poor Gub-Gub was dreadfully frightened; and the pushmi-pullyu began to sharpen his horns for a fight by rubbing them on the mast of the ship; while Jip kept springing into the air and barking and calling Ben Ali bad names in dog-language.
sentences.zh: 可怜的咕咕吓坏了；「推我拉你」开始在船桅上磨角，准备打一架；吉普则不停地跳起来叫，用狗话骂本·阿里。

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，那只两个头的奇怪动物；本书固定译名。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu, the two-headed animal; the name is written with a hyphen.

paragraphs.text: But presently something seemed to go wrong with the pirates; they stopped laughing and cracking jokes; they looked puzzled; something was making them uneasy.

sentences.text: But presently something seemed to go wrong with the pirates; they stopped laughing and cracking jokes; they looked puzzled; something was making them uneasy.
sentences.zh: 可过了一会儿，海盗们那边好像出了什么岔子；他们不笑了，也不说笑话了；他们满脸困惑；有什么东西让他们不安起来。

hints.zh: crack jokes 是「说笑话、讲俏皮话」，不是「把笑话弄裂」。
hints.en: To crack jokes means to tell jokes and make fun; nothing is being broken.

paragraphs.text: Then Ben Ali, staring down at his feet, suddenly bellowed out,

sentences.text: Then Ben Ali, staring down at his feet, suddenly bellowed out,
sentences.zh: 接着，本·阿里低头盯着自己的脚下，忽然大吼一声：

paragraphs.text: “Thunder and Lightning!—Men, the boat’s leaking!”

sentences.text: “Thunder and Lightning!—Men, the boat’s leaking!”
sentences.zh: 「雷电在上！——伙计们，船漏水了！」

paragraphs.text: And then the other pirates peered over the side and they saw that the boat was indeed getting lower and lower in the water. And one of them said to Ben Ali,

sentences.text: And then the other pirates peered over the side and they saw that the boat was indeed getting lower and lower in the water.
sentences.zh: 于是别的海盗也往船边探头看，果然看见船在水里越来越低。

sentences.text: And one of them said to Ben Ali,
sentences.zh: 其中一个对本·阿里说：

paragraphs.text: “But surely if this old boat were sinking we should see the rats leaving it.”

sentences.text: “But surely if this old boat were sinking we should see the rats leaving it.”
sentences.zh: 「可这条旧船要是真在下沉，我们总该看见老鼠往外跑吧。」

introduction.zh: 医生答应了图图的办法，可这一整夜该跟海盗聊些什么？吉普觉得根本不用聊：对方只有六个人，咬个真海盗，回家才好讲给隔壁的牧羊犬听。医生说他们有手枪和刀。船越来越近，海盗的笑声却忽然停了。
introduction.en: Too-Too’s plan is simple: keep the pirate talking. But what can the Doctor talk about all night? Jip thinks talking is a waste — there are only six pirates, and he would love to bite a real one. Then the pirates come closer, and their laughing stops.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor say no to Jip’s plan of fighting?
options: The Doctor wants to save the ship first.
The pirates have pistols and swords.
There are too many pirates for Jip.

feedback.zh: 吉普说六个海盗不算什么，医生马上提醒：他们有手枪和刀，打起来绝不行，还是得靠嘴谈。
feedback.en: Jip says six men are nothing, but the Doctor points out that they have pistols and swords, so fighting would never do.

quiz.question: What are the pirates doing as they sail nearer?
options: Laughing and asking who will catch the pig first.
Lowering a small boat to row to the island.
Shouting to the Doctor for the trunk of gold.

feedback.zh: 原文写他们兴高采烈地笑着，互相问「谁第一个去抓那头猪」，好像抓猪是件好玩的事。
feedback.en: They come on laughing with glee and asking one another who shall be the first to catch the pig.

grammar.excerpt: Jip kept springing into the air and barking

focus.zh: kept springing 是 keep + 动词 -ing：吉普一次又一次地跳起来叫，表示反复不停。
focus.en: Kept springing is keep + -ing: Jip jumped and barked again and again.

paragraphs.text: And Jip shouted across from the other ship,

sentences.text: And Jip shouted across from the other ship,
sentences.zh: 吉普从另一条船上隔着水大喊：

paragraphs.text: “You great duffers, there are no rats there to leave! They left two hours ago! ‘Ha, ha,’ to you, ‘my fine friends!’”

sentences.text: “You great duffers, there are no rats there to leave!
sentences.zh: 「你们这些大笨蛋，那儿根本没有老鼠可跑了！

sentences.text: They left two hours ago! ‘Ha, ha,’ to you, ‘my fine friends!’”
sentences.zh: 它们两个钟头前就走了！也送你们一句『哈，哈』，『我的好朋友』！」

hints.zh: duffer 是「笨蛋、不中用的家伙」，great 在这里加重嘲弄：你们这些大笨蛋。
hints.en: A duffer is a stupid, useless fellow; great here makes the mockery stronger.

hints.zh: 吉普把本·阿里刚才的「哈！哈！我的好朋友」原话掷回去，反过来嘲笑他们。
