hints.en: Jip throws Ben Ali’s own words back at him — “Ha, ha” and “my fine friends” — to mock the pirates.

paragraphs.text: But of course the men did not understand him.

sentences.text: But of course the men did not understand him.
sentences.zh: 当然，那些人听不懂他的话。

paragraphs.text: Soon the front end of the ship began to go down and down, faster and faster—till the boat looked almost as though it were standing on its head; and the pirates had to cling to the rails and the masts and the ropes and anything to keep from sliding off. Then the sea rushed roaring in through all the windows and the doors. And at last the ship plunged right down to the bottom of the sea, making a dreadful gurgling sound; and the six bad men were left bobbing about in the deep water of the bay.

sentences.text: Soon the front end of the ship began to go down and down, faster and faster—till the boat looked almost as though it were standing on its head; and the pirates had to cling to the rails and the masts and the ropes and anything to keep from sliding off.
sentences.zh: 不久，船头开始一点一点往下沉，越沉越快——最后那条船看上去几乎像倒立着；海盗们只好抓住栏杆、桅杆、绳索，抓住任何东西，免得滑下去。

sentences.text: Then the sea rushed roaring in through all the windows and the doors.
sentences.zh: 接着，海水轰响着从所有的窗户和门里灌进来。

sentences.text: And at last the ship plunged right down to the bottom of the sea, making a dreadful gurgling sound; and the six bad men were left bobbing about in the deep water of the bay.
sentences.zh: 最后，那条船咕嘟咕嘟发出可怕的声响，一头扎到海底；六个坏人被留在海湾的深水里上下浮沉。

hints.zh: on its head 指倒立、颠倒过来：船头朝下沉，看上去像倒立着。
hints.en: Standing on its head means turned upside down: the sinking ship looked as if it were standing on its nose.

hints.zh: keep from + 动词 -ing 是「避免、使自己不至于」：抓住东西免得滑下去。
hints.en: Keep from doing something means to stop yourself from doing it: they clung on so as not to slide off.

hints.zh: bob about 是「在水里一上一下地浮沉、漂来漂去」。
hints.en: To bob about means to float up and down on the water.

paragraphs.text: Some of them started to swim for the shores of the island; while others came and tried to get on to the boat where the Doctor was. But Jip kept snapping at their noses, so they were afraid to climb up the side of the ship.

sentences.text: Some of them started to swim for the shores of the island; while others came and tried to get on to the boat where the Doctor was.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有的朝岛岸游去；另一些游过来，想爬上医生待的这条船。

sentences.text: But Jip kept snapping at their noses, so they were afraid to climb up the side of the ship.
sentences.zh: 可吉普一个劲儿地咬他们的鼻子，所以他们不敢往船帮上爬。

hints.zh: snap at 是「猛地咬过去」：谁靠近，吉普就咬谁的鼻子。
hints.en: To snap at something is to bite at it suddenly: Jip bit at any nose that came near.

paragraphs.text: Then suddenly they all cried out in great fear,

sentences.text: Then suddenly they all cried out in great fear,
sentences.zh: 忽然，他们全都惊恐万分地叫起来：

paragraphs.text: “The sharks! The sharks are coming! Let us get on to the ship before they eat us! Help, help!—The sharks! The sharks!”

sentences.text: “The sharks!
sentences.zh: 「鲨鱼！

sentences.text: The sharks are coming!
sentences.zh: 鲨鱼来了！

sentences.text: Let us get on to the ship before they eat us!
sentences.zh: 让我们上船吧，别让它们把我们吃了！

sentences.text: Help, help!—The sharks!
sentences.zh: 救命，救命！——鲨鱼！

sentences.text: The sharks!”
sentences.zh: 鲨鱼！」

paragraphs.text: And now the Doctor could see, all over the bay, the backs of big fishes swimming swiftly through the water.

sentences.text: And now the Doctor could see, all over the bay, the backs of big fishes swimming swiftly through the water.
sentences.zh: 这时医生看得见，整个海湾里都是大鱼飞快游过时露出的脊背。

paragraphs.text: And one great shark came near to the ship, and poking his nose out of the water he said to the Doctor,

sentences.text: And one great shark came near to the ship, and poking his nose out of the water he said to the Doctor,
sentences.zh: 一条大鲨鱼游到船边，把鼻子探出水面，对医生说：

introduction.zh: 旧船紧挨着医生的船，海盗们还在笑：这一回跑不掉了。可笑着笑着，有人觉得脚下的船板不对劲，低头一看——水正从缝里往上冒。他们能撑到岸上吗？
introduction.en: The pirate ship is close beside the Doctor’s, and the pirates are still laughing: this time their prey cannot get away. Then one of them feels something wrong under his feet and looks down — water is coming up between the boards. Can they reach the shore?

quiz.question: Why do the men see no rats leaving the sinking boat?
options: The boat never had any rats on it.
The rats are hiding below the deck.
The rats left two hours earlier.

feedback.zh: 海盗以为船沉前总该有老鼠逃出来，吉普却喊：老鼠两个钟头前就走了，所以船上根本没有老鼠可看。
feedback.en: The pirates expect rats to leave a sinking ship, but Jip shouts that the rats left two hours ago, so none are left to see.

quiz.question: Why are the pirates afraid to climb up the side of the Doctor’s ship?
options: The Doctor pushes them back into the water.
Jip keeps biting at their noses.
The side of the ship is too high for them.

feedback.zh: 原文说吉普不停地咬他们的鼻子，所以他们不敢往船帮上爬，只能在水里泡着。
feedback.en: Jip kept snapping at their noses, so they were afraid to climb up the side of the ship.

grammar.excerpt: till the boat looked almost as though it were standing on its head

focus.zh: as though 后面用 were standing，是设想出来的样子：船并没有真的倒立，只是看上去像。
focus.en: As though takes were standing for an imagined picture: the boat was not really standing on its head.

paragraphs.text: “Are you John Dolittle, the famous animal-doctor?”

sentences.text: “Are you John Dolittle, the famous animal-doctor?”
sentences.zh: 「你就是那位有名的动物医生约翰·杜立德吗？」

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，就是杜立德医生；鲨鱼是慕名而来找他的。
hints.en: John Dolittle: the Doctor’s full name; the shark has heard of him.

paragraphs.text: “Yes,” said Doctor Dolittle. “That is my name.”

sentences.text: “Yes,” said Doctor Dolittle.
sentences.zh: 「是的，」杜立德医生说。

sentences.text: “That is my name.”
sentences.zh: 「那就是我的名字。」

paragraphs.text: “Well,” said the shark, “we know these pirates to be a bad lot—especially Ben Ali. If they are annoying you, we will gladly eat them up for you—and then you won’t be troubled any more.”

sentences.text: “Well,” said the shark, “we know these pirates to be a bad lot—especially Ben Ali.
sentences.zh: 「唔，」鲨鱼说，「我们知道这些海盗是一伙坏蛋——尤其是本·阿里。

sentences.text: If they are annoying you, we will gladly eat them up for you—and then you won’t be troubled any more.”
sentences.zh: 要是他们来烦你，我们很乐意替你把他们吃掉——这样你就再也不用为这事操心了。」

hints.zh: a bad lot 是「一伙坏人、不成器的东西」，lot 在这里指一群人。
hints.en: A bad lot means a group of bad people; lot here means a set of people.

paragraphs.text: “Thank you,” said the Doctor. “This is really most attentive. But I don’t think it will be necessary to eat them. Don’t let any of them reach the shore until I tell you—just keep them swimming about, will you? And please make Ben Ali swim over here that I may talk to him.”

sentences.text: “Thank you,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「谢谢你，」医生说。

sentences.text: “This is really most attentive.
sentences.zh: 「你们真是太周到了。

sentences.text: But I don’t think it will be necessary to eat them.
sentences.zh: 不过我看，不必把他们吃掉。

sentences.text: Don’t let any of them reach the shore until I tell you—just keep them swimming about, will you?
sentences.zh: 在我开口之前，别让其中任何一个上岸——就让他们一直在水里游着，行吗？

sentences.text: And please make Ben Ali swim over here that I may talk to him.”
sentences.zh: 还有，请让本·阿里游到这儿来，我要跟他谈谈。」

hints.zh: attentive 本义是「留心的」，这里指「周到、体贴」：医生客气地谢鲨鱼想得周到。
hints.en: Attentive usually means watchful; here it means kind and thoughtful — the Doctor is politely thanking the shark.

paragraphs.text: So the shark went off and chased Ben Ali over to the Doctor.

sentences.text: So the shark went off and chased Ben Ali over to the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 于是鲨鱼游开了，把本·阿里一路赶到医生这边。

paragraphs.text: “Listen, Ben Ali,” said John Dolittle, leaning over the side. “You have been a very bad man; and I understand that you have killed many people. These good sharks here have just offered to eat you up for me—and ’twould indeed be a good thing if the seas were rid of you. But if you will promise to do as I tell you, I will let you go in safety.”

sentences.text: “Listen, Ben Ali,” said John Dolittle, leaning over the side.
sentences.zh: 「听着，本·阿里，」约翰·杜立德靠在船边说。

sentences.text: “You have been a very bad man; and I understand that you have killed many people.
sentences.zh: 「你一直是个很坏的人；我听说你杀过不少人。

sentences.text: These good sharks here have just offered to eat you up for me—and ’twould indeed be a good thing if the seas were rid of you.
sentences.zh: 这儿这些好心的鲨鱼刚才提出，要替我把你吃掉——要是海里少了你这样的人，倒真是件好事。

sentences.text: But if you will promise to do as I tell you, I will let you go in safety.”
sentences.zh: 不过，只要你答应照我说的做，我就放你平安离开。」

hints.zh: be rid of 是「摆脱、除掉」：海里要是没了你，倒是件好事。
hints.en: To be rid of someone is to have them gone for good: the seas would be better without you.

paragraphs.text: “What must I do?” asked the pirate, looking down sideways at the big shark who was smelling his leg under the water.

sentences.text: “What must I do?” asked the pirate, looking down sideways at the big shark who was smelling his leg under the water.
sentences.zh: 「我该做什么？」海盗问，一边斜眼往下看那条正在水下嗅他腿的大鲨鱼。

paragraphs.text: “You must kill no more people,” said the Doctor; “you must stop stealing; you must never sink another ship; you must give up being a pirate altogether.”

sentences.text: “You must kill no more people,” said the Doctor; “you must stop stealing; you must never sink another ship; you must give up being a pirate altogether.”
sentences.zh: 「你不许再杀人，」医生说，「不许再偷东西；不许再弄沉任何一条船；你要彻底不当海盗了。」

hints.target: give up being a pirate altogether
hints.zh: give up 是「放弃、不再做」，altogether 是「彻底地」：从此完全不当海盗。
hints.en: Give up means to stop doing something for good; altogether adds “completely”.

paragraphs.text: “But what shall I do then?” asked Ben Ali. “How shall I live?”

sentences.text: “But what shall I do then?” asked Ben Ali.
sentences.zh: 「那我该做什么呢？」本·阿里问。

sentences.text: “How shall I live?”
sentences.zh: 「我靠什么活？」

introduction.zh: 一条大鲨鱼从水里探出鼻子，问船上的人是不是那位有名的动物医生。听说海盗在为难他，鲨鱼很愿意替他把这些人吃掉。医生道了谢，却提了另一个请求——那会是什么？
introduction.en: A big shark pokes his nose out of the water and asks whether the man on the ship is the famous animal-doctor. Hearing that the pirates are troubling him, the shark offers to eat them all. The Doctor thanks him — and asks for something else. What does he want?

quiz.question: What does the shark offer to do for the Doctor?
options: Eat the pirates up for him.
Pull his ship out of the bay.
Carry him safely to the island.

feedback.zh: 鲨鱼说他们知道这伙海盗是坏蛋，要是他们来烦医生，很乐意替医生把他们吃掉。
feedback.en: The shark says the pirates are a bad lot and offers to eat them up for the Doctor if they are annoying him.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor ask the shark to do with the pirates?
options: Frighten them away and never let them come back.
Take Ben Ali to the other side of the bay.
Keep them swimming and let none of them reach the shore.

feedback.zh: 医生不要鲨鱼吃人，只要求在他开口之前别让任何一个上岸，让他们一直在水里游；另外把本·阿里赶过来谈话。
feedback.en: He does not want them eaten: the sharks must keep them swimming and let none of them reach the shore until he says so.

grammar.excerpt: If they are annoying you, we will gladly eat them up for you

focus.zh: if 从句用一般现在时 are annoying 讲条件，主句用 will eat 讲结果；英语条件句里 if 后面不用 will。
focus.en: The if-clause uses the present (are annoying) for the condition and will eat for the result; English does not put will after if.

paragraphs.text: “You and all your men must go on to this island and be bird-seed-farmers,” the Doctor answered. “You must grow bird-seed for the canaries.”

sentences.text: “You and all your men must go on to this island and be bird-seed-farmers,” the Doctor answered.
sentences.zh: 「你和你手下所有的人都要到这个岛上去，当种鸟食的农夫，」医生回答。

sentences.text: “You must grow bird-seed for the canaries.”
sentences.zh: 「你们要种鸟食，卖给养金丝雀的人。」

hints.zh: 鸟食：喂笼鸟的草籽、小米一类，当时城里人养鸟要买，是可以换钱的作物。
hints.en: Bird-seed: the little seeds sold to feed cage birds — a crop a farmer could sell.

hints.zh: 金丝雀，养在笼子里的黄色小鸟，吃鸟食；所以要种给它们吃。
hints.en: Canaries: small yellow cage birds kept as pets; bird-seed is grown to feed them.

paragraphs.text: The Barbary Dragon turned pale with anger, “Grow bird-seed!” he groaned in disgust. “Can’t I be a sailor?”

sentences.text: The Barbary Dragon turned pale with anger, “Grow bird-seed!” he groaned in disgust.
sentences.zh: 巴巴里巨龙气得脸色发白，「种鸟食！」他厌恶地哼了一声。

sentences.text: “Can’t I be a sailor?”
sentences.zh: 「我就不能当水手吗？」

hints.zh: turn pale with anger 是「气得脸都白了」，pale 指脸色发白，不是「苍白无力」。
hints.en: To turn pale with anger is to go white in the face from rage.

hints.zh: in disgust 是「厌恶地、反感地」：他觉得种鸟食这行当太丢人。
hints.en: In disgust means with strong dislike: the very idea of growing bird-seed revolts him.

paragraphs.text: “No,” said the Doctor, “you cannot. You have been a sailor long enough—and sent many stout ships and good men to the bottom of the sea. For the rest of your life you must be a peaceful farmer. The shark is waiting. Do not waste any more of his time. Make up your mind.”

sentences.text: “No,” said the Doctor, “you cannot.
sentences.zh: 「不行，」医生说，「你不能。

sentences.text: You have been a sailor long enough—and sent many stout ships and good men to the bottom of the sea.
sentences.zh: 你当水手已经够久了——还把许多结实的船和好人送进了海底。

sentences.text: For the rest of your life you must be a peaceful farmer.
sentences.zh: 从今往后，你这一辈子都得当一个安分的农夫。

sentences.text: The shark is waiting.
sentences.zh: 鲨鱼还等着呢。

sentences.text: Do not waste any more of his time.
sentences.zh: 别再浪费他的时间了。

sentences.text: Make up your mind.”
sentences.zh: 拿定主意吧。」

hints.zh: stout 这里不是「胖的」，而是「结实的、坚固的」：结实的船。
hints.en: Stout here means strong and solid, not fat: well-built ships.

hints.zh: make up one’s mind 是「下定决心、拿定主意」，不是「做脑子」。
hints.en: To make up your mind is to decide; nothing is being built.

paragraphs.text: “Thunder and Lightning!” Ben Ali muttered—“Bird-seed!” Then he looked down into the water again and saw the great fish smelling his other leg.

sentences.text: “Thunder and Lightning!”
sentences.zh: 「雷电在上！」

sentences.text: Ben Ali muttered—“Bird-seed!”
sentences.zh: 本·阿里嘟囔着——「鸟食！」

sentences.text: Then he looked down into the water again and saw the great fish smelling his other leg.
sentences.zh: 然后他又低头看水里，看见那条大鱼正在嗅他的另一条腿。

paragraphs.text: “Very well,” he said sadly. “We’ll be farmers.”

sentences.text: “Very well,” he said sadly.
sentences.zh: 「好吧，」他沮丧地说。

sentences.text: “We’ll be farmers.”
sentences.zh: 「我们就当农夫吧。」

paragraphs.text: “And remember,” said the Doctor, “that if you do not keep your promise—if you start killing and stealing again, I shall hear of it, because the canaries will come and tell me. And be very sure that I will find a way to punish you. For though I may not be able to sail a ship as well as you, so long as the birds and the beasts and the fishes are my friends, I do not have to be afraid of a pirate chief—even though he call himself ‘The Dragon of Barbary.’ Now go and be a good farmer and live in peace.”

sentences.text: “And remember,” said the Doctor, “that if you do not keep your promise—if you start killing and stealing again, I shall hear of it, because the canaries will come and tell me.
sentences.zh: 「还要记住，」医生说，「要是你不守承诺——要是你又开始杀人抢东西，我会知道的，因为金丝雀会飞来告诉我。

sentences.text: And be very sure that I will find a way to punish you.
sentences.zh: 你尽管放心，我总有办法惩罚你。

sentences.text: For though I may not be able to sail a ship as well as you, so long as the birds and the beasts and the fishes are my friends, I do not have to be afraid of a pirate chief—even though he call himself ‘The Dragon of Barbary.’
sentences.zh: 因为，虽然我开船不如你，可是只要飞鸟、走兽和鱼都是我的朋友，我就不必怕一个海盗头子——哪怕他自称『巴巴里巨龙』。

sentences.text: Now go and be a good farmer and live in peace.”
sentences.zh: 好了，去当个好农夫，安安静静过日子吧。」

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor turned to the big shark, and waving his hand he said,

sentences.text: Then the Doctor turned to the big shark, and waving his hand he said,
sentences.zh: 接着医生转向那条大鲨鱼，摆摆手说：

paragraphs.text: “All right. Let them swim safely to the land.”

sentences.text: “All right.
sentences.zh: 「好了。

sentences.text: Let them swim safely to the land.”
sentences.zh: 让他们平安游上岸吧。」

introduction.zh: 海盗头子问：那我该怎么活？医生给他指了一条完全不同的路，还要他当场拿定主意。水里那条大鱼还在等着，时不时碰一碰他的腿。一个靠抢船为生的人，会答应这样的条件吗？
introduction.en: “How shall I live?” asks the pirate chief. The Doctor points him to a very different life, and wants an answer at once. All the while the great fish waits in the water, nosing at his leg. Will a man who has lived by robbing ships agree?

quiz.question: What does the Doctor say Ben Ali and his men must become?
options: Fishermen who work for the sharks.
Bird-seed farmers on the island.
Sailors on the Doctor’s ship.

feedback.zh: 医生给他指的路是：带着手下人到岛上种鸟食，靠种庄稼过日子，不再抢船。
feedback.en: The Doctor tells him to take all his men to the island and grow bird-seed for the canaries instead of robbing ships.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor say he does not have to be afraid of a pirate chief?
options: Because the birds, beasts and fishes are his friends.
Because he can sail a ship better than Ben Ali.
Because the sharks will stay beside him for ever.

feedback.zh: 医生承认自己开船不如对方，可他说只要飞鸟、走兽和鱼都是他的朋友，他就不必怕一个海盗头子。
feedback.en: He admits he cannot sail as well as Ben Ali, but with the birds, beasts and fishes as his friends he need not fear a pirate chief.

grammar.excerpt: though I may not be able to sail a ship as well as you

focus.zh: not … as well as you 是否定同级比较：我开船不如你；as 与 as 之间用原级 well。
focus.en: Not as well as you is a negative comparison — I cannot sail as well as you; the base form well sits between as and as.

paragraphs.text: Having thanked the sharks again for their kindness, the Doctor and his pets set off once more on their journey home in the swift ship with the three red sails.

sentences.text: Having thanked the sharks again for their kindness, the Doctor and his pets set off once more on their journey home in the swift ship with the three red sails.
sentences.zh: 又一次谢过鲨鱼们的好意之后，医生和他的动物们乘着那条挂着三面红帆的快船，再次踏上回家的路。

paragraphs.text: As they moved out into the open sea, the animals all went downstairs to see what their new boat was like inside; while the Doctor leant on the rail at the back of the ship with a pipe in his mouth, watching the Canary Islands fade away in the blue dusk of the evening.

sentences.text: As they moved out into the open sea, the animals all went downstairs to see what their new boat was like inside; while the Doctor leant on the rail at the back of the ship with a pipe in his mouth, watching the Canary Islands fade away in the blue dusk of the evening.
sentences.zh: 船驶入外海时，动物们都下到舱里，去看他们的新船里面是什么样子；医生则叼着烟斗，靠在船尾的栏杆上，望着加那利群岛在傍晚蓝色的暮色中渐渐退远。

hints.zh: 加那利群岛，非洲西北面大西洋上的群岛，船从这儿往北开回家。
hints.en: The Canary Islands, a group of islands in the Atlantic off north-west Africa.

paragraphs.text: While he was standing there, wondering how the monkeys were getting on—and what his garden would look like when he got back to Puddleby, Dab-Dab came tumbling up the stairs, all smiles and full of news.

sentences.text: While he was standing there, wondering how the monkeys were getting on—and what his garden would look like when he got back to Puddleby, Dab-Dab came tumbling up the stairs, all smiles and full of news.
sentences.zh: 他正站在那里，想着猴子们过得怎么样——也想着自己回到帕德尔比时，花园会是什么模样——达布达布满脸笑容、满肚子消息，连滚带爬地跑上楼梯。

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor’s home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

hints.zh: get on 在这里是「过得怎么样、进展如何」：他想知道猴子们近况如何。
hints.en: Get on here means to be getting along: he wonders how the monkeys are doing.

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

paragraphs.text: “Doctor!” she cried. “This ship of the pirates is simply beautiful—absolutely. The beds downstairs are made of primrose silk—with hundreds of big pillows and cushions; there are thick, soft carpets on the floors; the dishes are made of silver; and there are all sorts of good things to eat and drink—special things; the larder—well, it’s just like a shop, that’s all. You never saw anything like it in your life—Just think—they kept five different kinds of sardines, those men! Come and look.... Oh, and we found a little room down there with the door locked; and we are all crazy to get in and see what’s inside. Jip says it must be where the pirates kept their treasure. But we can’t open the door. Come down and see if you can let us in.”

sentences.text: “Doctor!” she cried.
sentences.zh: 「医生！」她喊道。

sentences.text: “This ship of the pirates is simply beautiful—absolutely.
sentences.zh: 「海盗这条船真是漂亮——漂亮极了。

sentences.text: The beds downstairs are made of primrose silk—with hundreds of big pillows and cushions; there are thick, soft carpets on the floors; the dishes are made of silver; and there are all sorts of good things to eat and drink—special things; the larder—well, it’s just like a shop, that’s all.
sentences.zh: 楼下的床是淡黄色丝绸做的——配着几百个大枕头和靠垫；地板上铺着又厚又软的地毯；盘子是银的；还有各种各样好吃的、好喝的——都是特别的东西；食品间嘛——唉，简直就像一家铺子，就这么回事。

sentences.text: You never saw anything like it in your life—Just think—they kept five different kinds of sardines, those men!
sentences.zh: 你这辈子都没见过这样的东西——你想想——那些人居然存了五种不同的沙丁鱼！

sentences.text: Come and look....
sentences.zh: 来看看吧……

sentences.text: Oh, and we found a little room down there with the door locked; and we are all crazy to get in and see what’s inside.
sentences.zh: 噢，我们还在下面发现一间小屋，门锁着；我们都急着想进去看看里面有什么。

sentences.text: Jip says it must be where the pirates kept their treasure.
sentences.zh: 吉普说，那一定是海盗存放财宝的地方。

sentences.text: But we can’t open the door.
sentences.zh: 可我们打不开那扇门。

sentences.text: Come down and see if you can let us in.”
sentences.zh: 你下来看看，能不能帮我们进去。」

hints.zh: 樱草色（淡黄色）的丝绸，当时是很贵重的料子。
hints.en: Primrose silk: silk in a pale yellow colour, an expensive stuff in those days.

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

introduction.zh: 三条红帆的船载着医生和动物们往家走。达布达布跑上楼梯，满嘴都是楼下的好东西：丝被、银盘、五种沙丁鱼。她还发现一间锁着的小屋，谁都打不开。
introduction.en: The ship with three red sails is taking the Doctor and his animals home. Dab-Dab runs up the stairs full of news: silk beds, silver dishes, five kinds of sardines. And one little door below that nobody can open.

quiz.question: What is the one thing the animals cannot get to downstairs?
options: The beds made of primrose silk
A little room whose door is locked
The silver dishes in the larder

feedback.zh: 达布达布特意提到楼下有间门锁着的小屋，大家都急着想进去看，可谁也打不开门。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab says they found a little room below with its door locked, and nobody can open it.

quiz.question: How does Dab-Dab seem when she comes up the stairs?
options: Excited, with a lot to tell
Tired and cross
Quiet and frightened

feedback.zh: 原文说她「满脸笑容、满肚子消息」，一开口就夸这条船漂亮极了。
feedback.en: She comes tumbling up all smiles and full of news, and at once calls the ship simply beautiful.

grammar.excerpt: As they moved out into the open sea

focus.zh: as 在这里相当于 when，引出「船驶入外海时」这个时间；从句在前，主语和主句之间用逗号隔开。
focus.en: As here means when: it sets the time — the moment the ship reached the open sea.

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor went downstairs and he saw that it was indeed a beautiful ship. He found the animals gathered round a little door, all talking at once, trying to guess what was inside. The Doctor turned the handle but it wouldn’t open. Then they all started to hunt for the key. They looked under the mat; they looked under all the carpets; they looked in all the cupboards and drawers and lockers—in the big chests in the ship’s dining-room; they looked everywhere.

sentences.text: So the Doctor went downstairs and he saw that it was indeed a beautiful ship.
sentences.zh: 于是医生下了楼，看出这确实是一条漂亮的船。

sentences.text: He found the animals gathered round a little door, all talking at once, trying to guess what was inside.
sentences.zh: 他发现动物们都围在一扇小门旁边，七嘴八舌地同时说着话，猜里面是什么。

sentences.text: The Doctor turned the handle but it wouldn’t open.
sentences.zh: 医生转了转门把手，门却打不开。

sentences.text: Then they all started to hunt for the key.
sentences.zh: 于是大家开始到处找钥匙。

sentences.text: They looked under the mat; they looked under all the carpets; they looked in all the cupboards and drawers and lockers—in the big chests in the ship’s dining-room; they looked everywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们看了垫子底下；看了所有地毯底下；查看了所有的碗柜、抽屉和储物柜——还有船上餐厅里那些大箱子；他们哪儿都找过了。

paragraphs.text: While they were doing this they discovered a lot of new and wonderful things that the pirates must have stolen from other ships: Kashmir shawls as thin as a cobweb, embroidered with flowers of gold; jars of fine tobacco from Jamaica; carved ivory boxes full of Russian tea; an old violin with a string broken and a picture on the back; a set of big chess-men, carved out of coral and amber; a walking-stick which had a sword inside it when you pulled the handle; six wine-glasses with tourquoise and silver round the rims; and a lovely great sugar-bowl, made of mother o’ pearl. But nowhere in the whole boat could they find a key to fit that lock.

sentences.text: While they were doing this they discovered a lot of new and wonderful things that the pirates must have stolen from other ships: Kashmir shawls as thin as a cobweb, embroidered with flowers of gold; jars of fine tobacco from Jamaica; carved ivory boxes full of Russian tea; an old violin with a string broken and a picture on the back; a set of big chess-men, carved out of coral and amber; a walking-stick which had a sword inside it when you pulled the handle; six wine-glasses with tourquoise and silver round the rims; and a lovely great sugar-bowl, made of mother o’ pearl.
sentences.zh: 找的过程中，他们发现了许多新奇好看的东西，一定是海盗从别的船上抢来的：薄得像蛛网、绣着金花的克什米尔披肩；一罐罐牙买加的上等烟草；装满俄罗斯茶叶的雕花象牙盒；一把断了弦、背面有画的旧小提琴；一副用珊瑚和琥珀雕成的大棋子；一根一拉把手、里面就露出剑来的手杖；六只杯口镶着绿松石和银子的酒杯；还有一只可爱的大糖罐，是用珍珠母做的。

sentences.text: But nowhere in the whole boat could they find a key to fit that lock.
sentences.zh: 可是整条船上，他们哪儿都找不到一把能开那把锁的钥匙。

hints.zh: 克什米尔披肩，产自克什米尔，以极薄极软出名，当时非常珍贵。
hints.en: Kashmir shawls: very fine, soft shawls from Kashmir, much prized in those days.

hints.zh: 棋子（单数 chess-man），不是「下棋的人」；这里指一副雕刻的大棋子。
hints.en: Chess-men are the pieces used in chess, not men playing it.

hints.zh: 绿松石，一种蓝绿色宝石；今天多拼作 turquoise。
hints.en: Turquoise, a blue-green gemstone; the usual spelling today is turquoise.

hints.zh: 珍珠母，贝壳内层那种带光泽的材料；o’ 是 of 的缩写。
hints.en: Mother o’ pearl is mother-of-pearl, the shiny inner layer of a shell; o’ is short for of.

paragraphs.text: So they all came back to the door, and Jip peered through the key-hole. But something had been stood against the wall on the inside and he could see nothing.

sentences.text: So they all came back to the door, and Jip peered through the key-hole.
sentences.zh: 于是大家又回到那扇门前，吉普凑到钥匙孔上往里瞧。

sentences.text: But something had been stood against the wall on the inside and he could see nothing.
sentences.zh: 可里面有什么东西靠墙立着，他什么也看不见。

hints.zh: peer 是「眯着眼使劲看」，不是「偷看」；吉普贴在钥匙孔上往里瞧。
hints.en: To peer is to look hard and closely, as Jip does through the keyhole.

paragraphs.text: While they were standing around, wondering what they should do, the owl, Too-Too, suddenly said,

sentences.text: While they were standing around, wondering what they should do, the owl, Too-Too, suddenly said,
sentences.zh: 他们站在那里，不知该怎么办，猫头鹰图图忽然说：

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰，耳朵极灵。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor’s owl, whose hearing is very sharp.

introduction.zh: 医生下楼去看那扇门。门把手转不动，动物们便分头找钥匙：垫子下、地毯下、柜子里、箱子里。翻找的时候，他们翻出了海盗从别的船上抢来的东西。
introduction.en: Downstairs, the handle will not turn, so everyone hunts for the key — under the mat, under the carpets, inside every chest. On the way they find what the pirates stole from other ships.

quiz.question: Why do the animals still not get the door open?
options: The door is locked from the outside
Jip has hidden the key
No key on the ship fits that lock

feedback.zh: 他们把整条船都找遍了，也找不到一把能开那把锁的钥匙。
feedback.en: They search the whole boat but find no key that fits the lock.

quiz.question: What does Jip see through the keyhole?
options: A man sitting on a chest
Nothing, because something stands against the door inside
A pile of gold in the dark

feedback.zh: 门里面有个东西靠墙立着，挡住了钥匙孔，所以吉普什么也看不见。
feedback.en: Something has been stood against the wall inside, so Jip can see nothing at all.

grammar.excerpt: a walking-stick which had a sword inside it

focus.zh: which 指前面的 a walking-stick，在从句里作主语，说明这根手杖里藏着剑。
focus.en: Which refers back to a walking-stick and is the subject of the clause: the stick had a sword inside it.

paragraphs.text: “Sh!—Listen!—I do believe there’s some one in there!”

sentences.text: “Sh!—Listen!—I do believe there’s some one in there!”
sentences.zh: 「嘘！——听！——我真觉得里面有人！」

hints.zh: 「嘘！」，叫人别出声的声音；图图一再这样让全家安静。
hints.en: Sh! is the sound people make to tell others to be quiet.

paragraphs.text: They all kept still a moment. Then the Doctor said,

sentences.text: They all kept still a moment.
sentences.zh: 大家都静静地待了一会儿。

sentences.text: Then the Doctor said,
sentences.zh: 然后医生说：

paragraphs.text: “You must be mistaken, Too-Too. I don’t hear anything.”

sentences.text: “You must be mistaken, Too-Too.
sentences.zh: 「图图，你一定弄错了。

sentences.text: I don’t hear anything.”
sentences.zh: 我什么也没听见。」

paragraphs.text: “I’m sure of it,” said the owl. “Sh!—There it is again—Don’t you hear that?”

sentences.text: “I’m sure of it,” said the owl.
sentences.zh: 「我敢肯定，」猫头鹰说。

sentences.text: “Sh!—There it is again—Don’t you hear that?”
sentences.zh: 「嘘！——又来了——你听见没有？」

paragraphs.text: “No, I do not,” said the Doctor. “What kind of a sound is it?”

sentences.text: “No, I do not,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「没有，我没听见，」医生说。

sentences.text: “What kind of a sound is it?”
sentences.zh: 「是什么样的声音？」

paragraphs.text: “I hear the noise of some one putting his hand in his pocket,” said the owl.

sentences.text: “I hear the noise of some one putting his hand in his pocket,” said the owl.
sentences.zh: 「我听见有人把手伸进口袋的声音，」猫头鹰说。

paragraphs.text: “But that makes hardly any sound at all,” said the Doctor. “You couldn’t hear that out here.”

sentences.text: “But that makes hardly any sound at all,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可那几乎发不出什么声音啊，」医生说。

sentences.text: “You couldn’t hear that out here.”
sentences.zh: 「在外面这儿，你不可能听见的。」

hints.zh: hardly 是「几乎不」，不是「努力地」（hard）：那几乎不发出声音。
hints.en: Hardly means almost not at all — not hard, the adverb of effort.

paragraphs.text: “Pardon me, but I can,” said Too-Too. “I tell you there is some one on the other side of that door putting his hand in his pocket. Almost everything makes some noise—if your ears are only sharp enough to catch it. Bats can hear a mole walking in his tunnel under the earth—and they think they’re good hearers. But we owls can tell you, using only one ear, the color of a kitten from the way it winks in the dark.”

sentences.text: “Pardon me, but I can,” said Too-Too.
sentences.zh: 「对不起，可我就是听得见，」图图说。

sentences.text: “I tell you there is some one on the other side of that door putting his hand in his pocket.
sentences.zh: 「我跟你说，那扇门另一边有个人正把手伸进口袋。

sentences.text: Almost everything makes some noise—if your ears are only sharp enough to catch it.
sentences.zh: 几乎样样东西都会发出点声音——只要你的耳朵够灵，能捕捉到它。

sentences.text: Bats can hear a mole walking in his tunnel under the earth—and they think they’re good hearers.
sentences.zh: 蝙蝠能听见鼹鼠在地底下的洞里走路——它们还自以为耳朵好使呢。

sentences.text: But we owls can tell you, using only one ear, the color of a kitten from the way it winks in the dark.”
sentences.zh: 可我们猫头鹰只用一只耳朵，就能从小猫在黑暗里眨眼的动静，听出它是什么颜色的。」

hints.zh: 「对不起／恕我直言」，这里用来礼貌地反驳对方。
hints.en: Pardon me here politely introduces a disagreement: excuse me, but I can.

hints.zh: 旧式写法，等于 someone「某人」；本书里都分成两个词写。
hints.en: An old-fashioned spelling of someone; this book always writes it as two words.

hints.zh: 听觉灵敏的动物；图图是在说蝙蝠自以为了不起，其实比不上猫头鹰。
hints.en: Good hearers are animals with sharp hearing; Too-Too means the bats only think they are.

paragraphs.text: “Well, well!” said the Doctor. “You surprise me. That’s very interesting.... Listen again and tell me what he’s doing now.”

sentences.text: “Well, well!” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「哎呀，哎呀！」医生说。

sentences.text: “You surprise me.
sentences.zh: 「你真让我吃惊。

sentences.text: That’s very interesting....
sentences.zh: 这太有意思了……

sentences.text: Listen again and tell me what he’s doing now.”
sentences.zh: 再听一次，告诉我他现在在做什么。」

paragraphs.text: “I’m not sure yet,” said Too-Too, “if it’s a man at all. Maybe it’s a woman. Lift me up and let me listen at the key-hole and I’ll soon tell you.”

sentences.text: “I’m not sure yet,” said Too-Too, “if it’s a man at all.
sentences.zh: 「我还不确定，」图图说，「那到底是不是个男人。

sentences.text: Maybe it’s a woman.
sentences.zh: 也许是个女人。

sentences.text: Lift me up and let me listen at the key-hole and I’ll soon tell you.”
sentences.zh: 把我举起来，让我贴着钥匙孔听一听，我马上就能告诉你。」

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor lifted the owl up and held him close to the lock of the door.

sentences.text: So the Doctor lifted the owl up and held him close to the lock of the door.
sentences.zh: 于是医生把猫头鹰举起来，凑近门上的锁。

introduction.zh: 图图忽然说门里有人。医生什么也没听见，觉得他一定弄错了。图图说，几乎一切都会发出声音，只要耳朵够灵。可门里那个人到底在做什么？
introduction.en: Too-Too says there is someone behind the door. The Doctor hears nothing and thinks the owl must be wrong. Too-Too says almost everything makes a noise, if your ears are sharp enough. So what is that person doing in there?

quiz.question: What does Too-Too say he can hear through the door?
options: Someone putting a hand in his pocket
Someone walking up and down
A bat moving in the dark

feedback.zh: 图图说他听见有人把手伸进口袋的声音，医生却觉得那种动作根本不会出声。
feedback.en: Too-Too hears someone putting his hand in his pocket, though the Doctor thinks that makes hardly any sound.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor think of Too-Too’s claim at first?
options: That a thief is hiding inside
That the door should be opened
That Too-Too must be mistaken

feedback.zh: 医生开口就说「你一定弄错了」，还说自己什么也没听见。
feedback.en: The Doctor says “You must be mistaken” and tells the owl that he hears nothing.

grammar.excerpt: if your ears are only sharp enough to catch it

focus.zh: if 从句提出条件「只要你的耳朵够灵」；主句说几乎一切都会发出声音，only 在这里是「只要」。
focus.en: The if-clause gives the condition — if your ears are sharp enough; only here means as long as.

paragraphs.text: After a moment Too-Too said,

sentences.text: After a moment Too-Too said,
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，图图说：

paragraphs.text: “Now he’s rubbing his face with his left hand. It is a small hand and a small face. It might be a woman—No. Now he pushes his hair back off his forehead—It’s a man all right.”

sentences.text: “Now he’s rubbing his face with his left hand.
sentences.zh: 「现在他在用左手抹脸。

sentences.text: It is a small hand and a small face.
sentences.zh: 那是一只小手，一张小脸。

sentences.text: It might be a woman—No.
sentences.zh: 也许是个女人——不对。

sentences.text: Now he pushes his hair back off his forehead—It’s a man all right.”
sentences.zh: 现在他把头发从额头上往后推——是个男人，没错。」

hints.zh: all right 在这里是「确实、没错」：It’s a man all right 就是「是个男人，错不了」。
hints.en: All right here means certainly: it’s a man all right = it is definitely a man.

paragraphs.text: “Women sometimes do that,” said the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Women sometimes do that,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「女人有时也这样，」医生说。

paragraphs.text: “True,” said the owl. “But when they do, their long hair makes quite a different sound.... Sh! Make that fidgety pig keep still. Now all hold your breath a moment so I can listen well. This is very difficult, what I’m doing now—and the pesky door is so thick! Sh! Everybody quite still—shut your eyes and don’t breathe.”

sentences.text: “True,” said the owl.
sentences.zh: 「不错，」猫头鹰说。

sentences.text: “But when they do, their long hair makes quite a different sound....
sentences.zh: 「可她们这样做的时候，长头发发出的声音完全不一样……

sentences.text: Sh!
sentences.zh: 嘘！

sentences.text: Make that fidgety pig keep still.
sentences.zh: 让那头坐不住的小猪别动。

sentences.text: Now all hold your breath a moment so I can listen well.
sentences.zh: 现在大家都屏住呼吸，让我好好听一听。

sentences.text: This is very difficult, what I’m doing now—and the pesky door is so thick!
sentences.zh: 我现在做的这事非常难——这扇该死的门又这么厚！

sentences.text: Sh!
sentences.zh: 嘘！

sentences.text: Everybody quite still—shut your eyes and don’t breathe.”
sentences.zh: 大家都不许动——闭上眼睛，别喘气。」

hints.zh: 屏住呼吸，暂时不喘气，好让耳朵听得更清楚。
hints.en: To hold your breath is to stop breathing for a moment.

paragraphs.text: Too-Too leaned down and listened again very hard and long.

sentences.text: Too-Too leaned down and listened again very hard and long.
sentences.zh: 图图低下头，又非常用力地听了很久。

paragraphs.text: At last he looked up into the Doctor’s face and said,

sentences.text: At last he looked up into the Doctor’s face and said,
sentences.zh: 最后他抬起头，望着医生的脸说：

paragraphs.text: “The man in there is unhappy. He weeps. He has taken care not to blubber or sniffle, lest we should find out that he is crying. But I heard—quite distinctly—the sound of a tear falling on his sleeve.”

sentences.text: “The man in there is unhappy.
sentences.zh: 「里面那个人很难过。

sentences.text: He weeps.
sentences.zh: 他在哭。

sentences.text: He has taken care not to blubber or sniffle, lest we should find out that he is crying.
sentences.zh: 他特意不让自己放声大哭或抽鼻子，免得我们发觉他在哭。

sentences.text: But I heard—quite distinctly—the sound of a tear falling on his sleeve.”
sentences.zh: 可我听见了——清清楚楚地——一滴眼泪落在他袖子上的声音。」

hints.zh: blubber 是放声大哭，sniffle 是抽鼻子；他忍着不弄出这两种声音。
hints.en: To blubber is to cry noisily, to sniffle is to sniff; he keeps from making those sounds.

hints.zh: 较旧的书面说法，「免得、以免」，后面常跟 should + 动词原形。
hints.en: Lest is an old, formal word for so that … not; it often takes should.

paragraphs.text: “How do you know it wasn’t a drop of water falling off the ceiling on him?” asked Gub-Gub.

sentences.text: “How do you know it wasn’t a drop of water falling off the ceiling on him?” asked Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「你怎么知道那不是从天花板上滴到他身上的一滴水呢？」咕咕问。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生养的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s little pig.

paragraphs.text: “Pshaw!—Such ignorance!” sniffed Too-Too. “A drop of water falling off the ceiling would have made ten times as much noise!”

sentences.text: “Pshaw!—Such ignorance!” sniffed Too-Too.
sentences.zh: 「呸！——真没见识！」图图哼了一声。

sentences.text: “A drop of water falling off the ceiling would have made ten times as much noise!”
sentences.zh: 「从天花板上滴下来的一滴水，发出的响声会比这大十倍！」

hints.zh: sniff 在这里是「哼着鼻子说」，表示轻蔑，不是「闻」。
hints.en: Sniffed here means said with a scornful sniff, not smelled.

paragraphs.text: “Well,” said the Doctor, “if the poor fellow’s unhappy, we’ve got to get in and see what’s the matter with him. Find me an axe, and I’ll chop the door down.”

sentences.text: “Well,” said the Doctor, “if the poor fellow’s unhappy, we’ve got to get in and see what’s the matter with him.
sentences.zh: 「好吧，」医生说，「如果这可怜的人这么难过，我们总得进去看看他出了什么事。

sentences.text: Find me an axe, and I’ll chop the door down.”
sentences.zh: 给我找把斧头来，我把门劈开。」

introduction.zh: 图图把耳朵贴在钥匙孔上，一点一点说出门里那个人在做什么：抬起手、抹一把脸、把头发往后推。咕咕觉得这些说法靠不住，图图听了很不高兴。这些细小的声音，真能说明门里出了什么事吗？
introduction.en: With his ear to the keyhole, Too-Too describes what the person inside does: a hand lifted, a face rubbed, hair pushed back. Gub-Gub thinks it is all guesswork, and the owl is not pleased. Can such tiny sounds really show what is happening in there?

quiz.question: How does Too-Too decide that the person inside is a man?
options: By the way the door handle turns
By the sound the hair makes when it is pushed back
By the size of the shoes on the floor

feedback.zh: 图图先猜是女人，接着听见他把头发往后推的声音，就断定是个男人。
feedback.en: Too-Too thinks it might be a woman, then hears the hair pushed back and says it is a man all right.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor want to break the door down?
options: Because the person inside is unhappy
Because the key has been lost
Because the door is too old

feedback.zh: 医生说，既然这位可怜的人这么难过，他们就得进去看看他出了什么事。
feedback.en: The Doctor says that if the poor fellow is unhappy, they must get in and see what is the matter with him.

grammar.excerpt: Make that fidgety pig keep still

focus.zh: make + 宾语 + 动词原形：让那头小猪「保持不动」；keep still 就是「别动」。
focus.en: Make takes an object and the base verb: make that pig keep still = get the pig to stop moving.

paragraphs.text: Right away an axe was found. And the Doctor soon chopped a hole in the door big enough to clamber through.

sentences.text: Right away an axe was found.
sentences.zh: 马上就找到了一把斧头。

sentences.text: And the Doctor soon chopped a hole in the door big enough to clamber through.
sentences.zh: 医生很快在门上砍出一个洞，大得足够人钻进去。

paragraphs.text: At first he could see nothing at all, it was so dark inside. So he struck a match.

sentences.text: At first he could see nothing at all, it was so dark inside.
sentences.zh: 起初他什么也看不见，里面太黑了。

sentences.text: So he struck a match.
sentences.zh: 于是他划着了一根火柴。

paragraphs.text: The room was quite small; no window; the ceiling, low. For furniture there was only one little stool. All round the room big barrels stood against the walls, fastened at the bottom so they wouldn’t tumble with the rolling of the ship; and above the barrels, pewter jugs of all sizes hung from wooden pegs. There was a strong, winey smell. And in the middle of the floor sat a little boy, about eight years old, crying bitterly.

sentences.text: The room was quite small; no window; the ceiling, low.
sentences.zh: 房间很小；没有窗户；天花板很低。

sentences.text: For furniture there was only one little stool.
sentences.zh: 家具只有一张小凳子。

sentences.text: All round the room big barrels stood against the walls, fastened at the bottom so they wouldn’t tumble with the rolling of the ship; and above the barrels, pewter jugs of all sizes hung from wooden pegs.
sentences.zh: 房间四周靠墙立着大木桶，桶底都固定住，免得船身一摇晃就倒下来；木桶上方，木钉上挂着大大小小的锡壶。

sentences.text: There was a strong, winey smell.
sentences.zh: 空气里有一股很浓的酒味。

sentences.text: And in the middle of the floor sat a little boy, about eight years old, crying bitterly.
sentences.zh: 地板正中坐着一个约莫八岁的小男孩，哭得很伤心。

paragraphs.text: “I declare, it is the pirates’ rum-room!” said Jip in a whisper.

sentences.text: “I declare, it is the pirates’ rum-room!” said Jip in a whisper.
sentences.zh: 「我说，这是海盗的朗姆酒舱！」吉普压低声音说。

hints.zh: 朗姆酒舱，船上存放朗姆酒的储藏室。
hints.en: The rum-room: the store-room on a ship where the rum is kept.

hints.zh: 感叹语，「我说」「真是的」，用来表示惊讶。
hints.en: An old exclamation of surprise: “Well, I must say!”

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

paragraphs.text: “Yes. Very rum!” said Gub-Gub. “The smell makes me giddy.”

sentences.text: “Yes.
sentences.zh: 「是啊。

sentences.text: Very rum!” said Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 真够『朗姆』的！」咕咕说。

sentences.text: “The smell makes me giddy.”
sentences.zh: 「这味儿熏得我头晕。」

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s pig.

hints.zh: 咕咕没听懂：rum 既是「朗姆酒」，也是英国旧口语里的「古怪」，他顺着酒味说「太朗姆了」。
hints.en: Gub-Gub misses the joke: rum is the drink, but in old slang it also means “odd”, so he says “very rum”.

paragraphs.text: The little boy seemed rather frightened to find a man standing there before him and all those animals staring in through the hole in the broken door. But as soon as he saw John Dolittle’s face by the light of the match, he stopped crying and got up.

sentences.text: The little boy seemed rather frightened to find a man standing there before him and all those animals staring in through the hole in the broken door.
sentences.zh: 小男孩发现面前站着一个男人，还有那么多动物从破门洞里朝里看，显得相当害怕。

sentences.text: But as soon as he saw John Dolittle’s face by the light of the match, he stopped crying and got up.
sentences.zh: 可火柴的光一照见约翰·杜立德的脸，他立刻不哭了，站起身来。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，医生的全名。
hints.en: John Dolittle: the Doctor’s full name.

introduction.zh: 门板被斧头劈开一个洞，医生钻进去，屋里却没有窗，只有贴着墙的大木桶、挂着的锡壶和一股酒味。他划亮一根火柴，往地上一照——这间锁着的小屋里，好像不只有木桶。
introduction.en: An axe is found, and the Doctor cuts a hole in a locked door. Inside there is no window, only barrels, pewter jugs and a smell of wine. He strikes a match and looks down at the floor. What is waiting in the dark little room?

quiz.question: What does Jip think the little room is?
options: The ship’s kitchen
A store-room for sails
The pirates’ rum-room

feedback.zh: 吉普一闻那酒味就说：「这是海盗的朗姆酒舱！」咕咕还跟着用 rum 这个词开玩笑。
feedback.en: Jip smells the wine and whispers that it is the pirates’ rum-room; Gub-Gub then makes a joke on the word rum.

quiz.question: What is the little boy doing when the Doctor first sees him?
options: Hiding behind the barrels
Sitting on the floor and crying
Sleeping on the little stool

feedback.zh: 火柴一亮，只见地板正中坐着一个八岁上下的男孩，哭得很伤心；凳子空着，桶边也没人躲着。
feedback.en: By the light of the match the Doctor sees a boy of about eight sitting in the middle of the floor, crying bitterly.

grammar.excerpt: For furniture there was only one little stool

focus.zh: For furniture 提到句首，先说「家具」这一项；真正的结构是 there was + 单数名词。
focus.en: For furniture is pulled to the front to name the topic; the real pattern is there was + a singular noun.

paragraphs.text: “You aren’t one of the pirates, are you?” he asked.

sentences.text: “You aren’t one of the pirates, are you?” he asked.
sentences.zh: 「你不是海盗吧？」他问。

paragraphs.text: And when the Doctor threw back his head and laughed long and loud, the little boy smiled too and came and took his hand.

sentences.text: And when the Doctor threw back his head and laughed long and loud, the little boy smiled too and came and took his hand.
sentences.zh: 医生仰起头，放声大笑；小男孩也笑了，走过来拉住他的手。

paragraphs.text: “You laugh like a friend,” he said—“not like a pirate. Could you tell me where my uncle is?”

sentences.text: “You laugh like a friend,” he said—“not like a pirate.
sentences.zh: 「你笑起来像个朋友，」他说，「不像海盗。

sentences.text: Could you tell me where my uncle is?”
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我我舅舅在哪儿吗？」

paragraphs.text: “I am afraid I can’t,” said the Doctor. “When did you see him last?”

sentences.text: “I am afraid I can’t,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「恐怕不行，」医生说。

sentences.text: “When did you see him last?”
sentences.zh: 「你最后一次见到他是什么时候？」

paragraphs.text: “It was the day before yesterday,” said the boy. “I and my uncle were out fishing in our little boat, when the pirates came and caught us. They sunk our fishing-boat and brought us both on to this ship. They told my uncle that they wanted him to be a pirate like them—for he was clever at sailing a ship in all weathers. But he said he didn’t want to be a pirate, because killing people and stealing was no work for a good fisherman to do. Then the leader, Ben Ali, got very angry and gnashed his teeth, and said they would throw my uncle into the sea if he didn’t do as they said. They sent me downstairs; and I heard the noise of a fight going on above. And when they let me come up again next day, my uncle was nowhere to be seen. I asked the pirates where he was; but they wouldn’t tell me. I am very much afraid they threw him into the sea and drowned him.”

sentences.text: “It was the day before yesterday,” said the boy.
sentences.zh: 「是前天，」男孩说。

sentences.text: “I and my uncle were out fishing in our little boat, when the pirates came and caught us.
sentences.zh: 「我和舅舅坐我们的小船出海打鱼，海盗来了，把我们抓住了。

sentences.text: They sunk our fishing-boat and brought us both on to this ship.
sentences.zh: 他们弄沉了我们的渔船，把我们两个都带到了这条船上。

sentences.text: They told my uncle that they wanted him to be a pirate like them—for he was clever at sailing a ship in all weathers.
sentences.zh: 他们说想让我舅舅跟他们一样当海盗——因为他在什么天气里都能把船驶得很好。

sentences.text: But he said he didn’t want to be a pirate, because killing people and stealing was no work for a good fisherman to do.
sentences.zh: 可他说他不想当海盗，因为杀人抢东西不是好渔夫干的活儿。

sentences.text: Then the leader, Ben Ali, got very angry and gnashed his teeth, and said they would throw my uncle into the sea if he didn’t do as they said.
sentences.zh: 于是头子本·阿里非常恼火，牙齿咬得咯咯响，说要是舅舅不照他们说的做，就把他扔进海里。

sentences.text: They sent me downstairs; and I heard the noise of a fight going on above.
sentences.zh: 他们把我打发到下面去；我听见上面有打斗的声音。

sentences.text: And when they let me come up again next day, my uncle was nowhere to be seen.
sentences.zh: 第二天他们让我上来时，舅舅却哪儿都看不见了。

sentences.text: I asked the pirates where he was; but they wouldn’t tell me.
sentences.zh: 我问海盗他在哪儿，可他们不肯告诉我。

sentences.text: I am very much afraid they threw him into the sea and drowned him.”
sentences.zh: 我很怕他们把他扔进海里，淹死了。」

hints.zh: sink 的过去式，这里是口语说法：弄沉、使船下沉。
hints.en: A colloquial past form of sink: they sank our boat.

hints.zh: 在各种天气里，不管风浪好坏。
hints.en: In all weathers: in every kind of weather, good or bad.

hints.zh: 本·阿里，这伙海盗的头子。
hints.en: Ben Ali, the leader of the pirates.

hints.zh: 咬牙切齿，气得直磨牙。
hints.en: Gnashed his teeth: he ground his teeth in anger.

hints.zh: 哪儿都看不见，人影也没有。
hints.en: Nowhere to be seen: he could not be found anywhere.

introduction.zh: 男孩先问一句：你不是海盗吧？然后说起前天的事——他和舅舅在海上打鱼，被海盗抓上了这条船。海盗要舅舅入伙，舅舅死活不肯。可第二天，男孩在船上再也找不到他了。
introduction.en: The boy asks the Doctor a nervous question: is he one of the pirates? Then he tells what happened two days ago. He and his uncle were fishing when the pirates caught them. They wanted the uncle to join them, and he said no. Next morning the uncle was gone.

quiz.question: Why does Ben Ali get angry with the boy’s uncle?
options: The uncle refuses to be a pirate
The uncle cannot sail in bad weather
The uncle has taken the pirates’ boat

feedback.zh: 舅舅说杀人抢东西不是好渔夫干的活儿，不肯入伙，本·阿里才发火，威胁把他扔下海。
feedback.en: The uncle had just said that killing and stealing was no work for a good fisherman, so Ben Ali lost his temper.

quiz.question: What does the boy fear has happened to his uncle?
options: He is locked in another room
He has sailed home without him
The pirates threw him into the sea

feedback.zh: 男孩最后说，他很怕海盗把舅舅扔进海里淹死了——这只是他的猜测，他并没有亲眼看见。
feedback.en: The boy ends by saying he is very much afraid they threw his uncle into the sea and drowned him.

grammar.excerpt: You aren’t one of the pirates, are you?

focus.zh: 前句是否定的 aren’t，后面就换成肯定的 are you；男孩用来说出自己的猜测，等医生点头。
focus.en: The statement is negative (aren’t), so the tag turns positive (are you): the boy is guessing and wants to be told he is right.

paragraphs.text: And the little boy began to cry again.

sentences.text: And the little boy began to cry again.
sentences.zh: 小男孩又哭了起来。

paragraphs.text: “Well now—wait a minute,” said the Doctor. “Don’t cry. Let’s go and have tea in the dining-room, and we’ll talk it over. Maybe your uncle is quite safe all the time. You don’t know that he was drowned, do you? And that’s something. Perhaps we can find him for you. First we’ll go and have tea—with strawberry-jam; and then we will see what can be done.”

sentences.text: “Well now—wait a minute,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「好了——等一等，」医生说。

sentences.text: “Don’t cry.
sentences.zh: 「别哭。

sentences.text: Let’s go and have tea in the dining-room, and we’ll talk it over.
sentences.zh: 我们去餐厅喝茶，一边喝一边商量。

sentences.text: Maybe your uncle is quite safe all the time.
sentences.zh: 也许你舅舅一直好好的呢。

sentences.text: You don’t know that he was drowned, do you?
sentences.zh: 你并不知道他淹死了，对吧？

sentences.text: And that’s something.
sentences.zh: 这总算是一点安慰。

sentences.text: Perhaps we can find him for you.
sentences.zh: 说不定我们能替你找到他。

sentences.text: First we’ll go and have tea—with strawberry-jam; and then we will see what can be done.”
sentences.zh: 我们先去喝茶——有草莓酱；然后再看能做些什么。」

hints.zh: 把事情谈一谈、商量清楚。
hints.en: Talk it over: to discuss it until things are clear.

paragraphs.text: All the animals had been standing around listening with great curiosity. And when they had gone into the ship’s dining-room and were having tea, Dab-Dab came up behind the Doctor’s chair and whispered.

sentences.text: All the animals had been standing around listening with great curiosity.
sentences.zh: 动物们一直围在旁边，非常好奇地听着。

sentences.text: And when they had gone into the ship’s dining-room and were having tea, Dab-Dab came up behind the Doctor’s chair and whispered.
sentences.zh: 他们进了船上的餐厅，正喝着茶，达布达布走到医生椅子后面，小声说起话来。

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

paragraphs.text: “Ask the porpoises if the boy’s uncle was drowned—they’ll know.”

sentences.text: “Ask the porpoises if the boy’s uncle was drowned—they’ll know.”
sentences.zh: 「去问问海豚，那男孩的舅舅是不是淹死了——它们准知道。」

hints.zh: 海豚（鼠海豚），一种小型的鲸类，常成群在船边游。
hints.en: Porpoises: small sea animals like dolphins, often swimming in groups.

paragraphs.text: “All right,” said the Doctor, taking a second piece of bread-and-jam.

sentences.text: “All right,” said the Doctor, taking a second piece of bread-and-jam.
sentences.zh: 「好哇，」医生说着，又拿起一块果酱面包。

paragraphs.text: “What are those funny, clicking noises you are making with your tongue?” asked the boy.

sentences.text: “What are those funny, clicking noises you are making with your tongue?” asked the boy.
sentences.zh: 「你舌头弄出的那种咔嗒咔嗒的怪声音是什么？」男孩问。

paragraphs.text: “Oh, I just said a couple of words in duck-language,” the Doctor answered. “This is Dab-Dab, one of my pets.”

sentences.text: “Oh, I just said a couple of words in duck-language,” the Doctor answered.
sentences.zh: 「哦，我只是用鸭子话说了两句，」医生回答。

sentences.text: “This is Dab-Dab, one of my pets.”
sentences.zh: 「这是达布达布，我的宠物之一。」

paragraphs.text: “I didn’t even know that ducks had a language,” said the boy. “Are all these other animals your pets, too? What is that strange-looking thing with two heads?”

sentences.text: “I didn’t even know that ducks had a language,” said the boy.
sentences.zh: 「我连鸭子有语言都不知道，」男孩说。

sentences.text: “Are all these other animals your pets, too?
sentences.zh: 「这些别的动物也都是你的宠物吗？

sentences.text: What is that strange-looking thing with two heads?”
sentences.zh: 那个两个脑袋的怪东西是什么？」

paragraphs.text: “Sh!” the Doctor whispered. “That is the pushmi-pullyu. Don’t let him see we’re talking about him—he gets so dreadfully embarrassed.... Tell me, how did you come to be locked up in that little room?”

sentences.text: “Sh!” the Doctor whispered.
sentences.zh: 「嘘！」医生小声说。

sentences.text: “That is the pushmi-pullyu.
sentences.zh: 「那是『推我拉你』。

sentences.text: Don’t let him see we’re talking about him—he gets so dreadfully embarrassed....
sentences.zh: 别让他看见我们在说他——他会羞得不得了的……

sentences.text: Tell me, how did you come to be locked up in that little room?”
sentences.zh: 告诉我，你怎么会被关在那间小屋子里的？」

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，那只两个脑袋的动物，医生从非洲带回来的。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu, the two-headed animal the Doctor brought from Africa.

hints.zh: come to be 是「怎么会落到……的地步」；这里在问男孩怎么被关进去的。
hints.en: Come to be means “happen to end up”: the Doctor asks how the boy ended up locked up.

introduction.zh: 男孩又哭了。医生没有追问，先带他去餐厅喝茶，桌上还有草莓酱。动物们围在一边听着，鸭子凑到医生椅背后，小声出了一个主意——这主意跟海里的动物有关。它真能问出答案吗？
introduction.en: The boy starts crying again. The Doctor does not push him; he takes him to the dining-room for tea. All the animals stand around and listen. Then Dab-Dab leans behind the Doctor’s chair and whispers a strange idea about the animals of the sea. Could it work?

quiz.question: What does the Doctor want them to do before they talk about the uncle?
options: Sail back to the boy’s village
Go and have tea in the dining-room
Search all the pirates’ rooms

feedback.zh: 医生先让孩子离开那间小屋：「我们去餐厅喝茶，一边喝一边商量。」还说有草莓酱。
feedback.en: The Doctor first says, “Let’s go and have tea in the dining-room, and we’ll talk it over.”

quiz.question: What does Dab-Dab whisper to the Doctor?
options: Ask the porpoises whether the uncle was drowned
Ask the boy to describe his uncle
Tell the boy that his uncle is safe

feedback.zh: 达布达布凑到椅背后说：去问海豚，它们准知道那男孩的舅舅有没有淹死。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab whispers that he should ask the porpoises: they will know whether the boy’s uncle was drowned.

grammar.excerpt: Let’s go and have tea in the dining-room

focus.zh: Let’s 把医生自己也算进去，等于「我们去吧」；go and have 两个动词直接相连，中间不用 to。
focus.en: Let’s includes the Doctor himself; go and have joins two verbs with and, not with to.

paragraphs.text: “The pirates shut me in there when they were going off to steal things from another ship. When I heard some one chopping on the door, I didn’t know who it could be. I was very glad to find it was you. Do you think you will be able to find my uncle for me?”

sentences.text: “The pirates shut me in there when they were going off to steal things from another ship.
sentences.zh: 「海盗要去抢另一条船上的东西，就把我关在那儿了。

sentences.text: When I heard some one chopping on the door, I didn’t know who it could be.
sentences.zh: 我听见有人砍门，不知道会是谁。

sentences.text: I was very glad to find it was you.
sentences.zh: 发现是你，我高兴极了。

sentences.text: Do you think you will be able to find my uncle for me?”
sentences.zh: 你觉得你能帮我找到舅舅吗？」

paragraphs.text: “Well, we are going to try very hard,” said the Doctor. “Now what was your uncle like to look at?”

sentences.text: “Well, we are going to try very hard,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「我们会拼命去试的，」医生说。

sentences.text: “Now what was your uncle like to look at?”
sentences.zh: 「那你舅舅长什么样？」

paragraphs.text: “He had red hair,” the boy answered—“very red hair, and the picture of an anchor tattooed on his arm. He was a strong man, a kind uncle and the best sailor in the South Atlantic. His fishing-boat was called The Saucy Sally—a cutter-rigged sloop.”

sentences.text: “He had red hair,” the boy answered—“very red hair, and the picture of an anchor tattooed on his arm.
sentences.zh: 「他有一头红头发，」男孩回答，「很红的头发，胳膊上还刺着一个锚。

sentences.text: He was a strong man, a kind uncle and the best sailor in the South Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 他力气大，是个好舅舅，也是南大西洋上最好的水手。

sentences.text: His fishing-boat was called The Saucy Sally—a cutter-rigged sloop.”
sentences.zh: 他的渔船叫『俏莎莉号』——一条单桅纵帆船。」

hints.zh: 南大西洋。
hints.en: The South Atlantic: the southern part of the Atlantic Ocean.

hints.zh: 「俏莎莉号」，舅舅那条渔船的名字。
hints.en: The Saucy Sally: the name of the uncle’s fishing-boat.

hints.zh: 帆船术语：cutter 是一种单桅纵帆的帆装，sloop 指单桅帆船。
hints.en: Sailing terms: a cutter-rigged sloop is a small boat with one mast and a particular sail plan.

paragraphs.text: “What’s ‘cutterigsloop’?” whispered Gub-Gub, turning to Jip.

sentences.text: “What’s ‘cutterigsloop’?” whispered Gub-Gub, turning to Jip.
sentences.zh: 「什么叫『卡特里格斯洛普』？」咕咕转向吉普，小声问。

hints.zh: 咕咕把 cutter-rigged sloop 听成了一个词，所以完全听不懂。
hints.en: Gub-Gub has run the two words together into one, so he cannot make any sense of it.

paragraphs.text: “Sh!—That’s the kind of a ship the man had,” said Jip. “Keep still, can’t you?”

sentences.text: “Sh!—That’s the kind of a ship the man had,” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「嘘！——那是说那人的船是什么样子的，」吉普说。

sentences.text: “Keep still, can’t you?”
sentences.zh: 「别出声，行不行？」

paragraphs.text: “Oh,” said the pig, “is that all? I thought it was something to drink.”

sentences.text: “Oh,” said the pig, “is that all?
sentences.zh: 「哦，」小猪说，「就这个？

sentences.text: I thought it was something to drink.”
sentences.zh: 我还以为是能喝的东西呢。」

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor left the boy to play with the animals in the dining-room, and went upstairs to look for passing porpoises.

sentences.text: So the Doctor left the boy to play with the animals in the dining-room, and went upstairs to look for passing porpoises.
sentences.zh: 于是医生让男孩留在餐厅跟动物们玩，自己上楼去找路过的海豚。

paragraphs.text: And soon a whole school came dancing and jumping through the water, on their way to Brazil.

sentences.text: And soon a whole school came dancing and jumping through the water, on their way to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，一大群海豚一路跳着、舞着穿过水面游来，正往巴西去。

hints.zh: school 这里不是「学校」，而是一大群鱼或海兽。
hints.en: School here is not a school building: it means a large group of sea animals.

hints.zh: 巴西，南美洲国家。
hints.en: Brazil, the country in South America.

paragraphs.text: When they saw the Doctor leaning on the rail of his ship, they came over to see how he was getting on.

sentences.text: When they saw the Doctor leaning on the rail of his ship, they came over to see how he was getting on.
sentences.zh: 它们看见医生靠在船栏杆上，就游过来看看他过得怎么样。

introduction.zh: 男孩说出舅舅的样子：一头很红的头发，胳膊上刺着一个锚，是南大西洋上最好的水手。医生记下了这些，也问清了船名。凭这几个记号，真能从茫茫大海上把一个人找出来吗？
introduction.en: The boy describes his uncle: very red hair, an anchor tattooed on his arm, the best sailor in the South Atlantic. The Doctor asks for the name of the boat too. Can a few marks like that really find one man on the sea?

quiz.question: Why did the pirates shut the boy in the little room?
options: He had tried to run away from them
They wanted him to work in the rum-room
They were going off to rob another ship

feedback.zh: 男孩说，海盗要去抢另一条船上的东西，走之前把他锁在了那间小屋里。
feedback.en: The boy explains that the pirates shut him in there when they were going off to steal things from another ship.

quiz.question: Which two things will help the Doctor know the uncle?
options: A wooden leg and a red coat
Red hair and an anchor tattooed on his arm
A white beard and a tall hat

feedback.zh: 男孩说舅舅有一头很红的头发，胳膊上还刺着一个锚——这两样最好认，也最难认错。
feedback.en: The boy says his uncle had very red hair and a picture of an anchor tattooed on his arm — the very marks the Doctor later describes.

grammar.excerpt: the best sailor in the South Atlantic

focus.zh: best 是 good 的不规则最高级；in the South Atlantic 划出范围：整个南大西洋上没有比他更好的水手。
focus.en: Best is the irregular superlative of good; in the South Atlantic marks the group he is the best of.

paragraphs.text: And the Doctor asked them if they had seen anything of a man with red hair and an anchor tattooed on his arm.

sentences.text: And the Doctor asked them if they had seen anything of a man with red hair and an anchor tattooed on his arm.
sentences.zh: 医生问它们有没有见过一个红头发、胳膊上刺着锚的男人。

paragraphs.text: “Do you mean the master of The Saucy Sally?” asked the porpoises.

sentences.text: “Do you mean the master of The Saucy Sally?” asked the porpoises.
sentences.zh: 「你说的是『俏莎莉号』的船主吗？」海豚们问。

hints.zh: 船主、船长；不是「主人」的意思。
hints.en: Master here means the owner or captain of the boat, not a servant’s master.

paragraphs.text: “Yes,” said the Doctor. “That’s the man. Has he been drowned?”

sentences.text: “Yes,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「对，」医生说。

sentences.text: “That’s the man.
sentences.zh: 「就是他。

sentences.text: Has he been drowned?”
sentences.zh: 他是不是淹死了？」

paragraphs.text: “His fishing-sloop was sunk,” said the porpoises—“for we saw it lying on the bottom of the sea. But there was nobody inside it, because we went and looked.”

sentences.text: “His fishing-sloop was sunk,” said the porpoises—“for we saw it lying on the bottom of the sea.
sentences.zh: 「他的渔船沉了，」海豚们说，「因为我们看见它躺在海底。

sentences.text: But there was nobody inside it, because we went and looked.”
sentences.zh: 可里面没有人，我们特意进去看过了。」

paragraphs.text: “His little nephew is on the ship with me here,” said the Doctor. “And he is terribly afraid that the pirates threw his uncle into the sea. Would you be so good as to find out for me, for sure, whether he has been drowned or not?”

sentences.text: “His little nephew is on the ship with me here,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「他的小外甥就在我这条船上，」医生说。

sentences.text: “And he is terribly afraid that the pirates threw his uncle into the sea.
sentences.zh: 「他非常害怕，怕海盗把他舅舅扔进了海里。

sentences.text: Would you be so good as to find out for me, for sure, whether he has been drowned or not?”
sentences.zh: 能不能请你们帮我查清楚，他到底有没有淹死？」

hints.zh: 外甥；这里指船上那个男孩，舅舅就是沉船的主人。
hints.en: Nephew: the boy on the ship, whose uncle owned the sunken boat.

hints.target: Would you be so good as to
hints.zh: 很客气的请求：「能不能劳驾你们……」
hints.en: A very polite request: “would you kindly …”

hints.zh: 确切地、肯定地。
hints.en: For sure: certainly, without any doubt.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, he isn’t drowned,” said the porpoises. “If he were, we would be sure to have heard of it from the deep-sea Decapods. We hear all the salt-water news. The shell-fish call us ‘The Ocean Gossips.’ No—tell the little boy we are sorry we do not know where his uncle is; but we are quite certain he hasn’t been drowned in the sea.”

sentences.text: “Oh, he isn’t drowned,” said the porpoises.
sentences.zh: 「哦，他没淹死，」海豚们说。

sentences.text: “If he were, we would be sure to have heard of it from the deep-sea Decapods.
sentences.zh: 「要是他淹死了，深海的甲壳类一定会告诉我们。

sentences.text: We hear all the salt-water news.
sentences.zh: 海上的消息，我们全都听得到。

sentences.text: The shell-fish call us ‘The Ocean Gossips.’
sentences.zh: 贝类管我们叫『海洋闲话家』。

sentences.text: No—tell the little boy we are sorry we do not know where his uncle is; but we are quite certain he hasn’t been drowned in the sea.”
sentences.zh: 不——告诉那小男孩，我们很遗憾不知道他舅舅在哪儿；但我们非常确定，他没有在海里淹死。」

hints.zh: 十足类动物（虾、蟹等甲壳类）；原文大写，像是海底消息最灵通的一群。
hints.en: Decapods: ten-legged sea creatures such as crabs and shrimps, here treated as a group that knows the sea’s news.

hints.zh: 「海洋闲话家」，贝类给海豚起的绰号，说它们爱传消息。
hints.en: “The Ocean Gossips”: the nickname the shell-fish give the porpoises, who carry all the news.

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor ran downstairs with the news and told the nephew, who clapped his hands with happiness. And the pushmi-pullyu took the little boy on his back and gave him a ride round the dining-room table; while all the other animals followed behind, beating the dish-covers with spoons, pretending it was a parade.

sentences.text: So the Doctor ran downstairs with the news and told the nephew, who clapped his hands with happiness.
sentences.zh: 于是医生带着这个消息跑下楼，告诉了那个小外甥；孩子高兴得拍起手来。

sentences.text: And the pushmi-pullyu took the little boy on his back and gave him a ride round the dining-room table; while all the other animals followed behind, beating the dish-covers with spoons, pretending it was a parade.
sentences.zh: 『推我拉你』把男孩驮在背上，绕着餐厅的桌子跑了一圈；其他动物都跟在后面，用勺子敲着菜盘盖子，装成一支游行队伍。

introduction.zh: 医生把红头发和胳膊上的锚说给海豚听。它们说，那条船确实沉在海底，可它们还讲了别的——关于海底的甲壳类，关于海上的闲话是怎么传开的。它们究竟知不知道那个人的下落？
introduction.en: The Doctor describes the red hair and the anchor on the arm. The porpoises know the boat at once: they have seen it lying on the bottom of the sea. They also claim to hear everything that happens in the water. Is the man dead or alive?

quiz.question: What did the porpoises find inside the sunken fishing-boat?
options: Nobody at all
The uncle, fast asleep
A big catch of fish

feedback.zh: 海豚说它们看见船躺在海底，还特意进去看过：里面一个人也没有。
feedback.en: The porpoises saw the sloop on the bottom of the sea and went inside to look: there was nobody there.

quiz.question: Why do the shell-fish call the porpoises “The Ocean Gossips”?
options: Because they never stop talking to ships
Because they swim from ocean to ocean
Because they hear and carry all the news of the sea

feedback.zh: 海豚说自己听得到海上所有的消息，所以贝类管它们叫「海洋闲话家」。
feedback.en: The porpoises say, “We hear all the salt-water news,” which is why the shell-fish call them The Ocean Gossips.

grammar.excerpt: If he were, we would be sure to have heard of it

focus.zh: If he were 是与眼下事实相反的假设——他并没有淹死；所以主句用 would，不用 will。
focus.en: If he were imagines something untrue now — he is not drowned — so the main clause takes would, not will.

paragraphs.text: “YOUR uncle must now be found,” said the Doctor—“that is the next thing—now that we know he wasn’t thrown into the sea.”

sentences.text: “YOUR uncle must now be found,” said the Doctor—“that is the next thing—now that we know he wasn’t thrown into the sea.”
sentences.zh: 「现在非得把你叔叔找到不可，」医生说，「这是接下来要做的事——既然我们已经知道他没有被扔进海里。」

paragraphs.text: Then Dab-Dab came up to him again and whispered,

sentences.text: Then Dab-Dab came up to him again and whispered,
sentences.zh: 这时达布达布又走到他跟前，小声说：

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生养的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

paragraphs.text: “Ask the eagles to look for the man. No living creature can see better than an eagle. When they are miles high in the air they can count the ants crawling on the ground. Ask the eagles.”

sentences.text: “Ask the eagles to look for the man.
sentences.zh: 「让老鹰去找那个人吧。

sentences.text: No living creature can see better than an eagle.
sentences.zh: 没有哪种活物比老鹰的眼力更好。

sentences.text: When they are miles high in the air they can count the ants crawling on the ground.
sentences.zh: 它们飞到几英里高的空中，还能数清地上爬的蚂蚁。

sentences.text: Ask the eagles.”
sentences.zh: 去请老鹰吧。」

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor sent one of the swallows off to get some eagles.

sentences.text: So the Doctor sent one of the swallows off to get some eagles.
sentences.zh: 于是医生派了一只燕子去请老鹰。

paragraphs.text: And in about an hour the little bird came back with six different kinds of eagles: a Black Eagle, a Bald Eagle, a Fish Eagle, a Golden Eagle, an Eagle-Vulture, and a White-tailed Sea Eagle. Twice as high as the boy they were, each one of them. And they stood on the rail of the ship, like round-shouldered soldiers all in a row, stern and still and stiff; while their great, gleaming, black eyes shot darting glances here and there and everywhere.

sentences.text: And in about an hour the little bird came back with six different kinds of eagles: a Black Eagle, a Bald Eagle, a Fish Eagle, a Golden Eagle, an Eagle-Vulture, and a White-tailed Sea Eagle.
sentences.zh: 大约过了一个钟头，那只小鸟带回了六种不同的老鹰：一只黑鹰、一只白头海雕、一只鱼鹰、一只金雕、一只鹰鹫，还有一只白尾海雕。

sentences.text: Twice as high as the boy they were, each one of them.
sentences.zh: 它们每一只都有那男孩的两倍那么高。

sentences.text: And they stood on the rail of the ship, like round-shouldered soldiers all in a row, stern and still and stiff; while their great, gleaming, black eyes shot darting glances here and there and everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们站在船栏上，像一排驼背的士兵，严厉、一动不动、僵直；那一双双又大又亮、乌黑的眼睛，向这儿、那儿、四面八方投出锐利的目光。

hints.zh: 鹰鹫，一种体形很大的猛禽，常被算作老鹰的一类。
hints.en: Eagle-vulture: a large bird of prey, counted here as one kind of eagle.

paragraphs.text: Gub-Gub was scared of them and got behind a barrel. He said he felt as though those terrible eyes were looking right inside of him to see what he had stolen for lunch.

sentences.text: Gub-Gub was scared of them and got behind a barrel.
sentences.zh: 咕咕被它们吓着了，躲到一只木桶后面。

sentences.text: He said he felt as though those terrible eyes were looking right inside of him to see what he had stolen for lunch.
sentences.zh: 他说，他觉得那些可怕的眼睛好像直看到他身子里面，要瞧出他午饭偷吃了什么。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生养的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s baby pig.

paragraphs.text: And the Doctor said to the eagles,

sentences.text: And the Doctor said to the eagles,
sentences.zh: 医生对老鹰们说：

paragraphs.text: “A man has been lost—a fisherman with red hair and an anchor marked on his arm. Would you be so kind as to see if you can find him for us? This boy is the man’s nephew.”

sentences.text: “A man has been lost—a fisherman with red hair and an anchor marked on his arm.
sentences.zh: 「有一个人失踪了——一个红头发、手臂上刺着锚的渔夫。

sentences.text: Would you be so kind as to see if you can find him for us?
sentences.zh: 能不能劳烦你们帮忙找一找他？

sentences.text: This boy is the man’s nephew.”
sentences.zh: 这个男孩是他的侄子。」

hints.target: an anchor marked on his arm
hints.zh: 手臂上刺着锚的图案：旧时水手和渔夫常把锚刺在身上作记号，认出一个人就靠这个。
hints.en: An anchor tattooed on the arm: sailors and fishermen often carried this mark, so it helps to identify a man.

introduction.zh: 既然已经知道男孩的叔叔没有被扔进海里，杜立德医生就得把他找回来。达布达布凑到他耳边出了个主意：去请老鹰。这些大鸟能从几英里高的天上数清地上的蚂蚁——可一个人藏在半个世界的角落里，它们真能看见吗？
introduction.en: The boy’s uncle was not thrown into the sea — so where is he? Dab-Dab whispers a plan to the Doctor: ask the eagles. From miles up they can count ants on the ground. But can an eagle’s eye find one lost fisherman in half the world?

quiz.question: Why does Dab-Dab tell the Doctor to ask the eagles?
options: No living creature can see better than an eagle.
Eagles can talk to fishermen.
Eagles live near the sea and know the ships.

feedback.zh: 达布达布的理由是眼力：她说没有哪种活物比老鹰看得更清楚。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab’s reason is eyesight: no living creature can see better than an eagle.

quiz.question: How will the eagles know which man to look for?
options: He is a tall sailor in a blue coat.
He is the boy’s father, who has lost a ring.
He is a red-haired fisherman with an anchor marked on his arm.

feedback.zh: 医生给出两个特征：红头发，手臂上刺着锚；还说这男孩是那人的侄子。
feedback.en: The Doctor gives two marks: red hair and an anchor on his arm, and adds that the boy is the man’s nephew.

grammar.excerpt: No living creature can see better than an eagle

focus.zh: better 是 well 的不规则比较级，than an eagle 引出比较对象：没有谁比老鹰看得更清楚。
focus.en: Better is the irregular comparative of well, and than an eagle names what the eagle is compared with.

paragraphs.text: Eagles do not talk very much. And all they answered in their husky voices was,

sentences.text: Eagles do not talk very much.
sentences.zh: 老鹰不大爱说话。

sentences.text: And all they answered in their husky voices was,
sentences.zh: 它们用沙哑的嗓子只回答了这么一句：

paragraphs.text: “You may be sure that we will do our best—for John Dolittle.”

sentences.text: “You may be sure that we will do our best—for John Dolittle.”
sentences.zh: 「你可以放心，我们一定尽力——为了约翰·杜立德。」

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，就是医生本人；动物们郑重起来时常连名带姓地叫他。
hints.en: John Dolittle: the Doctor himself; the animals use his full name when they mean to be serious.

paragraphs.text: Then they flew off—and Gub-Gub came out from behind his barrel to see them go. Up and up and up they went—higher and higher and higher still. Then, when the Doctor could only just see them, they parted company and started going off all different ways—North, East, South and West, looking like tiny grains of black sand creeping across the wide, blue sky.

sentences.text: Then they flew off—and Gub-Gub came out from behind his barrel to see them go.
sentences.zh: 然后它们就飞走了——咕咕从木桶后面出来看它们离去。

sentences.text: Up and up and up they went—higher and higher and higher still.
sentences.zh: 它们往上、往上、再往上——越飞越高，越来越高。

sentences.text: Then, when the Doctor could only just see them, they parted company and started going off all different ways—North, East, South and West, looking like tiny grains of black sand creeping across the wide, blue sky.
sentences.zh: 后来，医生只能勉强看见它们的时候，它们分了开来，朝四面八方飞去——北、东、南、西，看起来像几粒黑色的细沙，在广阔蔚蓝的天空里缓缓挪动。

hints.zh: 散伙、各走各的；这里指六只老鹰在空中分开，分头去搜。
hints.en: Parted company: they separated and each went its own way.

paragraphs.text: “My gracious!” said Gub-Gub in a hushed voice. “What a height! I wonder they don’t scorch their feathers—so near the sun!”

sentences.text: “My gracious!” said Gub-Gub in a hushed voice.
sentences.zh: 「我的天哪！」咕咕压低了声音说。

sentences.text: “What a height!
sentences.zh: 「飞得多高啊！

sentences.text: I wonder they don’t scorch their feathers—so near the sun!”
sentences.zh: 我真奇怪它们怎么没把羽毛烤焦——离太阳那么近！」

paragraphs.text: They were gone a long time. And when they came back it was almost night.

sentences.text: They were gone a long time.
sentences.zh: 它们去了很久。

sentences.text: And when they came back it was almost night.
sentences.zh: 等它们回来时，天几乎黑了。

paragraphs.text: And the eagles said to the Doctor,

sentences.text: And the eagles said to the Doctor,
sentences.zh: 老鹰们对医生说：

paragraphs.text: “We have searched all the seas and all the countries and all the islands and all the cities and all the villages in this half of the world. But we have failed. In the main street of Gibraltar we saw three red hairs lying on a wheelbarrow before a baker’s door. But they were not the hairs of a man—they were the hairs out of a fur-coat. Nowhere, on land or water, could we see any sign of this boy’s uncle. And if we could not see him, then he is not to be seen.... For John Dolittle—we have done our best.”

sentences.text: “We have searched all the seas and all the countries and all the islands and all the cities and all the villages in this half of the world.
sentences.zh: 「我们搜遍了这个半个世界所有的海、所有的国家、所有的岛屿、所有的城市和所有的村庄。

sentences.text: But we have failed.
sentences.zh: 可是我们失败了。

sentences.text: In the main street of Gibraltar we saw three red hairs lying on a wheelbarrow before a baker’s door.
sentences.zh: 在直布罗陀的大街上，我们看见三根红头发，落在一家面包店门前的手推车上。

sentences.text: But they were not the hairs of a man—they were the hairs out of a fur-coat.
sentences.zh: 可那不是人的头发——那是从一件皮大衣上掉下来的毛。

sentences.text: Nowhere, on land or water, could we see any sign of this boy’s uncle.
sentences.zh: 无论在陆地上还是水面上，我们都看不到这男孩叔叔的一点踪影。

sentences.text: And if we could not see him, then he is not to be seen....
sentences.zh: 既然我们看不见他，那就是谁也看不见他了……

sentences.text: For John Dolittle—we have done our best.”
sentences.zh: 为了约翰·杜立德——我们已经尽了力。」

hints.zh: 直布罗陀，地中海口的港口要塞，船出海时常在那里停靠。
hints.en: Gibraltar: the port and fortress at the mouth of the Mediterranean, a usual stop for ships.

introduction.zh: 六只老鹰站在船栏上，答应为约翰·杜立德尽力，随即一只只升上天空，越飞越高，最后朝东南西北分开，小得像几粒黑沙。船上的人等了很久。天黑下来时，它们终于回来了——带回来的会是什么消息？
introduction.en: Six eagles stand on the rail and promise to do their best for John Dolittle. Up they go, higher and higher, then split up and vanish north, east, south and west. The ship waits all day. When the birds come back at dusk, what news do they bring?

quiz.question: What do the eagles do after they answer the Doctor?
options: They fly straight back to their mountain homes.
They fly apart and go off north, east, south and west.
They stay on the rail of the ship all day.

feedback.zh: 它们一直往上飞，飞到医院只能勉强看见时，就分开朝四个方向去搜。
feedback.en: They climb higher and higher, and when the Doctor can barely see them they split up and search in four directions.

quiz.question: What did the eagles find in the main street of Gibraltar?
options: Three red hairs, but they came from a fur coat.
A fisherman’s red hair on a baker’s door.
A wheelbarrow full of snuff.

feedback.zh: 三根红头发起初像是线索，但老鹰说明那不是人的头发，是皮大衣上掉的毛。
feedback.en: The three red hairs looked like a clue, but the eagles say they were not a man’s hair — they came from a fur coat.

grammar.excerpt: higher and higher and higher still

focus.zh: higher and higher 用 and 连两个比较级，表示越来越高；still 再加一层「还在往上升」。
focus.en: Higher and higher links two comparatives with and to show a change that keeps growing; still adds that it goes on.

paragraphs.text: Then the six great birds flapped their big wings and flew back to their homes in the mountains and the rocks.

sentences.text: Then the six great birds flapped their big wings and flew back to their homes in the mountains and the rocks.
sentences.zh: 于是那六只大鸟拍着大翅膀，飞回它们在群山和岩石间的家。

paragraphs.text: “Well,” said Dab-Dab, after they had gone, “what are we going to do now? The boy’s uncle must be found—there’s no two ways about that. The lad isn’t old enough to be knocking around the world by himself. Boys aren’t like ducklings—they have to be taken care of till they’re quite old.... I wish Chee-Chee were here. He would soon find the man. Good old Chee-Chee! I wonder how he’s getting on!”

sentences.text: “Well,” said Dab-Dab, after they had gone, “what are we going to do now?
sentences.zh: 「那么，」它们走后，达布达布说，「我们现在怎么办？

sentences.text: The boy’s uncle must be found—there’s no two ways about that.
sentences.zh: 这男孩的叔叔必须找到——这事没有别的说法。

sentences.text: The lad isn’t old enough to be knocking around the world by himself.
sentences.zh: 这孩子还太小，不能一个人在外面闯荡。

sentences.text: Boys aren’t like ducklings—they have to be taken care of till they’re quite old....
sentences.zh: 男孩子可不像小鸭子——得有人照看他们，一直照看到很大才行……

sentences.text: I wish Chee-Chee were here.
sentences.zh: 要是奇奇在这儿就好了。

sentences.text: He would soon find the man.
sentences.zh: 他很快就能找到那个人。

sentences.text: Good old Chee-Chee!
sentences.zh: 好样的老奇奇！

sentences.text: I wonder how he’s getting on!”
sentences.zh: 不知道他现在过得怎么样！」

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子；这时它留在非洲，不在船上。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey, who is not on the ship just now.

hints.zh: 在外面到处闯、四处漂泊；不是「敲打世界」。
hints.en: Knocking around the world: wandering about the world on one’s own.

paragraphs.text: “If we only had Polynesia with us,” said the white mouse. “She would soon think of some way. Do you remember how she got us all out of prison—the second time? My, but she was a clever one!”

sentences.text: “If we only had Polynesia with us,” said the white mouse.
sentences.zh: 「要是波利尼西亚跟我们一起就好了，」白老鼠说。

sentences.text: “She would soon think of some way.
sentences.zh: 「她很快就能想出办法。

sentences.text: Do you remember how she got us all out of prison—the second time?
sentences.zh: 你还记得她怎么把我们大家从牢里弄出来的吗——第二次？

sentences.text: My, but she was a clever one!”
sentences.zh: 哎呀，她可真是个机灵的家伙！」

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，那只见多识广的鹦鹉。
hints.en: Polynesia, the much-travelled parrot.

hints.target: got us all out of prison
hints.zh: 把我们从牢里弄出来；指从前被乔利金基国王关起来后逃走的那一回。
hints.en: Got us all out of prison: it points back to an earlier escape after the King of Jolliginki locked them up.

paragraphs.text: “I don’t think so much of those eagle-fellows,” said Jip. “They’re just conceited. They may have very good eyesight and all that; but when you ask them to find a man for you, they can’t do it—and they have the cheek to come back and say that nobody else could do it. They’re just conceited—like that collie in Puddleby. And I don’t think a whole lot of those gossipy old porpoises either. All they could tell us was that the man isn’t in the sea. We don’t want to know where he isn’t—we want to know where he is.”

sentences.text: “I don’t think so much of those eagle-fellows,” said Jip.
