sentences.zh: 「我可不大看得上那些老鹰伙计，」吉普说。

sentences.text: “They’re just conceited.
sentences.zh: 「它们就是自大。

sentences.text: They may have very good eyesight and all that; but when you ask them to find a man for you, they can’t do it—and they have the cheek to come back and say that nobody else could do it.
sentences.zh: 也许它们眼力确实好得很，诸如此类；可你要是请它们帮你找个人，它们就办不到——还厚着脸皮回来说，别的谁也办不到。

sentences.text: They’re just conceited—like that collie in Puddleby.
sentences.zh: 它们就是自大——像帕德尔比那条柯利牧羊犬一样。

sentences.text: And I don’t think a whole lot of those gossipy old porpoises either.
sentences.zh: 我也不大瞧得上那些爱说闲话的老鼠海豚。

sentences.text: All they could tell us was that the man isn’t in the sea.
sentences.zh: 它们能告诉我们的只是：那个人不在海里。

sentences.text: We don’t want to know where he isn’t—we want to know where he is.”
sentences.zh: 我们不想知道他不在哪儿——我们想知道他在哪儿。」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生养的狗，鼻子最灵。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog, with the best nose on the ship.

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡小镇。
hints.en: Puddleby, the little town the Doctor comes from.

introduction.zh: 老鹰拍着翅膀回了山里的家，甲板上安静下来。达布达布念叨起猴子奇奇，白老鼠想起了鹦鹉波利尼西亚；吉普却对老鹰和鼠海豚一肚子意见，说它们只会讲自己办不到。难道就没有别的法子了？
introduction.en: The eagles flap away to their mountain homes and the deck goes quiet. Dab-Dab wishes Chee-Chee were there; the white mouse thinks of Polynesia. Jip has no kind words for the eagles or the porpoises. Is there any other way to find a lost man?

quiz.question: Why does Dab-Dab wish Chee-Chee were with them?
options: He could fly higher than the eagles.
He could talk to the fish in the sea.
He would soon find the man.

feedback.zh: 达布达布说，奇奇在这儿很快就能找到那个人，还夸他「好样的老奇奇」。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab says Chee-Chee would soon find the man, and calls him “good old Chee-Chee”.

quiz.question: What is Jip’s complaint about the eagles?
options: They ate the food that belonged to the boy.
They are conceited, and they say that nobody else could do it.
They are too old and too slow to fly.

feedback.zh: 吉普说它们找不着人，还厚着脸皮回来说别人也办不到——这就是自大。
feedback.en: Jip says they fail, then have the cheek to claim that nobody else could do it: that is being conceited.

grammar.excerpt: I wish Chee-Chee were here

focus.zh: wish 后面用过去式 were，表示与现在事实相反的愿望：可惜奇奇此刻不在这儿。
focus.en: After wish we use the past form were for a wish about now: Chee-Chee is not here.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, don’t talk so much,” said Gub-Gub. “It’s easy to talk; but it isn’t so easy to find a man when you have got the whole world to hunt him in. Maybe the fisherman’s hair has turned white, worrying about the boy; and that was why the eagles didn’t find him. You don’t know everything. You’re just talking. You are not doing anything to help. You couldn’t find the boy’s uncle any more than the eagles could—you couldn’t do as well.”

sentences.text: “Oh, don’t talk so much,” said Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「哦，别这么唠叨了，」咕咕说。

sentences.text: “It’s easy to talk; but it isn’t so easy to find a man when you have got the whole world to hunt him in.
sentences.zh: 「说话容易；可要是让你满世界去找一个人，那就不容易了。

sentences.text: Maybe the fisherman’s hair has turned white, worrying about the boy; and that was why the eagles didn’t find him.
sentences.zh: 也许那渔夫因为担心这孩子，头发都变白了；所以老鹰才没找到他。

sentences.text: You don’t know everything.
sentences.zh: 你也不是什么都懂。

sentences.text: You’re just talking.
sentences.zh: 你就光会说。

sentences.text: You are not doing anything to help.
sentences.zh: 你什么忙也没帮上。

sentences.text: You couldn’t find the boy’s uncle any more than the eagles could—you couldn’t do as well.”
sentences.zh: 你找不到那男孩的叔叔，跟老鹰一样找不到——你也好不到哪儿去。」

hints.target: any more than the eagles could
hints.zh: 跟……一样（不行）；not … any more than 表示两边同样办不到。
hints.en: Not any more than means the two are equally unable: you could no more find him than the eagles could.

paragraphs.text: “Couldn’t I?” said the dog. “That’s all you know, you stupid piece of warm bacon! I haven’t begun to try yet, have I? You wait and see!”

sentences.text: “Couldn’t I?” said the dog.
sentences.zh: 「我找不到？」狗说。

sentences.text: “That’s all you know, you stupid piece of warm bacon!
sentences.zh: 「你就知道这些，你这块蠢头蠢脑的温热咸肉！

sentences.text: I haven’t begun to try yet, have I?
sentences.zh: 我还没开始试呢，不是吗？

sentences.text: You wait and see!”
sentences.zh: 你等着瞧吧！」

hints.zh: 「温热的咸肉」：吉普骂猪的话，暗指咕咕是一块会走路的肉。
hints.en: Warm bacon: an insult aimed at a pig — a piece of meat that walks and talks.

paragraphs.text: Then Jip went to the Doctor and said,

sentences.text: Then Jip went to the Doctor and said,
sentences.zh: 然后吉普走到医生跟前说：

paragraphs.text: “Ask the boy if he has anything in his pockets that belonged to his uncle, will you, please?”

sentences.text: “Ask the boy if he has anything in his pockets that belonged to his uncle, will you, please?”
sentences.zh: 「请您问问那男孩，他口袋里有没有属于他叔叔的东西，好吗？」

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor asked him. And the boy showed them a gold ring which he wore on a piece of string around his neck because it was too big for his finger. He said his uncle gave it to him when they saw the pirates coming.

sentences.text: So the Doctor asked him.
sentences.zh: 于是医生问了他。

sentences.text: And the boy showed them a gold ring which he wore on a piece of string around his neck because it was too big for his finger.
sentences.zh: 男孩给他们看了一枚金戒指，他用一根绳子挂在脖子上，因为戴在手指上太大了。

sentences.text: He said his uncle gave it to him when they saw the pirates coming.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是他们看见海盗过来的时候，叔叔给他的。

hints.zh: 海盗；指本·阿里那伙人，男孩的叔叔就是被他们劫走的。
hints.en: Pirates: Ben Ali’s men, who took the boy’s uncle.

paragraphs.text: Jip smelt the ring and said,

sentences.text: Jip smelt the ring and said,
sentences.zh: 吉普闻了闻戒指，说：

paragraphs.text: “That’s no good. Ask him if he has anything else that belonged to his uncle.”

sentences.text: “That’s no good.
sentences.zh: 「这个不行。

sentences.text: Ask him if he has anything else that belonged to his uncle.”
sentences.zh: 问问他还有没有别的属于他叔叔的东西。」

paragraphs.text: Then the boy took from his pocket a great, big red handkerchief and said, “This was my uncle’s too.”

sentences.text: Then the boy took from his pocket a great, big red handkerchief and said, “This was my uncle’s too.”
sentences.zh: 于是男孩从口袋里掏出一块很大的红手帕，说：「这也是我叔叔的。」

paragraphs.text: As soon as the boy pulled it out, Jip shouted,

sentences.text: As soon as the boy pulled it out, Jip shouted,
sentences.zh: 男孩刚一掏出来，吉普就大声叫起来：

paragraphs.text: “Snuff, by Jingo!—Black Rappee snuff. Don’t you smell it? His uncle took snuff—Ask him, Doctor.”

sentences.text: “Snuff, by Jingo!—Black Rappee snuff.
sentences.zh: 「鼻烟，天哪！——黑拉皮鼻烟。

sentences.text: Don’t you smell it?
sentences.zh: 你们没闻到吗？

sentences.text: His uncle took snuff—Ask him, Doctor.”
sentences.zh: 他叔叔吸鼻烟——问问他，医生。」

hints.zh: 黑拉皮鼻烟，一种深色、磨得较粗的鼻烟，气味很重。
hints.en: Black Rappee: a dark, coarsely ground snuff with a strong smell.

hints.zh: 感叹语，表示惊讶或兴奋，相当于「天哪」「好家伙」。
hints.en: By Jingo: an old exclamation of surprise or excitement.

introduction.zh: 咕咕说吉普光会吹牛，吉普气得让他等着瞧。它转身请医生去问那男孩：身上有没有属于叔叔的东西。男孩先拿出一枚挂在绳子上的金戒指，又掏出一块大红手帕。狗鼻子凑上去的时候，能闻到什么？
introduction.en: Gub-Gub calls Jip a boaster, and Jip is furious: wait and see. Then he asks the Doctor to question the boy: has he anything that belonged to his uncle? First comes a gold ring on a string, then a big red handkerchief. What will a dog’s nose find?

quiz.question: What does Jip ask the Doctor to do?
options: Ask the boy whether he has anything that belonged to his uncle.
Ask the boy where the pirates have gone.
Ask Dab-Dab to fly back home for help.

feedback.zh: 吉普的办法是先闻气味，所以它要医生问男孩口袋里有没有叔叔的东西。
feedback.en: Jip’s plan starts from a smell, so he asks the Doctor to find out whether the boy carries anything of his uncle’s.

quiz.question: What did the boy do with the gold ring?
options: He kept it hidden in his pocket.
He gave it back to the pirates.
He wore it on a piece of string around his neck.

feedback.zh: 戒指太大，戴不上手指，男孩就用一根绳子把它挂在脖子上。
feedback.en: The ring was too big for his finger, so the boy wore it on a string around his neck.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as the boy pulled it out, Jip shouted

focus.zh: as soon as 引出先发生的动作，主句紧接着发生；前后两处都用一般过去时。
focus.en: As soon as introduces the first action and the main clause follows at once; both verbs are in the past.

paragraphs.text: The Doctor questioned the boy again; and he said, “Yes. My uncle took a lot of snuff.”

sentences.text: The Doctor questioned the boy again; and he said, “Yes.
sentences.zh: 医生又问那男孩；他说：「是的。

sentences.text: My uncle took a lot of snuff.”
sentences.zh: 我叔叔吸很多鼻烟。」

paragraphs.text: “Fine!” said Jip. “The man’s as good as found. ’Twill be as easy as stealing milk from a kitten. Tell the boy I’ll find his uncle for him in less than a week. Let us go upstairs and see which way the wind is blowing.”

sentences.text: “Fine!” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「太好了！」吉普说。

sentences.text: “The man’s as good as found. ’Twill be as easy as stealing milk from a kitten.
sentences.zh: 「这人跟找到了一样。这就像从小猫那儿偷奶一样容易。

sentences.text: Tell the boy I’ll find his uncle for him in less than a week.
sentences.zh: 告诉那男孩，我用不了一个星期就能替他找到叔叔。

sentences.text: Let us go upstairs and see which way the wind is blowing.”
sentences.zh: 我们上楼去，看看风往哪边吹。」

hints.zh: 等于已经找到了；as good as 表示「实际上差不多就是」。
hints.en: As good as found: for practical purposes he is already found.

hints.zh: 旧式缩略说法，等于 it will，常见于老书和乡间口语。
hints.en: ’Twill is an old contraction of it will, common in older books and country speech.

paragraphs.text: “But it is dark now,” said the Doctor. “You can’t find him in the dark!”

sentences.text: “But it is dark now,” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「可是现在天黑了，」医生说。

sentences.text: “You can’t find him in the dark!”
sentences.zh: 「你在黑地里可找不到他！」

paragraphs.text: “I don’t need any light to look for a man who smells of Black Rappee snuff,” said Jip as he climbed the stairs. “If the man had a hard smell, like string, now—or hot water, it would be different. But snuff!—Tut, tut!”

sentences.text: “I don’t need any light to look for a man who smells of Black Rappee snuff,” said Jip as he climbed the stairs.
sentences.zh: 「我要找的是一个身上有黑拉皮鼻烟气味的男人，用不着什么光，」吉普一边上楼一边说。

sentences.text: “If the man had a hard smell, like string, now—or hot water, it would be different.
sentences.zh: 「要是这人身上是股难缠的气味，比如绳子——或者热水，那就另当别论了。

sentences.text: But snuff!—Tut, tut!”
sentences.zh: 可鼻烟！——啧，啧！」

hints.zh: 难追踪的气味；这里 hard 说的是气味不好循着找，不是「浓烈」。
hints.en: A hard smell: one that is hard to follow, not a strong one.

hints.zh: 啧、啧：咂嘴的声音，表示不以为然或觉得太容易了。
hints.en: Tut, tut: a click of the tongue showing mild scorn or “how easy!”

paragraphs.text: “Does hot water have a smell?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Does hot water have a smell?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「热水有气味吗？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “Certainly it has,” said Jip. “Hot water smells quite different from cold water. It is warm water—or ice—that has the really difficult smell. Why, I once followed a man for ten miles on a dark night by the smell of the hot water he had used to shave with—for the poor fellow had no soap.... Now then, let us see which way the wind is blowing. Wind is very important in long-distant smelling. It mustn’t be too fierce a wind—and of course it must blow the right way. A nice, steady, damp breeze is the best of all.... Ha!—This wind is from the North.”

sentences.text: “Certainly it has,” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「当然有，」吉普说。

sentences.text: “Hot water smells quite different from cold water.
sentences.zh: 「热水的味道和冷水大不一样。

sentences.text: It is warm water—or ice—that has the really difficult smell.
sentences.zh: 真正难闻出来的是温水——或者冰。

sentences.text: Why, I once followed a man for ten miles on a dark night by the smell of the hot water he had used to shave with—for the poor fellow had no soap....
sentences.zh: 哎，有一回，我在一个漆黑的夜里跟着一个人走了十英里，全凭他用热水刮胡子留下的气味——那可怜的家伙没有肥皂……

sentences.text: Now then, let us see which way the wind is blowing.
sentences.zh: 好了，咱们来看看风往哪边吹。

sentences.text: Wind is very important in long-distant smelling.
sentences.zh: 远程闻气味，风非常重要。

sentences.text: It mustn’t be too fierce a wind—and of course it must blow the right way.
sentences.zh: 风不能太猛——当然还得朝对的方向吹。

sentences.text: A nice, steady, damp breeze is the best of all....
sentences.zh: 一阵柔和、稳定、带湿气的微风最好……

sentences.text: Ha!—This wind is from the North.”
sentences.zh: 哈！——这风是从北边来的。」

hints.zh: 远距离闻气味；作者自造的说法，用连字符把三个词拼在一起。
hints.en: Long-distant smelling: the author’s own compound for smelling things far away.

introduction.zh: 男孩承认叔叔吸很多鼻烟，吉普立刻说这人等于已经找到了。可天已经黑了，医生想不出没有光怎么找。吉普却说，找一个满身鼻烟味的人根本不用灯——它只要知道风往哪边吹。
introduction.en: The boy says his uncle took a lot of snuff, and Jip calls the man as good as found. But it is dark, and the Doctor does not see how anyone can search without a light. Jip needs only to know which way the wind blows.

quiz.question: Why does Jip say the man is as good as found?
options: Because the wind is already blowing from the south.
Because a man who smells of snuff will be easy to follow by nose.
Because the boy knows exactly where his uncle went.

feedback.zh: 吉普认为有鼻烟味这条线索，找起来就像从小猫那儿偷奶一样容易。
feedback.en: With the snuff smell to follow, Jip thinks the search will be as easy as stealing milk from a kitten.

quiz.question: Why does Jip go upstairs?
options: To see which way the wind is blowing.
To fetch a lamp for the Doctor.
To look at the stars and find the north.

feedback.zh: 吉普要上楼去看风往哪边吹——远距离闻气味全靠风。
feedback.en: Jip wants to see which way the wind blows, because wind matters for smelling things far off.

grammar.excerpt: to look for a man who smells of Black Rappee snuff

focus.zh: who smells… 是修饰 a man 的关系从句，说明吉普要找的是怎样一个人。
focus.en: The who-clause describes a man: it tells us what kind of man Jip means to look for.

paragraphs.text: Then Jip went up to the front of the ship and smelt the wind; and he started muttering to himself,

sentences.text: Then Jip went up to the front of the ship and smelt the wind; and he started muttering to himself,
sentences.zh: 然后吉普走到船头，闻了闻风；他开始自言自语地嘟囔：

paragraphs.text: “Tar; Spanish onions; kerosene oil; wet raincoats; crushed laurel-leaves; rubber burning; lace-curtains being washed—No, my mistake, lace-curtains hanging out to dry; and foxes—hundreds of ’em—cubs; and—”

sentences.text: “Tar; Spanish onions; kerosene oil; wet raincoats; crushed laurel-leaves; rubber burning; lace-curtains being washed—No, my mistake, lace-curtains hanging out to dry; and foxes—hundreds of ’em—cubs; and—”
sentences.zh: 「焦油；西班牙洋葱；煤油；淋湿的雨衣；揉碎的月桂叶；橡胶烧着的味道；正在洗的蕾丝窗帘——不对，我说错了，是挂出去晾的蕾丝窗帘；还有狐狸——好几百只——小狐狸；还有——」

hints.zh: them 的口语缩略，前面常省掉 of：hundreds of ’em 就是「好几百只」。
hints.en: ’Em is a spoken form of them: hundreds of ’em means hundreds of them.

paragraphs.text: “Can you really smell all those different things in this one wind?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “Can you really smell all those different things in this one wind?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「这一阵风里，你真能闻出所有这些不同的东西？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “Why, of course!” said Jip. “And those are only a few of the easy smells—the strong ones. Any mongrel could smell those with a cold in the head. Wait now, and I’ll tell you some of the harder scents that are coming on this wind—a few of the dainty ones.”

sentences.text: “Why, of course!” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「哎，当然！」吉普说。

sentences.text: “And those are only a few of the easy smells—the strong ones.
sentences.zh: 「这些还只是些容易闻的气味——那些浓的。

sentences.text: Any mongrel could smell those with a cold in the head.
sentences.zh: 随便哪条杂种狗，就算鼻子伤风也闻得出来。

sentences.text: Wait now, and I’ll tell you some of the harder scents that are coming on this wind—a few of the dainty ones.”
sentences.zh: 等等，我再说说这风里送来的几种更难分辨的气味——几样清淡细微的。」

hints.zh: 鼻子伤风、鼻塞；鼻子不通气时闻不出味道。
hints.en: A cold in the head: a blocked nose, when you can hardly smell anything.

hints.zh: dainty 这里指气味清淡、细微，不是「漂亮」；指最难分辨的那几种。
hints.en: The dainty ones: smells that are light and faint, the hardest to pick out.

paragraphs.text: Then the dog shut his eyes tight, poked his nose straight up in the air and sniffed hard with his mouth half-open.

sentences.text: Then the dog shut his eyes tight, poked his nose straight up in the air and sniffed hard with his mouth half-open.
sentences.zh: 然后狗紧紧闭上眼睛，把鼻子直直地朝天上翘起，半张着嘴使劲地嗅。

paragraphs.text: For a long time he said nothing. He kept as still as a stone. He hardly seemed to be breathing at all. When at last he began to speak, it sounded almost as though he were singing, sadly, in a dream.

sentences.text: For a long time he said nothing.
sentences.zh: 好长一段时间，他什么也没说。

sentences.text: He kept as still as a stone.
sentences.zh: 他像石头一样一动不动。

sentences.text: He hardly seemed to be breathing at all.
sentences.zh: 他几乎一点气都不喘。

sentences.text: When at last he began to speak, it sounded almost as though he were singing, sadly, in a dream.
sentences.zh: 等他终于开口时，那声音几乎像是在梦里忧伤地唱歌。

paragraphs.text: “Bricks,” he whispered, very low—“old yellow bricks, crumbling with age in a garden-wall; the sweet breath of young cows standing in a mountain-stream; the lead roof of a dove-cote—or perhaps a granary—with the mid-day sun on it; black kid gloves lying in a bureau-drawer of walnut-wood; a dusty road with a horses’ drinking-trough beneath the sycamores; little mushrooms bursting through the rotting leaves; and—and—and—”

sentences.text: “Bricks,” he whispered, very low—“old yellow bricks, crumbling with age in a garden-wall; the sweet breath of young cows standing in a mountain-stream; the lead roof of a dove-cote—or perhaps a granary—with the mid-day sun on it; black kid gloves lying in a bureau-drawer of walnut-wood; a dusty road with a horses’ drinking-trough beneath the sycamores; little mushrooms bursting through the rotting leaves; and—and—and—”
sentences.zh: 「砖头，」他低声说，声音很轻——「老旧发黄的砖，在花园的围墙里随岁月碎成粉末；站在山溪里的年轻母牛呼出的甜甜气息；鸽舍的铅皮屋顶——也许是谷仓的——正晒着正午的太阳；放在胡桃木五斗柜抽屉里的黑色小羊皮手套；一条尘土飞扬的大路，梧桐树下有马匹饮水的水槽；小蘑菇从腐烂的树叶下面钻出来；还有——还有——还有——」

hints.zh: 五斗柜的抽屉；bureau 在这里是带抽屉的柜子，不是「办公室」。
hints.en: A bureau-drawer: a drawer in a chest of drawers; bureau here is not an office.

introduction.zh: 吉普走到船头，迎着风念念有词：焦油、西班牙洋葱、煤油、湿雨衣、揉碎的月桂叶……医生问，一阵风里真有这么多东西？吉普哼了一声，说这不过是最容易的几样。它闭上眼，把鼻子翘向天空。
introduction.en: At the front of the ship Jip mutters into the wind: tar, Spanish onions, kerosene, wet raincoats, crushed laurel leaves. Can one wind carry all that? Those, says Jip, are the easy smells. He shuts his eyes and lifts his nose to the sky.

quiz.question: Which of these does Jip smell first in the wind?
options: Fresh bread and roasted coffee.
Fish, seaweed and wet sand.
Tar, Spanish onions and wet raincoats.

feedback.zh: 吉普一口气报出焦油、西班牙洋葱、煤油、湿雨衣、月桂叶等，还算上了狐狸。
feedback.en: Jip runs through tar, Spanish onions, kerosene, wet raincoats and laurel leaves, and adds foxes too.

quiz.question: What does Jip do before he names the harder smells?
options: He asks the Doctor for a pipe of tobacco.
He shuts his eyes, lifts his nose and sniffs hard.
He runs to the back of the ship and hides.

feedback.zh: 他闭上眼、把鼻子朝天竖起、半张着嘴使劲嗅，还一动不动地站了很久。
feedback.en: He shuts his eyes, pokes his nose up and sniffs hard, then stands as still as a stone for a long time.

grammar.excerpt: He hardly seemed to be breathing at all

focus.zh: hardly 意思是「几乎不」，本身已带否定，句子后面不再加 not。
focus.en: Hardly already means almost not, so the sentence needs no not.

paragraphs.text: “Any parsnips?” asked Gub-Gub.

sentences.text: “Any parsnips?” asked Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「有防风草吗？」咕咕问。

hints.zh: 防风草，一种像白胡萝卜的根菜；咕咕是猪，只惦记吃的。
hints.en: Parsnips: white root vegetables like carrots; Gub-Gub the pig thinks only of food.

paragraphs.text: “No,” said Jip. “You always think of things to eat. No parsnips whatever. And no snuff—plenty of pipes and cigarettes, and a few cigars. But no snuff. We must wait till the wind changes to the South.”

sentences.text: “No,” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「没有，」吉普说。

sentences.text: “You always think of things to eat.
sentences.zh: 「你总是想着吃的东西。

sentences.text: No parsnips whatever.
sentences.zh: 一点防风草也没有。

sentences.text: And no snuff—plenty of pipes and cigarettes, and a few cigars.
sentences.zh: 也没有鼻烟——烟斗和香烟倒不少，还有几支雪茄。

sentences.text: But no snuff.
sentences.zh: 可就是没有鼻烟。

sentences.text: We must wait till the wind changes to the South.”
sentences.zh: 我们得等风转到南边。」

paragraphs.text: “Yes, it’s a poor wind, that,” said Gub-Gub. “I think you’re a fake, Jip. Who ever heard of finding a man in the middle of the ocean just by smell! I told you you couldn’t do it.”

sentences.text: “Yes, it’s a poor wind, that,” said Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「是啊，这风不行啊，这风，」咕咕说。

sentences.text: “I think you’re a fake, Jip.
sentences.zh: 「我看你是个骗子，吉普。

sentences.text: Who ever heard of finding a man in the middle of the ocean just by smell!
sentences.zh: 谁听说过在汪洋大海中间光靠闻气味就能找到人！

sentences.text: I told you you couldn’t do it.”
sentences.zh: 我早就跟你说过你办不到。」

paragraphs.text: “Look here,” said Jip, getting really angry. “You’re going to get a bite on the nose in a minute! You needn’t think that just because the Doctor won’t let us give you what you deserve, that you can be as cheeky as you like!”

sentences.text: “Look here,” said Jip, getting really angry.
sentences.zh: 「你听着，」吉普真的生气了。

sentences.text: “You’re going to get a bite on the nose in a minute!
sentences.zh: 「你再过一会儿鼻子上就要挨一口了！

sentences.text: You needn’t think that just because the Doctor won’t let us give you what you deserve, that you can be as cheeky as you like!”
sentences.zh: 你别以为医生不让我们给你点应得的教训，你就可以这么放肆！」

hints.zh: 鼻子上挨一口：吉普威胁要咬咕咕的鼻子。
hints.en: A bite on the nose: Jip is threatening to bite Gub-Gub’s nose.

paragraphs.text: “Stop quarreling!” said the Doctor—“Stop it! Life’s too short. Tell me, Jip, where do you think those smells are coming from?”

sentences.text: “Stop quarreling!” said the Doctor—“Stop it!
sentences.zh: 「别吵了！」医生说——「停一停！

sentences.text: Life’s too short.
sentences.zh: 人生太短了。

sentences.text: Tell me, Jip, where do you think those smells are coming from?”
sentences.zh: 告诉我，吉普，你觉得这些气味是从哪儿来的？」

hints.zh: 人生太短（不值得浪费在吵架上）；这是劝人别争的一句常用话。
hints.en: Life’s too short: a set phrase meaning it is not worth wasting time on a quarrel.

paragraphs.text: “From Devon and Wales—most of them,” said Jip—“The wind is coming that way.”

sentences.text: “From Devon and Wales—most of them,” said Jip—“The wind is coming that way.”
sentences.zh: 「从德文郡和威尔士来——大部分是，」吉普说——「风就是从那边来的。」

hints.zh: 德文郡和威尔士，英格兰西南面的两个地方，正在这条船的北风上游。
hints.en: Devon and Wales: two places in the south-west of Britain, upwind of the ship.

paragraphs.text: “Well, well!” said the Doctor. “You know that’s really quite remarkable—quite. I must make a note of that for my new book. I wonder if you could train me to smell as well as that.... But no—perhaps I’m better off the way I am. ‘Enough is as good as a feast,’ they say. Let’s go down to supper. I’m quite hungry.”

sentences.text: “Well, well!” said the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「好了，好了！」医生说。

sentences.text: “You know that’s really quite remarkable—quite.
sentences.zh: 「你知道吗，这真是相当了不起——相当了不起。

sentences.text: I must make a note of that for my new book.
sentences.zh: 我得把这件事记下来，写进我的新书里。

sentences.text: I wonder if you could train me to smell as well as that....
sentences.zh: 不知道你能不能把我训练得也那么会闻……

sentences.text: But no—perhaps I’m better off the way I am. ‘Enough is as good as a feast,’ they say.
sentences.zh: 不过算了——也许我这样反倒更好。俗话说『知足常乐』。

sentences.text: Let’s go down to supper.
sentences.zh: 咱们下去吃晚饭吧。

sentences.text: I’m quite hungry.”
sentences.zh: 我挺饿了。」

hints.target: ‘Enough is as good as a feast,’
hints.zh: 英国谚语：饱餐不过如此，够吃就等于盛宴——意思相近于「知足常乐」。
hints.en: An old proverb: enough is as good as a feast — be content with what you have.

paragraphs.text: “So am I,” said Gub-Gub.

sentences.text: “So am I,” said Gub-Gub.
sentences.zh: 「我也饿了，」咕咕说。

introduction.zh: 咕咕只想知道风里有没有防风草；吉普说这阵风里有烟斗和雪茄，却没有鼻烟，得等风转到南边。咕咕便笑它是个骗子，吉普火了，医生赶紧叫停。他问吉普：这些气味究竟是从哪儿来的？
introduction.en: Gub-Gub wants to know if there are parsnips in the wind. Jip finds pipes and cigars there, but no snuff — they must wait for the wind to turn south. Gub-Gub laughs at him, Jip loses his temper, and the Doctor stops the quarrel.

quiz.question: Why must they wait?
options: The wind must change to the south before the snuff smell can reach them.
The boy must find another handkerchief for Jip to smell.
The Doctor must buy a map of Devon and Wales.

feedback.zh: 这阵北风里只有烟斗、香烟和雪茄的气味，没有鼻烟，所以要等风转到南边。
feedback.en: This north wind carries pipes, cigarettes and cigars but no snuff, so they must wait for the wind to turn south.

quiz.question: Where does Jip say most of the smells come from?
options: From Spain and Africa.
From the islands of the North Sea.
From Devon and Wales.

feedback.zh: 吉普说这些气味大部分来自德文郡和威尔士——风就是从那个方向吹来的。
feedback.en: Jip says most of the smells come from Devon and Wales, because the wind is blowing from that way.

grammar.excerpt: Let’s go down to supper

focus.zh: Let’s + 动词原形，提议一起做某事，说话人自己也算在内。
focus.en: Let’s + base verb suggests doing something together, with the speaker included.

title.en: The Dog Who Sniffs the Wind

paragraphs.text: Up they got, early next morning, out of the silken beds; and they saw that the sun was shining brightly and that the wind was blowing from the South.

sentences.text: Up they got, early next morning, out of the silken beds; and they saw that the sun was shining brightly and that the wind was blowing from the South.
sentences.zh: 第二天一早，他们就起了身，离开那些铺着丝绸的床；他们看见太阳明亮地照着，风从南边吹来。

paragraphs.text: Jip smelt the South wind for half an hour. Then he came to the Doctor, shaking his head.

sentences.text: Jip smelt the South wind for half an hour.
sentences.zh: 吉普闻了半个钟头的南风。

sentences.text: Then he came to the Doctor, shaking his head.
sentences.zh: 然后他走到医生跟前，摇了摇头。

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗，鼻子特别灵。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog, whose nose can smell things far away.

paragraphs.text: “I smell no snuff as yet,” he said. “We must wait till the wind changes to the East.”

sentences.text: “I smell no snuff as yet,” he said.
sentences.zh: 「我还闻不到鼻烟味呢。」他说。

sentences.text: “We must wait till the wind changes to the East.”
sentences.zh: 「我们得等到风转向东边。」

hints.zh: 到目前为止（还没）；I smell no snuff as yet 就是「我到现在还没闻到鼻烟味」。
hints.en: As yet means up to now: I smell no snuff as yet — I have not smelt any so far.

paragraphs.text: But even when the East wind came, at three o’clock that afternoon, the dog could not catch the smell of snuff.

sentences.text: But even when the East wind came, at three o’clock that afternoon, the dog could not catch the smell of snuff.
sentences.zh: 可就算那天下午三点钟东风来了，狗还是闻不到鼻烟的气味。

paragraphs.text: The little boy was terribly disappointed and began to cry again, saying that no one seemed to be able to find his uncle for him. But all Jip said to the Doctor was,

sentences.text: The little boy was terribly disappointed and began to cry again, saying that no one seemed to be able to find his uncle for him.
sentences.zh: 小男孩失望极了，又哭了起来，说好像谁都没法替他找到叔叔。

sentences.text: But all Jip said to the Doctor was,
sentences.zh: 可吉普只对医生说了一句话：

paragraphs.text: “Tell him that when the wind changes to the West, I’ll find his uncle even though he be in China—so long as he is still taking Black Rappee snuff.”

sentences.text: “Tell him that when the wind changes to the West, I’ll find his uncle even though he be in China—so long as he is still taking Black Rappee snuff.”
sentences.zh: 「你告诉他，等风转到西边，我就能找到他叔叔，哪怕他在中国——只要他还在吸黑拉皮鼻烟。」

hints.zh: 黑拉皮鼻烟，一种味道很冲的鼻烟；男孩的叔叔一直吸这种烟。
hints.en: Black Rappee, a strong kind of snuff; the boy’s uncle always takes this sort.

hints.zh: 只要；so long as he is still taking Black Rappee snuff 就是「只要他还在吸黑拉皮鼻烟」。
hints.en: So long as means provided that: as long as he still takes the snuff.

paragraphs.text: Three days they had to wait before the West wind came. This was on a Friday morning, early—just as it was getting light. A fine rainy mist lay on the sea like a thin fog. And the wind was soft and warm and wet.

sentences.text: Three days they had to wait before the West wind came.
sentences.zh: 他们等了三天，西风才来。

sentences.text: This was on a Friday morning, early—just as it was getting light.
sentences.zh: 那是星期五清早——天刚蒙蒙亮。

sentences.text: A fine rainy mist lay on the sea like a thin fog.
sentences.zh: 海面上笼着一层细密的雨雾，薄得像一层轻纱。

sentences.text: And the wind was soft and warm and wet.
sentences.zh: 风又柔又暖，还带着湿气。

paragraphs.text: As soon as Jip awoke he ran upstairs and poked his nose in the air. Then he got most frightfully excited and rushed down again to wake the Doctor up.

sentences.text: As soon as Jip awoke he ran upstairs and poked his nose in the air.
sentences.zh: 吉普一醒来就跑上楼，把鼻子往空中一伸。

sentences.text: Then he got most frightfully excited and rushed down again to wake the Doctor up.
sentences.zh: 接着他兴奋得不得了，又冲下楼去把医生叫醒。

hints.target: poked his nose in the air
hints.zh: 把鼻子往空中一伸，去嗅风里的味道。
hints.en: He pushed his nose up into the air to catch the smell on the wind.

paragraphs.text: “Doctor!” he cried. “I’ve got it! Doctor! Doctor! Wake up! Listen! I’ve got it! The wind’s from the West and it smells of nothing but snuff. Come upstairs and start the ship—quick!”

sentences.text: “Doctor!” he cried.
sentences.zh: 「医生！」他喊道。

sentences.text: “I’ve got it!
sentences.zh: 「我闻到了！

sentences.text: Doctor!
sentences.zh: 医生！

sentences.text: Doctor!
sentences.zh: 医生！

sentences.text: Wake up!
sentences.zh: 醒醒！

sentences.text: Listen!
sentences.zh: 你听！

sentences.text: I’ve got it!
sentences.zh: 我闻到了！

sentences.text: The wind’s from the West and it smells of nothing but snuff.
sentences.zh: 风是从西边来的，里面除了鼻烟味什么也没有。

sentences.text: Come upstairs and start the ship—quick!”
sentences.zh: 快上楼来开船——快！」

introduction.zh: 小男孩的叔叔不见了，能帮上忙的只有吉普的鼻子。南风里闻不到鼻烟味，换了东风还是没有。吉普到底在等哪一种风？
introduction.en: The little boy’s uncle is lost somewhere on the sea, and only Jip’s nose can help. The dog sniffs the south wind, then the east wind, and shakes his head. What kind of wind is he waiting for?

quiz.question: What is Jip trying to smell in the wind?
options: Smoke from a ship
Snuff — the tobacco the boy’s uncle takes
Food cooking on a far-off island
Fresh water from the sea

feedback.zh: 吉普一开口就是「我还闻不到鼻烟味呢」，可见它在风里找的正是鼻烟味，也就是男孩叔叔吸的那种烟。
feedback.en: Jip’s first words are “I smell no snuff as yet”: the smell he is hunting for in the wind is snuff, the tobacco the boy’s uncle takes.

quiz.question: What does the little boy do when the east wind brings nothing?
options: He asks the Doctor to sail back home
He goes off to look for his uncle alone
He tells Jip to stop sniffing the wind
He cries again and says no one can find his uncle

feedback.zh: 东风来了，狗还是闻不到；小男孩失望极了，又哭起来，说好像谁都没法替他找到叔叔。
feedback.en: When the east wind brings no smell, the boy is terribly disappointed and cries again, saying that no one seems able to find his uncle.

grammar.excerpt: Tell him that when the wind changes to the West, I’ll find his uncle

focus.zh: Tell him that 后面是要转告的内容；that 从句里又套了一个 when 从句，交代「等风转向西边」这个前提。
focus.en: Tell him that introduces the message; inside it, the when-clause gives the condition: when the wind turns west.

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor tumbled out of bed and went to the rudder to steer the ship.

sentences.text: So the Doctor tumbled out of bed and went to the rudder to steer the ship.
sentences.zh: 于是医生一骨碌爬下床，走到船舵那儿去掌舵。

hints.zh: 一骨碌爬下床，形容匆忙、顾不上整齐。
hints.en: Tumbled out of bed: got up in a hurry, without care.

paragraphs.text: “Now I’ll go up to the front,” said Jip; “and you watch my nose—whichever way I point it, you turn the ship the same way. The man cannot be far off—with the smell as strong as this. And the wind’s all lovely and wet. Now watch me!”

sentences.text: “Now I’ll go up to the front,” said Jip; “and you watch my nose—whichever way I point it, you turn the ship the same way.
sentences.zh: 「现在我上船头去，」吉普说，「你盯着我的鼻子——它朝哪边指，你就把船往哪边转。

sentences.text: The man cannot be far off—with the smell as strong as this.
sentences.zh: 那人一定离得不远——味道这么冲。

sentences.text: And the wind’s all lovely and wet.
sentences.zh: 这风又舒服又潮湿。

sentences.text: Now watch me!”
sentences.zh: 好，看我的！」

hints.zh: 不管朝哪个方向；whichever 就是「无论哪一个」。
hints.en: Whichever way means no matter which direction: any way the nose points.

paragraphs.text: So all that morning Jip stood in the front part of the ship, sniffing the wind and pointing the way for the Doctor to steer; while all the animals and the little boy stood round with their eyes wide open, watching the dog in wonder.

sentences.text: So all that morning Jip stood in the front part of the ship, sniffing the wind and pointing the way for the Doctor to steer; while all the animals and the little boy stood round with their eyes wide open, watching the dog in wonder.
sentences.zh: 于是一整个上午，吉普都站在船头，一边嗅着风，一边指出方向让医生掌舵；而所有动物和小男孩都围在旁边，眼睛睁得大大的，惊奇地看着这条狗。

paragraphs.text: About lunch-time Jip asked Dab-Dab to tell the Doctor that he was getting worried and wanted to speak to him. So Dab-Dab went and fetched the Doctor from the other end of the ship and Jip said to him,

sentences.text: About lunch-time Jip asked Dab-Dab to tell the Doctor that he was getting worried and wanted to speak to him.
sentences.zh: 快到午饭时，吉普请达布达布去告诉医生，说他心里越来越不安，想跟医生说话。

sentences.text: So Dab-Dab went and fetched the Doctor from the other end of the ship and Jip said to him,
sentences.zh: 于是达布达布从船的另一头把医生请了来，吉普对他说：

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

paragraphs.text: “The boy’s uncle is starving. We must make the ship go as fast as we can.”

sentences.text: “The boy’s uncle is starving.
sentences.zh: 「小男孩的叔叔快饿死了。

sentences.text: We must make the ship go as fast as we can.”
sentences.zh: 我们得让船走得越快越好。」

paragraphs.text: “How do you know he is starving?” asked the Doctor.

sentences.text: “How do you know he is starving?” asked the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 「你怎么知道他要饿死了？」医生问。

paragraphs.text: “Because there is no other smell in the West wind but snuff,” said Jip. “If the man were cooking or eating food of any kind, I would be bound to smell it too. But he hasn’t even fresh water to drink. All he is taking is snuff—in large pinches. We are getting nearer to him all the time, because the smell grows stronger every minute. But make the ship go as fast as you can, for I am certain that the man is starving.”

sentences.text: “Because there is no other smell in the West wind but snuff,” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「因为西风里除了鼻烟味，再没有别的味道了，」吉普说。

sentences.text: “If the man were cooking or eating food of any kind, I would be bound to smell it too.
sentences.zh: 「要是那人在做饭，或者在吃什么东西，我肯定会闻到的。

sentences.text: But he hasn’t even fresh water to drink.
sentences.zh: 可他连一口清水都没得喝。

sentences.text: All he is taking is snuff—in large pinches.
sentences.zh: 他只吸鼻烟——而且是一大撮一大撮地吸。

sentences.text: We are getting nearer to him all the time, because the smell grows stronger every minute.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在离他越来越近，因为那味道每分钟都在变浓。

sentences.text: But make the ship go as fast as you can, for I am certain that the man is starving.”
sentences.zh: 不过还是让船走得越快越好，因为我敢肯定，那人快饿死了。」

hints.zh: be bound to 一定、必然会；I would be bound to smell it 就是「我一定会闻到」。
hints.en: Be bound to means certain to: I would be bound to smell it — I would certainly smell it.

hints.zh: 一大撮一大撮地；pinch 指用手指捏起来的那一点量。
hints.en: In large pinches: taking big pinches of snuff between finger and thumb.

introduction.zh: 风终于对了，可船还得有人指路。吉普站在船头，让医生照着它的鼻子转舵。快到中午，它忽然非要跟医生说句话不可——它闻出了什么？
introduction.en: The wind is right at last, but someone must show the ship the way. Jip stands at the front and points with his nose. Near lunch-time he suddenly asks for the Doctor. What has he smelt in the wind?

quiz.question: How does Jip show the Doctor which way to steer?
options: He stands by the rudder and pushes it himself
He calls out the names of the islands
He points his nose in that direction
He barks once for left and twice for right

feedback.zh: 吉普让医生盯住它的鼻子：鼻子朝哪边指，船就往哪边转。
feedback.en: Jip tells the Doctor to watch his nose: whichever way it points, the Doctor turns the ship the same way.

quiz.question: Why does Jip think the boy’s uncle is starving?
options: The west wind smells only of snuff, with no food or water in it
The man has not been seen for three days
The boy says his uncle never eats much
There is no food left on the ship

feedback.zh: 吉普的理由是气味：西风里除了鼻烟没有别的味道，那人在做饭或吃东西的话它一定会闻到，可他连清水都没有。
feedback.en: Jip’s reason is smell: there is no smell in the west wind but snuff, so the man is not cooking or eating — he has not even fresh water.

grammar.excerpt: If the man were cooking or eating food of any kind, I would be bound to smell it too

focus.zh: If 从句用 were、主句用 would，是与现在相反的假设：他此刻并没有在做饭，所以吉普闻不到食物味。
focus.en: Were in the if-clause and would in the main clause mark an unreal condition: he is not cooking now, so no food smell reaches Jip.

paragraphs.text: “All right,” said the Doctor; and he sent Dab-Dab to ask the swallows to pull the ship, the same as they had done when the pirates were chasing them.

sentences.text: “All right,” said the Doctor; and he sent Dab-Dab to ask the swallows to pull the ship, the same as they had done when the pirates were chasing them.
sentences.zh: 「好吧，」医生说；他打发达布达布去请燕子来拉船，就像当初海盗追他们时那样。

paragraphs.text: So the stout little birds came down and once more harnessed themselves to the ship.

sentences.text: So the stout little birds came down and once more harnessed themselves to the ship.
sentences.zh: 于是这些壮实的小鸟飞了下来，又一次把绳索套在自己身上，拉起了船。

hints.zh: 把挽具套在自己身上；这里指燕子像拉车的牲口一样套上绳索去拉船。
hints.en: They put the harness on themselves: the swallows were tied to the ship like animals pulling a cart.

paragraphs.text: And now the boat went bounding through the waves at a terrible speed. It went so fast that the fishes in the sea had to jump for their lives to get out of the way and not be run over.

sentences.text: And now the boat went bounding through the waves at a terrible speed.
sentences.zh: 这一下，小船在浪里飞跳着前进，快得吓人。

sentences.text: It went so fast that the fishes in the sea had to jump for their lives to get out of the way and not be run over.
sentences.zh: 它快得让海里的鱼不得不拼命跳开，免得被船撞上。

hints.zh: 为了保命、拼命；jump for their lives 就是「拼命跳开逃命」。
hints.en: For their lives means to save themselves: they jumped for their lives — they jumped to escape.

paragraphs.text: And all the animals got tremendously excited; and they gave up looking at Jip and turned to watch the sea in front, to spy out any land or islands where the starving man might be.

sentences.text: And all the animals got tremendously excited; and they gave up looking at Jip and turned to watch the sea in front, to spy out any land or islands where the starving man might be.
sentences.zh: 所有动物都兴奋极了；他们不再看吉普，转过头去盯着前方的海面，想找出那个快饿死的人可能在的陆地或岛屿。

hints.zh: 搜寻出、发现；spy out any land 就是「找出一块陆地」。
hints.en: Spy out means to make out or discover: to spy out any land — to find land.

paragraphs.text: But hour after hour went by and still the ship went rushing on, over the same flat, flat sea; and no land anywhere came in sight.

sentences.text: But hour after hour went by and still the ship went rushing on, over the same flat, flat sea; and no land anywhere came in sight.
sentences.zh: 可是一小时又一小时过去，船仍旧往前冲，掠过的还是那片平平的、平平的海；哪儿也不见陆地。

paragraphs.text: And now the animals gave up chattering and sat around silent, anxious and miserable. The little boy again grew sad. And on Jip’s face there was a worried look.

sentences.text: And now the animals gave up chattering and sat around silent, anxious and miserable.
sentences.zh: 这时候，动物们不再叽叽喳喳，都默默地坐着，又着急又难受。

sentences.text: The little boy again grew sad.
sentences.zh: 小男孩又伤心起来。

sentences.text: And on Jip’s face there was a worried look.
sentences.zh: 吉普的脸上也露出忧虑的神色。

paragraphs.text: At last, late in the afternoon, just as the sun was going down, the owl, Too-Too, who was perched on the tip of the mast, suddenly startled them all by crying out at the top of his voice,

sentences.text: At last, late in the afternoon, just as the sun was going down, the owl, Too-Too, who was perched on the tip of the mast, suddenly startled them all by crying out at the top of his voice,
sentences.zh: 终于，在下午晚些时候，太阳正要落下去，停在桅杆顶上的猫头鹰图图忽然扯着嗓子大叫起来，把大家都吓了一跳：

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰，眼力好。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor’s owl, who has sharp eyes.

paragraphs.text: “Jip! Jip! I see a great, great rock in front of us—look—way out there where the sky and the water meet. See the sun shine on it—like gold! Is the smell coming from there?”

sentences.text: “Jip!
sentences.zh: 「吉普！

sentences.text: Jip!
sentences.zh: 吉普！

sentences.text: I see a great, great rock in front of us—look—way out there where the sky and the water meet.
sentences.zh: 我看见前面有一块好大好大的礁石——你看——就在很远很远、天和水相接的地方。

sentences.text: See the sun shine on it—like gold!
sentences.zh: 你瞧太阳照在它上面——像金子一样！

sentences.text: Is the smell coming from there?”
sentences.zh: 那味道是从那儿来的吗？」

introduction.zh: 船飞快地掠过海面，动物们都盯着前方，想找到一块陆地。可一小时一小时过去，海上还是空空的。天快黑时，桅杆顶上忽然传来图图的喊声。
introduction.en: The swallows pull the ship and it races over the waves. All the animals watch the sea for land, but hour after hour there is nothing. Then, near sunset, Too-Too cries out from the top of the mast. What has he seen?

quiz.question: Why do the swallows come down to the ship?
options: To look for land from high in the sky
To bring news of the missing man
To rest on the mast for a while
To pull the ship so that it goes faster

feedback.zh: 医生听了吉普的话，打发达布达布去请燕子拉船，就像当初海盗追他们时那样。
feedback.en: The Doctor sends Dab-Dab to ask the swallows to pull the ship, just as they did when the pirates were chasing them.

quiz.question: What does Too-Too see far away?
options: A whale jumping out of the sea
A huge rock shining like gold where sky and water meet
A small island covered with trees
Another ship sailing towards them

feedback.zh: 图图喊大家看前面：天和水相接的地方有一块好大好大的礁石，太阳照在上面像金子一样。
feedback.en: Too-Too calls out that there is a great, great rock ahead, far off where sky and water meet, with the sun shining on it like gold.

grammar.excerpt: It went so fast that the fishes in the sea had to jump for their lives

focus.zh: so fast that 说「快到什么程度、结果怎样」；that 后面引出结果，不是目的。
focus.en: So fast that gives the result of the speed: the fishes had to jump out of the way.

title.en: A Rock as Big as a Field

paragraphs.text: And Jip called back,

sentences.text: And Jip called back,
sentences.zh: 吉普在那边回答：

paragraphs.text: “Yes. That’s it. That is where the man is.—At last, at last!”

sentences.text: “Yes.
That’s it.
sentences.zh: 就是这儿。

sentences.text: That is where the man is.—At last, at last!”
sentences.zh: 那人就在这儿。——总算，总算找到了！」

paragraphs.text: And when they got nearer they could see that the rock was very large—as large as a big field. No trees grew on it, no grass—nothing. The great rock was as smooth and as bare as the back of a tortoise.

sentences.text: And when they got nearer they could see that the rock was very large—as large as a big field.
sentences.zh: 等他们靠近些，就看出那块礁石非常大——大得像一整片田野。

sentences.text: No trees grew on it, no grass—nothing.
sentences.zh: 上面不长树，也不长草——什么都没有。

sentences.text: The great rock was as smooth and as bare as the back of a tortoise.
sentences.zh: 这块大礁石又光又秃，活像乌龟的背。

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor sailed the ship right round the rock. But nowhere on it could a man be seen. All the animals screwed up their eyes and looked as hard as they could; and John Dolittle got a telescope from downstairs.

sentences.text: Then the Doctor sailed the ship right round the rock.
sentences.zh: 接着，医生驾着船绕着礁石转了一整圈。

sentences.text: But nowhere on it could a man be seen.
sentences.zh: 可上面哪儿也看不见人。

sentences.text: All the animals screwed up their eyes and looked as hard as they could; and John Dolittle got a telescope from downstairs.
sentences.zh: 动物们都眯起眼睛，使劲地看；约翰·杜立德从楼下拿来了一架望远镜。

hints.zh: 眯起眼睛（好使劲看清远处的东西）。
hints.en: Screwed up their eyes: narrowed them to see better.

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，就是杜立德医生。
hints.en: John Dolittle — Doctor Dolittle himself.

paragraphs.text: But not one living thing could they spy—not even a gull, nor a star-fish, nor a shred of sea-weed.

sentences.text: But not one living thing could they spy—not even a gull, nor a star-fish, nor a shred of sea-weed.
sentences.zh: 可他们连一个活物也没瞧见——连一只海鸥、一只海星、一片海草都没有。

hints.zh: 一丝、一片；a shred of sea-weed 就是「一片海草」，用来说连这么点东西都没有。
hints.en: A shred of means the smallest scrap: not a shred of sea-weed — not even a tiny bit of it.

paragraphs.text: They all stood still and listened, straining their ears for any sound. But the only noise they heard was the gentle lapping of the little waves against the sides of their ship.

sentences.text: They all stood still and listened, straining their ears for any sound.
sentences.zh: 他们全都站住不动，侧耳细听，想抓住一点声响。

sentences.text: But the only noise they heard was the gentle lapping of the little waves against the sides of their ship.
sentences.zh: 可他们听到的唯一声音，是小浪轻轻拍打船舷的水声。

hints.zh: 竖起耳朵使劲听，唯恐漏掉一点声音。
hints.en: Straining their ears: listening as hard as they could.

paragraphs.text: Then they all started calling, “Hulloa, there!—HULLOA!” till their voices were hoarse. But only the echo came back from the rock.

sentences.text: Then they all started calling, “Hulloa, there!—HULLOA!” till their voices were hoarse.
sentences.zh: 于是大家一齐喊起来：「喂——那边！——喂——」一直喊到嗓子都哑了。

sentences.text: But only the echo came back from the rock.
sentences.zh: 可从礁石那边回来的，只有回声。

hints.zh: 「喂！」的喊声，hullo、halloa 的旧拼法，用来招呼远处的人。
hints.en: Hulloa is an old spelling of hullo/halloa, used to call to someone far away.

paragraphs.text: And the little boy burst into tears and said,

sentences.text: And the little boy burst into tears and said,
sentences.zh: 小男孩放声大哭，说：

paragraphs.text: “I am afraid I shall never see my uncle any more! What shall I tell them when I get home!”

sentences.text: “I am afraid I shall never see my uncle any more!
sentences.zh: 「我怕是再也见不到我叔叔了！

sentences.text: What shall I tell them when I get home!”
sentences.zh: 等我回了家，该怎么跟他们说呀！」

paragraphs.text: But Jip called to the Doctor,

sentences.text: But Jip called to the Doctor,
sentences.zh: 可吉普冲着医生喊：

paragraphs.text: “He must be there—he must—he must! The smell goes on no further. He must be there, I tell you! Sail the ship close to the rock and let me jump out on it.”

sentences.text: “He must be there—he must—he must!
sentences.zh: 「他一定在那儿——一定——一定在！

sentences.text: The smell goes on no further.
sentences.zh: 气味到这儿就不再往前了。

sentences.text: He must be there, I tell you!
sentences.zh: 他一定在那儿，我跟你说！

sentences.text: Sail the ship close to the rock and let me jump out on it.”
sentences.zh: 把船靠到礁石边上，让我跳上去。」

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor brought the ship as close as he could and let down the anchor. Then he and Jip got out of the ship on to the rock.

sentences.text: So the Doctor brought the ship as close as he could and let down the anchor.
sentences.zh: 于是医生把船尽量靠过去，抛下了锚。

sentences.text: Then he and Jip got out of the ship on to the rock.
sentences.zh: 然后他和吉普下船，上了礁石。

introduction.zh: 船靠近了那块大石头：它大得像一片田野，光溜溜的，连草都不长。大家绕着它转了一圈又一圈，喊得嗓子都哑了。要是那个人真在这里，他能藏在哪儿？
introduction.en: The ship comes close to a rock as big as a field. It is smooth and bare, with nothing growing on it. The animals sail round and round it and call until their voices are hoarse. If the man is really here, where can he hide?

quiz.question: What is the rock like?
options: Very large, smooth and bare, with nothing growing on it
Covered with grass and small trees
Small, sharp and black
Full of birds and sea-weed

feedback.zh: 原文说礁石大得像一片田野，不长树也不长草，又光又秃，像乌龟的背。
feedback.en: The rock is as large as a big field, with no trees and no grass; it is as smooth and bare as the back of a tortoise.

quiz.question: What happens when they all call out to the rock?
options: Jip jumps into the water
The birds on the rock fly away
Only the echo comes back from the rock
A man’s voice answers from a cave

feedback.zh: 大家喊到嗓子都哑了，可礁石那边回来的只有回声，没有一个人应答。
feedback.en: They call until their voices are hoarse, but only the echo comes back from the rock.

grammar.excerpt: The great rock was as smooth and as bare as the back of a tortoise

focus.zh: 两个 as 中间放形容词：礁石的光滑、光秃，程度和乌龟背一样；第二个 as 后面是比较对象。
focus.en: As + adjective + as compares two things: the rock is as smooth and bare as a tortoise’s back.

title.en: Jip Sits Down by a Hole

paragraphs.text: Jip at once put his nose down close to the ground and began to run all over the place. Up and down he went, back and forth—zig-zagging, twisting, doubling and turning. And everywhere he went, the Doctor ran behind him, close at his heels—till he was terribly out of breath.

sentences.text: Jip at once put his nose down close to the ground and began to run all over the place.
sentences.zh: 吉普立刻把鼻子贴近地面，开始在礁石上到处跑。

sentences.text: Up and down he went, back and forth—zig-zagging, twisting, doubling and turning.
sentences.zh: 他跑上跑下，来来回回——忽左忽右，弯来绕去，折返又转身。

sentences.text: And everywhere he went, the Doctor ran behind him, close at his heels—till he was terribly out of breath.
sentences.zh: 不管他跑到哪儿，医生都紧跟在后面，贴着他的脚后跟——直到累得上气不接下气。

hints.zh: 走之字形，忽左忽右地拐着跑。
hints.en: Zig-zagging: running in sharp turns, first one way then the other.

hints.zh: 紧跟在脚后跟，形容跟得非常近。
hints.en: At his heels: right behind him, following closely.

hints.zh: 上气不接下气，喘不过气来。
hints.en: Out of breath: breathing hard after running.

paragraphs.text: At last Jip let out a great bark and sat down. And when the Doctor came running up to him, he found the dog staring into a big, deep hole in the middle of the rock.

sentences.text: At last Jip let out a great bark and sat down.
sentences.zh: 最后，吉普大叫了一声，坐了下来。

sentences.text: And when the Doctor came running up to him, he found the dog staring into a big, deep hole in the middle of the rock.
sentences.zh: 医生跑上前去，发现这条狗正盯着礁石中间一个又大又深的窟窿。

paragraphs.text: “The boy’s uncle is down there,” said Jip quietly. “No wonder those silly eagles couldn’t see him!—It takes a dog to find a man.”

sentences.text: “The boy’s uncle is down there,” said Jip quietly.
sentences.zh: 「小男孩的叔叔就在下面，」吉普轻声说。

sentences.text: “No wonder those silly eagles couldn’t see him!—It takes a dog to find a man.”
sentences.zh: 「难怪那些傻鹰看不见他！——找个人还得靠狗。」

hints.zh: 难怪；No wonder those silly eagles couldn’t see him 就是「难怪那些傻鹰看不见他」。
hints.en: No wonder means it is not surprising: no wonder the eagles could not see him.

hints.zh: 鹰。先前是它们在高空帮忙找人，从天上看当然看不见洞里的人。
hints.en: Eagles: earlier the eagles helped search from high in the air, so they could not see a man down in a hole.

paragraphs.text: So the Doctor got down into the hole, which seemed to be a kind of cave, or tunnel, running a long way under the ground. Then he struck a match and started to make his way along the dark passage with Jip following behind.

sentences.text: So the Doctor got down into the hole, which seemed to be a kind of cave, or tunnel, running a long way under the ground.
sentences.zh: 于是医生下到那个洞里——它像是一个洞穴，或者一条隧道，在地底下延伸了很远。

sentences.text: Then he struck a match and started to make his way along the dark passage with Jip following behind.
sentences.zh: 然后他划着一根火柴，沿着黑暗的通道往前走，吉普跟在后面。

hints.zh: 划着一根火柴；strike a match 是固定说法，不用 burn。
hints.en: Struck a match: lighted one by rubbing it; strike is the usual verb with match.

paragraphs.text: The Doctor’s match soon went out; and he had to strike another and another and another.

sentences.text: The Doctor’s match soon went out; and he had to strike another and another and another.
sentences.zh: 医生的火柴很快就灭了；他只好划一根，又划一根，再划一根。

paragraphs.text: At last the passage came to an end; and the Doctor found himself in a kind of tiny room with walls of rock.

sentences.text: At last the passage came to an end; and the Doctor found himself in a kind of tiny room with walls of rock.
sentences.zh: 终于，通道到了尽头；医生发现自己来到了一个小房间，四壁都是岩石。

paragraphs.text: And there, in the middle of the room, his head resting on his arms, lay a man with very red hair—fast asleep!

sentences.text: And there, in the middle of the room, his head resting on his arms, lay a man with very red hair—fast asleep!
sentences.zh: 就在房间正中躺着一个人，头枕在胳膊上，一头火红的头发——睡得正沉！

paragraphs.text: Jip went up and sniffed at something lying on the ground beside him. The Doctor stooped and picked it up. It was an enormous snuff-box. And it was full of Black Rappee!

sentences.text: Jip went up and sniffed at something lying on the ground beside him.
sentences.zh: 吉普走上前，嗅了嗅他身边地上的什么东西。

sentences.text: The Doctor stooped and picked it up.
sentences.zh: 医生弯下腰，把它捡了起来。

sentences.text: It was an enormous snuff-box.
sentences.zh: 那是一个大得不得了的鼻烟盒。

sentences.text: And it was full of Black Rappee!
sentences.zh: 里面装满了黑拉皮鼻烟！

introduction.zh: 吉普一上礁石，鼻子就贴着地面到处乱跑，医生跟在后头追得直喘。忽然它大叫一声，就地坐下，再也不动了。它死死盯着的那个黑窟窿，底下会有什么？
introduction.en: Jip jumps onto the rock and runs everywhere with his nose to the ground, while the Doctor runs after him out of breath. Then the dog gives one great bark and sits down. He is staring into a deep, dark hole. What is down there?

quiz.question: Why does Jip bark and sit down on the rock?
options: He has found the snuff-box lying on the rock
He has found a deep hole in the middle of the rock
He is too tired to run any further
He wants the Doctor to take him back to the ship

feedback.zh: 吉普在礁石上到处跑，最后大叫一声坐下；医生跑过去，看见它正盯着礁石中间一个大深洞。
feedback.en: Jip runs all over the rock, then barks and sits down; the Doctor finds him staring into a big, deep hole in the middle of the rock.

quiz.question: Where does the Doctor find the man?
options: Asleep on top of the rock in the sun
In the ship’s cabin under a blanket
Behind a big stone on the shore
In a tiny rock room at the end of a dark passage

feedback.zh: 通道尽头是一个四壁是岩石的小房间，一个人枕着胳膊躺在那里，一头红发，睡得很沉。
feedback.en: At the end of the passage the Doctor finds a tiny room with rock walls, and a red-haired man asleep in the middle of it.

grammar.excerpt: which seemed to be a kind of cave, or tunnel, running a long way under the ground

focus.zh: 逗号后的 which 不限定、只补充说明这个洞像什么；后面 running 短语再补充洞在地下延伸很远。
focus.en: The which-clause after a comma adds information about the hole; the running-phrase then says how far it goes.

paragraphs.text: Gently then—very gently, the Doctor woke the man up.

sentences.text: Gently then—very gently, the Doctor woke the man up.
sentences.zh: 于是，医生轻轻地——非常轻地，把那个人摇醒了。

paragraphs.text: But just at that moment the match went out again. And the man thought it was Ben Ali coming back, and he began to punch the Doctor in the dark.

sentences.text: But just at that moment the match went out again.
sentences.zh: 可就在这时，火柴又灭了。

sentences.text: And the man thought it was Ben Ali coming back, and he began to punch the Doctor in the dark.
sentences.zh: 那个人以为是本·阿里回来了，就在黑暗里挥拳打医生。

hints.zh: 本·阿里，海盗头子，这条海盗船原来的主人。
hints.en: Ben Ali, the pirate captain whose ship this was.

paragraphs.text: But when John Dolittle told him who it was, and that he had his little nephew safe on his ship, the man was tremendously glad, and said he was sorry he had fought the Doctor. He had not hurt him much though—because it was too dark to punch properly. Then he gave the Doctor a pinch of snuff.

sentences.text: But when John Dolittle told him who it was, and that he had his little nephew safe on his ship, the man was tremendously glad, and said he was sorry he had fought the Doctor.
sentences.zh: 可是等约翰·杜立德告诉他来的人是谁，又说他的小外甥平平安安地待在船上，那个人高兴极了，还说自己很抱歉跟医生动了手。

sentences.text: He had not hurt him much though—because it was too dark to punch properly.
sentences.zh: 不过他没把医生打伤多少——因为天太黑，拳头打不准。

sentences.text: Then he gave the Doctor a pinch of snuff.
sentences.zh: 然后他给了医生一撮鼻烟。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，就是杜立德医生，那位会给动物看病的人。
hints.en: John Dolittle: Doctor Dolittle, the man who can talk to animals.

hints.zh: 一撮鼻烟：把烟粉吸进鼻子里提神的东西。
hints.en: A pinch of snuff: powdered tobacco sniffed up the nose.

paragraphs.text: And the man told how the Barbary Dragon had put him on to this rock and left him there, when he wouldn’t promise to become a pirate; and how he used to sleep down in this hole because there was no house on the rock to keep him warm.

sentences.text: And the man told how the Barbary Dragon had put him on to this rock and left him there, when he wouldn’t promise to become a pirate; and how he used to sleep down in this hole because there was no house on the rock to keep him warm.
sentences.zh: 那个人讲起「巴巴里巨龙」怎样把他弄到这块岩石上扔下不管，因为他不肯答应去做海盗；还讲起他过去总睡在这个洞里，因为岩石上没有房子给他挡风御寒。

hints.zh: 「巴巴里巨龙」，海盗本·阿里的诨名。
hints.en: The Barbary Dragon: the nickname of the pirate Ben Ali.

paragraphs.text: And then he said,

sentences.text: And then he said,
sentences.zh: 然后他说：

paragraphs.text: “For four days I have had nothing to eat or drink. I have lived on snuff.”

sentences.text: “For four days I have had nothing to eat or drink.
sentences.zh: 「我已经四天没吃没喝了。

sentences.text: I have lived on snuff.”
sentences.zh: 我就靠鼻烟活着。」

paragraphs.text: “There you are!” said Jip. “What did I tell you?”

sentences.text: “There you are!” said Jip.
sentences.zh: 「你看吧！」吉普说。

sentences.text: “What did I tell you?”
sentences.zh: 「我跟你说过什么？」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

paragraphs.text: So they struck some more matches and made their way out through the passage into the daylight; and the Doctor hurried the man down to the boat to get some soup.

sentences.text: So they struck some more matches and made their way out through the passage into the daylight; and the Doctor hurried the man down to the boat to get some soup.
sentences.zh: 于是他们又划了几根火柴，顺着通道走到外面的天光下；医生催着那个人下到小船里，好让他喝点汤。

paragraphs.text: When the animals and the little boy saw the Doctor and Jip coming back to the ship with a red-headed man, they began to cheer and yell and dance about the boat. And the swallows up above started whistling at the top of their voices—thousands and millions of them—to show that they too were glad that the boy’s brave uncle had been found. The noise they made was so great that sailors far out at sea thought that a terrible storm was coming. “Hark to that gale howling in the East!” they said.

sentences.text: When the animals and the little boy saw the Doctor and Jip coming back to the ship with a red-headed man, they began to cheer and yell and dance about the boat.
sentences.zh: 动物们和小男孩看见医生和吉普带着一个红头发的男人回到船上，就欢呼大叫，围着船跳起舞来。

sentences.text: And the swallows up above started whistling at the top of their voices—thousands and millions of them—to show that they too were glad that the boy’s brave uncle had been found.
sentences.zh: 头顶的燕子也放开嗓子尖声叫起来——成千上万只——表示它们也一样高兴：男孩那位勇敢的舅舅找到了。

sentences.text: The noise they made was so great that sailors far out at sea thought that a terrible storm was coming.
sentences.zh: 它们闹出的声音太大，连远在海上的水手都以为一场可怕的风暴要来了。

sentences.text: “Hark to that gale howling in the East!” they said.
sentences.zh: 「听东边那阵狂风在吼！」他们说。

hints.zh: hark 是旧时「听」的说法，hark to 就是「听那……」；gale 指大风。
hints.en: Hark is an old word for listen: “listen to that gale.”

introduction.zh: 追着地道走到尽头，医生终于在黑洞里摸到了那个失踪的渔夫。他轻轻把人摇醒，火柴却在这时又灭了。黑暗里忽然挥来一双拳头——那人以为回来的是谁？
introduction.en: At the end of the tunnel the Doctor finds the missing uncle at last. He wakes him very gently. Then the match goes out, and in the dark two fists swing at the Doctor. Who does the man think has come back?

quiz.question: Why did the man begin to punch the Doctor in the dark?
options: He was angry because the Doctor woke him.
He wanted the Doctor’s matches.
He thought Ben Ali had come back.

feedback.zh: 火柴灭了，那人以为回来的是本·阿里，所以朝黑暗里的人挥拳，并不知道对方是医生。
feedback.en: The match went out and the man thought Ben Ali was coming back, so he hit out in the dark without knowing who was there.

quiz.question: What had the man been living on for four days?
options: Sea water
Snuff
Soup and bread

feedback.zh: 他说四天没吃没喝，「I have lived on snuff」——只靠鼻烟撑着。
feedback.en: He says he has had nothing to eat or drink for four days and has lived on snuff.

grammar.excerpt: it was too dark to punch properly

focus.zh: too dark to punch 是「太黑，打不准」：too + 形容词 + to do 本身含否定，不能读成「太黑去打」。
focus.en: Too dark to punch means it was so dark that he could not punch well; too + adjective + to do carries the negative idea.

paragraphs.text: And Jip was awfully proud of himself—though he tried hard not to look conceited. When Dab-Dab came to him and said, “Jip, I had no idea you were so clever!” he just tossed his head and answered,

sentences.text: And Jip was awfully proud of himself—though he tried hard not to look conceited.
sentences.zh: 吉普得意极了——尽管他竭力不露出自命不凡的样子。

sentences.text: When Dab-Dab came to him and said, “Jip, I had no idea you were so clever!” he just tossed his head and answered,
sentences.zh: 达布达布走过来对他说：「吉普，我真没想到你这么聪明！」他只是把头一扬，回答说：

hints.zh: awfully proud 是「得意得不得了」；awfully 在这里等于 very，不是「可怕地」。
hints.en: Awfully proud means very proud; here awfully simply means very.

hints.zh: 把头一扬：一副不以为然、又有点得意的样子。
hints.en: Tossed his head: jerked his head up, looking cool and rather pleased.

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

paragraphs.text: “Oh, that’s nothing special. But it takes a dog to find a man, you know. Birds are no good for a game like that.”

sentences.text: “Oh, that’s nothing special.
sentences.zh: 「哦，这没什么了不起的。

sentences.text: But it takes a dog to find a man, you know.
sentences.zh: 不过你知道，要找一个人，非得狗才行。

sentences.text: Birds are no good for a game like that.”
sentences.zh: 干这种事，鸟是不行的。」

paragraphs.text: Then the Doctor asked the red-haired fisherman where his home was. And when he had told him, the Doctor asked the swallows to guide the ship there first.

sentences.text: Then the Doctor asked the red-haired fisherman where his home was.
sentences.zh: 接着医生问那个红头发的渔夫家在哪里。

sentences.text: And when he had told him, the Doctor asked the swallows to guide the ship there first.
sentences.zh: 等他说了之后，医生就请燕子先把船领到那儿去。

paragraphs.text: And when they had come to the land which the man had spoken of, they saw a little fishing-town at the foot of a rocky mountain; and the man pointed out the house where he lived.

sentences.text: And when they had come to the land which the man had spoken of, they saw a little fishing-town at the foot of a rocky mountain; and the man pointed out the house where he lived.
sentences.zh: 等他们到了那个人说的那片陆地，只见一座多石的山脚下有个小小的渔镇；那个人指出了他住的那所房子。

paragraphs.text: And while they were letting down the anchor, the little boy’s mother (who was also the man’s sister) came running down to the shore to meet them, laughing and crying at the same time. She had been sitting on a hill for twenty days, watching the sea and waiting for them to return.

sentences.text: And while they were letting down the anchor, the little boy’s mother (who was also the man’s sister) came running down to the shore to meet them, laughing and crying at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他们正在抛锚的时候，小男孩的母亲（她也是那个人的姐姐）从岸上跑下来迎接他们，一边笑一边哭。

sentences.text: She had been sitting on a hill for twenty days, watching the sea and waiting for them to return.
sentences.zh: 她在山上坐了二十天，望着大海，等他们回来。

hints.zh: 抛锚：把锚放下，让船停住。
hints.en: Letting down the anchor: lowering it to stop the ship.

paragraphs.text: And she kissed the Doctor many times, so that he giggled and blushed like a school-girl. And she tried to kiss Jip too; but he ran away and hid inside the ship.

sentences.text: And she kissed the Doctor many times, so that he giggled and blushed like a school-girl.
sentences.zh: 她亲了医生好多下，弄得他像女学生一样咯咯笑，脸都红了。

sentences.text: And she tried to kiss Jip too; but he ran away and hid inside the ship.
sentences.zh: 她还想亲吉普；可吉普跑开了，躲进船里。

paragraphs.text: “It’s a silly business, this kissing,” he said. “I don’t hold by it. Let her go and kiss Gub-Gub—if she must kiss something.”

sentences.text: “It’s a silly business, this kissing,” he said.
sentences.zh: 「亲来亲去这种事，真是傻气，」他说。

sentences.text: “I don’t hold by it.
sentences.zh: 「我可不赞成这一套。

sentences.text: Let her go and kiss Gub-Gub—if she must kiss something.”
sentences.zh: 要是她非得亲点什么，就让她去亲咕咕吧。」

hints.zh: hold by 是旧时的说法，「赞成、认同」；I don’t hold by it 就是「我不吃这一套」。
hints.en: Hold by is an old way of saying approve of; I don’t hold by it means I don’t approve of it.

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s little pig.

paragraphs.text: The fisherman and his sister didn’t want the Doctor to go away again in a hurry. They begged him to spend a few days with them. So John Dolittle and his animals had to stay at their house a whole Saturday and Sunday and half of Monday.

sentences.text: The fisherman and his sister didn’t want the Doctor to go away again in a hurry.
sentences.zh: 渔夫和他的姐姐不愿医生这么快就又走。

sentences.text: They begged him to spend a few days with them.
sentences.zh: 他们求他在他们家待几天。

sentences.text: So John Dolittle and his animals had to stay at their house a whole Saturday and Sunday and half of Monday.
sentences.zh: 于是约翰·杜立德和他的动物们只好在他们家待了整整一个星期六、一个星期天，还有半个星期一。

introduction.zh: 吉普立了大功，却努力装出一脸不在乎。船头一转，朝着红头发渔夫说的地方开去。山脚下的小镇岸边，有个女人又笑又哭地朝船跑来——她在那儿已经等了多久？
introduction.en: Jip has done something clever, and he tries hard not to look pleased with himself. Then the ship turns towards the red-haired fisherman’s town. On the shore a woman runs towards them, laughing and crying at once. How long has she been waiting?

quiz.question: What does Jip say is needed to find a man?
options: A dog
A bird
A fast ship

feedback.zh: 吉普说「it takes a dog to find a man」，还说鸟干这种事不行——它把功劳都算在狗身上。
feedback.en: Jip says it takes a dog to find a man, and that birds are no good for a game like that.

quiz.question: How long had the little boy’s mother been waiting on the hill?
options: Four days
Two days
Twenty days

feedback.zh: 原文说她在山上坐了二十天，一直望着海，等他们回来。
feedback.en: She had been sitting on a hill for twenty days, watching the sea and waiting for them to return.

grammar.excerpt: the Doctor asked the swallows to guide the ship there first

focus.zh: asked the swallows to guide 是 ask + 宾语 + to do：请燕子去领航，to 后面用动词原形。
focus.en: Asked the swallows to guide follows ask + object + to do: he asked the birds to lead the way.

paragraphs.text: And all the little boys of the fishing-village went down to the beach and pointed at the great ship anchored there, and said to one another in whispers,

sentences.text: And all the little boys of the fishing-village went down to the beach and pointed at the great ship anchored there, and said to one another in whispers,
sentences.zh: 渔村里的小男孩们都跑到海滩上，指着停在那儿的大船，小声地你一句我一句：

paragraphs.text: “Look! That was a pirate-ship—Ben Ali’s—the most terrible pirate that ever sailed the Seven Seas! That old gentleman with the high hat, who’s staying up at Mrs. Trevelyan’s, he took the ship away from The Barbary Dragon—and made him into a farmer. Who’d have thought it of him—him so gentle-like and all!... Look at the great red sails! Ain’t she the wicked-looking ship—and fast?—My!”

sentences.text: “Look!
That was a pirate-ship—Ben Ali’s—the most terrible pirate that ever sailed the Seven Seas!
sentences.zh: 那是条海盗船——本·阿里的——是古往今来航行七大洋最可怕的海盗！

sentences.text: That old gentleman with the high hat, who’s staying up at Mrs.
sentences.zh: 那位戴高礼帽的老先生，就住在特里维廉太太

sentences.text: Trevelyan’s, he took the ship away from The Barbary Dragon—and made him into a farmer.
sentences.zh: 家——他把船从「巴巴里巨龙」手里夺了过来——还把那家伙变成了农夫。

sentences.text: Who’d have thought it of him—him so gentle-like and all!...
sentences.zh: 谁能想到他会干这种事——他看上去那么斯文，那么和气！……

sentences.text: Look at the great red sails!
sentences.zh: 瞧那大红帆！

sentences.text: Ain’t she the wicked-looking ship—and fast?—My!”
sentences.zh: 这条船瞧着一副凶相——还跑得飞快？——我的天！」

hints.zh: 「七大洋」，旧时对全世界海洋的统称。
hints.en: The Seven Seas: an old name for all the oceans of the world.

hints.zh: 特里维廉太太家：她在渔夫镇出租房间，医生就住在那儿。
hints.en: Mrs. Trevelyan’s: she lets rooms in the town, and the Doctor is staying there.

hints.zh: 把海盗变成了农夫：船被夺走，他只能上岸种地。
hints.en: Made him into a farmer: with his ship gone, the pirate had to farm for a living.

hints.zh: ain’t 是 isn’t 的土话说法；这里是感叹：「这条船多凶啊！」
hints.en: Ain’t is a folksy way of saying isn’t; here it is an exclamation: “isn’t she a fierce-looking ship!”

paragraphs.text: All those two days and a half that the Doctor stayed at the little fishing-town the people kept asking him out to teas and luncheons and dinners and parties; all the ladies sent him boxes of flowers and candies; and the village-band played tunes under his window every night.

sentences.text: All those two days and a half that the Doctor stayed at the little fishing-town the people kept asking him out to teas and luncheons and dinners and parties; all the ladies sent him boxes of flowers and candies; and the village-band played tunes under his window every night.
sentences.zh: 医生在那个小渔镇待的两天半里，人们不停地请他出去喝茶、赴午宴、吃晚饭、参加聚会；太太们纷纷送来一盒盒鲜花和糖果；村里的乐队每天晚上都在他窗下奏曲子。

hints.zh: tea 指下午茶点，luncheon 是正式的午宴，都比 dinner 轻。
hints.en: Teas are light afternoon meals and luncheons are formal midday meals.

paragraphs.text: At last the Doctor said,

sentences.text: At last the Doctor said,
sentences.zh: 最后医生说：

paragraphs.text: “Good people, I must go home now. You have really been most kind. I shall always remember it. But I must go home—for I have things to do.”

sentences.text: “Good people, I must go home now.
sentences.zh: 「好心的人们，我现在得回家了。

sentences.text: You have really been most kind.
sentences.zh: 你们真是太好了。

sentences.text: I shall always remember it.
sentences.zh: 我会永远记得这份情意。

sentences.text: But I must go home—for I have things to do.”
sentences.zh: 可我必须回家——因为我还有事情要做。」

paragraphs.text: Then, just as the Doctor was about to leave, the Mayor of the town came down the street and a lot of other people in grand clothes with him. And the Mayor stopped before the house where the Doctor was living; and everybody in the village gathered round to see what was going to happen.

sentences.text: Then, just as the Doctor was about to leave, the Mayor of the town came down the street and a lot of other people in grand clothes with him.
sentences.zh: 后来，就在医生正要动身的时候，镇长沿着大街走来，身边还跟着许多穿着体面衣服的人。

sentences.text: And the Mayor stopped before the house where the Doctor was living; and everybody in the village gathered round to see what was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 镇长在医生住的那所房子前停下；村里的人都围拢过来，想看看要出什么事。

paragraphs.text: After six page-boys had blown on shining trumpets to make the people stop talking, the Doctor came out on to the steps and the Mayor spoke.

sentences.text: After six page-boys had blown on shining trumpets to make the people stop talking, the Doctor came out on to the steps and the Mayor spoke.
sentences.zh: 六个小侍童吹响锃亮的喇叭，让人群安静下来之后，医生走到台阶上，镇长开口讲话了。

hints.zh: page-boy 是穿号衣的小听差，仪式上吹号、跑腿的少年。
hints.en: Page-boys were young servants in uniform who ran errands and played trumpets at ceremonies.

introduction.zh: 渔村的孩子们挤在海滩上，小声议论那条红帆大船和戴高礼帽的老先生。这两天半里，镇上的人争着请医生喝茶吃饭。就在他要走时，镇长带着一群人来了——他们想干什么？
introduction.en: The village boys whisper about the red-sailed ship and the old gentleman in the high hat. For two days and a half the town feeds the Doctor and sends him flowers. Then, just as he is leaving, the Mayor arrives with men in fine clothes. What do they want?

quiz.question: What did the townspeople do while the Doctor was staying there?
options: They stayed away from him.
They kept inviting him to teas, dinners and parties.
They asked him to take them out to sea.

feedback.zh: 原文说人们不断请他喝茶、赴午宴、参加聚会，太太们送花送糖，乐队每晚在他窗下演奏。
feedback.en: People kept asking him out to teas, luncheons, dinners and parties, the ladies sent flowers and candies, and the band played under his window.

quiz.question: Why did the six page-boys blow on their trumpets?
options: To make the people stop talking
To welcome the ship
To call the children home

feedback.zh: 原文说六个小侍童吹喇叭，是为了让众人安静下来，之后医生才走到台阶上。
feedback.en: The page-boys blew their trumpets to make the people stop talking before the Doctor came out.

grammar.excerpt: That old gentleman with the high hat, who’s staying up at Mrs. Trevelyan’s

focus.zh: who’s staying… 是逗号隔开的非限制性定语从句，补充说明那位老先生住在哪儿；主句的主语是后面的 he。
focus.en: Who’s staying up at Mrs. Trevelyan’s is a non-restrictive relative clause, set off by commas; the main clause still needs its own subject, he.

paragraphs.text: “Doctor John Dolittle,” said he: “It is a great pleasure for me to present to the man who rid the seas of the Dragon of Barbary this little token from the grateful people of our worthy Town.”

sentences.text: “Doctor John Dolittle,” said he: “It is a great pleasure for me to present to the man who rid the seas of the Dragon of Barbary this little token from the grateful people of our worthy Town.”
sentences.zh: 「约翰·杜立德医生，」他说，「能代表我们这座可敬的镇子里满怀感激的百姓，把这份小小的纪念品献给这位为海上除掉了巴巴里巨龙的人，我深感荣幸。」

hints.zh: 纪念品、表示心意的小东西，不是「代币」。
hints.en: A token here is a small gift that stands for thanks, not a coin.

hints.zh: rid A of B：把 B 从 A 里清除掉；这里说医生为海上除掉了那个海盗。
hints.en: Rid the seas of him: clear him out of the seas for good.

paragraphs.text: And the Mayor took from his pocket a little tissue-paper packet, and opening it, he handed to the Doctor a perfectly beautiful watch with real diamonds in the back.

sentences.text: And the Mayor took from his pocket a little tissue-paper packet, and opening it, he handed to the Doctor a perfectly beautiful watch with real diamonds in the back.
sentences.zh: 镇长从口袋里取出一个小小的薄纸包，打开来，把一只背面镶着真钻石、漂亮极了的手表递给医生。

paragraphs.text: Then the Mayor pulled out of his pocket a still larger parcel and said,

sentences.text: Then the Mayor pulled out of his pocket a still larger parcel and said,
sentences.zh: 接着镇长又从口袋里掏出一个更大的包裹，说：

paragraphs.text: “Where is the dog?”

sentences.text: “Where is the dog?”
sentences.zh: 「那只狗在哪儿？」

paragraphs.text: Then everybody started to hunt for Jip. And at last Dab-Dab found him on the other side of the village in a stable-yard, where all the dogs of the country-side were standing round him speechless with admiration and respect.

sentences.text: Then everybody started to hunt for Jip.
sentences.zh: 于是大家开始找吉普。

sentences.text: And at last Dab-Dab found him on the other side of the village in a stable-yard, where all the dogs of the country-side were standing round him speechless with admiration and respect.
sentences.zh: 最后达布达布在村子另一头的马厩院子里找到了他，附近一带的狗都围着他站着，佩服得说不出话来。

hints.zh: 佩服得说不出话：speechless 由 emotion 或 admiration 引起，不是真的不能说话。
hints.en: Speechless with admiration: so full of respect that they could not say a word.

paragraphs.text: When Jip was brought to the Doctor’s side, the Mayor opened the larger parcel; and inside was a dog-collar made of solid gold! And a great murmur of wonder went up from the village-folk as the Mayor bent down and fastened it round the dog’s neck with his own hands.

sentences.text: When Jip was brought to the Doctor’s side, the Mayor opened the larger parcel; and inside was a dog-collar made of solid gold!
sentences.zh: 吉普被带到医生身边时，镇长打开了那个大包裹；里面是一只纯金打的狗项圈！

sentences.text: And a great murmur of wonder went up from the village-folk as the Mayor bent down and fastened it round the dog’s neck with his own hands.
sentences.zh: 镇长弯下腰，亲手把它系在狗的脖子上，村里人发出一片惊叹的低语。

hints.zh: 纯金、实心的金子，不是镀金。
hints.en: Solid gold: real gold all the way through, not just gold-coloured.

paragraphs.text: For written on the collar in big letters were these words: “JIP—The Cleverest Dog in the World.”

sentences.text: For written on the collar in big letters were these words: “JIP—The Cleverest Dog in the World.”
sentences.zh: 因为项圈上用大字写着这样一句话：「吉普——世上最聪明的狗。」

paragraphs.text: Then the whole crowd moved down to the beach to see them off. And after the red-haired fisherman and his sister and the little boy had thanked the Doctor and his dog over and over and over again, the great, swift ship with the red sails was turned once more towards Puddleby and they sailed out to sea, while the village-band played music on the shore.

sentences.text: Then the whole crowd moved down to the beach to see them off.
sentences.zh: 然后整个人群都往海滩走去，给他们送行。

sentences.text: And after the red-haired fisherman and his sister and the little boy had thanked the Doctor and his dog over and over and over again, the great, swift ship with the red sails was turned once more towards Puddleby and they sailed out to sea, while the village-band played music on the shore.
sentences.zh: 等红头发的渔夫、他的姐姐和小男孩一遍又一遍地向医生和他的狗道过谢，那条挂着红帆、又大又快的船又一次掉头朝向帕德尔比，驶向大海，村里的乐队在岸上奏着音乐。

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡，远在英格兰。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor’s home town, far away in England.

hints.zh: see sb off 是「给某人送行」，看着他们出发。
hints.en: See them off: go to the shore to say goodbye as they leave.

introduction.zh: 镇长站在台阶上，先说了一番客气话，又递上一份厚礼。接着他又从口袋里掏出一个更大的包裹，却先问：「那只狗在哪儿？」——大包裹里装的是什么？
introduction.en: On the steps the Mayor makes a fine speech and gives the Doctor one present. Then he takes out a bigger parcel — and asks a strange question first: “Where is the dog?” The whole village starts hunting for Jip. What is in the parcel?

quiz.question: Why did the Mayor ask where the dog was?
options: He wanted to buy the dog.
He was afraid of the dog.
He had a second present for the dog.

feedback.zh: 大包裹里是一只纯金狗项圈，镇长要亲手给吉普戴上，所以才先找它。
feedback.en: The larger parcel held a dog-collar of solid gold, which the Mayor wanted to fasten round Jip’s neck himself.

quiz.question: Where was Jip found?
options: Inside the Doctor’s room
In a stable-yard on the other side of the village
On the beach beside the boat

feedback.zh: 达布达布在村子另一头的马厩院子里找到他，周围的狗都围着他，佩服得说不出话。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab found him in a stable-yard on the other side of the village, with all the local dogs standing round him in silence.

grammar.excerpt: a dog-collar made of solid gold

focus.zh: made of solid gold 是过去分词短语，放在 dog-collar 后面说明它用什么做的，等于「纯金做的狗项圈」。
focus.en: Made of solid gold is a past-participle phrase after dog-collar, telling us what it is made of.

paragraphs.text: March winds had come and gone; April’s showers were over; May’s buds had opened into flower; and the June sun was shining on the pleasant fields, when John Dolittle at last got back to his own country.

sentences.text: March winds had come and gone; April’s showers were over; May’s buds had opened into flower; and the June sun was shining on the pleasant fields, when John Dolittle at last got back to his own country.
sentences.zh: 三月的风来了又走了；四月的阵雨过去了；五月的花苞开成了花；六月的阳光照在宜人的田野上，这时约翰·杜立德终于回到了自己的国家。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，就是医生本人；书里说正经事时才会连名带姓地叫他。
hints.en: John Dolittle: the Doctor himself; the book uses his full name when the tone is serious.

paragraphs.text: But he did not yet go home to Puddleby. First he went traveling through the land with the pushmi-pullyu in a gipsy-wagon, stopping at all the country-fairs. And there, with the acrobats on one side of them and the Punch-and-Judy show on the other, they would hang out a big sign which read, “COME AND SEE THE MARVELOUS TWO-HEADED ANIMAL FROM THE JUNGLES OF AFRICA. Admission SIXPENCE.”

sentences.text: But he did not yet go home to Puddleby.
sentences.zh: 可是他还没有回帕德尔比的家。

sentences.text: First he went traveling through the land with the pushmi-pullyu in a gipsy-wagon, stopping at all the country-fairs.
sentences.zh: 他先带着「推我拉你」乘一辆吉卜赛大车周游各地，在每个乡村集市上停下来。

sentences.text: And there, with the acrobats on one side of them and the Punch-and-Judy show on the other, they would hang out a big sign which read, “COME AND SEE THE MARVELOUS TWO-HEADED ANIMAL FROM THE JUNGLES OF AFRICA.
sentences.zh: 在那里，一边是杂技艺人，另一边是潘趣与朱迪木偶戏，他们就挂出一块大招牌，上面写着：「快来看来自非洲丛林的神奇双头动物。

sentences.text: Admission SIXPENCE.”
sentences.zh: 门票六便士。」

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡小镇；全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby: the Doctor’s home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，那头两个头的动物，医生从非洲带回来的。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu (“push me, pull you”): the two-headed animal he brought back from Africa.

hints.zh: 潘趣与朱迪，英国街头常见的木偶戏。
hints.en: Punch-and-Judy: a traditional English puppet show, played in the street.

paragraphs.text: And the pushmi-pullyu would stay inside the wagon, while the other animals would lie about underneath. The Doctor sat in a chair in front taking the sixpences and smiling on the people as they went in; and Dab-Dab was kept busy all the time scolding him because he would let the children in for nothing when she wasn’t looking.

sentences.text: And the pushmi-pullyu would stay inside the wagon, while the other animals would lie about underneath.
sentences.zh: 「推我拉你」待在车里，别的动物就躺在车子底下。

sentences.text: The Doctor sat in a chair in front taking the sixpences and smiling on the people as they went in; and Dab-Dab was kept busy all the time scolding him because he would let the children in for nothing when she wasn’t looking.
sentences.zh: 医生坐在车前的椅子上收六便士，一边看着人们走进去，一边冲他们笑；达布达布则一直忙着数落他，因为只要她一不留神，他就会让孩子们白看。

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子，管着家里的钱和规矩。
