hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck, who keeps an eye on the money and the rules.

paragraphs.text: And menagerie-keepers and circus-men came and asked the Doctor to sell them the strange creature, saying they would pay a tremendous lot of money for him. But the Doctor always shook his head and said,

sentences.text: And menagerie-keepers and circus-men came and asked the Doctor to sell them the strange creature, saying they would pay a tremendous lot of money for him.
sentences.zh: 还有巡回动物园的老板和马戏团的人跑来，请医生把这头奇怪的动物卖给他们，说愿意为他出一大笔钱。

sentences.text: But the Doctor always shook his head and said,
sentences.zh: 可医生总是摇摇头说：

hints.zh: 巡回动物园的老板；menagerie 指流动展出的动物。
hints.en: Menagerie-keepers: owners of travelling collections of animals.

paragraphs.text: “No. The pushmi-pullyu shall never be shut up in a cage. He shall be free always to come and go, like you and me.”

sentences.text: “No.
sentences.zh: 「不行。

sentences.text: The pushmi-pullyu shall never be shut up in a cage.
sentences.zh: 「推我拉你」绝不能被关进笼子里。

sentences.text: He shall be free always to come and go, like you and me.”
sentences.zh: 他应该永远自由地来去，就像你我一样。」

introduction.zh: 三月的风、四月的雨都过去了，六月的阳光照在田野上，约翰·杜立德终于回到自己的国家——却没有回帕德尔比的家。他赶着吉卜赛大车走集市，招牌上写着：六便士，看非洲丛林来的双头怪兽。他为什么不回家？
introduction.en: Spring is over and the June sun is on the English fields. John Dolittle is back in his own country — but not in Puddleby. He drives a painted wagon from fair to fair, with a sign: sixpence to see the two-headed animal from Africa. Why isn’t he going home?

quiz.question: Why does Dab-Dab keep scolding the Doctor?
options: He lets children in without paying.
He charges too much for the show.
He forgets to feed the animals.

feedback.zh: 原文说只要达布达布没留神，医生就会让孩子们白看，所以她一直忙着数落他。
feedback.en: The text says he would let the children in for nothing whenever she was not looking, so she was kept busy scolding him.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor refuse to do?
options: Show the animal at country fairs
Take the sixpences himself
Sell the pushmi-pullyu to a circus

feedback.zh: 马戏团和动物园的人出大钱要买这头动物，医生每次都摇头：他要让它自由来去，绝不关进笼子。
feedback.en: Menagerie-keepers and circus-men offered a lot of money, but he always shook his head: the animal must be free, never shut in a cage.

grammar.excerpt: they would hang out a big sign

focus.zh: would hang out 不是「愿意挂」，而是说过去每到一处集市都这么挂：一种旧习惯。
focus.en: Would hang out does not mean willingness or the future: it describes what they did again and again at every fair.

paragraphs.text: Many curious sights and happenings they saw in this wandering life; but they all seemed quite ordinary after the great things they had seen and done in foreign lands. It was very interesting at first, being sort of part of a circus; but after a few weeks they all got dreadfully tired of it and the Doctor and all of them were longing to go home.

sentences.text: Many curious sights and happenings they saw in this wandering life; but they all seemed quite ordinary after the great things they had seen and done in foreign lands.
sentences.zh: 在这段漂泊的日子里，他们见过许多稀奇的东西和事情；可比起他们在外国见过的、做过的大事，这些全都显得平平常常。

sentences.text: It was very interesting at first, being sort of part of a circus; but after a few weeks they all got dreadfully tired of it and the Doctor and all of them were longing to go home.
sentences.zh: 一开始，多少算马戏班的一分子，还挺有意思；可几个星期之后，他们全都厌烦得不行，医生和大家一样都盼着回家。

paragraphs.text: But so many people came flocking to the little wagon and paid the sixpence to go inside and see the pushmi-pullyu that very soon the Doctor was able to give up being a showman.

sentences.text: But so many people came flocking to the little wagon and paid the sixpence to go inside and see the pushmi-pullyu that very soon the Doctor was able to give up being a showman.
sentences.zh: 可是来的人太多了，他们成群结队地涌向那辆小车，付六便士进去看「推我拉你」，所以没过多久，医生就不用再当班主了。

hints.zh: 跑江湖的班主，靠展览、表演赚钱的人。
hints.en: A showman: someone who earns money by putting on shows.

paragraphs.text: And one fine day, when the hollyhocks were in full bloom, he came back to Puddleby a rich man, to live in the little house with the big garden.

sentences.text: And one fine day, when the hollyhocks were in full bloom, he came back to Puddleby a rich man, to live in the little house with the big garden.
sentences.zh: 有一天，正当蜀葵开得满满的时候，他回到了帕德尔比，成了一个有钱人，住进那座带大花园的小房子。

paragraphs.text: And the old lame horse in the stable was glad to see him; and so were the swallows who had already built their nests under the eaves of his roof and had young ones. And Dab-Dab was glad, too, to get back to the house she knew so well—although there was a terrible lot of dusting to be done, with cobwebs everywhere.

sentences.text: And the old lame horse in the stable was glad to see him; and so were the swallows who had already built their nests under the eaves of his roof and had young ones.
sentences.zh: 马厩里那匹瘸腿的老马见到他很高兴；那些已经在他屋檐下筑了巢、还孵出了雏鸟的燕子也一样高兴。

sentences.text: And Dab-Dab was glad, too, to get back to the house she knew so well—although there was a terrible lot of dusting to be done, with cobwebs everywhere.
sentences.zh: 达布达布也很高兴回到她那么熟悉的屋子——尽管要打扫的地方实在太多，到处都是蛛网。

paragraphs.text: And after Jip had gone and shown his golden collar to the conceited collie next-door, he came back and began running round the garden like a crazy thing, looking for the bones he had buried long ago, and chasing the rats out of the tool-shed; while Gub-Gub dug up the horseradish which had grown three feet high in the corner by the garden-wall.

sentences.text: And after Jip had gone and shown his golden collar to the conceited collie next-door, he came back and began running round the garden like a crazy thing, looking for the bones he had buried long ago, and chasing the rats out of the tool-shed; while Gub-Gub dug up the horseradish which had grown three feet high in the corner by the garden-wall.
sentences.zh: 吉普跑去把它的金项圈给隔壁那条自以为了不起的牧羊犬看过之后，回来就在花园里像发了疯一样到处跑，找它很久以前埋下的骨头，还把老鼠从工具棚里赶出去；咕咕则把墙角那棵长到三英尺高的辣根拱了出来。

hints.zh: 隔壁那条自以为了不起的牧羊犬；collie 是牧羊犬。
hints.en: The conceited collie next door: a proud sheepdog.

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s little pig.

hints.zh: 辣根，根茎辛辣的植物；猪爱把它拱出来啃。
hints.en: Horseradish: a plant with a hot root, which pigs like to dig up.

introduction.zh: 一路上的新鲜事不少，可比不上在外国见过的大事。几个星期后，马戏班的日子又长又闷，人人都开始想家；小车前排队的人却越来越多。这样的日子还要过多久？
introduction.en: There are new sights on the road, but after Africa they look ordinary. A few weeks of fairs and the animals are tired of it; they want their own beds and their own garden. Yet the crowds at the wagon grow bigger every day. How long can this go on?

quiz.question: Why do the Doctor and the animals get tired of the wandering life?
options: Nobody comes to see the two-headed animal.
The fairs seem ordinary after what they saw in Africa.
The wagon is too small for all of them.

feedback.zh: 原文说这些新鲜事比起他们在外国见过、做过的大事都显得平常，几个星期后大家就都厌倦了。
feedback.en: The text says the sights looked quite ordinary after the great things they had seen abroad, and after a few weeks they were all tired of it.

quiz.question: What does the crowd at the little wagon make possible?
options: The Doctor can stop being a showman.
The Doctor can buy a bigger wagon.
The animals can stop working at night.

feedback.zh: 来的人太多，六便士的门票源源不断，所以没过多久医生就不用再当班主了。
feedback.en: So many people paid sixpence to go in that very soon the Doctor was able to give up being a showman.

grammar.excerpt: after Jip had gone and shown his golden collar

focus.zh: had gone and shown 比 came back 更早：吉普先给隔壁的狗看项圈，然后才跑回花园。
focus.en: Had gone and shown happened before came back: first he showed the collar to the dog next door, then he ran back into the garden.

paragraphs.text: And the Doctor went and saw the sailor who had lent him the boat, and he bought two new ships for him and a rubber-doll for his baby; and he paid the grocer for the food he had lent him for the journey to Africa. And he bought another piano and put the white mice back in it—because they said the bureau-drawer was drafty.

sentences.text: And the Doctor went and saw the sailor who had lent him the boat, and he bought two new ships for him and a rubber-doll for his baby; and he paid the grocer for the food he had lent him for the journey to Africa.
sentences.zh: 医生去看望了那个把船借给他的水手，给他买了两条新船，又给他的宝宝买了一个橡皮娃娃；他还把欠杂货店老板的钱付了——去非洲的路上，那些食物是老板赊给他的。

sentences.text: And he bought another piano and put the white mice back in it—because they said the bureau-drawer was drafty.
sentences.zh: 他又买了一架钢琴，把白鼠放回琴里——因为它们说五斗柜的抽屉漏风。

paragraphs.text: Even when the Doctor had filled the old money-box on the dresser-shelf, he still had a lot of money left; and he had to get three more money-boxes, just as big, to put the rest in.

sentences.text: Even when the Doctor had filled the old money-box on the dresser-shelf, he still had a lot of money left; and he had to get three more money-boxes, just as big, to put the rest in.
sentences.zh: 即使把餐具柜搁板上那个旧存钱盒装满了，他剩下的钱还是很多；他只好又买了三个一样大的存钱盒，把其余的钱装进去。

hints.zh: 餐具柜上的搁板；dresser 这里指厨房里的餐具柜。
hints.en: The shelf of the dresser: the kitchen cupboard where plates are kept.

paragraphs.text: “Money,” he said, “is a terrible nuisance. But it’s nice not to have to worry.”

sentences.text: “Money,” he said, “is a terrible nuisance.
sentences.zh: 「钱，」他说，「真是个麻烦东西。

sentences.text: But it’s nice not to have to worry.”
sentences.zh: 不过不用操心钱的事，倒挺好。」

paragraphs.text: “Yes,” said Dab-Dab, who was toasting muffins for his tea, “it is indeed!”

sentences.text: “Yes,” said Dab-Dab, who was toasting muffins for his tea, “it is indeed!”
sentences.zh: 「是啊，」正在给他烤茶点小圆饼的达布达布说，「说得太对了！」

hints.zh: 英式小圆饼，烤热了抹上黄油，配茶吃。
hints.en: Muffins: small round cakes, toasted and eaten with butter at tea.

paragraphs.text: And when the Winter came again, and the snow flew against the kitchen-window, the Doctor and his animals would sit round the big, warm fire after supper; and he would read aloud to them out of his books.

sentences.text: And when the Winter came again, and the snow flew against the kitchen-window, the Doctor and his animals would sit round the big, warm fire after supper; and he would read aloud to them out of his books.
sentences.zh: 等到冬天又来了，雪花打在厨房的窗户上，晚饭后医生和他的动物们就围坐在又大又暖的火炉边；他会从书里念故事给他们听。

paragraphs.text: But far away in Africa, where the monkeys chattered in the palm-trees before they went to bed under the big yellow moon, they would say to one another,

sentences.text: But far away in Africa, where the monkeys chattered in the palm-trees before they went to bed under the big yellow moon, they would say to one another,
sentences.zh: 可在遥远的非洲，猴子们在棕榈树上叽叽喳喳，然后在又大又黄的月亮下上床睡觉之前，他们会互相说：

paragraphs.text: “I wonder what The Good Man’s doing now—over there, in the Land of the White Men! Do you think he ever will come back?”

sentences.text: “I wonder what The Good Man’s doing now—over there, in the Land of the White Men!
sentences.zh: 「不知道那位好人现在在做什么——在那边，在白人的地方！

sentences.text: Do you think he ever will come back?”
sentences.zh: 你觉得他还会回来吗？」

hints.zh: 「好人」，猴子们对杜立德的称呼。
hints.en: “The Good Man”: what the monkeys call the Doctor.

hints.target: the Land of the White Men
hints.zh: 「白人的地方」，猴子眼中的远方，指英国。
hints.en: “The Land of the White Men”: Britain, as the monkeys picture it.

paragraphs.text: And Polynesia would squeak out from the vines,

sentences.text: And Polynesia would squeak out from the vines,
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚就会从藤蔓里尖声叫出来：

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor’s parrot.

hints.zh: 尖声叫出来；squeak 是老鼠、小鸟那种又高又细的声音。
hints.en: To squeak out: to say something in a high, thin voice.

paragraphs.text: “I think he will—I guess he will—I hope he will!”

sentences.text: “I think he will—I guess he will—I hope he will!”
sentences.zh: 「我想他会——我猜他会——我希望他会！」

paragraphs.text: And then the crocodile would grunt up at them from the black mud of the river,

sentences.text: And then the crocodile would grunt up at them from the black mud of the river,
sentences.zh: 这时鳄鱼会从河里的黑泥中朝他们咕哝：

paragraphs.text: “I’m SURE he will—Go to sleep!”

sentences.text: “I’m SURE he will—Go to sleep!”
sentences.zh: 「我敢肯定他会——睡觉吧！」

introduction.zh: 回到帕德尔比，医生的钱多到要把旧存钱盒装满，还得再买三个。他拿这些钱去还债、买礼物，也给白鼠买回一架钢琴。可远在非洲的猴子们，夜里还在问同一个问题。
introduction.en: Back in Puddleby the Doctor has more money than his old money-box can hold, so he buys three more. He pays back old debts, buys presents, and gives the white mice a new piano. Far away in Africa, the monkeys still ask one question at night. What is it?

quiz.question: What does the Doctor do with his money first?
options: He buys a bigger house.
He sends it to the monkeys in Africa.
He pays back the sailor and the grocer.

feedback.zh: 他给借船的水手买了两条新船和一个橡皮娃娃，又付清了路上赊账的食物钱。
feedback.en: He bought two new ships and a rubber doll for the sailor who lent him the boat, and paid the grocer for the food.

quiz.question: What do the monkeys in Africa talk about at night?
options: Where the crocodile sleeps
What the Good Man is doing and whether he will come back
How to find more palm-trees

feedback.zh: 棕榈树上的猴子们互相问：那位好人在白人的地方做什么，他还会不会回来。
feedback.en: Up in the palm-trees the monkeys ask each other what the Good Man is doing over there, and whether he will ever come back.

grammar.excerpt: I wonder what The Good Man’s doing now

focus.zh: wonder 后面接 what 从句，从句用陈述语序 The Good Man’s doing，不能说 what is he doing。
focus.en: Wonder takes a wh-clause with statement order: what The Good Man’s doing, not what is he doing.
